items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"De temps en temps,","t":"from time to time,"},{"w":"des bénévoles","t":"volunteers"},{"w":"distribuent des repas","t":"distribute meals"},{"w":"aux personnes âgées.","t":"to elderly people"}]}
The x in “yeux” is silent, it never marks a spoken sound here.

items.fr: Mon frère a mal au dos.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ a mal o do
items.notes: “au” is the required contraction of “à” plus “le” before “dos”.
“longs” takes a final -s to agree with the plural “cheveux”.

items.fr: Elle s'est cassé la jambe en tombant dans l'escalier.
items.en: She broke her leg falling down the stairs.
items.ipa: ɛl sɛ ka.se la ʒɑ̃b ɑ̃ tɔ̃.bɑ̃ dɑ̃ lɛs.ka.lje
items.notes: “cassé” stays masculine singular because “la jambe” is the direct object, not the reflexive pronoun.

items.fr: Il a mal au cou après avoir dormi dans le train.
items.en: His neck hurts after sleeping on the train.
items.ipa: il a mal o ku a.pʁɛ a.vwaʁ dɔʁ.mi dɑ̃ lə tʁɛ̃
items.notes: “cou” (neck) is a homophone of “coup” (a blow), only context decides the spelling.

items.fr: Ses yeux et ses oreilles sont très sensibles au bruit.
items.en: His eyes and ears are very sensitive to noise.
items.ipa: sɛ.z‿jø e sɛ.z‿ɔ.ʁɛj sɔ̃ tʁɛ sɑ̃.sibl o bʁɥi
items.notes: The final “s” of “ses” is pronounced as a liaison [z] before the vowel of “yeux”.

items.fr: L'épaule me fait mal depuis hier.
items.en: My shoulder has been hurting since yesterday.
items.ipa: le.pol mə fɛ mal də.pɥi jɛʁ
items.notes: “Le” elides to “L'” before the vowel-initial “épaule”.

items.fr: J'ai de la fièvre et je tousse beaucoup.
items.en: I have a fever and I'm coughing a lot.
items.ipa: ʒe də la fjɛvʁ e ʒə tus bo.ku
items.notes: “fièvre” needs a grave accent on the first e, not an acute one.

items.fr: Elle a le nez bouché et mal à la gorge.
items.en: Her nose is stuffy and her throat hurts.
items.ipa: ɛl a lə ne bu.ʃe e mal a la gɔʁʒ
items.notes: “bouché” is spelled with “ch”, never “sh” as in English.

items.fr: Je me sens fatigué depuis plusieurs jours.
items.en: I've been feeling tired for several days.
items.ipa: ʒə mə sɑ̃ fa.ti.ge də.pɥi ply.zjœʁ ʒuʁ
items.notes: “sens” is the irregular je-form of “se sentir”, not a regular -er ending.

items.fr: As-tu de la fièvre, des frissons ou des courbatures ?
items.en: Do you have a fever, chills, or body aches?
items.ipa: a ty də la fjɛvʁ, de fʁi.sɔ̃ u de kuʁ.ba.tyʁ
items.notes: French always requires a space before the final question mark “?”.

items.fr: Le médecin lui a dit d'aller à la pharmacie.
items.en: The doctor told him to go to the pharmacy.
items.ipa: lə med.sɛ̃ lɥi a di da.le a la faʁ.ma.si
items.notes: “a” (from “avoir”) has no accent, while “à” before “la pharmacie” always takes the grave accent.

items.fr: La radio qu'il a passée n'a rien révélé d'anormal.
items.en: The X-ray he had didn't reveal anything unusual.
items.ipa: la ʁa.djo kil a pa.se na ʁjɛ̃ ʁe.ve.le da.nɔʁ.mal
items.notes: “passée” agrees in the feminine because its direct object “que” (standing for “la radio”) comes before the verb.

items.fr: Il aurait fallu consulter un spécialiste plus tôt.
items.en: He should have seen a specialist sooner.
items.ipa: il o.ʁɛ fa.ly kɔ̃.syl.te ɛ̃ spe.sja.list ply to
items.notes: “fallu” is the invariable past participle of the impersonal verb “falloir”, used here after “aurait”.

items.fr: Elle fait des exercices de respiration tous les soirs.
items.en: She does breathing exercises every evening.
items.ipa: ɛl fɛ de.z‿ɛg.zɛʁ.sis də ʁɛs.pi.ʁa.sjɔ̃ tu lɛ swaʁ
items.notes: The “s” of “des” links to “exercices” with a [z] sound, a liaison.

items.fr: Elle prend le temps de se reposer chaque après-midi.
items.en: She takes time to rest every afternoon.
items.ipa: ɛl pʁɑ̃ lə tɑ̃ də sə ʁə.po.ze ʃak a.pʁɛ mi.di
items.notes: The final “ps” in “temps” is silent, the word is pronounced simply [tɑ̃].

items.fr: Il vaut mieux dormir tôt pour bien récupérer.
items.en: It's better to sleep early to recover well.
items.ipa: il vo mjø dɔʁ.miʁ to puʁ bjɛ̃ ʁe.ky.pe.ʁe
items.notes: “il vaut mieux” is a fixed impersonal phrase, always kept in the third-person singular of “valoir”.

items.fr: Les bienfaits d'une bonne hygiène de vie sont nombreux et durables.
items.en: The benefits of a healthy lifestyle are numerous and lasting.
items.ipa: le bjɛ̃.fɛ dyn bɔn i.ʒjɛn də vi sɔ̃ nɔ̃.bʁø e dy.ʁabl
items.notes: “nombreux” and “durables” both take plural endings to agree with the plural “bienfaits”.
{"tiles":[{"w":"J'ai froid","t":"I'm cold"},{"w":"aux pieds.","t":"in the feet"}]}

items.fr: Elle se lave les mains avant le dîner.
items.en: She washes her hands before dinner.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle se lave les mains","t":"she washes her hands"},{"w":"avant le dîner.","t":"before dinner"}]}

items.fr: Mon dos me fait mal ce soir.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Mon dos","t":"my back"},{"w":"me fait mal","t":"hurts"},{"w":"ce soir.","t":"tonight"}]}

items.fr: Elle s'est fait mal au genou en courant.
items.en: She hurt her knee while running.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle s'est fait mal au genou","t":"she hurt her knee"},{"w":"en courant.","t":"while running"}]}

items.fr: Il faut se laver les dents matin et soir.
items.en: You have to brush your teeth morning and night.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il faut se laver les dents","t":"you have to brush your teeth"},{"w":"matin et soir.","t":"morning and night"}]}

items.fr: Elle a un bleu sur le bras depuis hier.
items.en: She has had a bruise on her arm since yesterday.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle a un bleu","t":"she has had a bruise"},{"w":"sur le bras","t":"on her arm"},{"w":"depuis hier.","t":"since yesterday"}]}

items.fr: J'ai mal à la gorge et je n'ai pas faim.
items.en: My throat hurts and I have no appetite.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"J'ai mal à la gorge","t":"my throat hurts"},{"w":"et je n'ai pas faim.","t":"and I have no appetite"}]}

items.fr: Il tousse depuis trois jours et il est fatigué.
items.en: He's been coughing for three days and he's tired.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il tousse","t":"he's been coughing"},{"w":"depuis trois jours","t":"for three days"},{"w":"et il est fatigué.","t":"and he's tired"}]}

items.fr: Elle a de la fièvre depuis ce matin.
items.en: She has had a fever since this morning.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle a de la fièvre","t":"she has had a fever"},{"w":"depuis ce matin.","t":"since this morning"}]}

items.fr: Mon nez coule et j'ai mal à la tête.
items.en: My nose is running and I have a headache.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Mon nez coule","t":"my nose is running"},{"w":"et j'ai mal à la tête.","t":"and I have a headache"}]}

items.fr: Il a des vertiges quand il se lève trop vite.
items.en: He gets dizzy when he stands up too quickly.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il a des vertiges","t":"he gets dizzy"},{"w":"quand il se lève","t":"when he stands up"},{"w":"trop vite.","t":"too quickly"}]}

items.fr: Il vaut mieux prendre rendez-vous avant que la douleur empire.
items.en: It's better to make an appointment before the pain gets worse.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il vaut mieux","t":"it's better to"},{"w":"prendre rendez-vous","t":"make an appointment"},{"w":"avant que la douleur empire.","t":"before the pain gets worse"}]}

items.fr: Le médecin lui a recommandé de faire plus attention à son alimentation.
items.en: The doctor recommended that he pay more attention to his diet.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le médecin","t":"the doctor"},{"w":"lui a recommandé de","t":"recommended that he"},{"w":"faire plus attention","t":"pay more attention"},{"w":"à son alimentation.","t":"to his diet"}]}

items.fr: Il est indispensable de suivre le traitement jusqu'au bout pour éviter une rechute.
items.en: It's essential to follow the treatment all the way through to avoid a relapse.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il est indispensable","t":"it's essential"},{"w":"de suivre le traitement","t":"to follow the treatment"},{"w":"jusqu'au bout","t":"all the way through"},{"w":"pour éviter une rechute.","t":"to avoid a relapse"}]}

items.fr: Elle essaie de faire du sport trois fois par semaine.
items.en: She tries to exercise three times a week.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle essaie de faire du sport","t":"she tries to exercise"},{"w":"trois fois par semaine.","t":"three times a week"}]}

items.fr: Prendre du temps pour soi aide à réduire le stress.
items.en: Taking time for yourself helps reduce stress.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Prendre du temps pour soi","t":"taking time for yourself"},{"w":"aide à réduire","t":"helps reduce"},{"w":"le stress.","t":"stress"}]}

items.fr: De temps en temps, il est bon de déconnecter complètement du travail.
items.en: From time to time, it's good to unplug completely from work.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"De temps en temps,","t":"from time to time,"},{"w":"il est bon","t":"it's good"},{"w":"de déconnecter complètement","t":"to unplug completely"},{"w":"du travail.","t":"from work"}]}

items.fr: Avoir besoin de repos ne veut pas dire qu'on est faible.
items.en: Needing rest doesn't mean you're weak.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Avoir besoin de repos","t":"needing rest"},{"w":"ne veut pas dire","t":"doesn't mean"},{"w":"qu'on est faible.","t":"that you're weak"}]}

items.fr: Elle est infirmière et elle travaille la nuit.
items.en: She's a nurse and she works nights.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ.t‿ɛ̃.fiʁ.mjɛʁ e ɛl tʁa.vaj la nɥi
items.notes: “et” (and) and “est” (is) sound identical, but only “et” can link the two clauses here.

items.fr: Mon père est cuisinier, pas serveur.
items.en: My father is a cook, not a waiter.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ pɛʁ ɛ kɥi.zi.nje pa sɛʁ.vœʁ
items.notes: “cuisinier” stays masculine with no article to agree with “mon père”.

items.fr: Ma tante est boulangère depuis dix ans.
items.en: My aunt has been a baker for ten years.
items.ipa: ma tɑ̃t ɛ bu.lɑ̃.ʒɛʁ də.pɥi di.z‿ɑ̃
items.notes: The “x” in “dix” is pronounced as a liaison “z” before the vowel sound in “ans”.

items.fr: Mon cousin est avocat dans un grand cabinet.
items.en: My cousin is a lawyer at a big law firm.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ ku.zɛ̃ ɛ.t‿a.vɔ.ka dɑ̃.z‿œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ ka.bi.nɛ
items.notes: The final “t” in “avocat” stays silent, unlike in the feminine form “avocate”.

items.fr: Elle a longtemps hésité avant de choisir ce métier.
items.en: She hesitated for a long time before choosing this profession.
items.ipa: ɛl a lɔ̃.tɑ̃ e.zi.te a.vɑ̃ də ʃwa.ziʁ sə me.tje
items.notes: “hésité” ends in é because it follows “a” in the passé composé.

items.fr: L'employé arrive toujours avant l'ouverture du bureau.
items.en: The employee always arrives before the office opens.
items.ipa: lɑ̃.plwa.je a.ʁiv tu.ʒuʁ a.vɑ̃ lu.vɛʁ.tyʁ dy by.ʁo
items.notes: “Le employé” elides to “L'employé” before a word starting with a vowel sound.

items.fr: Les collègues envoient leurs rapports avant midi.
items.en: The colleagues send their reports before noon.
items.ipa: le kɔ.lɛg ɑ̃.vwa lœʁ ʁa.pɔʁ a.vɑ̃ mi.di
items.notes: “rapports” takes a silent plural “s” to agree with “leurs”, the plural possessive.

items.fr: Il faut que le rapport soit prêt avant vendredi.
items.en: The report needs to be ready before Friday.
items.ipa: il fo kə lə ʁa.pɔʁ swa pʁɛ a.vɑ̃ vɑ̃.dʁə.di
items.notes: “il faut que” requires the subjunctive “soit”, not the indicative “est”.

items.fr: La secrétaire a immédiatement transmis le message au directeur.
items.en: The secretary immediately forwarded the message to the director.
items.ipa: la sə.kʁe.tɛʁ a i.me.dja.tmɑ̃ tʁɑ̃s.mi lə me.saʒ o di.ʁɛk.tœʁ
items.notes: “immédiatement” doubles the “m” after the prefix “im-”, unlike words formed with “in-”.

items.fr: Le directeur a demandé : « Où en est le budget ? »
items.en: The director asked, "Where do things stand with the budget?"
items.ipa: lə di.ʁɛk.tœʁ a də.mɑ̃.de u ɑ̃.n‿ɛ lə by.dʒɛ
items.notes: French requires a space before the colon and before the closing guillemet, unlike English punctuation.

items.fr: Ces chiffres montrent que l'entreprise a progressé cette année.
items.en: These figures show that the company made progress this year.
items.ipa: se ʃifʁ mɔ̃tʁ kə lɑ̃.tʁə.pʁiz a pʁɔ.gʁɛ.se sɛt a.ne
items.notes: “Ces” (these) sounds identical to “ses” and “c'est”, but only the demonstrative “ces” fits before “chiffres”.

items.fr: Le conseil d'administration aurait préféré reporter la décision.
items.en: The board would have preferred to postpone the decision.
items.ipa: lə kɔ̃.sɛj d‿ad.mi.nis.tʁa.sjɔ̃ o.ʁɛ pʁe.fe.ʁe ʁə.pɔʁ.te la de.si.zjɔ̃
items.notes: “aurait préféré” is the past conditional, spelled “-ait”, not the future ending “-a”.

items.fr: Les décisions que le comité a prises ont surpris tout le monde.
items.en: The decisions the committee made surprised everyone.
items.ipa: le de.si.zjɔ̃ kə lə kɔ.mi.te a pʁiz ɔ̃ syʁ.pʁi tu lə mɔ̃d
items.notes: “prises” agrees in gender and number with “décisions”, the preceding direct object of “a prises”.

items.fr: Je suis professeur dans une école primaire.
items.en: I'm a teacher at an elementary school.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Je suis professeur","t":"I'm a teacher"},{"w":"dans une école primaire.","t":"at an elementary school"}]}

items.fr: Il travaille comme cuisinier dans un petit restaurant.
items.en: He works as a cook at a small restaurant.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il travaille comme cuisinier","t":"he works as a cook"},{"w":"dans un petit restaurant.","t":"at a small restaurant"}]}

items.fr: Elle vient de trouver un nouveau travail dans un hôpital.
items.en: She just found a new job at a hospital.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle","t":"she"},{"w":"vient de","t":"just (recently)"},{"w":"trouver","t":"find"},{"w":"un nouveau travail","t":"a new job"},{"w":"dans un hôpital.","t":"at a hospital"}]}

items.fr: Mon oncle a changé de métier après vingt ans.
items.en: My uncle changed careers after twenty years.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Mon oncle","t":"my uncle"},{"w":"a changé de métier","t":"changed careers"},{"w":"après vingt ans.","t":"after twenty years"}]}

items.fr: Beaucoup de jeunes hésitent avant de choisir une carrière stable.
items.en: Many young people hesitate before settling on a stable career.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Beaucoup de jeunes","t":"many young people"},{"w":"hésitent","t":"hesitate"},{"w":"avant de choisir","t":"before settling on"},{"w":"une carrière stable.","t":"a stable career"}]}

items.fr: Il y a une imprimante au fond du couloir.
items.en: There's a printer at the end of the hallway.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il y a","t":"there is"},{"w":"une imprimante","t":"a printer"},{"w":"au fond du couloir.","t":"at the end of the hallway"}]}

items.fr: Elle prend toujours une pause à midi.
items.en: She always takes a break at noon.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle prend toujours","t":"she always takes"},{"w":"une pause","t":"a break"},{"w":"à midi.","t":"at noon"}]}

items.fr: Il vaut mieux prévenir ton collègue avant de partir plus tôt.
items.en: It's better to give your colleague a heads-up before leaving early.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il vaut mieux","t":"it's better to"},{"w":"prévenir ton collègue","t":"give your colleague a heads-up"},{"w":"avant de partir","t":"before leaving"},{"w":"plus tôt.","t":"early"}]}

items.fr: Le stagiaire a dû apprendre à gérer plusieurs dossiers en même temps.
items.en: The intern had to learn to manage several files at once.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le stagiaire","t":"the intern"},{"w":"a dû apprendre à","t":"had to learn to"},{"w":"gérer plusieurs dossiers","t":"manage several files"},{"w":"en même temps.","t":"at once"}]}

items.fr: L'entreprise a besoin d'investisseurs pour se développer à l'international.
items.en: The company needs investors to expand internationally.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"L'entreprise","t":"the company"},{"w":"a besoin d'investisseurs","t":"needs investors"},{"w":"pour se développer","t":"to expand"},{"w":"à l'international.","t":"internationally"}]}

items.fr: Les deux sociétés négocient un partenariat depuis plusieurs semaines.
items.en: The two companies have been negotiating a partnership for several weeks.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Les deux sociétés","t":"the two companies"},{"w":"négocient","t":"have been negotiating"},{"w":"un partenariat","t":"a partnership"},{"w":"depuis plusieurs semaines.","t":"for several weeks"}]}

items.fr: Il serait judicieux de tenir compte de l'avis des actionnaires avant de trancher.
items.en: It would be wise to take the shareholders' views into account before deciding.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il serait judicieux de","t":"it would be wise to"},{"w":"tenir compte de","t":"take into account"},{"w":"l'avis des actionnaires","t":"the shareholders' views"},{"w":"avant de trancher.","t":"before deciding"}]}

items.fr: La direction a fini par céder aux exigences des syndicats après des mois de tension.
items.en: Management eventually gave in to the unions' demands after months of tension.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"La direction","t":"management"},{"w":"a fini par céder","t":"eventually gave in"},{"w":"aux exigences des syndicats","t":"to the unions' demands"},{"w":"après des mois de tension.","t":"after months of tension"}]}

items.fr: Le train a du retard aujourd'hui.
items.en: The train is running late today.
items.ipa: lə tʁɛ̃ a dy ʁə.taʁ o.ʒuʁ.dɥi
items.notes: “a” (from avoir) and “à” sound identical, but only the verb “a” fits after “le train”.

items.fr: L'arrêt de bus est juste à côté.
items.en: The bus stop is right next door.
items.ipa: la.ʁɛ də bys ɛ ʒys.t‿a ko.te
items.notes: “arrêt” needs a circumflex accent on the e, without it the word is misspelled.

items.fr: Cette station est fermée pour travaux.
items.en: This station is closed for renovations.
items.ipa: sɛt sta.sjɔ̃ ɛ fɛʁ.me puʁ tʁa.vo
items.notes: “fermée” takes an extra e to agree with the feminine noun “station”.

items.fr: Il faut composter le billet avant de monter.
items.en: You have to validate your ticket before boarding.
items.ipa: il fo kɔ̃.pɔs.te lə bi.jɛ a.vɑ̃ də mɔ̃.te
items.notes: The final “t” in “billet” is silent.

items.fr: Les enfants adorent visiter le musée.
items.en: The kids love visiting the museum.
items.notes: “Les enfants” requires a liaison: a z-sound links “les” and “enfants”.

items.fr: L'office de tourisme ouvre à neuf heures.
items.en: The tourist office opens at nine.
items.ipa: lɔ.fis də tu.ʁism uvʁ a nœ.v‿œʁ
items.notes: “Le” elides to “L'” before the vowel sound in “office”.

items.fr: Ils se sont promenés dans la vieille ville toute la journée.
items.en: They strolled around the old town all day.
items.ipa: il sə sɔ̃ pʁɔ.mə.ne dɑ̃ la vjɛj vil tut la ʒuʁ.ne
items.notes: “promenés” takes a final s because the reflexive pronoun “se” acts as the plural direct object.

items.fr: Il faut que nous réservions l'hôtel avant le week-end.
items.en: We need to book the hotel before the weekend.
items.ipa: il fo kə nu ʁe.zɛʁ.vjɔ̃ lo.tɛl a.vɑ̃ lə wik.ɛnd
items.notes: After “il faut que” the verb takes the subjunctive: “réservions”, not the indicative “réservons”.

items.fr: Nous avons réellement apprécié notre excursion en bateau.
items.en: We really enjoyed our boat trip.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʁe.ɛl.mɑ̃ a.pʁe.sje nɔ.tʁ ɛks.kyʁ.sjɔ̃ ɑ̃ ba.to
items.notes: “réellement” has two e's in a row (é then e), not a single one.

items.fr: Les chambres sont propres et bien rangées.
items.en: The rooms are clean and tidy.
items.ipa: le ʃɑ̃bʁ sɔ̃ pʁɔpʁ e bjɛ̃ ʁɑ̃.ʒe
items.notes: “rangées” agrees in gender and number with the feminine plural “chambres”.

items.fr: Est-ce que le petit-déjeuner est compris dans le prix ?
items.en: Is breakfast included in the price?
items.ipa: ɛs kə lə pə.ti de.ʒœ.ne ɛ kɔ̃.pʁi dɑ̃ lə pʁi
items.notes: French requires a space before the question mark, as in “prix ?”.

items.fr: Notre chambre donne directement sur la mer.
items.en: Our room looks directly out over the sea.
items.ipa: nɔtʁ ʃɑ̃bʁ dɔn di.ʁɛk.tə.mɑ̃ syʁ la mɛʁ
items.notes: “mer” sounds like “mère” and “maire”, but only “mer” fits a room with a sea view.

items.fr: Le tarif comprend le petit-déjeuner et le blanchissage du linge.
items.en: The rate includes breakfast and a laundry service.
items.ipa: lə ta.ʁif kɔ̃.pʁɑ̃ lə pə.ti de.ʒœ.ne e lə blɑ̃.ʃi.saʒ dy lɛ̃ʒ
items.notes: The final “d” in “comprend” is silent.

items.fr: Si nous avions réservé plus tôt, nous aurions payé moins cher.
items.en: If we had booked earlier, we would have paid less.
items.ipa: si nu.z‿a.vjɔ̃ ʁe.zɛʁ.ve ply to, nu.z‿o.ʁjɔ̃ pɛ.je mwɛ̃ ʃɛʁ
items.notes: “aurions” is the conditional, easily confused with the future “aurons”; the “si” clause here calls for the conditional.

items.fr: Elle est italienne, mais elle habite en France.
items.en: She's Italian, but she lives in France.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ i.ta.ljɛn mɛ ɛl a.bit ɑ̃ fʁɑ̃s
items.notes: “italienne” doubles the n and adds an e to agree with the feminine subject.

items.fr: Nous allons en Espagne cet été.
items.en: We're going to Spain this summer.
items.notes: There's a liaison between “en” and “Espagne”: a linking n-sound is pronounced.

items.fr: J'habite en Belgique depuis trois ans.
items.en: I've been living in Belgium for three years.
items.notes: “Je” elides to “J'” before the vowel sound in “habite”.

items.fr: Les Français aiment beaucoup voyager en été.
items.en: The French really love to travel in summer.
items.ipa: le fʁɑ̃.sɛ ɛm bo.ku vwa.ja.ʒe ɑ̃.n‿e.te
items.notes: “Français” is capitalized here because it names the people, not the lowercase adjective “français”.

items.fr: Je prends le métro tous les matins.
items.en: I take the subway every morning.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Je","t":"I"},{"w":"prends","t":"take"},{"w":"le métro","t":"the subway"},{"w":"tous les matins.","t":"every morning"}]}

items.fr: Le taxi nous attend devant l'hôtel.
items.en: The taxi is waiting for us in front of the hotel.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le taxi","t":"the taxi"},{"w":"nous attend","t":"is waiting for us"},{"w":"devant l'hôtel.","t":"in front of the hotel"}]}

items.fr: Il vaut mieux réserver les billets de train à l'avance.
items.en: It's better to book train tickets in advance.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il vaut mieux","t":"it's better to"},{"w":"réserver","t":"book"},{"w":"les billets de train","t":"the train tickets"},{"w":"à l'avance.","t":"in advance"}]}

items.fr: Nous avons raté la correspondance à la gare.
items.en: We missed our connection at the station.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons raté","t":"we missed"},{"w":"la correspondance","t":"our connection"},{"w":"à la gare.","t":"at the station"}]}

items.fr: Cette ville a beaucoup de monuments à voir.
items.en: This town has a lot of monuments to see.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Cette ville","t":"this town"},{"w":"a","t":"has"},{"w":"beaucoup de monuments","t":"a lot of monuments"},{"w":"à voir.","t":"to see"}]}

items.fr: Il y a une longue file d'attente devant le musée.
items.en: There's a long line in front of the museum.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il y a","t":"there is"},{"w":"une longue file d'attente","t":"a long line"},{"w":"devant le musée.","t":"in front of the museum"}]}

items.fr: Les touristes viennent de découvrir un petit café caché dans une ruelle.
items.en: The tourists just discovered a small café hidden down an alley.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Les touristes","t":"the tourists"},{"w":"viennent de découvrir","t":"just discovered"},{"w":"un petit café caché","t":"a small hidden café"},{"w":"dans une ruelle.","t":"down an alley"}]}

items.fr: Bien que la visite guidée soit un peu chère, elle vaut vraiment le détour.
items.en: Even though the guided tour is a bit pricey, it's really worth it.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Bien que","t":"even though"},{"w":"la visite guidée","t":"the guided tour"},{"w":"soit un peu chère,","t":"is a bit pricey,"},{"w":"elle vaut vraiment","t":"it's really worth"},{"w":"le détour.","t":"it"}]}

items.fr: Nous avons pris le temps de flâner dans les petites rues du quartier historique.
items.en: We took the time to wander through the little streets of the old quarter.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons pris le temps de","t":"we took the time to"},{"w":"flâner","t":"wander"},{"w":"dans les petites rues","t":"through the little streets"},{"w":"du quartier historique.","t":"of the old quarter"}]}

items.fr: L'auberge de jeunesse propose des chambres à petit prix.
items.en: The youth hostel offers rooms at low prices.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"L'auberge de jeunesse","t":"the youth hostel"},{"w":"propose","t":"offers"},{"w":"des chambres","t":"rooms"},{"w":"à petit prix.","t":"at low prices"}]}

items.fr: Nous avons besoin d'une chambre pour trois nuits.
items.en: We need a room for three nights.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons besoin","t":"we need"},{"w":"d'une chambre","t":"a room"},{"w":"pour trois nuits.","t":"for three nights"}]}

items.fr: Si la réception est fermée, il faut appeler ce numéro pour obtenir les clés.
items.en: If the front desk is closed, you have to call this number to get the keys.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Si la réception est fermée,","t":"if the front desk is closed,"},{"w":"il faut appeler","t":"you have to call"},{"w":"ce numéro","t":"this number"},{"w":"pour obtenir les clés.","t":"to get the keys"}]}

items.fr: L'appartement que nous avons loué donnait sur une petite cour tranquille.
items.en: The apartment we rented looked out over a quiet little courtyard.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"L'appartement","t":"the apartment"},{"w":"que nous avons loué","t":"we rented"},{"w":"donnait sur","t":"looked out over"},{"w":"une petite cour tranquille.","t":"a quiet little courtyard"}]}

items.fr: Il vaudrait mieux annuler la réservation si nous arrivons après minuit.
items.en: We'd better cancel the reservation if we arrive after midnight.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il vaudrait mieux","t":"we'd better"},{"w":"annuler la réservation","t":"cancel the reservation"},{"w":"si nous arrivons","t":"if we arrive"},{"w":"après minuit.","t":"after midnight"}]}

items.fr: Mon voisin est japonais et parle très bien français.
items.en: My neighbor is Japanese and speaks French very well.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Mon voisin","t":"my neighbor"},{"w":"est japonais","t":"is Japanese"},{"w":"et parle","t":"and speaks"},{"w":"très bien français.","t":"French very well"}]}

items.fr: Elle vient du Portugal, pas d'Espagne.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle vient du Portugal,","t":"she's from Portugal,"},{"w":"pas d'Espagne.","t":"not Spain"}]}

items.fr: Beaucoup de touristes allemands visitent cette région chaque année.
items.en: Many German tourists visit this region every year.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Beaucoup de touristes allemands","t":"many German tourists"},{"w":"visitent","t":"visit"},{"w":"cette région","t":"this region"},{"w":"chaque année.","t":"every year"}]}

items.fr: De temps en temps, nous recevons des amis brésiliens à la maison.
items.en: Every once in a while, we host Brazilian friends at home.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"De temps en temps,","t":"every once in a while,"},{"w":"nous recevons","t":"we host"},{"w":"des amis brésiliens","t":"Brazilian friends"},{"w":"à la maison.","t":"at home"}]}

items.fr: Il fait très froid ce soir.
items.ipa: il fɛ tʁɛ fʁwa sə swaʁ
items.notes: “très” keeps its grave accent on the e, unlike the misspelling “tres”.

items.fr: Le vent souffle fort dans les arbres.
items.en: The wind is blowing hard through the trees.
items.ipa: lə vɑ̃ suf.lə fɔʁ dɑ̃ le.z‿aʁbʁ
items.notes: There's a liaison between “les” and “arbres”, pronounced with a z sound.

items.en: Is it going to rain tomorrow?
items.notes: French requires a space before the question mark, as in “demain ?”, not “demain?”.

items.fr: Les températures ont chuté depuis hier.
items.ipa: le tɑ̃.pe.ʁa.tyʁ ɔ̃ ʃy.te də.pɥi jɛʁ
items.notes: “chuté” stays invariable here since there is no preceding direct object with “avoir”.

items.fr: Le chien aboie quand il entend du bruit.
items.en: The dog barks when it hears a noise.
items.ipa: lə ʃjɛ̃ a.bwa kɑ̃ il ɑ̃.tɑ̃ dy bʁɥi
items.notes: “quand” sounds like “qu'en”, but only “quand” fits before “il”.

items.fr: Les chats adorent dormir au soleil.
items.en: Cats love sleeping in the sun.
items.ipa: le ʃa a.dɔʁ dɔʁ.miʁ o sɔ.lɛj
items.notes: “adorent” takes the -ent ending to agree with the plural subject “les chats”.
“le” elides to “L'” before the vowel sound in “oiseau”.

items.fr: Le renard s'est caché derrière les buissons.
items.en: The fox hid behind the bushes.
items.ipa: lə ʁə.naʁ sɛ ka.ʃe dɛ.ʁjɛʁ le bɥi.sɔ̃
items.notes: “caché” agrees with the masculine subject “le renard”, so it takes no extra “e”.

items.fr: La forêt sent bon après la pluie.
items.en: The forest smells nice after the rain.
items.ipa: la fɔ.ʁɛ sɑ̃ bɔ̃ a.pʁɛ la plɥi
items.notes: “forêt” has a circumflex accent marking a letter that disappeared long ago.

items.fr: Le sommet de la montagne est couvert de neige.
items.en: The mountain's summit is covered in snow.
items.ipa: lə sɔ.mɛ də la mɔ̃.taɲ ɛ ku.vɛʁ də nɛʒ
items.notes: The final “t” in “sommet” is silent.

items.fr: Les randonneurs ont admiré le paysage depuis le sommet.
items.en: The hikers admired the scenery from the summit.
items.ipa: le ʁɑ̃.dɔ.nœʁ ɔ̃.t‿ad.mi.ʁe lə pe.i.zaʒ də.pɥi lə sɔ.mɛ
items.notes: There's a liaison between “ont” and “admiré”, pronounced with a t sound.

items.fr: La rivière qu'ils ont traversée était glacée.
items.en: The river they crossed was freezing cold.
items.ipa: la ʁi.vjɛʁ kil.z‿ɔ̃ tʁa.vɛʁ.se e.tɛ gla.se
items.notes: “traversée” agrees with “la rivière” because the direct object “qu'” comes before the auxiliary “ont”.

items.fr: Il faut réduire nos déchets pour protéger la planète.
items.en: We need to cut down on our waste to protect the planet.
items.ipa: il fo ʁe.dɥiʁ no de.ʃɛ puʁ pʁɔ.te.ʒe la pla.nɛt
items.notes: “faut” sounds like “faux”, but only “faut” fits after “il”.

items.fr: Les usines rejettent trop de gaz polluants dans l'atmosphère.
items.en: Factories release too much polluting gas into the atmosphere.
items.ipa: le.z‿y.zin ʁə.ʒɛt tʁo də gaz pɔ.lɥɑ̃ dɑ̃ lat.mɔs.fɛʁ
items.notes: “le” elides to “l'” before the vowel sound in “atmosphère”.

items.fr: On recycle de plus en plus de plastique en France.
items.en: More and more plastic is being recycled in France.
items.ipa: ɔ̃ ʁə.si.kl də ply.z‿ɑ̃ ply də plas.tik ɑ̃ fʁɑ̃s
items.notes: “recycle” keeps its Greek-derived “y”, not an “i”.

items.fr: Le réchauffement climatique menace plusieurs espèces animales.
items.en: Climate change is threatening several animal species.
items.ipa: lə ʁe.ʃof.mɑ̃ kli.ma.tik mə.nas ply.zjœʁ ɛs.pɛs a.ni.mal
items.notes: “animales” takes an -es ending to agree with the plural feminine noun “espèces”.

items.fr: Malgré les efforts déployés, la biodiversité continue de décliner.
items.en: Despite the efforts made, biodiversity keeps declining.
items.ipa: mal.gʁe le.z‿e.fɔʁ de.plwa.je la bjo.di.vɛʁ.si.te kɔ̃.ti.ny də de.kli.ne
items.notes: “déployés” agrees with the masculine plural noun “les efforts”, taking an -s ending.

items.fr: Les scientifiques s'inquiètent des conséquences irréversibles du changement climatique.
items.en: Scientists are worried about the irreversible consequences of climate change.
items.ipa: le sjɑ̃.ti.fik sɛ̃.kjɛt de kɔ̃.se.kɑ̃s i.ʁe.vɛʁ.sibl dy ʃɑ̃.ʒmɑ̃ kli.ma.tik
items.notes: “s'inquiètent” shifts the accent from é to è because the ending “-ent” is unstressed.

items.fr: Il y a du soleil aujourd'hui.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il y a","t":"there is"},{"w":"du soleil","t":"sunshine"},{"w":"aujourd'hui.","t":"today"}]}

items.fr: Le ciel devient gris avant l'orage.
items.en: The sky turns grey before the storm.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le ciel","t":"the sky"},{"w":"devient gris","t":"turns grey"},{"w":"avant l'orage.","t":"before the storm"}]}

items.fr: Elle met un manteau parce qu'il fait froid.
items.en: She's putting on a coat because it's cold.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle met","t":"she's putting on"},{"w":"un manteau","t":"a coat"},{"w":"parce qu'il fait froid.","t":"because it's cold"}]}

items.fr: La météo va changer de temps en temps cette semaine.
items.en: The weather will change now and then this week.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"La météo","t":"the weather"},{"w":"va changer","t":"is going to change"},{"w":"de temps en temps","t":"now and then"},{"w":"cette semaine.","t":"this week"}]}

items.fr: Le petit chat boit du lait chaque matin.
items.en: The little cat drinks milk every morning.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le petit chat","t":"the little cat"},{"w":"boit","t":"drinks"},{"w":"du lait","t":"milk"},{"w":"chaque matin.","t":"every morning"}]}

items.fr: Les oiseaux volent vers le sud en hiver.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Les oiseaux","t":"birds"},{"w":"volent","t":"fly"},{"w":"vers le sud","t":"south"},{"w":"en hiver.","t":"in winter"}]}

items.fr: Mon chien a besoin de sortir tous les jours.
items.en: My dog needs to go out every day.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Mon chien","t":"my dog"},{"w":"a besoin de","t":"needs to"},{"w":"sortir","t":"go out"},{"w":"tous les jours.","t":"every day"}]}

items.fr: Le fermier vient de nourrir les poules.
items.en: The farmer just fed the chickens.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le fermier","t":"the farmer"},{"w":"vient de nourrir","t":"just fed"},{"w":"les poules.","t":"the chickens"}]}

items.fr: On voit la mer depuis cette colline.
items.en: You can see the sea from this hill.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"On voit","t":"you can see"},{"w":"la mer","t":"the sea"},{"w":"depuis cette colline.","t":"from this hill"}]}

items.fr: Le sentier traverse une forêt de pins.
items.en: The trail goes through a pine forest.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le sentier","t":"the trail"},{"w":"traverse","t":"goes through"},{"w":"une forêt de pins.","t":"a pine forest"}]}

items.fr: Il vaut mieux partir tôt si on veut éviter la foule sur le sentier.
items.en: It's better to leave early if you want to avoid the crowds on the trail.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il vaut mieux","t":"it's better to"},{"w":"partir tôt","t":"leave early"},{"w":"si on veut éviter","t":"if you want to avoid"},{"w":"la foule","t":"the crowds"},{"w":"sur le sentier.","t":"on the trail"}]}

items.fr: Le lac est tellement calme qu'on dirait un miroir.
items.en: The lake is so calm it looks like a mirror.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le lac est","t":"the lake is"},{"w":"tellement calme","t":"so calm"},{"w":"qu'on dirait","t":"it looks like"},{"w":"un miroir.","t":"a mirror"}]}

items.fr: Les nuages s'accumulent derrière les collines depuis ce matin.
items.en: Clouds have been gathering behind the hills since this morning.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Les nuages s'accumulent","t":"clouds have been gathering"},{"w":"derrière les collines","t":"behind the hills"},{"w":"depuis ce matin.","t":"since this morning"}]}

items.fr: Il faut tenir compte de l'impact environnemental avant de construire cette usine.
items.en: We need to factor in the environmental impact before building this factory.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il faut tenir compte de","t":"we need to factor in"},{"w":"l'impact environnemental","t":"the environmental impact"},{"w":"avant de construire","t":"before building"},{"w":"cette usine.","t":"this factory"}]}

items.fr: De nombreuses associations luttent contre la déforestation en Amazonie.
items.en: Many organizations are fighting deforestation in the Amazon.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"De nombreuses associations","t":"many organizations"},{"w":"luttent contre","t":"are fighting"},{"w":"la déforestation","t":"deforestation"},{"w":"en Amazonie.","t":"in the Amazon"}]}

items.fr: Le gouvernement encourage les citoyens à trier leurs déchets.
items.en: The government is encouraging citizens to sort their waste.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le gouvernement","t":"the government"},{"w":"encourage","t":"is encouraging"},{"w":"les citoyens","t":"citizens"},{"w":"à trier leurs déchets.","t":"to sort their waste"}]}

items.fr: Cette rivière était autrefois polluée par les usines voisines.
items.en: This river used to be polluted by the nearby factories.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Cette rivière","t":"this river"},{"w":"était autrefois polluée","t":"used to be polluted"},{"w":"par les usines voisines.","t":"by the nearby factories"}]}

items.fr: Au fur et à mesure que la température grimpe, certaines espèces migrent vers le nord.
items.en: As the temperature keeps rising, certain species are migrating northward.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Au fur et à mesure que","t":"as"},{"w":"la température","t":"the temperature"},{"w":"grimpe,","t":"rises,"},{"w":"certaines espèces","t":"certain species"},{"w":"migrent","t":"migrate"},{"w":"vers le nord.","t":"northward"}]}

items.fr: Les élèves ont un nouveau cahier ce matin.
items.en: The students have a new notebook this morning.
items.ipa: le.z‿e.lɛv ɔ̃.t‿œ̃ nu.vo ka.je sə ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: “ont” (from avoir) sounds like “on”, but the plural subject requires “ont”.

items.fr: La maîtresse répète la leçon très lentement.
items.en: The teacher repeats the lesson very slowly.
items.ipa: la mɛ.tʁɛs ʁe.pɛt la lə.sɔ̃ tʁɛ lɑ̃t.mɑ̃
items.notes: “répète” needs an accent grave on the second e for the open sound.

items.fr: Son cartable est lourd et sa trousse est pleine.
items.en: His backpack is heavy and his pencil case is full.
items.ipa: sɔ̃ kaʁ.tabl ɛ luʁ e sa tʁus ɛ plɛn
items.notes: “trousse” is feminine, so the possessive is “sa”, not “son”.

items.fr: Elle a rangé cent feuilles blanches dans le tiroir.
items.en: She put a hundred blank sheets of paper away in the drawer.
items.ipa: ɛl a ʁɑ̃.ʒe sɑ̃ fœj blɑ̃ʃ dɑ̃ lə ti.ʁwaʁ
items.notes: The final t of “cent” stays silent here.

items.fr: Les enfants attendent leur professeur devant l'école.
items.en: The children are waiting for their teacher in front of the school.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ a.tɑ̃d lœʁ pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ də.vɑ̃ le.kɔl
items.notes: The s in “les” links to “enfants” with a z sound because of the liaison.

items.fr: L'institutrice explique l'exercice une deuxième fois.
items.en: The teacher explains the exercise a second time.
items.notes: “La institutrice” becomes “L'institutrice” because “la” elides before a vowel.

items.fr: Les élèves auraient préféré rester à la maison ce jour-là.
items.en: The students would have preferred to stay home that day.
items.ipa: le.z‿e.lɛv o.ʁɛ pʁe.fe.ʁe ʁɛs.te a la mɛ.zɔ̃ sə ʒuʁ.la
items.notes: “auraient” carries the conditional past ending -aient even though it sounds like “ai”.

items.fr: Il y a vingt élèves dans notre classe.
items.en: There are twenty students in our class.
items.ipa: il i a vɛ̃.t‿e.lɛv dɑ̃ nɔtʁ klas
items.notes: “vingt” keeps its silent g and t together when nothing follows it.

items.fr: Les cahiers rouges sont sur l'étagère du fond.
items.en: The red notebooks are on the back shelf.
items.ipa: le ka.je ʁuʒ sɔ̃ syʁ le.ta.ʒɛʁ dy fɔ̃
items.notes: “rouges” takes a plural s to agree with “cahiers”, though the sound doesn't change.

items.fr: Est-ce que la récréation commence bientôt ?
items.ipa: ɛs kə la ʁe.kʁe.a.sjɔ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃s bjɛ̃.to
items.notes: French requires a space before the question mark: “bientôt ?”.

items.fr: La nouvelle directrice a visité toutes les classes.
items.en: The new principal visited every classroom.
items.ipa: la nu.vɛl di.ʁɛk.tʁis a vi.zi.te tut le klas
items.notes: “nouvelle” takes the feminine form because “directrice” is a woman.

items.fr: Où est-ce que tu ranges tes affaires de sport ?
items.en: Where do you keep your sports gear?
items.ipa: u ɛs kə ty ʁɑ̃ʒ te.z‿a.fɛʁ də spɔʁ
items.notes: “où” with the accent means “where”, unlike “ou” meaning “or”.

items.fr: Chaque élève doit apporter son propre goûter.
items.en: Each student has to bring their own snack.
items.ipa: ʃak e.lɛv dwa a.pɔʁ.te sɔ̃ pʁɔpʁ gu.te
items.notes: “chaque” is always singular, so “élève” stays without a plural s.

items.fr: Tu finis toujours tes exercices avant la récré.
items.en: You always finish your exercises before recess.
items.ipa: ty fi.ni tu.ʒuʁ te.z‿ɛg.zɛʁ.sis a.vɑ̃ la ʁe.kʁe
items.notes: “finis” ends in a silent s for the tu form.

items.fr: Nous apprenons une nouvelle leçon chaque semaine.
items.en: We learn a new lesson every week.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.pʁə.nɔ̃ yn nu.vɛl lə.sɔ̃ ʃak sə.mɛn
items.notes: “apprenons” keeps a single p, unlike what its sound might suggest.

items.fr: Vous répondez très vite pendant le contrôle.
items.en: You answer very quickly during the test.
items.ipa: vu ʁe.pɔ̃.de tʁɛ vit pɑ̃.dɑ̃ lə kɔ̃.tʁol
items.notes: “répondez” takes an accent aigu on the first e, not a grave.

items.fr: Le professeur a expliqué la règle avant que nous ayons commencé.
items.en: The teacher explained the rule before we had started.
items.ipa: lə pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ a ɛks.pli.ke la ʁɛgl a.vɑ̃ kə nu.z‿ɛ.jɔ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃.se
items.notes: “ayons” is the subjunctive form required after “avant que”.

items.fr: Il faut que les résultats soient prêts avant la fin du mois.
items.en: The results need to be ready before the end of the month.
items.ipa: il fo kə le ʁe.zyl.ta swa pʁɛ a.vɑ̃ la fɛ̃ dy mwa
items.notes: “soient” is the subjunctive of être required after “il faut que”, not “sont”.

items.fr: Les mathématiques sont ma matière préférée cette année.
items.en: Math is my favorite subject this year.
items.ipa: le ma.te.ma.tik sɔ̃ ma ma.tjɛʁ pʁe.fe.ʁe sɛt a.ne
items.notes: “mathématiques” is always plural in French, so the verb agrees with “sont”.

items.fr: La chimie est une matière difficile mais passionnante.
items.en: Chemistry is a difficult but fascinating subject.
items.ipa: la ʃi.mi ɛ.t‿yn ma.tjɛʁ di.fi.sil mɛ pa.sjɔ.nɑ̃t
items.notes: “difficile” and “passionnante” must both agree with the feminine noun “matière”.

items.fr: Ces documents historiques appartiennent à ses archives personnelles.
items.en: These historical documents belong to her personal archives.
items.ipa: se dɔ.ky.mɑ̃ is.tɔ.ʁik a.paʁ.tjɛn a se.z‿aʁ.ʃiv pɛʁ.sɔ.nɛl
items.notes: “ces” (these) and “ses” (her) sound identical but are spelled differently.

items.fr: Les élèves ont eu un excellent professeur de philosophie.
items.en: The students had an excellent philosophy teacher.
items.ipa: le.z‿e.lɛv ɔ̃.t‿y œ̃.n‿ɛk.sɛ.lɑ̃ pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ də fi.lɔ.zɔ.fi
items.notes: The liaison between “ont” and “eu” adds a t sound: “ont eu”.

items.fr: Elle s'est inscrite en deuxième année de droit à la fac.
items.en: She enrolled in her second year of law school at university.

items.fr: Les invités sont arrivés en retard à la fête.
items.en: The guests arrived late to the party.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɛ̃.vi.te sɔ̃.t‿a.ʁi.ve ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ a la fɛt
items.notes: “arrivés” agrees in number with “invités” because the verb uses “être”.

items.fr: C'est une tradition à laquelle je tiens beaucoup.
items.en: It's a tradition I care about a lot.
items.ipa: sɛ.t‿yn tʁa.di.sjɔ̃ a la.kɛl ʒə tjɛ̃ bo.ku
items.notes: “à laquelle” agrees with the feminine “tradition” and reflects the phrase “tenir à”.

items.fr: Le musée où nous sommes allés hier expose des œuvres impressionnistes.
items.en: The museum we went to yesterday is showing Impressionist works.
items.ipa: lə my.ze u nu sɔm a.le jɛʁ ɛks.poz de.z‿œvʁ ɛ̃.pʁe.sjɔ.nist
items.notes: “allés” agrees with the plural subject because “aller” is conjugated with “être”.

items.fr: Cette exposition a attiré des milliers de visiteurs.
items.en: This exhibition attracted thousands of visitors.
items.ipa: sɛt ɛks.po.zi.sjɔ̃ a a.ti.ʁe de mi.lje də vi.zi.tœʁ
items.notes: “a” here is the verb “avoir”, not the preposition “à”, even though they sound identical.

items.fr: Les guides du musée connaissent parfaitement l'histoire de chaque tableau.
items.en: The museum guides know the history of every painting perfectly.
items.ipa: le gid dy my.ze kɔ.nɛs paʁ.fɛt.mɑ̃ lis.twaʁ də ʃak ta.blo
items.notes: “connaissent” keeps the double “s” and the “ai” from the infinitive “connaître”.

items.fr: Il aurait fallu réserver nos billets à l'avance pour éviter la queue.
items.en: We should have booked our tickets in advance to avoid the line.
items.ipa: il o.ʁɛ fa.ly ʁe.zɛʁ.ve no bi.jɛ a la.vɑ̃s puʁ e.vi.te la kø
items.notes: “fallu” is the invariable past participle of the impersonal verb “falloir”.

items.fr: Cet auteur a écrit plusieurs romans que les lycéens étudient encore.
items.en: This author wrote several novels that high schoolers still study.
items.ipa: sɛ.t‿o.tœʁ a e.kʁi ply.zjœʁ ʁo.mɑ̃ kə le li.se.ɛ̃ e.ty.dj ɑ̃.kɔʁ
items.notes: “écrit” stays unchanged because with “avoir” the past participle doesn't agree with a direct object placed after the verb.

items.fr: La poésie qu'elle a publiée l'année dernière a été très bien accueillie.
items.en: The poetry she published last year was very well received.
items.ipa: la po.e.zi kɛl a py.bli.e la.ne dɛʁ.njɛʁ a e.te tʁɛ bjɛ̃ a.kœ.ji
items.notes: “publiée” agrees with the feminine “poésie” because its direct object “que” comes before the verb.

items.fr: Les critiques ne sont pas toujours d'accord sur la valeur d'un roman.
items.en: Critics don't always agree on the value of a novel.
items.ipa: le kʁi.tik nə sɔ̃ pa tu.ʒuʁ da.kɔʁ syʁ la va.lœʁ dœ̃ ʁo.mɑ̃
items.notes: “de” elides to “d'” before the vowel sound in both “accord” and “un”.

items.fr: Quoiqu'il soit reconnu pour son style, cet écrivain reste peu lu du grand public.
items.en: Although he is recognized for his style, this writer remains little read by the general public.
items.ipa: kwa.kil swa ʁə.kɔ.ny puʁ sɔ̃ stil sɛ.t‿e.kʁi.vɛ̃ ʁɛst pø ly dy ɡʁɑ̃ py.blik
items.notes: “quoique” always triggers the subjunctive, hence “soit” instead of “est”.

items.fr: Cette coutume se transmet de génération en génération dans notre région.
items.en: This custom is passed down from generation to generation in our region.
items.ipa: sɛt ku.tym sə tʁɑ̃s.mɛ də ʒe.ne.ʁa.sjɔ̃ ɑ̃ ʒe.ne.ʁa.sjɔ̃ dɑ̃ nɔtʁ ʁe.ʒjɔ̃
items.notes: “coutume” is feminine, so it takes “cette”, not “ce”.

items.fr: Est-ce qu'on célèbre encore cette fête dans ta région ?
items.en: Is this celebration still observed in your region?
items.ipa: ɛs kɔ̃ se.lɛbʁ ɑ̃.kɔʁ sɛt fɛt dɑ̃ ta ʁe.ʒjɔ̃
items.notes: French requires a space before a question mark, so it's “région ?” not “région?”.

items.fr: On raconte cette légende aux enfants depuis des siècles.
items.en: This legend has been told to children for centuries.
items.ipa: ɔ̃ ʁa.kɔ̃t sɛt le.ʒɑ̃d o.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ də.pɥi de sjɛkl
items.notes: “aux” links to “enfants” with a “z” sound because it ends in an “x” before a vowel.

items.fr: Bien que cette fête soit ancienne, ses rituels continuent d'évoluer avec le temps.
items.en: Although this celebration is ancient, its rituals continue to evolve over time.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃ kə sɛt fɛt swa ɑ̃.sjɛn se ʁi.tɥɛl kɔ̃.ti.ny de.vɔ.lɥe a.vɛk lə tɑ̃
items.notes: “soit” is the subjunctive form of “être”, required after “bien que”.

items.fr: Le maire habite près de la mairie.
items.en: The mayor lives near city hall.
items.ipa: lə mɛʁ a.bit pʁɛ də la mɛ.ʁi
items.notes: “maire” sounds like “mère” and “mer”, but only “maire” fits here as mayor.
“votent” ends in a silent -ent because the “ils/elles” verb form drops the sound.

items.fr: Le gouvernement annonce de nouvelles lois.
items.en: The government is announcing new laws.
items.ipa: lə gu.vɛʁn.mɑ̃ a.nɔ̃s də nu.vɛl lwa
items.notes: “gouvernement” is often misspelled without its second e, before “ment”.

items.fr: Le prix du pain a augmenté.
items.en: The price of bread has gone up.
items.ipa: lə pʁi dy pɛ̃ a oɡ.mɑ̃.te
items.notes: “augmenté” ends in -é, not -er, because it follows “a” in the passé composé.
“banque” is feminine, so it takes “une”, not “un”.

items.fr: Les impôts sont élevés cette année.
items.notes: “impôts” needs a circumflex on the o, which is often forgotten.

items.fr: Le Premier ministre a promis de réduire le chômage.
items.en: The Prime Minister promised to reduce unemployment.
items.ipa: lə pʁə.mje mi.nistʁ a pʁɔ.mi də ʁe.dɥiʁ lə ʃo.maʒ
items.notes: “promis” is the irregular past participle of “promettre”, not “promettu”.

items.fr: Les électeurs se sont déplacés malgré la pluie.
items.en: Voters turned out despite the rain.
items.ipa: le.z‿e.lɛk.tœʁ sə sɔ̃ de.pla.se mal.ɡʁe la plɥi
items.notes: “déplacés” takes a final -s to agree with the plural subject “les électeurs” in this reflexive form.

items.fr: L'entreprise a licencié plusieurs employés à cause de la crise.
items.en: The company laid off several employees because of the crisis.
items.ipa: lɑ̃.tʁə.pʁiz a li.sɑ̃.sje ply.zjœʁ ɑ̃.plwa.je a koz də la kʁiz
items.notes: “La entreprise” elides to “L'entreprise” because “entreprise” begins with a vowel sound.

items.fr: Les inégalités entre riches et pauvres se creusent chaque année.
items.en: The gap between rich and poor widens every year.
items.ipa: le.z‿i.ne.ga.li.te ɑ̃tʁ ʁiʃ e povʁ sə kʁøz ʃak a.ne
items.notes: “Les inégalités” is linked with a liaison, pronounced “le-z-inégalités”, though nothing changes in spelling.

items.fr: On parle souvent des discriminations au travail.
items.en: People often talk about discrimination at work.
items.ipa: ɔ̃ paʁl su.vɑ̃ de dis.kʁi.mi.na.sjɔ̃ o tʁa.vaj
items.notes: “on” (people, we) sounds like “ont” (have), but the impersonal subject here requires “on”.

items.fr: L'avocate a défendu son client devant le tribunal.
items.en: The lawyer defended her client in court.
items.ipa: la.vɔ.kat a de.fɑ̃.dy sɔ̃ kli.jɑ̃ də.vɑ̃ lə tʁi.by.nal
items.notes: “avocate” needs the final -e because the lawyer described here is a woman.

items.fr: Les négociations entre les partis se sont enlisées faute de compromis.
items.en: Negotiations between the parties stalled for lack of compromise.
items.ipa: le ne.gɔ.sja.sjɔ̃ ɑ̃tʁ le paʁ.ti sə sɔ̃t‿ɑ̃.li.ze fot də kɔ̃.pʁɔ.mi
items.notes: “enlisées” ends in -ées to agree with the feminine plural subject “les négociations”.

items.fr: La croissance économique a ralenti au deuxième trimestre.
items.en: Economic growth slowed in the second quarter.
items.ipa: la kʁwa.sɑ̃s e.ko.no.mik a ʁa.lɑ̃.ti o dø.zjɛm tʁi.mɛstʁ
items.notes: “économique” needs an acute accent on the first e, which is often dropped.

items.fr: Les investisseurs craignent une nouvelle hausse des taux d'intérêt.
items.en: Investors fear another rise in interest rates.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɛ̃.vɛs.ti.sœʁ kʁɛɲ yn nu.vɛl os de to dɛ̃.te.ʁɛ
items.notes: “craignent” is the irregular present-tense form of “craindre”, not a regular “craindent”.

items.fr: Le vieillissement de la population pose de nouveaux défis pour les retraites.
items.en: The aging population poses new challenges for pensions.
items.ipa: lə vjɛ.ji.smɑ̃ də la pɔ.py.la.sjɔ̃ poz də nu.vo de.fi puʁ le ʁə.tʁɛt
items.notes: The double “ill” in “vieillissement” is pronounced like a “y” sound, not a hard “l”.

items.fr: Le juge a demandé : « Êtes-vous certain de vos déclarations ? »
items.en: The judge asked: “Are you sure about your statements?”
items.ipa: lə ʒyʒ a də.mɑ̃.de ɛt.vu sɛʁ.tɛ̃ də vo de.kla.ʁa.sjɔ̃
items.notes: French punctuation places a space before “:” and before “?”, unlike English.

items.fr: Il faut que le témoin dise toute la vérité.
items.en: The witness must tell the whole truth.
items.ipa: il fo kə lə te.mwɛ̃ diz tut la ve.ʁi.te
items.notes: “dise” is the subjunctive form required after “il faut que”, not the indicative “dit”.

items.fr: La biologie est ma matière préférée.
items.ipa: la bjɔ.lɔ.ʒi ɛ ma ma.tjɛʁ pʁe.fe.ʁe
items.notes: “préférée” takes an extra e to agree with the feminine noun “matière”.

items.fr: Les élèves étudient la chimie et la physique.
items.en: The students study chemistry and physics.
items.ipa: le.z‿e.lɛv e.ty.di la ʃi.mi e la fi.zik
items.notes: “Les” links to “élèves” with a hidden z sound that isn't written.

items.fr: Le professeur a expliqué la théorie de l'évolution en détail.
items.en: The teacher explained the theory of evolution in detail.
items.ipa: lə pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ a ɛk.spli.ke la te.ɔ.ʁi də le.vɔ.ly.sjɔ̃ ɑ̃ de.taj
items.notes: “expliqué” ends in é because it follows “a” in the passé composé.

items.fr: Les élèves ont posé plusieurs questions difficiles au professeur.
items.en: The students asked the teacher several difficult questions.
items.ipa: le.z‿e.lɛv ɔ̃ po.ze ply.zjœʁ kɛs.tjɔ̃ di.fi.sil o pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ
items.notes: “difficiles” takes a final s to agree with the plural noun “questions”.

items.fr: Le corps humain contient plus de deux cents os.
items.en: The human body contains more than two hundred bones.
items.ipa: lə kɔʁ y.mɛ̃ kɔ̃.tjɛ̃ ply də dø sɑ̃ o
items.notes: the letters “ps” in “corps” are completely silent.

items.fr: C'est en observant les roches que les géologues comprennent l'histoire de la Terre.
items.en: It's by studying rocks that geologists understand the Earth's history.
items.ipa: sɛ.t‿ɑ̃n‿ɔp.sɛʁ.vɑ̃ le ʁɔʃ kə le ʒe.ɔ.lɔɡ kɔ̃.pʁɛn lis.twaʁ də la tɛʁ
items.notes: “C'est” is easily confused with “s'est”, but only “c'est” fits this construction.

items.fr: L'astrophysique étudie l'origine et l'évolution de l'univers.
items.en: Astrophysics studies the origin and evolution of the universe.
items.ipa: las.tʁo.fi.zik e.ty.di lɔ.ʁi.ʒin e le.vɔ.ly.sjɔ̃ də ly.ni.vɛʁ
items.notes: “l'astrophysique” elides “la” before a word starting with a vowel sound.

items.fr: Il faut que l'hypothèse soit testée avant d'être validée.
items.en: The hypothesis needs to be tested before it can be confirmed.
items.ipa: il fo kə li.pɔ.tɛz swa tɛs.te a.vɑ̃ dɛtʁ va.li.de
items.notes: “soit” is the subjunctive form of être required after “il faut que”.

items.fr: L'expérience doit être reproductible pour être considérée comme scientifique.
items.en: An experiment must be reproducible to be considered scientific.
items.ipa: lɛk.spe.ʁjɑ̃s dwa ɛtʁ ʁə.pʁɔ.dyk.tibl puʁ ɛtʁ kɔ̃.si.de.ʁe kɔm sjɑ̃.ti.fik
items.notes: “être” needs a circumflex accent on the e; without it the word wouldn't exist.

items.fr: Comment peut-on distinguer une corrélation d'une relation de cause à effet ?
items.en: How can you tell a correlation apart from a cause-and-effect relationship?
items.ipa: kɔ.mɑ̃ pø.t‿ɔ̃ dis.tɛ̃.ɡe yn kɔ.ʁe.la.sjɔ̃ dyn ʁə.la.sjɔ̃ də koz a e.fɛ
items.notes: French requires a space before the question mark “?” at the end of a sentence.

items.fr: Marie Curie a reçu deux prix Nobel dans deux disciplines différentes.
items.en: Marie Curie received two Nobel Prizes in two different fields.
items.ipa: ma.ʁi kyʁi a ʁə.sy dø pʁi nɔ.bɛl dɑ̃ dø di.si.plin di.fe.ʁɑ̃t
items.notes: “reçu” needs a cedilla under the c to keep the soft s sound before u.

items.fr: La pénicilline a été découverte presque par hasard, en 1928.
items.en: Penicillin was discovered almost by accident, in 1928.
items.ipa: la pe.ni.si.lin a e.te de.ku.vɛʁt pʁɛsk paʁ a.zaʁ ɑ̃ diz.nœf sɑ̃ vɛ̃t‿ɥit
items.notes: “découverte” takes a final e to agree with the feminine subject “la pénicilline” in this passive construction.

items.fr: Longtemps, les chercheurs pensaient que cette théorie était indémontrable.
items.en: For a long time, researchers thought this theory was impossible to prove.
items.ipa: lɔ̃.tɑ̃ le ʃɛʁ.ʃœʁ pɑ̃.sɛ kə sɛt te.ɔ.ʁi e.tɛ ɛ̃.de.mɔ̃.tʁabl
items.notes: “pensaient” ends in the silent “-aient” of the imparfait, matching the plural subject “les chercheurs”.

items.fr: Elle a choisi de faire des études de médecine parce qu'elle veut aider les gens.

items.fr: Ce n'est qu'après coup que l'on a mesuré l'ampleur de cette découverte pour la médecine moderne.

“a” (from avoir) sounds like “à” but takes no accent here because it's the verb.

items.fr: Je suis très fatigué ce soir.
items.ipa: ʒə sɥi tʁɛ fa.ti.ge sə swaʁ
items.notes: “fatigué” needs the é accent to keep its final vowel sound, unlike the noun “fatigue”.
“heureuse” takes an e because “elle” is feminine, unlike the masculine “heureux”.

items.fr: Mes parents sont fiers de moi.
items.en: My parents are proud of me.
items.ipa: me pa.ʁɑ̃ sɔ̃ fjɛʁ də mwa
items.notes: “fiers” takes a silent s to agree with the plural “parents”.

items.fr: Il est content, mais il ne le montre pas.
items.en: He's happy, but he doesn't show it.
items.ipa: il ɛ kɔ̃.tɑ̃, mɛ il nə lə mɔ̃tʁ pa
items.notes: The final “t” in “content” stays silent when the word stands alone like this.

items.fr: Nous sommes énervés par ce bruit.
items.notes: There's a liaison between “sommes” and “énervés”, pronounced with a z sound.

items.fr: Elle n'ose pas lui parler tellement elle est gênée.
items.en: She doesn't dare talk to him, she's so embarrassed.
items.ipa: ɛl nɔz pa lɥi paʁ.le tɛl.mɑ̃ ɛl ɛ ʒɛ.ne
items.notes: “ne” becomes “n'” before the vowel that starts “ose”.

items.fr: Elle serait plus sereine si elle dormait davantage.
items.en: She'd be calmer if she slept more.
items.ipa: ɛl sə.ʁɛ ply sə.ʁɛn si ɛl dɔʁ.mɛ da.vɑ̃.taʒ
items.notes: The conditional “serait” pairs with the imperfect “dormait” in this si-clause, not another conditional.

items.fr: Elle a longtemps caché sa tristesse à ses proches.
items.en: She hid her sadness from her loved ones for a long time.
items.ipa: ɛl a lɔ̃.tɑ̃ ka.ʃe sa tʁis.tɛs a se pʁɔʃ
items.notes: “caché” ends in é because it's the past participle after “a” in the passé composé.

items.fr: Il tient toujours ses promesses, même quand c'est difficile.
items.en: He always keeps his promises, even when it's hard.
items.ipa: il tjɛ̃ tu.ʒuʁ se pʁɔ.mɛs, mɛm kɑ̃ sɛ di.fi.sil
items.notes: “promesses” doubles the s to keep the s sound rather than a z sound.

items.ipa: pø ty vʁɛ.mɑ̃ lɥi fɛʁ kɔ̃.fjɑ̃s
items.notes: French requires a space before the closing “?”, unlike English.

items.fr: Ses valeurs guident toutes ses décisions.
items.en: Her values guide all her decisions.
items.ipa: se va.lœʁ gid tut se de.si.zjɔ̃
items.notes: “Ses” (possessive) sounds like “ces” and “c'est”, but only “ses” fits before “valeurs”.

items.fr: La générosité qu'il montre envers autrui force le respect.
items.en: The generosity he shows toward others commands respect.
items.ipa: la ʒe.ne.ʁo.zi.te kil mɔ̃tʁ ɑ̃.vɛʁ o.tʁɥi fɔʁs lə ʁɛs.pɛ
items.notes: “générosité” carries two é accents that must not be dropped or swapped for è.

items.fr: Cette décision soulève un dilemme éthique majeur.
items.en: This decision raises a major ethical dilemma.
items.ipa: sɛt de.si.zjɔ̃ su.lɛv œ̃ di.lɛm e.tik ma.ʒœʁ
items.notes: “dilemme” is masculine, so it takes “un” and “majeur”, not “une” and “majeure”.

items.fr: Les chercheurs doivent respecter des règles déontologiques strictes.
items.en: Researchers must follow strict codes of professional ethics.
items.ipa: le ʃɛʁ.ʃœʁ dwav ʁɛs.pɛk.te de ʁɛgl de.ɔ̃.tɔ.lɔ.ʒik stʁikt
items.notes: “déontologiques” and “strictes” both take a final s to agree with the plural “règles”.

items.fr: Le philosophe dénonce l'hypocrisie de ceux qui prêchent la vertu sans jamais l'incarner.
items.en: The philosopher denounces the hypocrisy of those who preach virtue without ever embodying it.
items.ipa: lə fi.lɔ.zɔf de.nɔ̃s li.pɔ.kʁi.zi də sø ki pʁɛʃ la vɛʁ.ty sɑ̃ ʒa.mɛ lɛ̃.kaʁ.ne
items.notes: The h in “hypocrisie” is silent but still allows elision, giving “l'hypocrisie” rather than “la hypocrisie”.

items.fr: Les anciens Grecs s'interrogeaient déjà sur le sens de l'existence.
items.en: The ancient Greeks were already wondering about the meaning of existence.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.sjɛ̃ gʁɛk sɛ̃.tɛ.ʁɔ.ʒɛ dɛ.ʒa syʁ lə sɑ̃s də lɛg.zis.tɑ̃s
items.notes: There's an obligatory liaison between “les” and “anciens”, pronounced with a z sound.

items.fr: Nul n'aurait imaginé que cette théorie bouleverserait à ce point notre conception du réel.
items.en: No one would have imagined that this theory would upset our conception of reality to this extent.
items.ipa: nyl no.ʁɛ i.ma.ʒi.ne kə sɛt te.ɔ.ʁi bul.vɛʁ.sə.ʁɛ a sə pwɛ̃ nɔtʁ kɔ̃.sɛp.sjɔ̃ dy ʁe.ɛl
items.notes: “aurait imaginé” is the past conditional, built from “aurait” plus the invariable past participle “imaginé”.

items.fr: Mes voisins ont deux chats noirs.

items.notes: The final “t” in “dort” is silent.

items.notes: There is a liaison between “nos” and “enfants”, pronounced “no.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃”.

items.fr: L'oiseau de ma sœur chante tous les matins.
items.en: My sister's bird sings every morning.

items.notes: “le” elides to “l'” before the vowel in “oiseau”.

items.fr: Il faut sortir le chien avant le petit-déjeuner.
items.en: You have to walk the dog before breakfast.
items.ipa: il fo sɔʁ.tiʁ lə ʃjɛ̃ a.vɑ̃ lə pə.ti de.ʒœ.ne
items.notes: “Il faut” is followed directly by the infinitive, never by “que”.

items.fr: Mes chats mangent leurs croquettes le matin.
items.en: My cats eat their kibble in the morning.
items.ipa: me ʃa mɑ̃ʒ lœʁ kʁɔ.kɛt lə ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: “mangent” ends in a silent -ent because the subject “mes chats” is plural.

items.fr: Mon chaton adore courir après une balle.
items.en: My kitten loves chasing a ball.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ ʃa.tɔ̃ a.dɔʁ ku.ʁiʁ a.pʁɛ yn bal
items.notes: “chaton” is spelled with a single t, not a double one.

items.fr: Est-ce que ton chien aboie la nuit ?
items.en: Does your dog bark at night?
items.ipa: ɛs kə tɔ̃ ʃjɛ̃ a.bwa la nɥi
items.notes: A space is required before the question mark in French: “nuit ?”.

items.fr: Le chat de ma tante est noir et blanc.
items.en: My aunt's cat is black and white.
items.ipa: lə ʃa də ma tɑ̃t ɛ nwaʁ e blɑ̃
items.notes: “est” (from être) and “et” (and) sound alike, but only “est” fits here.

items.fr: Ma sœur a un chien très fidèle.
items.en: My sister has a very loyal dog.
items.ipa: ma sœʁ a œ̃ ʃjɛ̃ tʁɛ fi.dɛl
items.notes: “fidèle” takes a grave accent on the second e, not an acute one.

items.fr: Notre nouvelle chienne est arrivée du refuge hier matin.
items.en: Our new dog arrived from the shelter yesterday morning.
items.ipa: nɔtʁ nu.vɛl ʃjɛn ɛ.t‿a.ʁi.ve dy ʁə.fyʒ jɛʁ ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: “arrivée” takes an extra e to agree with the feminine subject “chienne” in this passé composé with être.

items.fr: Nos chiens sont très bruyants le matin.
items.en: Our dogs are very noisy in the morning.
items.ipa: no ʃjɛ̃ sɔ̃ tʁɛ bʁɥi.jɑ̃ lə ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: “bruyants” ends in s to match the plural “chiens”.

items.fr: Le chien aboie très fort dans le jardin le soir.
items.en: The dog barks very loudly in the garden in the evening.
items.ipa: lə ʃjɛ̃ a.bwa tʁɛ fɔʁ dɑ̃ lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃ lə swaʁ
items.notes: The final “e” of “aboie” is silent.

items.fr: Les animaux ont besoin d'eau fraîche chaque jour.
items.en: Animals need fresh water every day.
items.ipa: le.z‿a.ni.mo ɔ̃ bə.zwɛ̃ do fʁɛʃ ʃak ʒuʁ
items.notes: There is a liaison between “les” and “animaux”, pronounced “le.z‿a.ni.mo”.

items.fr: L'animal préféré de mon frère est un iguane.
items.en: My brother's favorite animal is an iguana.
items.ipa: la.ni.mal pʁe.fe.ʁe də mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ ɛ.t‿œ̃.n‿i.gɥan
items.notes: “le” elides to “l'” before the vowel in “animal”.

items.fr: Il ne faut jamais donner de chocolat à un chien.
items.en: You should never give chocolate to a dog.
items.ipa: il nə fo ʒa.mɛ dɔ.ne də ʃɔ.kɔ.la a œ̃ ʃjɛ̃
items.notes: After a negated “il faut”, the partitive becomes simply “de” instead of “du”.

items.fr: Mon voisin a adopté un chaton la semaine dernière.
items.en: My neighbor adopted a kitten last week.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ vwa.zɛ̃ a a.dɔp.te œ̃ ʃa.tɔ̃ la sə.mɛn dɛʁ.njɛʁ
items.notes: “adopté” ends in é because it follows “a” in the passé composé.

items.fr: Nous devons acheter des croquettes pour le chat.
items.en: We need to buy some kibble for the cat.
items.ipa: nu də.vɔ̃ aʃ.te de kʁɔ.kɛt puʁ lə ʃa
items.notes: “croquettes” is spelled with two t's, not one.
French requires a space before the question mark: “chien ?”.

items.fr: Mon chat et mon chien sont amis.
items.en: My cat and my dog are friends.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ ʃa e mɔ̃ ʃjɛ̃ sɔ̃ a.mi
items.notes: “et” (and) sounds identical to “est” but the two words are never interchangeable.

items.fr: Ma collègue préfère les chats aux chiens.
items.en: My colleague prefers cats to dogs.
items.ipa: ma kɔ.lɛg pʁe.fɛʁ le ʃa o ʃjɛ̃
items.notes: “préfère” has an acute accent on the first e and a grave accent on the second.

items.fr: La tortue de mon oncle est très lente.
items.en: My uncle's turtle is very slow.
items.ipa: la tɔʁ.ty də mɔ̃.n‿ɔ̃kl ɛ tʁɛ lɑ̃t
items.notes: “lente” takes a final e to agree with the feminine noun “tortue”.

items.fr: Les griffes de mon chat sont devenues trop longues.
items.en: My cat's claws have gotten too long.
items.ipa: le gʁif də mɔ̃ ʃa sɔ̃ də.və.ny tʁo lɔ̃g
items.notes: “devenues” agrees in number and gender with the plural feminine “griffes”.

items.fr: Le lapin mange une carotte dans son enclos.
items.en: The rabbit is eating a carrot in its pen.
items.ipa: lə la.pɛ̃ mɑ̃ʒ yn ka.ʁɔt dɑ̃ sɔ̃.n‿ɑ̃.klo
items.notes: The n in “lapin” nasalizes the vowel and is not pronounced as a separate consonant.

items.fr: Mon oncle a un chien et deux chats.
items.en: My uncle has a dog and two cats.
items.ipa: mɔ̃.n‿ɔ̃kl a œ̃ ʃjɛ̃ e dø ʃa
items.notes: There is a liaison between “mon” and “oncle”, pronounced “mɔ̃.n‿ɔ̃kl”.

items.fr: L'éleveur nous a montré tous les chiots.
items.en: The breeder showed us all the puppies.
items.ipa: le.lə.vœʁ nu.z‿a mɔ̃.tʁe tu le ʃjo
items.notes: “le” elides to “l'” before the vowel in “éleveur”.

items.fr: Ils viennent de rentrer du parc à chiens.
items.en: They just got back from the dog park.
items.ipa: il vjɛn də ʁɑ̃.tʁe dy paʁk a ʃjɛ̃
items.notes: “venir de” plus the infinitive expresses an action that just happened.

items.fr: Le chat gratte souvent la porte du salon.
items.en: The cat often scratches at the living room door.
items.ipa: lə ʃa gʁat su.vɑ̃ la pɔʁt dy sa.lɔ̃
items.notes: “gratte” has no extra ending because “le chat” is a third-person singular subject.

items.fr: Nous avons pris rendez-vous chez le vétérinaire pour la vaccination.
items.en: We made an appointment with the vet for the vaccination.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ pʁi ʁɑ̃.de.vu ʃe lə ve.te.ʁi.nɛʁ puʁ la vak.si.na.sjɔ̃
items.notes: “rendez-vous” keeps its hyphen and the z is not pronounced as a separate sound.

items.fr: Ton chat miaule toujours le soir, n'est-ce pas ?
items.en: Your cat always meows in the evening, doesn't it?
items.ipa: tɔ̃ ʃa mjol tu.ʒuʁ lə swaʁ nɛs pa
items.notes: A space is needed before the question mark after “n'est-ce pas ?”.

items.fr: Son chat et sa chienne s'entendent bien.
items.en: His cat and his dog get along well.
items.ipa: sɔ̃ ʃa e sa ʃjɛn sɑ̃.tɑ̃d bjɛ̃
items.notes: “son” and “sa” sound different but both mean “his/her”, chosen by the gender of the noun that follows.

items.en: Our favorite cat is called Minou.
items.notes: “préféré” has three accented e's, all acute.

items.fr: La chienne perdue de mes voisins est enfin rentrée à la maison.
items.en: My neighbors' lost dog has finally come back home.
items.ipa: la ʃjɛn pɛʁ.dy də me vwa.zɛ̃ ɛ.t‿ɑ̃.fɛ̃ ʁɑ̃.tʁe a la mɛ.zɔ̃
items.notes: “rentrée” takes an extra e to agree with the feminine subject “chienne” since the verb uses être.

items.fr: La chatte du voisin est montée directement sur le canapé.
items.en: The neighbor's cat climbed straight onto the sofa.
items.ipa: la ʃat dy vwa.zɛ̃ ɛ mɔ̃.te di.ʁɛk.tə.mɑ̃ syʁ lə ka.na.pe
items.notes: “montée” takes an extra e to agree with the feminine subject “chatte”.

items.fr: Notre nouvelle chatte est vraiment très calme.
items.en: Our new cat is really very calm.
items.ipa: nɔtʁ nu.vɛl ʃat ɛ vʁɛ.mɑ̃ tʁɛ kalm
items.notes: “nouvelle” takes the feminine form because “chatte” is feminine.

items.fr: Les deux chattes sont sorties par la fenêtre du salon.
items.en: The two cats went out through the living room window.
items.ipa: le dø ʃat sɔ̃ sɔʁ.ti paʁ la fə.nɛtʁ dy sa.lɔ̃
items.notes: “sorties” takes the -ies ending to agree with the plural feminine subject “chattes”.

items.fr: Nos deux chiennes sont devenues inséparables depuis l'adoption.
items.en: Our two dogs have become inseparable since the adoption.
items.ipa: no dø ʃjɛn sɔ̃ də.və.ny ɛ̃.se.pa.ʁabl də.pɥi la.dɔp.sjɔ̃
items.notes: “inséparables” takes a final s to agree with the plural “chiennes”.

items.fr: Ses deux hamsters dorment le jour et jouent la nuit.
items.en: His two hamsters sleep during the day and play at night.
items.ipa: se dø am.stɛʁ dɔʁm lə ʒuʁ e ʒu la nɥi
items.notes: “hamsters” takes an s because there are two of them.

items.fr: Le perroquet de mes grands-parents répète les mêmes mots toute la journée.
items.en: My grandparents' parrot repeats the same words all day long.
items.ipa: lə pɛ.ʁɔ.kɛ də me gʁɑ̃.pa.ʁɑ̃ ʁe.pɛt le mɛm mo tut la ʒuʁ.ne
items.notes: The final t in “perroquet” is silent.

items.fr: Notre chat blanc perd beaucoup de poils au printemps.
items.en: Our white cat sheds a lot of fur in the spring.
items.ipa: nɔtʁ ʃa blɑ̃ pɛʁ bo.ku də pwal o pʁɛ̃.tɑ̃
items.notes: The final d in “perd” is silent.

items.fr: Mon petit chien dort beaucoup pendant la journée.
items.en: My little dog sleeps a lot during the day.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ pə.ti ʃjɛ̃ dɔʁ bo.ku pɑ̃.dɑ̃ la ʒuʁ.ne
items.notes: The final t in “petit” is silent.

items.fr: Mes amis ont un chien et un chat très proches l'un de l'autre.
items.en: My friends have a dog and a cat that are very close to each other.
items.ipa: me.z‿a.mi ɔ̃.t‿œ̃ ʃjɛ̃ e œ̃ ʃa tʁɛ pʁɔʃ lœ̃ də lotʁ
items.notes: There is a liaison between “ont” and “un”, pronounced “ɔ̃.t‿œ̃”.

items.fr: Les autres chats du quartier viennent parfois manger chez nous.
items.en: The other cats in the neighborhood sometimes come eat at our place.
items.ipa: le.z‿otʁ ʃa dy kaʁ.tje vjɛn paʁ.fwa mɑ̃.ʒe ʃe nu
items.notes: There is a liaison between “les” and “autres”, pronounced “le.z‿otʁ”.

items.fr: L'animal de mon ami est un cochon d'Inde très craintif.
items.en: My friend's pet is a very timid guinea pig.
items.ipa: la.ni.mal də mɔ̃.n‿a.mi ɛ.t‿œ̃ kɔ.ʃɔ̃ dɛ̃d tʁɛ kʁɛ̃.tif
items.notes: “le” elides to “l'” before the vowel in “animal”.

items.fr: L'odeur de la litière dérange souvent les invités.
items.en: The smell of the litter box often bothers guests.
items.ipa: lɔ.dœʁ də la li.tjɛʁ de.ʁɑ̃ʒ su.vɑ̃ le.z‿ɛ̃.vi.te
items.notes: “la” elides to “l'” before the vowel in “odeur”.

items.fr: Il faut aller chez le vétérinaire avant midi pour le vaccin.
items.en: We need to go to the vet before noon for the vaccine.
items.ipa: il fo a.le ʃe lə ve.te.ʁi.nɛʁ a.vɑ̃ mi.di puʁ lə vak.sɛ̃
items.notes: “il faut” is followed directly by the infinitive “aller”, never by a conjugated verb.

items.fr: Je dois promener le chien avant d'aller au travail.
items.en: I have to walk the dog before going to work.
items.ipa: ʒə dwa pʁɔ.mə.ne lə ʃjɛ̃ a.vɑ̃ da.le o tʁa.vaj
items.notes: “avant de” is always followed by the infinitive, not a conjugated verb.

items.fr: Mes voisins ont gardé notre chat pendant les vacances.
items.en: My neighbors looked after our cat during the vacation.
items.ipa: me vwa.zɛ̃ ɔ̃ gaʁ.de nɔtʁ ʃa pɑ̃.dɑ̃ le va.kɑ̃s
items.notes: “gardé” ends in é because it follows “ont” in the passé composé.

items.fr: Avant son opération, le chaton mangeait très peu.
items.en: Before its surgery, the kitten was eating very little.
items.ipa: a.vɑ̃ sɔ̃.n‿ɔ.pe.ʁa.sjɔ̃ lə ʃa.tɔ̃ mɑ̃.ʒɛ tʁɛ pø
items.notes: “mangeait” keeps the e before -ait to preserve the soft sound of “manger”.

items.fr: Le chien porte un collier avec son nom dessus.
items.en: The dog wears a collar with its name on it.
items.ipa: lə ʃjɛ̃ pɔʁt œ̃ kɔ.lje a.vɛk sɔ̃ nɔ̃ də.sy
items.notes: “collier” takes two l's, not one.

items.fr: Nous avons installé une nouvelle niche dans le jardin pour l'hiver.
items.en: We set up a new doghouse in the garden for the winter.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ɛ̃s.ta.le yn nu.vɛl niʃ dɑ̃ lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃ puʁ li.vɛʁ
items.notes: “niche” is spelled with ch, not sh, to make the sh sound.

items.fr: Pourquoi ton chat griffe-t-il toujours le canapé ?
items.en: Why does your cat always scratch the sofa?
items.ipa: puʁ.kwa tɔ̃ ʃa gʁif til tu.ʒuʁ lə ka.na.pe
items.notes: The inverted t in “griffe-t-il” needs hyphens on both sides, and a space before the final question mark.

items.fr: Attention, ne laisse pas la porte ouverte !
items.en: Careful, don't leave the door open!
items.ipa: a.tɑ̃.sjɔ̃ nə lɛs pa la pɔʁt u.vɛʁt
items.notes: A space is required before the exclamation mark: “ouverte !”.

items.fr: Ces croquettes-là sont ses préférées depuis toujours.
items.en: That kibble has always been his favorite.
items.ipa: se kʁɔ.kɛt la sɔ̃ se pʁe.fe.ʁe də.pɥi tu.ʒuʁ
items.notes: “ces” (these) and “ses” (his/her) sound identical but are never interchangeable.

items.fr: Où est ton chat en ce moment ?
items.en: Where is your cat right now?
items.ipa: u ɛ tɔ̃ ʃa ɑ̃ sə mɔ.mɑ̃
items.notes: “où” (where) and “ou” (or) sound alike, but only “où” fits as a question word here.

items.fr: Mon frère espère trouver un chien très équilibré au refuge.
items.en: My brother hopes to find a very well-balanced dog at the shelter.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ ɛs.pɛʁ tʁu.ve œ̃ ʃjɛ̃ tʁɛ e.ki.li.bʁe o ʁə.fyʒ
items.notes: “espère” has a grave accent on the second e, not an acute one.

items.fr: La régularité des repas aide le chien à se sentir en sécurité.
items.en: A regular feeding schedule helps the dog feel secure.
items.ipa: la ʁe.gy.la.ʁi.te de ʁə.pa ɛd lə ʃjɛ̃ a sə sɑ̃.tiʁ ɑ̃ se.ky.ʁi.te
items.notes: “régularité” has acute accents on both e's near the start of the word.

items.en: Our cat is used to sleeping near the window.

items.en: My girlfriend is looking for a small dog for her apartment.

items.en: Our cat just gave birth in the garage.

items.fr: Le perroquet de mon oncle répète des mots amusants.
items.en: My uncle's parrot repeats funny words.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le perroquet de mon oncle","t":"my uncle's parrot"},{"w":"répète","t":"repeats"},{"w":"des mots amusants.","t":"funny words"}]}
