items.fr: Mon chat préfère les croquettes au poulet.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Mon chat","t":"my cat"},{"w":"préfère","t":"prefers"},{"w":"les croquettes au poulet.","t":"chicken-flavored kibble"}]}

items.fr: Où as-tu mis le marteau ou la pince ?
items.en: Where did you put the hammer or the pliers?
items.ipa: u a ty mi lə maʁ.to u la pɛ̃s
items.notes: “Où” takes a grave accent when it means “where”, unlike “ou” meaning “or”.

items.fr: La perceuse est neuve, mais le tournevis est cassé.
items.en: The drill is new, but the screwdriver is broken.
items.ipa: la pɛʁ.søz ɛ nœv mɛ lə tuʁ.nə.vi ɛ ka.se
items.notes: “neuve” agrees with the feminine “perceuse”, while a masculine noun would take “neuf”.

items.fr: Range le tournevis dans la boîte à outils.
items.en: Put the screwdriver back in the toolbox.
items.ipa: ʁɑ̃ʒ lə tuʁ.nə.vi dɑ̃ la bwat a u.ti
items.notes: The final “s” in “tournevis” is silent.

items.fr: Les outils sont rangés dans le garage.
items.en: The tools are put away in the garage.
items.ipa: le.z‿u.ti sɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.ʒe dɑ̃ lə ga.ʁaʒ
items.notes: There is a liaison between “les” and “outils”, pronounced “le-z-outils”.

items.fr: L'échelle est trop courte pour atteindre le toit.
items.en: The ladder is too short to reach the roof.
items.ipa: le.ʃɛl ɛ tʁo kuʁt puʁ a.tɛ̃dʁ lə twa
items.notes: “La” becomes “l'” before the vowel in “échelle”.

items.fr: Mon père a réparé le robinet de la salle de bains.
items.en: My dad fixed the bathroom faucet.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ pɛʁ a ʁe.pa.ʁe lə ʁɔ.bi.nɛ də la sal də bɛ̃
items.notes: “réparé” ends in é because it follows “a” in the passé composé.

items.fr: Tu as fini de monter l'étagère ?
items.en: Have you finished putting up the shelf?
items.ipa: ty a fi.ni də mɔ̃.te le.ta.ʒɛʁ
items.notes: French requires a space before the question mark, as in “étagère ?”.

items.fr: Les clous sont tombés par terre.
items.en: The nails fell on the floor.
items.ipa: le klu sɔ̃ tɔ̃.be paʁ tɛʁ
items.notes: “sont tombés” takes an s to agree with the plural “les clous”.

items.fr: Mes parents ont acheté une nouvelle perceuse.
items.en: My parents bought a new drill.
items.ipa: me pa.ʁɑ̃ ɔ̃ a.ʃə.te yn nu.vɛl pɛʁ.søz
items.notes: “ont” (from avoir) sounds like “on” but only “ont” fits with “mes parents”.

items.fr: Il faut appeler un électricien pour cette prise.
items.en: We need to call an electrician for this outlet.
items.ipa: il fo a.pə.le œ̃.n‿e.lɛk.tʁi.sjɛ̃ puʁ sɛt pʁiz
items.notes: “appeler” has only one “l” in the infinitive, unlike conjugated forms such as “appelle”.

items.fr: La fenêtre de la cuisine ne ferme plus bien.
items.en: The kitchen window doesn't close properly anymore.
items.ipa: la fə.nɛtʁ də la kɥi.zin nə fɛʁm ply bjɛ̃
items.notes: “fenêtre” takes a circumflex accent on the e.

items.fr: Il faut que tu ranges les outils avant ce soir.
items.en: You need to put the tools away before tonight.
items.ipa: il fo kə ty ʁɑ̃ʒ le.z‿u.ti a.vɑ̃ sə swaʁ
items.notes: After “il faut que”, the verb “ranger” goes into the subjunctive: “ranges”.

items.fr: Il se sert d'un tournevis pour ouvrir la boîte à vis.
items.en: He uses a screwdriver to open the screw box.
items.ipa: il sə sɛʁ dœ̃ tuʁ.nə.vi puʁ u.vʁiʁ la bwat a vis
items.notes: “se” (reflexive pronoun) sounds like “ce” but the reflexive verb needs “se sert”.

items.fr: Il y a des trous dans le mur après avoir retiré les étagères.
items.en: There are holes in the wall after taking down the shelves.
items.ipa: il.j‿a de tʁu dɑ̃ lə myʁ a.pʁɛ a.vwaʁ ʁə.ti.ʁe le.z‿e.ta.ʒɛʁ
items.notes: The final “s” in “trous” is silent.

items.fr: La nouvelle scie électrique coupe très bien le bois.
items.en: The new electric saw cuts wood really well.
items.ipa: la nu.vɛl si e.lɛk.tʁik kup tʁɛ bjɛ̃ lə bwa
items.notes: “nouvelle” et “électrique” both agree with the feminine noun “scie”.

items.fr: Nous avons besoin d'un escabeau pour peindre le plafond.
items.en: We need a stepladder to paint the ceiling.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ bə.zwɛ̃ dœ̃.n‿ɛs.ka.bo puʁ pɛ̃dʁ lə pla.fɔ̃
items.notes: There is a liaison between “nous” and “avons”, pronounced “nou-z-avons”.

items.fr: J'ai trouvé la fuite sous l'évier.
items.en: I found the leak under the sink.
items.ipa: ʒe tʁu.ve la fɥit su le.vje
items.notes: “je” becomes “j'” before the vowel in “ai”.

items.fr: Elle a peint le mur du salon en gris.
items.en: She painted the living room wall gray.
items.ipa: ɛl a pɛ̃ lə myʁ dy sa.lɔ̃ ɑ̃ gʁi
items.notes: The past participle “peint” stays masculine singular here because “mur” comes after the verb, not before.

items.fr: Ces vis-là ne sont pas les bonnes pour ses étagères.
items.en: Those screws aren't the right ones for her shelves.
items.ipa: se vi la nə sɔ̃ pa le bɔn puʁ se ze.ta.ʒɛʁ
items.notes: “Ces” (these/those) and “ses” (his/her) sound the same but are spelled differently.

items.fr: Range tes outils, s'il te plaît !
items.notes: French requires a space before the exclamation mark, as in “plaît !”.

items.fr: Il a posé une nouvelle étagère dans l'entrée.
items.en: He put up a new shelf in the entryway.
items.ipa: il a po.ze yn nu.vɛl e.ta.ʒɛʁ dɑ̃ lɑ̃.tʁe
items.notes: “étagère” takes an acute accent on the first e and a grave accent on the second.

items.fr: Toutes les vis doivent être bien serrées.
items.en: All the screws need to be tightened properly.
items.ipa: tut le vi dwav‿ɛtʁ bjɛ̃ se.ʁe
items.notes: “serrées” agrees in the feminine plural with “les vis”.

items.fr: Le peintre a renversé le seau de peinture sur le sol.
items.en: The painter knocked over the paint bucket onto the floor.
items.ipa: lə pɛ̃tʁ a ʁɑ̃.vɛʁ.se lə so də pɛ̃.tyʁ syʁ lə sɔl
items.notes: “seau” (bucket) is a homophone of “sceau” and “saut”.

items.fr: Avant de percer le mur, il faut vérifier qu'il n'y a pas de câble.
items.en: Before drilling into the wall, you need to check there's no cable.
items.ipa: a.vɑ̃ də pɛʁ.se lə myʁ il fo ve.ʁi.fje kil nja pa də kabl
items.notes: “avant de” is followed by an infinitive, so “percer” stays unconjugated.

items.fr: Mon frère a jeté les vieux clous rouillés.
items.en: My brother threw out the old rusty nails.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ a ʒə.te le vjø klu ʁu.je
items.notes: “jeté” has only one t, unlike “jette” in the present tense.

items.fr: Il porte des gants pour manipuler la scie.
items.en: He wears gloves to handle the saw.
items.ipa: il pɔʁt de gɑ̃ puʁ ma.ni.py.le la si
items.notes: The final “t” in “gants” is silent, as in most words ending in “-ant”.

items.fr: L'escabeau est trop bas pour peindre le plafond.
items.en: The stepladder is too low to paint the ceiling.
items.ipa: lɛs.ka.bo ɛ tʁo bɑ puʁ pɛ̃dʁ lə pla.fɔ̃
items.notes: “escabeau” is masculine, so it takes “trop bas”, not “trop basse”.

items.fr: Il ne sait pas quelle prise brancher en premier.
items.en: He doesn't know which outlet to plug in first.
items.ipa: il nə sɛ pa kɛl pʁiz bʁɑ̃.ʃe ɑ̃ pʁə.mje
items.notes: “quelle” (which) sounds like “qu'elle” (that she) but only “quelle” fits before a noun.

items.fr: Mes anciens outils sont encore utiles.
items.en: My old tools are still useful.
items.notes: There are two liaisons here: “mes-z-anciens” and “anciens-z-outils”.

items.fr: L'artisan viendra demain matin pour le devis.
items.en: The contractor will come tomorrow morning for the estimate.
items.ipa: laʁ.ti.zɑ̃ vjɛ̃.dʁa də.mɛ̃ ma.tɛ̃ puʁ lə də.vi
items.notes: “le” becomes “l'” before the vowel in “artisan”.

items.fr: Nous avons monté le meuble tout seuls ce week-end.
items.en: We put the furniture together by ourselves this weekend.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ mɔ̃.te lə mœbl tu sœl sə wik.ɛnd
items.notes: “monté” doesn't change with “nous” here because the auxiliary is “avoir”, not “être”.

items.fr: On jette les emballages de la nouvelle perceuse.
items.en: We're throwing away the packaging from the new drill.
items.ipa: ɔ̃ ʒɛt le.z‿ɑ̃.ba.laʒ də la nu.vɛl pɛʁ.søz
items.notes: “jette” doubles the “t” in the present tense, unlike the infinitive “jeter”.

items.fr: Elle a acheté de la peinture blanche pour le couloir.
items.en: She bought white paint for the hallway.
items.ipa: ɛl a a.ʃə.te də la pɛ̃.tyʁ blɑ̃ʃ puʁ lə ku.lwaʁ
items.notes: “blanche” agrees with the feminine noun “peinture”; the masculine form would be “blanc”.

items.fr: La perceuse est là où tu l'as laissée hier.
items.en: The drill is right where you left it yesterday.
items.ipa: la pɛʁ.søz ɛ la u ty la lɛ.se jɛʁ
items.notes: “où” with an accent means “where”, unlike “ou” meaning “or”.

items.fr: Le vendeur du magasin de bricolage nous a bien conseillés.
items.en: The hardware store clerk gave us good advice.
items.ipa: lə vɑ̃.dœʁ dy ma.ga.zɛ̃ də bʁi.kɔ.laʒ nu.z‿a bjɛ̃ kɔ̃.sɛ.je
items.notes: “conseillés” takes an acute accent on the final e.

items.fr: C'est le voisin qui nous a prêté l'échelle.
items.en: It's our neighbor who lent us the ladder.
items.ipa: sɛ lə vwa.zɛ̃ ki nu.z‿a pʁɛ.te le.ʃɛl
items.notes: The relative pronoun “qui” is used because it replaces the subject “le voisin”.

items.fr: Attention, la peinture est encore fraîche !
items.en: Careful, the paint is still wet!
items.notes: A space is required before the exclamation mark, as in “fraîche !”.

items.fr: Le tapis cache un trou dans le plancher.
items.en: The rug is hiding a hole in the floor.
items.ipa: lə ta.pi kaʃ œ̃ tʁu dɑ̃ lə plɑ̃.ʃe
items.notes: The final “s” in “tapis” is silent.

items.fr: Les nouvelles ampoules sont plus économiques.
items.en: The new light bulbs are more energy-efficient.
items.notes: “nouvelles” et “économiques” both take an s to agree with the plural “ampoules”.

items.fr: Un bon artisan sait toujours écouter ses clients.
items.en: A good contractor always knows how to listen to his clients.
items.ipa: œ̃.n‿bɔ.n‿aʁ.ti.zɑ̃ sɛ tu.ʒuʁ e.ku.te se kli.jɑ̃
items.notes: There is a liaison between “un” and “bon”, and between “bon” and “artisan”.

items.fr: Le plombier a dit qu'il reviendrait dès qu'il aurait la pièce détachée.
items.en: The plumber said he would come back as soon as he had the spare part.
items.ipa: lə plɔ̃.bje a di kil ʁə.vjɛ̃.dʁɛ dɛ kil o.ʁɛ la pjɛs de.ta.ʃe
items.notes: “reviendrait” is in the conditional because it depends on the future-in-the-past construction.

items.fr: Il faut que le mur sèche complètement avant qu'on finisse la deuxième couche.
items.en: The wall needs to dry completely before we finish the second coat.
items.ipa: il fo kə lə myʁ sɛʃ kɔ̃.plɛt.mɑ̃ a.vɑ̃ kɔ̃ fi.nis la dø.zjɛm kuʃ
items.notes: “finisse” is subjunctive because it follows “avant que”, unlike the indicative “finit”.

items.fr: Quand elle a vu que ça fuyait encore, elle a rappelé le même plombier.
items.en: When she saw that it was still leaking, she called the same plumber again.
items.ipa: kɑ̃.t‿ɛl a vy kə sa fɥi.jɛ ɑ̃.kɔʁ ɛl a ʁa.pə.le lə mɛm plɔ̃.bje
items.notes: “ça” and “sa” sound alike, but only “ça” (that) fits as the subject of “fuyait”.

items.fr: La nouvelle installation électrique que l'artisan a posée fonctionne parfaitement.
items.en: The new electrical setup the contractor installed works perfectly.
items.ipa: la nu.vɛl ɛ̃s.ta.la.sjɔ̃ e.lɛk.tʁik kə laʁ.ti.zɑ̃ a po.ze fɔ̃k.sjɔn paʁ.fɛt.mɑ̃
items.notes: “posée” agrees with the feminine “installation” because the direct object “que” comes before the verb.

items.fr: Toutes les étagères que nous avons montées tiennent bien au mur.
items.en: All the shelves we put up are holding well on the wall.
items.ipa: tut le.z‿e.ta.ʒɛʁ kə nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ mɔ̃.te tjɛn bjɛ̃ o myʁ
items.notes: “montées” agrees in the feminine plural with “étagères” because “que” precedes the verb.

items.fr: Mon oncle a rangé son tas de planches dans le fond du garage.
items.en: My uncle stacked his pile of planks at the back of the garage.
items.ipa: mɔ̃.n‿ɔ̃kl a ʁɑ̃.ʒe sɔ̃ ta də plɑ̃ʃ dɑ̃ lə fɔ̃ dy ga.ʁaʒ
items.notes: The final “s” in “tas” is silent, so it's pronounced just “ta”.

items.fr: Les anciens habitants avaient laissé des outils dans les combles.
items.en: The former occupants had left tools in the attic.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.sjɛ̃.z‿a.bi.tɑ̃ a.vɛ lɛ.se de.z‿u.ti dɑ̃ le kɔ̃bl
items.notes: There is a liaison between “anciens” and “habitants”, pronounced “anciens-z-habitants”.

items.fr: L'électricien nous a expliqué pourquoi le disjoncteur sautait souvent.
items.en: The electrician explained to us why the circuit breaker kept tripping.
items.ipa: le.lɛk.tʁi.sjɛ̃ nu.z‿a ɛk.spli.ke puʁ.kwa lə dis.ʒɔ̃k.tœʁ so.tɛ su.vɑ̃
items.notes: “le” becomes “l'” before the vowel in “électricien”.

items.fr: Si nous avions eu le bon tournevis, nous aurions fini plus vite.
items.en: If we had had the right screwdriver, we would have finished faster.
items.ipa: si nu.z‿a.vjɔ̃.z‿y lə bɔ̃ tuʁ.nə.vi nu.z‿o.ʁjɔ̃ fi.ni ply vit
items.notes: The past conditional “aurions fini” follows the pluperfect “si” clause, forming the third conditional.

items.fr: Le tuyau que mon père a percé par accident coûtera cher à remplacer.
items.en: The pipe my dad accidentally drilled through will be expensive to replace.
items.ipa: lə tɥi.jo kə mɔ̃ pɛʁ a pɛʁ.se paʁ ak.si.dɑ̃ ku.tə.ʁa ʃɛʁ a ʁɑ̃.pla.se
items.notes: “coûtera” keeps the circumflex accent from “coûter” even when conjugated.

items.fr: Elle ne savait pas si c'était son marteau ou celui de son frère.
items.en: She didn't know whether it was her hammer or her brother's.
items.ipa: ɛl nə sa.vɛ pa si se.tɛ sɔ̃ maʁ.to u sə.lɥi də sɔ̃ fʁɛʁ
items.notes: “si” (if/whether) is a homophone of “s'y” but only “si” fits before “c'était”.

items.fr: Nous préférons appeler un professionnel plutôt que de tout casser.
items.en: We would rather call a professional than break everything.
items.ipa: nu pʁe.fe.ʁɔ̃ a.pə.le œ̃ pʁɔ.fɛ.sjɔ.nɛl ply.to kə də tu ka.se
items.notes: “professionnel” doubles both the “s” and the “n”, a common spelling mistake.

items.fr: Sais-tu combien coûte une bonne perceuse sans fil ?
items.en: Do you know how much a good cordless drill costs?
items.ipa: sɛ ty kɔ̃.bjɛ̃ kut yn bɔn pɛʁ.søz sɑ̃ fil
items.notes: French requires a space before the question mark, as in “fil ?”.

items.fr: La vieille échelle en bois que mon grand-père utilisait est encore solide.
items.en: The old wooden ladder my grandfather used is still sturdy.
items.ipa: la vjɛj e.ʃɛl ɑ̃ bwa kə mɔ̃ gʁɑ̃.pɛʁ y.ti.li.zɛ ɛ.t‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ sɔ.lid
items.notes: “vieille” agrees with the feminine “échelle”; before a vowel a masculine noun would take “vieil”.

items.fr: C'est le voisin dont je t'ai parlé qui va nous aider à repeindre la façade.
items.en: It's the neighbor I told you about who's going to help us repaint the front of the house.

items.notes: “dont” replaces “de qui”, since the verb “parler” is followed by “de”.

items.fr: Le bricoleur du dimanche range toujours ses outils avant le repas.

items.fr: Ils ont installé une nouvelle étagère en moins d'une heure.

items.fr: Depuis qu'elle a suivi un cours de bricolage, elle répare tout elle-même.

items.fr: Plus on attend pour réparer la fuite, plus les dégâts seront importants.
items.en: The longer we wait to fix the leak, the worse the damage will be.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Plus on attend","t":"the longer we wait"},{"w":"pour réparer la fuite,","t":"to fix the leak,"},{"w":"plus les dégâts","t":"the worse the damage"},{"w":"seront importants.","t":"will be"}]}

items.fr: Mon père arrose son jardin chaque soir.
items.en: My father waters his garden every evening.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ pɛʁ a.ʁoz sɔ̃ ʒaʁ.dɛ̃ ʃak swaʁ
items.notes: “son” (his) and “sont” (are) sound identical, but only “son” fits before “jardin”.

items.en: Where did you put the pruning shears?
items.ipa: u a ty ʁɑ̃.ʒe lə se.ka.tœʁ
items.notes: “Où” needs its grave accent here to mean “where”, unlike “ou” meaning “or”.

items.fr: La pelle est cassée, il faut en acheter une nouvelle.
items.en: The shovel is broken, we need to buy a new one.
items.ipa: la pɛl ɛ ka.se, il fo ɑ̃.n‿a.ʃə.te yn nu.vɛl
items.notes: “nouvelle” takes the feminine ending because it stands in for “la pelle”.

items.fr: Les roses rouges sentent très bon dans le jardin.
items.en: The red roses smell very good in the garden.
items.ipa: le ʁoz ʁuʒ sɑ̃t tʁɛ bɔ̃ dɑ̃ lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃
items.notes: “rouges” ends in s to agree with the plural noun “roses”.

items.fr: Nous n'avons pas beaucoup de temps pour désherber.
items.en: We don't have much time to weed the garden.
items.ipa: nu na.vɔ̃ pa bo.ku də tɑ̃ puʁ de.zɛʁ.be
items.notes: the final “ps” in “temps” is silent.

items.fr: Les arbres du jardin ont besoin d'eau.
items.en: The trees in the garden need water.
items.ipa: le.z‿aʁbʁ dy ʒaʁ.dɛ̃ ɔ̃ bə.zwɛ̃ do
items.notes: liaison makes the s of “les” sound like a z before “arbres”.

items.fr: J'arrose mes plantes avant d'aller travailler.
items.en: I water my plants before going to work.
items.ipa: ʒa.ʁoz me plɑ̃t a.vɑ̃ da.le tʁa.va.je
items.notes: “je” becomes “j'” before the vowel in “arrose”.

items.fr: Il faut que nous arrosions les tomates avant midi.
items.en: We need to water the tomatoes before noon.
items.ipa: il fo kə nu.z‿a.ʁo.zjɔ̃ le to.mat a.vɑ̃ mi.di
items.notes: after “il faut que”, the verb takes the subjunctive form “arrosions”, not “arrosons”.

items.fr: Hier, j'ai taillé les rosiers du jardin.
items.en: Yesterday, I pruned the rose bushes in the garden.
items.ipa: jɛʁ, ʒe ta.je le ʁo.zje dy ʒaʁ.dɛ̃
items.notes: “taillé” ends in é because it follows “ai” in the passé composé.

items.fr: Mon grand-père appelle toujours son jardin son royaume.
items.en: My grandfather always calls his garden his kingdom.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ ɡʁɑ̃.pɛʁ a.pɛl tu.ʒuʁ sɔ̃ ʒaʁ.dɛ̃ sɔ̃ ʁwa.jom
items.notes: “appelle” is spelled with a double p and a double l, as in the verb “appeler”.

items.fr: Est-ce que tu as arrosé les plantes aujourd'hui ?
items.en: Did you water the plants today?
items.ipa: ɛs kə ty a a.ʁo.ze le plɑ̃t o.ʒuʁ.dɥi
items.notes: French requires a space before the question mark, as in “aujourd'hui ?”.

items.fr: Ces fleurs sont belles, mais ses feuilles jaunissent.
items.en: These flowers are beautiful, but its leaves are turning yellow.
items.ipa: se flœʁ sɔ̃ bɛl, mɛ se fœj ʒo.nis
items.notes: “ces” (these) and “ses” (his/her) sound the same, but only “ces” fits before “fleurs”.

items.fr: Le jardinier préfère planter les graines tôt le matin.
items.en: The gardener prefers to plant the seeds early in the morning.
items.ipa: lə ʒaʁ.di.nje pʁe.fɛʁ plɑ̃.te le ɡʁɛn to lə ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: “préfère” takes a grave accent on the second e because the next syllable is silent.

items.fr: La tondeuse est neuve, je l'ai achetée hier.
items.en: The lawnmower is new, I bought it yesterday.
items.ipa: la tɔ̃.døz ɛ nœv, ʒə lɛ aʃ.te jɛʁ
items.notes: “achetée” agrees in gender with “la tondeuse” through the preceding pronoun “l'”.

items.fr: Les petits pots de fleurs décorent la terrasse.
items.en: The small flower pots decorate the terrace.
items.ipa: le pə.ti po də flœʁ de.kɔʁ la tɛ.ʁas
items.notes: “petits” takes an s to agree with the plural noun “pots”.

items.fr: Nous plantons des haricots verts dans le potager.
items.en: We are planting green beans in the vegetable garden.
items.ipa: nu plɑ̃.tɔ̃ de a.ʁi.ko vɛʁ dɑ̃ lə pɔ.ta.ʒe
items.notes: the h in “haricots” is aspirate, so it stays silent with no liaison before it.

items.fr: Nous avons un grand jardin avec beaucoup d'arbres.
items.en: We have a big garden with lots of trees.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃.z‿œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ ʒaʁ.dɛ̃ a.vɛk bo.ku daʁbʁ
items.notes: liaison turns the s of “avons” into a z sound before “un”.

items.en: The watering can is full of fresh water.
items.notes: “le” becomes “l'” before the vowel in “arrosoir”.

items.fr: Si tu arroses les plantes ce soir, elles pousseront vite.
items.en: If you water the plants tonight, they will grow quickly.
items.ipa: si ty a.ʁoz le plɑ̃t sə swaʁ, ɛl pu.sə.ʁɔ̃ vit
items.notes: after “si” for a real condition, French uses the present tense “arroses”, not the future.

items.fr: Nous désherberons le jardin demain matin.
items.en: We will weed the garden tomorrow morning.
items.ipa: nu de.zɛʁ.bə.ʁɔ̃ lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃ də.mɛ̃ ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: the future of “désherber” keeps the full infinitive before adding “-ons”.

items.fr: Ma sœur ramasse les feuilles mortes avec un râteau.
items.en: My sister rakes up the dead leaves with a rake.
items.ipa: ma sœʁ ʁa.mas le fœj mɔʁt a.vɛk œ̃ ʁa.to
items.notes: “sœur” is spelled with the œ ligature, not with a separate o and e.

items.fr: Quelle belle récolte de tomates cette année !
items.en: What a beautiful tomato harvest this year!
items.ipa: kɛl bɛl ʁe.kɔlt də to.mat sɛt a.ne
items.notes: French requires a space before the exclamation mark, as in “année !”.

items.fr: Il a mis les graines à germer près de la fenêtre.
items.en: He put the seeds out to germinate near the window.
items.ipa: il a mi le ɡʁɛn a ʒɛʁ.me pʁɛ də la fə.nɛtʁ
items.notes: “a” (has) and “à” (to) sound the same, but this sentence needs the preposition “à”.

items.fr: Les élèves apprennent à jardiner à l'école primaire.
items.en: The students are learning to garden at primary school.
items.ipa: le.z‿e.lɛv a.pʁɛn a ʒaʁ.di.ne a le.kɔl pʁi.mɛʁ
items.notes: “élèves” needs both an acute accent and a grave accent, one on each e.

items.fr: La récolte a été excellente cette saison.
items.en: The harvest was excellent this season.
items.ipa: la ʁe.kɔlt a e.te ɛk.sɛ.lɑ̃t sɛt sɛ.zɔ̃
items.notes: “excellente” ends in e to agree with the feminine noun “récolte”.

items.fr: Les outils de jardinage sont rangés dans la remise.
items.en: The gardening tools are stored in the shed.
items.ipa: le.z‿u.ti də ʒaʁ.di.naʒ sɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.ʒe dɑ̃ la ʁə.miz
items.notes: “rangés” takes an s to agree with the plural masculine noun “outils”.

items.fr: Il ne faut pas arroser trop souvent les cactus.
items.en: You shouldn't water cactuses too often.
items.ipa: il nə fo pa a.ʁo.ze tʁo su.vɑ̃ le kak.tys
items.notes: the final p in “trop” is silent.

items.fr: Mes enfants adorent planter des fleurs au printemps.
items.en: My children love planting flowers in spring.
items.ipa: me.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ a.dɔʁ plɑ̃.te de flœʁ o pʁɛ̃.tɑ̃
items.notes: liaison links “mes” and “enfants” with a z sound.

items.fr: J'ai oublié d'arroser les plantes ce matin.
items.en: I forgot to water the plants this morning.
items.ipa: ʒe u.bli.je da.ʁo.ze le plɑ̃t sə ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: “de” becomes “d'” before the vowel in “arroser”.

items.fr: Bien que le jardin soit petit, il est très productif.
items.en: Although the garden is small, it is very productive.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃ kə lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃ swa pə.ti, il ɛ tʁɛ pʁɔ.dyk.tif
items.notes: “bien que” always requires the subjunctive, hence “soit” instead of “est”.

items.fr: L'année dernière, nous avons semé des carottes en mars.
items.en: Last year, we planted carrot seeds in March.
items.ipa: la.ne dɛʁ.njɛʁ, nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ sə.me de ka.ʁɔt ɑ̃ maʁs
items.notes: “semé” ends in é because it follows “avons” in the passé composé.

items.fr: Le jardinier utilise un sécateur pour tailler les haies.
items.en: The gardener uses pruning shears to trim the hedges.
items.ipa: lə ʒaʁ.di.nje y.ti.liz œ̃ se.ka.tœʁ puʁ ta.je le ɛ
items.notes: “sécateur” is spelled with a single c, not a double one.

items.fr: Combien de tomates as-tu récoltées cette semaine ?
items.en: How many tomatoes did you harvest this week?
items.ipa: kɔ̃.bjɛ̃ də to.mat a ty ʁe.kɔl.te sɛt sə.mɛn
items.notes: French keeps a space before the closing question mark, as in “semaine ?”.

items.fr: On a planté des tomates, et elles ont bien poussé.
items.en: We planted tomatoes, and they grew well.
items.ipa: ɔ̃.n‿a plɑ̃.te de to.mat, e ɛl ɔ̃ bjɛ̃ pu.se
items.notes: “on” (we) and “ont” (have) sound alike but play different roles here.

items.fr: Il faut arroser régulièrement les jeunes pousses.
items.en: You need to water the young shoots regularly.
items.ipa: il fo a.ʁo.ze ʁe.ɡy.ljɛʁ.mɑ̃ le ʒœn pus
items.notes: “régulièrement” combines an acute accent and a grave accent, easy to mix up.

items.fr: La terre est sèche, il faut l'arroser tout de suite.
items.en: The soil is dry, it needs watering right away.
items.ipa: la tɛʁ ɛ sɛʃ, il fo la.ʁo.ze tu də sɥit
items.notes: “sèche” takes the feminine ending to agree with “la terre”.

items.fr: Les fleurs fanées doivent être coupées.
items.en: The wilted flowers need to be cut.
items.ipa: le flœʁ fa.ne dwav ɛtʁ ku.pe
items.notes: both “fanées” and “coupées” end in -ées to agree with the feminine plural “fleurs”.

items.fr: Le tuyau d'arrosage est trop long pour le petit jardin.
items.en: The garden hose is too long for the small garden.
items.ipa: lə tɥi.jo da.ʁo.zaʒ ɛ tʁo lɔ̃ puʁ lə pə.ti ʒaʁ.dɛ̃
items.notes: the final g in “long” is silent.

items.fr: Les oiseaux mangent les graines que j'ai plantées.
items.en: The birds eat the seeds I planted.
items.ipa: le.z‿wa.zo mɑ̃ʒ le ɡʁɛn kə ʒe plɑ̃.te
items.notes: liaison links “les” to “oiseaux” with a z sound.

items.fr: L'arbre du jardin a perdu toutes ses feuilles.
items.en: The tree in the garden lost all its leaves.
items.ipa: laʁbʁ dy ʒaʁ.dɛ̃ a pɛʁ.dy tut se fœj
items.notes: “le” becomes “l'” before the vowel in “arbre”.

items.fr: Je voudrais que le jardin soit prêt avant l'été.
items.en: I would like the garden to be ready before summer.
items.ipa: ʒə vu.dʁɛ kə lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃ swa pʁɛ a.vɑ̃ le.te
items.notes: “je voudrais que” requires the subjunctive “soit”, not the indicative “est”.

items.fr: Demain, je tondrai la pelouse avant qu'il pleuve.
items.en: Tomorrow, I will mow the lawn before it rains.
items.ipa: də.mɛ̃, ʒə tɔ̃.dʁe la pə.luz a.vɑ̃ kil plœv
items.notes: the future of “tondre” is “tondrai”, built on the infinitive minus the final e.

items.fr: Nous avons acheté de l'engrais pour les rosiers.
items.en: We bought fertilizer for the rose bushes.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃.z‿aʃ.te də lɑ̃.ɡʁɛ puʁ le ʁo.zje
items.notes: “engrais” ends in “-ais”, not “-ez” or “-est”.

items.fr: Attention, ne marche pas sur les fraises !
items.en: Careful, don't step on the strawberries!
items.ipa: a.tɑ̃.sjɔ̃, nə maʁʃ pa syʁ le fʁɛz
items.notes: a comma follows “Attention” and a space precedes the exclamation mark.

items.fr: Le compost sent mauvais, mais c'est bon pour les plantes.
items.en: The compost smells bad, but it's good for the plants.
items.ipa: lə kɔ̃.pɔst sɑ̃ mo.vɛ, mɛ sɛ bɔ̃ puʁ le plɑ̃t
items.notes: “c'est” (it is) and “s'est” sound alike, but only “c'est” fits this meaning.

items.fr: La terrasse est très ensoleillée l'après-midi.
items.en: The terrace is very sunny in the afternoon.
items.ipa: la tɛ.ʁas ɛ tʁɛ ɑ̃.sɔ.lɛ.je la.pʁɛ mi.di
items.notes: “après” needs a grave accent on the e, part of its fixed spelling.

items.fr: Cette plante grimpante est parfaite pour le balcon.
items.en: This climbing plant is perfect for the balcony.
items.ipa: sɛt plɑ̃t ɡʁɛ̃.pɑ̃t ɛ paʁ.fɛt puʁ lə bal.kɔ̃
items.notes: “grimpante” ends in e to agree with the feminine noun “plante”.

items.fr: Toutes les tomates rouges sont mûres.
items.en: All the red tomatoes are ripe.
items.ipa: tut le to.mat ʁuʒ sɔ̃ myʁ
items.notes: “mûres” ends in s, agreeing with the plural feminine noun “tomates”.

items.fr: Le jardinier porte toujours des gants en cuir.
items.en: The gardener always wears leather gloves.
items.ipa: lə ʒaʁ.di.nje pɔʁt tu.ʒuʁ de ɡɑ̃ ɑ̃ kɥiʁ
items.notes: the final “ts” in “gants” is silent.

items.fr: Vous avez de très belles fleurs sur votre balcon.
items.en: You have very beautiful flowers on your balcony.
items.ipa: vu.z‿a.ve də tʁɛ bɛl flœʁ syʁ vɔtʁ bal.kɔ̃
items.notes: liaison links “vous” and “avez”, pronounced with a z sound.

items.fr: Elle a un joli jardin plein d'herbes aromatiques.
items.en: She has a lovely garden full of aromatic herbs.
items.ipa: ɛl a œ̃ ʒɔ.li ʒaʁ.dɛ̃ plɛ̃ dɛʁb a.ʁɔ.ma.tik
items.notes: “de” becomes “d'” before “herbes” because the h is silent (h muet).

items.fr: Après avoir arrosé les plantes, elle a fermé la serre.
items.en: After watering the plants, she closed the greenhouse.
items.ipa: a.pʁɛ.z‿a.vwaʁ a.ʁo.ze le plɑ̃t, ɛl a fɛʁ.me la sɛʁ
items.notes: “après” is followed by “avoir” plus the past participle, not the infinitive alone.

items.fr: Quand j'étais petit, je jardinais avec mon grand-père.
items.en: When I was little, I used to garden with my grandfather.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ ʒe.tɛ pə.ti, ʒə ʒaʁ.di.nɛ a.vɛk mɔ̃ ɡʁɑ̃.pɛʁ
items.notes: “jardinais” is in the imperfect tense, marked by the “-ais” ending.

items.fr: Le jardinier arrose ses plantations chaque matin.
items.en: The gardener waters his plantings every morning.
items.ipa: lə ʒaʁ.di.nje a.ʁoz se plɑ̃.ta.sjɔ̃ ʃak ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: “plantations” is written with “-tion” even though it's pronounced like “sion”.

items.fr: Voici les outils dont tu as besoin : une pelle, un râteau et un arrosoir.
items.en: Here are the tools you need: a shovel, a rake, and a watering can.
items.ipa: vwa.si le.z‿u.ti dɔ̃ ty a bə.zwɛ̃ yn pɛl, œ̃ ʁa.to e œ̃.n‿a.ʁo.zwaʁ
items.notes: a colon introduces the list, and French puts a space before the colon too.

items.fr: Sais-tu où j'ai rangé les graines de courgette ?
items.en: Do you know where I put the zucchini seeds?
items.ipa: sɛ ty u ʒe ʁɑ̃.ʒe le ɡʁɛn də kuʁ.ʒɛt
items.notes: “où” (where) needs its grave accent to differ from “ou” (or).

items.fr: Le jardin possède une jolie tonnelle décorée de lierre.
items.en: The garden has a pretty arbor decorated with ivy.
items.ipa: lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃ pɔ.sɛd yn ʒɔ.li tɔ.nɛl de.kɔ.ʁe də ljɛʁ
items.notes: “décorée” carries an acute accent on each of its first two e's.

items.fr: La haie verte borde tout le jardin.
items.en: The green hedge borders the whole garden.
items.ipa: la ɛ vɛʁt bɔʁd tu lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃
items.notes: “verte” ends in e to agree with the feminine noun “haie”.

items.fr: Les nouvelles graines doivent être semées au printemps.
items.en: The new seeds need to be planted in spring.
items.ipa: le nu.vɛl ɡʁɛn dwav ɛtʁ sə.me o pʁɛ̃.tɑ̃
items.notes: “semées” ends in -ées to agree with the feminine plural noun “graines”.

items.fr: Le jardin sent bon grâce aux nombreuses fleurs.
items.en: The garden smells good thanks to its many flowers.
items.ipa: lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃ sɑ̃ bɔ̃ ɡʁas o nɔ̃.bʁøz flœʁ
items.notes: the final t in “sent” is silent.

items.fr: J'arrose les tomates tous les matins.
items.en: I water the tomatoes every morning.

items.en: My father mows the lawn on Saturdays.

items.en: You need to water the plants in the evening.

items.fr: Ma voisine cultive des tomates et des courgettes.
items.en: My neighbor grows tomatoes and zucchini.

items.fr: Le chat dort sous le rosier.
items.en: The cat is sleeping under the rose bush.

items.fr: Nous avons acheté un nouveau râteau.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons acheté","t":"we bought"},{"w":"un nouveau râteau.","t":"a new rake"}]}

items.fr: Elle porte des gants pour désherber le jardin.
items.en: She wears gloves to weed the garden.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle porte","t":"she wears"},{"w":"des gants","t":"gloves"},{"w":"pour désherber","t":"to weed"},{"w":"le jardin.","t":"the garden"}]}

items.fr: Le soleil brille sur le potager.
items.en: The sun is shining on the vegetable garden.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le soleil","t":"the sun"},{"w":"brille","t":"is shining"},{"w":"sur le potager.","t":"on the vegetable garden"}]}

items.fr: Mon frère plante des carottes chaque printemps.
items.en: My brother plants carrots every spring.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Mon frère","t":"my brother"},{"w":"plante","t":"plants"},{"w":"des carottes","t":"carrots"},{"w":"chaque printemps.","t":"every spring"}]}

items.fr: Il y a beaucoup de fleurs dans ce jardin.
items.en: There are a lot of flowers in this garden.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il y a","t":"there are"},{"w":"beaucoup de fleurs","t":"a lot of flowers"},{"w":"dans ce jardin.","t":"in this garden"}]}

items.fr: Les tomates rouges sont prêtes à être cueillies.
items.en: The red tomatoes are ready to be picked.

items.en: Can you lend me your stepladder?

items.fr: Si les voisins étaient plus discrets, tout le monde dormirait mieux.

items.en: Everyone should make an effort to keep the building clean.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il faudrait que chacun fasse un effort","t":"everyone should make an effort"},{"w":"pour que l'immeuble","t":"so that the building"},{"w":"reste propre.","t":"stays clean"}]}

items.fr: Elle en a marre d'entendre la même dispute à travers le mur.
items.en: She's tired of hearing the same argument through the wall.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle en a marre","t":"she's tired"},{"w":"d'entendre","t":"of hearing"},{"w":"la même dispute","t":"the same argument"},{"w":"à travers le mur.","t":"through the wall"}]}

items.fr: Le voisin du dessus s'est enfin excusé après plusieurs plaintes.
items.en: The upstairs neighbor finally apologized after several complaints.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le voisin du dessus","t":"the upstairs neighbor"},{"w":"s'est enfin excusé","t":"finally apologized"},{"w":"après plusieurs plaintes.","t":"after several complaints"}]}

items.fr: Nous avons organisé une réunion pour discuter du partage des charges.
items.en: We organized a meeting to discuss splitting the shared expenses.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons organisé","t":"we organized"},{"w":"une réunion","t":"a meeting"},{"w":"pour discuter du partage","t":"to discuss splitting"},{"w":"des charges.","t":"the shared expenses"}]}

items.fr: Même si elle ne les connaît pas bien, elle salue toujours ses voisins.
items.en: Even though she doesn't know them well, she always greets her neighbors.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Même si","t":"even though"},{"w":"elle ne les connaît pas bien,","t":"she doesn't know them well,"},{"w":"elle salue toujours","t":"she always greets"},{"w":"ses voisins.","t":"her neighbors."}]}

items.fr: Le comité a décidé que la fête des voisins aurait lieu en juin.
items.en: The committee decided that the block party would take place in June.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le comité","t":"the committee"},{"w":"a décidé que","t":"decided that"},{"w":"la fête des voisins","t":"the block party"},{"w":"aurait lieu","t":"would take place"},{"w":"en juin.","t":"in June."}]}

items.fr: Il s'est rendu compte que sa musique dérangeait tout l'étage.
items.en: He realized that his music was disturbing the whole floor.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il s'est rendu compte","t":"he realized"},{"w":"que sa musique","t":"that his music"},{"w":"dérangeait","t":"was disturbing"},{"w":"tout l'étage.","t":"the whole floor"}]}

items.fr: Malgré les rappels du syndic, certains oublient encore de sortir les poubelles.
items.en: Despite the building manager's reminders, some people still forget to take out the trash.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Malgré les rappels du syndic,","t":"despite the building manager's reminders,"},{"w":"certains oublient encore de","t":"some people still forget to"},{"w":"sortir les poubelles.","t":"take out the trash."}]}

items.fr: C'est grâce à la vigilance des voisins que le cambriolage a été évité.
items.en: It's thanks to the neighbors' vigilance that the burglary was prevented.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"C'est grâce à","t":"it's thanks to"},{"w":"la vigilance des voisins","t":"the neighbors' vigilance"},{"w":"que le cambriolage","t":"that the burglary"},{"w":"a été évité.","t":"was prevented."}]}

items.fr: Une fois que les travaux seront terminés, l'ascenseur remarchera normalement.
items.en: Once the renovations are finished, the elevator will work normally again.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Une fois que","t":"once"},{"w":"les travaux seront terminés,","t":"the renovations are finished,"},{"w":"l'ascenseur remarchera","t":"the elevator will work again"},{"w":"normalement.","t":"normally"}]}

items.fr: Je paie mes factures chaque mois.
items.en: I pay my bills every month.
items.ipa: ʒə pɛ me fak.tyʁ ʃak mwa
items.notes: “paie” keeps the silent e even though it sounds like “pè”.

items.fr: J'ai vingt euros dans mon porte-monnaie.
items.en: I have twenty euros in my wallet.
items.notes: There is a liaison between “vingt” and “euros”: “vingt_euros”.
“fonctionne” takes a double n, not a single one.
“bloquée” ends in ée because it agrees with the feminine “carte”.

items.fr: Il me faut de la monnaie pour le bus.
items.en: I need change for the bus.
items.ipa: il mə fo də la mɔ.nɛ puʁ lə bys
items.notes: The impersonal construction is “il faut”, never “il fait”.

items.en: We're splitting the bill at the restaurant.
items.notes: “la addition” elides to “l'addition” before a vowel sound.

items.fr: Elle met de l'argent de côté chaque semaine.
items.en: She puts money aside every week.
items.ipa: ɛl mɛ də laʁ.ʒɑ̃ də ko.te ʃak sə.mɛn
items.notes: “côté” needs a circumflex accent on the o.

items.fr: Le loyer coûte cinq cents euros.
items.en: The rent costs five hundred euros.
items.notes: “cents” takes an s here because five hundred is an exact multiple.

items.fr: J'ai oublié mon code à la banque.
items.en: I forgot my PIN at the bank.
items.ipa: ʒe u.bli.je mɔ̃ kɔd a la bɑ̃k
items.notes: “à” needs a grave accent to distinguish it from “a” (avoir).

items.fr: J'ai retiré cinquante euros au distributeur.
items.en: I withdrew fifty euros from the ATM.
items.ipa: ʒe ʁə.ti.ʁe sɛ̃.kɑ̃t ø.ʁo o dis.tʁi.by.tœʁ
items.notes: “retiré” ends in é because it follows “ai” in the passé composé.

items.en: We're saving up for our vacation.
items.notes: There is a liaison between “nous” and “économisons”.

items.fr: Le salaire arrive le premier du mois.
items.en: The paycheck arrives on the first of the month.
items.ipa: lə sa.lɛʁ a.ʁiv lə pʁə.mje dy mwa
items.notes: “arrive” is written with a double r.
“espèces” needs a grave accent on the second e.

items.fr: Ma facture d'électricité est trop chère.
items.en: My electricity bill is too expensive.
items.ipa: ma fak.tyʁ de.lɛk.tʁi.si.te ɛ tʁo ʃɛʁ
items.notes: “chère” takes a final e to agree with the feminine “facture”.

items.fr: Le distributeur a avalé ma carte.
items.ipa: lə dis.tʁi.by.tœʁ a a.va.le ma kaʁt
items.notes: “avalé” ends in é because it follows “a” in the passé composé.

items.en: I need to withdraw some money.
items.notes: “de l'argent” elides because “argent” starts with a vowel.

items.fr: Le vendeur me rend la monnaie.
items.en: The seller gives me my change.
items.ipa: lə vɑ̃.dœʁ mə ʁɑ̃ la mɔ.nɛ
items.notes: The final s in “rends” is silent, but “il” takes no s at all: “il rend”.

items.fr: Les courses coûtent cher ce mois-ci.
items.ipa: le kuʁs kut ʃɛʁ sə mwa.si
items.notes: “coûtent” needs the plural ending ent to agree with “les courses”.

items.fr: J'ai un rendez-vous à la banque demain.
items.en: I have an appointment at the bank tomorrow.
items.ipa: ʒe œ̃ ʁɑ̃.de.vu a la bɑ̃k də.mɛ̃
items.notes: “rendez-vous” keeps its z even though it isn't pronounced.

items.fr: Elle paie son loyer en ligne.
items.ipa: ɛl pɛ sɔ̃ lwa.je ɑ̃ liɲ
items.notes: “son” agrees with “loyer”, a masculine noun, not with “elle”.

items.fr: Le prix a augmenté encore une fois.
items.ipa: lə pʁi a oɡ.mɑ̃.te ɑ̃.kɔʁ yn fwa
items.notes: “augmenté” ends in é because it follows “a” in the passé composé.

items.en: We don't have any cash left.
items.notes: The negation needs both “ne” and “plus” placed around the verb.

items.fr: Ils achètent une nouvelle voiture à crédit.
items.en: They're buying a new car on credit.
items.ipa: il.z‿a.ʃɛt yn nu.vɛl vwa.tyʁ a kʁe.di
items.notes: “achètent” takes a grave accent on the e before a silent ending.
The p in “compte” is silent.

items.fr: Le distributeur est fermé le dimanche.
items.en: The ATM is closed on Sundays.
items.ipa: lə dis.tʁi.by.tœʁ ɛ fɛʁ.me lə di.mɑ̃ʃ
items.notes: “fermé” agrees with the masculine “distributeur”, so it takes no extra e.

items.fr: J'ai reçu un relevé de compte ce matin.
items.en: I received a bank statement this morning.
items.ipa: ʒe ʁə.sy œ̃ ʁəl.ve də kɔ̃t sə ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: “reçu” needs a cedilla so the c keeps its soft s sound.

items.fr: Le banquier m'a expliqué les frais bancaires.
items.en: The banker explained the bank fees to me.
items.ipa: lə bɑ̃.kje ma ɛks.pli.ke le fʁɛ bɑ̃.kɛʁ
items.notes: “frais” already ends in s and stays the same in the plural.

items.fr: Nous devons faire un virement avant vendredi.
items.en: We need to make a transfer before Friday.
items.ipa: nu də.vɔ̃ fɛʁ œ̃ viʁ.mɑ̃ a.vɑ̃ vɑ̃.dʁə.di
items.notes: “devons” is the nous form of devoir, not “devont”.

items.fr: Sa carte a été refusée au supermarché.
items.en: Her card was declined at the supermarket.
items.ipa: sa kaʁt a e.te ʁə.fy.ze o sy.pɛʁ.maʁ.ʃe
items.notes: “refusée” agrees in gender with the feminine “carte”.

items.fr: Il faut prévoir un budget pour les courses.
items.en: You need to plan a budget for groceries.
items.ipa: il fo pʁe.vwaʁ œ̃ by.dʒɛ puʁ le kuʁs
items.notes: “prévoir” needs an accent on the first e.

items.fr: Le découvert coûte cher à la banque.
items.en: Being overdrawn is expensive at the bank.
items.ipa: lə de.ku.vɛʁ kut ʃɛʁ a la bɑ̃k
items.notes: “coûte” needs a circumflex accent on the u.

items.fr: Elle a demandé un prêt pour sa voiture.
items.en: She applied for a loan for her car.
items.ipa: ɛl a də.mɑ̃.de œ̃ pʁɛ puʁ sa vwa.tyʁ
items.notes: “prêt” needs a circumflex accent, unlike the homophone “pré”.

items.fr: Le montant du chèque était incorrect.
items.en: The amount on the check was wrong.
items.ipa: lə mɔ̃.tɑ̃ dy ʃɛk e.tɛ ɛ̃.kɔ.ʁɛkt
items.notes: “chèque” needs a grave accent on the e.
“abonnement” is spelled with a double n.

items.fr: Le taux d'intérêt a encore augmenté.
items.en: The interest rate went up again.
items.ipa: lə to dɛ̃.te.ʁɛ a ɑ̃.kɔʁ oɡ.mɑ̃.te
items.notes: “taux” ends in a silent x.

items.fr: Nous avons ouvert un compte d'épargne.
items.notes: There is a liaison between “nous” and “avons”, and between “avons” and “ouvert”.

items.fr: Le commerçant n'accepte pas les chèques.
items.ipa: lə kɔ.mɛʁ.sɑ̃ nak.sɛpt pa le ʃɛk
items.notes: “commerçant” needs a cedilla so the c stays soft before a.

items.fr: Il paie ses impôts en plusieurs fois.
items.en: He pays his taxes in several installments.
items.ipa: il pɛ se.z‿ɛ̃.po ɑ̃ ply.zjœʁ fwa
items.notes: “impôts” needs a circumflex accent on the o.

items.fr: Elle a économisé pour son voyage.
items.en: She saved up for her trip.
items.ipa: ɛl a e.kɔ.no.mi.ze puʁ sɔ̃ vwa.jaʒ
items.notes: “économisé” ends in é because it follows “a” in the passé composé.

items.fr: La banque m'a envoyé une nouvelle carte.
items.en: The bank sent me a new card.
items.ipa: la bɑ̃k ma ɑ̃.vwa.je yn nu.vɛl kaʁt
items.notes: “envoyé” doesn't agree with “carte” because the direct object comes after the verb.

items.fr: J'ai vérifié mon solde sur l'application.
items.en: I checked my balance on the app.
items.ipa: ʒe ve.ʁi.fje mɔ̃ sɔld syʁ la.pli.ka.sjɔ̃
items.notes: “l'application” elides because the noun starts with a vowel.

items.fr: Est-ce que tu as payé le loyer ce mois-ci ?
items.en: Did you pay the rent this month?
items.ipa: ɛs.kə ty a pe.je lə lwa.je sə mwa.si
items.notes: French requires a space before the question mark: “ci ?” not “ci?”.

items.fr: Nous partageons les frais du dîner.
items.en: We're splitting the cost of dinner.
items.ipa: nu paʁ.ta.ʒɔ̃ le fʁɛ dy di.ne
items.notes: “dîner” needs a circumflex accent on the i.

items.fr: Il a perdu son code secret.
items.ipa: il a pɛʁ.dy sɔ̃ kɔd sə.kʁɛ
items.notes: “perdu” agrees with “il”, so it stays masculine singular with no extra e.

items.fr: Le distributeur limite les retraits à deux cents euros.
items.en: The ATM limits withdrawals to two hundred euros.
items.ipa: lə dis.tʁi.by.tœʁ li.mit le ʁə.tʁɛ a dø sɑ̃.z‿ø.ʁo
items.notes: “retraits” keeps a silent final s and t in the plural.

items.fr: Bien que le salaire ait augmenté, les dépenses restent élevées.
items.en: Even though the salary went up, expenses remain high.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃ kə lə sa.lɛʁ ɛ oɡ.mɑ̃.te, le de.pɑ̃s ʁɛst e.le.ve
items.notes: “bien que” requires the subjunctive, so it's “ait” and not “a”.

items.fr: Elle a dû emprunter de l'argent parce que son compte était à découvert.
items.en: She had to borrow money because her account was overdrawn.
items.ipa: ɛl a dy ɑ̃.pʁœ̃.te də laʁ.ʒɑ̃ paʁs.kə sɔ̃ kɔ̃t e.tɛ a de.ku.vɛʁ
items.notes: “dû” keeps its circumflex accent to distinguish it from the article “du”.

items.fr: Quand la facture arrive, il faut la payer avant la date limite.
items.en: When the bill arrives, you have to pay it before the deadline.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ la fak.tyʁ a.ʁiv, il fo la pe.je a.vɑ̃ la dat li.mit
items.notes: The infinitive of “paie” is always spelled “payer”, with a y.

items.fr: Le conseiller bancaire nous a recommandé d'ouvrir un livret d'épargne.
items.en: The bank advisor recommended that we open a savings account.
items.ipa: lə kɔ̃.sɛ.je bɑ̃.kɛʁ nu.z‿a ʁə.kɔ.mɑ̃.de du.vʁiʁ œ̃ liv.ʁɛ de.paʁɲ
items.notes: “recommandé” ends in é because it follows “a” in the passé composé.

items.fr: Si tu dépenses moins, tu pourras économiser davantage.
items.en: If you spend less, you'll be able to save more.
items.ipa: si ty de.pɑ̃s mwɛ̃, ty puʁ.ʁa e.kɔ.no.mi.ze da.vɑ̃.taʒ
items.notes: After “si” in the present, the second verb goes in the future: “tu pourras”.

items.fr: Les sommes qu'ils ont retirées dépassaient leur budget mensuel.
items.en: The amounts they withdrew exceeded their monthly budget.
items.ipa: le sɔm kil.z‿ɔ̃ ʁə.ti.ʁe de.pa.sɛ lœʁ by.dʒɛ mɑ̃.sɥɛl
items.notes: “retirées” takes an extra s and e to agree with “sommes”, the preceding direct object.

items.fr: Puisque sa carte était bloquée, il a dû payer en espèces.
items.en: Since his card was blocked, he had to pay in cash.
items.ipa: pɥis.kə sa kaʁt e.tɛ blɔ.ke, il a dy pe.je ɑ̃.n‿ɛs.pɛs
items.notes: There's a liaison between “en” and “espèces”: “en_espèces”.

items.fr: Les frais bancaires qu'elle a payés étaient plus élevés que prévu.
items.en: The bank fees she paid were higher than expected.
items.ipa: le fʁɛ bɑ̃.kɛʁ kɛl a pe.je e.tɛ ply.z‿e.le.ve kə pʁe.vy
items.notes: “payés” agrees with the plural masculine “frais” that precedes the verb.

items.fr: Il vaut mieux comparer les taux avant de signer un prêt.
items.en: It's better to compare rates before signing a loan.
items.ipa: il vo mjø kɔ̃.pa.ʁe le to a.vɑ̃ də si.ɲe œ̃ pʁɛ
items.notes: “vaut” ends in a silent t that you would not expect from its sound.

items.fr: Le budget que nous avons établi ne couvre pas les imprévus.
items.en: The budget we set doesn't cover unexpected expenses.
items.ipa: lə by.dʒɛ kə nu.z‿a.vɔ̃.z‿e.ta.bli nə kuvʁ pa le.z‿ɛ̃.pʁe.vy
items.notes: “établi” stays masculine singular here because “budget”, the preceding direct object, is already masculine singular.

items.fr: Bien qu'elle économise chaque mois, elle n'a pas assez pour l'appartement.
items.en: Even though she saves every month, she doesn't have enough for the apartment.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃ kɛl e.kɔ.no.miz ʃak mwa, ɛl na pa a.se puʁ la.paʁ.tə.mɑ̃
items.notes: “bien qu'elle” elides “que” before the vowel of “elle”.

items.fr: Le virement qu'il a effectué n'est pas encore arrivé sur mon compte.
items.en: The transfer he made hasn't reached my account yet.
items.ipa: lə viʁ.mɑ̃ kil a e.fɛk.tɥe nɛ pa.z‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ a.ʁi.ve syʁ mɔ̃ kɔ̃t
items.notes: “effectué” takes two f's, not one.

items.fr: Comme les prix augmentent, nous devons revoir notre budget.
items.en: Since prices are rising, we need to revise our budget.
items.ipa: kɔm le pʁi oɡ.mɑ̃t, nu də.vɔ̃ ʁə.vwaʁ nɔtʁ by.dʒɛ
items.notes: “augmentent” takes ent to agree with the plural subject “les prix”.

items.fr: Le banquier a expliqué pourquoi le prélèvement avait échoué.
items.en: The banker explained why the direct debit had failed.
items.ipa: lə bɑ̃.kje a ɛks.pli.ke puʁ.kwa lə pʁe.lɛv.mɑ̃ a.vɛ e.ʃwe
items.notes: “échoué” ends in é, following the auxiliary “avait” in the plus-que-parfait.

items.fr: Après avoir vérifié son solde, elle a annulé la commande.
items.en: After checking her balance, she canceled the order.
items.ipa: a.pʁɛ.z‿a.vwaʁ ve.ʁi.fje sɔ̃ sɔld, ɛl a a.ny.le la kɔ.mɑ̃d
items.notes: “après avoir vérifié” requires the past infinitive, not “après vérifier”.

items.fr: J'ai besoin d'argent pour le bus.
items.en: I need money for the bus.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"J'ai besoin d'argent","t":"I need money"},{"w":"pour le bus.","t":"for the bus"}]}

items.fr: Le distributeur est au coin de la rue.
items.en: The ATM is on the street corner.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le distributeur","t":"the ATM"},{"w":"est","t":"is"},{"w":"au coin de la rue.","t":"on the street corner."}]}

items.en: I don't have any change left.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Je","t":"I"},{"w":"n'ai plus de","t":"don't have any more"},{"w":"monnaie.","t":"change"}]}
{"tiles":[{"w":"Elle paie toujours","t":"she always pays"},{"w":"par carte.","t":"by card."}]}

items.fr: Nous devons payer le loyer aujourd'hui.
items.en: We need to pay the rent today.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous devons payer","t":"we need to pay"},{"w":"le loyer","t":"the rent"},{"w":"aujourd'hui.","t":"today."}]}
{"tiles":[{"w":"Mon compte","t":"my account"},{"w":"est à découvert.","t":"is overdrawn."}]}

items.fr: Il y a une longue file au distributeur.
items.en: There's a long line at the ATM.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il y a","t":"there is"},{"w":"une longue file","t":"a long line"},{"w":"au distributeur.","t":"at the ATM"}]}

items.fr: Tu peux me prêter dix euros ?
items.en: Can you lend me ten euros?
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Tu peux","t":"can you"},{"w":"me prêter","t":"lend me"},{"w":"dix euros ?","t":"ten euros?"}]}

items.fr: La baguette coûte un euro dix.
items.en: The baguette costs one euro ten.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"La baguette","t":"the baguette"},{"w":"coûte","t":"costs"},{"w":"un euro dix.","t":"one euro ten."}]}

items.fr: Je garde toujours un peu d'argent liquide.
items.en: I always keep a bit of cash on hand.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Je garde toujours","t":"I always keep"},{"w":"un peu d'argent liquide.","t":"a bit of cash on hand."}]}

items.fr: Elle a mis cent euros de côté.
items.en: She put aside a hundred euros.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle a mis","t":"she put"},{"w":"cent euros","t":"a hundred euros"},{"w":"de côté.","t":"aside."}]}

items.fr: Nous partageons la facture en deux.
items.en: We're splitting the bill in two.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous partageons","t":"we're splitting"},{"w":"la facture","t":"the bill"},{"w":"en deux.","t":"in two."}]}

items.fr: Mon salaire tombe le trente du mois.
items.en: My paycheck comes on the thirtieth of the month.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Mon salaire tombe","t":"my paycheck comes"},{"w":"le trente du mois.","t":"on the thirtieth of the month."}]}

items.fr: Il paie ses achats sans contact.
items.en: He pays for his purchases contactless.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il paie ses achats","t":"he pays for his purchases"},{"w":"sans contact.","t":"contactless"}]}

items.fr: J'ai oublié ma carte à la maison.
items.en: I forgot my card at home.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"J'ai oublié","t":"I forgot"},{"w":"ma carte","t":"my card"},{"w":"à la maison.","t":"at home."}]}

items.fr: Le loyer est dû le premier.
items.en: The rent is due on the first.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le loyer","t":"the rent"},{"w":"est dû","t":"is due"},{"w":"le premier.","t":"on the first."}]}

items.fr: Nous économisons pour un nouveau canapé.
items.en: We're saving up for a new sofa.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous économisons","t":"we're saving up"},{"w":"pour un nouveau canapé.","t":"for a new sofa."}]}

items.fr: Elle vérifie son solde tous les matins.
items.en: She checks her balance every morning.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle vérifie","t":"she checks"},{"w":"son solde","t":"her balance"},{"w":"tous les matins.","t":"every morning."}]}

items.fr: J'ai rendez-vous avec mon banquier lundi.
items.en: I have an appointment with my banker on Monday.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"J'ai rendez-vous","t":"I have an appointment"},{"w":"avec mon banquier","t":"with my banker"},{"w":"lundi.","t":"on Monday."}]}

items.en: They pay the electricity bill every month.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Ils paient","t":"they pay"},{"w":"l'électricité","t":"the electricity bill"},{"w":"chaque mois.","t":"every month."}]}

items.fr: Je dois retirer de l'argent avant midi.
items.en: I need to withdraw money before noon.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Je dois retirer","t":"I need to withdraw"},{"w":"de l'argent","t":"money"},{"w":"avant midi.","t":"before noon."}]}

items.en: The waiter brings us the check.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le serveur","t":"the waiter"},{"w":"nous apporte","t":"brings us"},{"w":"l'addition.","t":"the check."}]}

items.fr: Nous avons dépensé tout notre budget.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons dépensé","t":"we spent"},{"w":"tout notre budget.","t":"our whole budget."}]}

items.fr: Elle range ses reçus dans un tiroir.
items.en: She keeps her receipts in a drawer.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle range","t":"she keeps"},{"w":"ses reçus","t":"her receipts"},{"w":"dans un tiroir.","t":"in a drawer."}]}

items.fr: Mon frère me doit vingt euros.
items.en: My brother owes me twenty euros.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Mon frère","t":"my brother"},{"w":"me doit","t":"owes me"},{"w":"vingt euros.","t":"twenty euros."}]}

items.fr: Il vaut mieux comparer les prix avant d'acheter.
items.en: It's better to compare prices before buying.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il vaut mieux","t":"it's better to"},{"w":"comparer les prix","t":"compare prices"},{"w":"avant d'acheter.","t":"before buying"}]}

items.fr: Sa carte a été refusée à la caisse.
items.en: Her card was declined at the checkout.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Sa carte","t":"her card"},{"w":"a été refusée","t":"was declined"},{"w":"à la caisse.","t":"at the checkout."}]}

items.fr: Nous venons de payer toutes nos factures.
items.en: We just paid all our bills.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous venons de payer","t":"we just paid"},{"w":"toutes nos factures.","t":"all our bills"}]}

items.fr: J'ai annulé mon abonnement à la salle de sport.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"J'ai annulé","t":"I canceled"},{"w":"mon abonnement","t":"my membership"},{"w":"à la salle de sport.","t":"at the gym."}]}

items.fr: Le banquier nous a proposé un meilleur taux.
items.en: The banker offered us a better rate.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le banquier","t":"the banker"},{"w":"nous a proposé","t":"offered us"},{"w":"un meilleur taux.","t":"a better rate."}]}

items.fr: De temps en temps, je vérifie mes dépenses.
items.en: From time to time, I check my spending.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"De temps en temps,","t":"from time to time,"},{"w":"je vérifie","t":"I check"},{"w":"mes dépenses.","t":"my spending"}]}

items.fr: Nous devons faire attention à notre budget.
items.en: We need to watch our budget.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous devons faire attention à","t":"we need to watch"},{"w":"notre budget.","t":"our budget"}]}

items.fr: Elle a du mal à finir le mois.
items.en: She struggles to make it to the end of the month.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle a du mal à","t":"she struggles to"},{"w":"finir le mois.","t":"make it to the end of the month"}]}

items.fr: Le distributeur ne délivre plus de billets.
items.en: The ATM no longer dispenses cash.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le distributeur","t":"the ATM"},{"w":"ne délivre plus de","t":"no longer dispenses"},{"w":"billets.","t":"cash."}]}

items.fr: Ils ont ouvert un compte joint récemment.
items.en: They recently opened a joint account.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Ils ont ouvert","t":"they opened"},{"w":"un compte joint","t":"a joint account"},{"w":"récemment.","t":"recently."}]}

items.fr: Je dois tenir compte de mes dettes.
items.en: I need to take my debts into account.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Je dois tenir compte de","t":"I need to take into account"},{"w":"mes dettes.","t":"my debts"}]}

items.fr: Le prélèvement automatique a échoué ce mois-ci.
items.en: The direct debit failed this month.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le prélèvement automatique","t":"the direct debit"},{"w":"a échoué","t":"failed"},{"w":"ce mois-ci.","t":"this month."}]}

items.fr: Nous payons le crédit de la voiture chaque mois.
items.en: We pay off the car loan every month.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous payons","t":"we pay off"},{"w":"le crédit de la voiture","t":"the car loan"},{"w":"chaque mois.","t":"every month."}]}

items.fr: Elle a demandé un délai pour payer le loyer.
items.en: She asked for extra time to pay the rent.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle a demandé","t":"she asked for"},{"w":"un délai","t":"extra time"},{"w":"pour payer le loyer.","t":"to pay the rent."}]}

items.fr: Grâce à ses économies, il a pu acheter une moto.
items.en: Thanks to his savings, he was able to buy a motorcycle.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Grâce à ses économies,","t":"thanks to his savings,"},{"w":"il a pu acheter","t":"he was able to buy"},{"w":"une moto.","t":"a motorcycle"}]}

items.fr: Le virement met deux jours à arriver.
items.en: The transfer takes two days to arrive.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le virement met","t":"the transfer takes"},{"w":"deux jours","t":"two days"},{"w":"à arriver.","t":"to arrive."}]}

items.fr: Nous avons dépassé notre budget ce mois-ci.
items.en: We went over our budget this month.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons dépassé","t":"we went over"},{"w":"notre budget","t":"our budget"},{"w":"ce mois-ci.","t":"this month."}]}

items.fr: Le commerçant préfère les paiements en espèces.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le commerçant préfère","t":"the shopkeeper prefers"},{"w":"les paiements en espèces.","t":"cash payments."}]}
{"tiles":[{"w":"J'ai reçu","t":"I got"},{"w":"un remboursement inattendu.","t":"an unexpected refund."}]}

items.fr: Ils négocient le prix du loyer avec le propriétaire.
items.en: They're negotiating the rent price with the landlord.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Ils négocient","t":"they're negotiating"},{"w":"le prix du loyer","t":"the rent price"},{"w":"avec le propriétaire.","t":"with the landlord."}]}

items.fr: Bien que le loyer soit élevé, ils arrivent à économiser un peu.
items.en: Even though the rent is high, they manage to save a little.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Bien que","t":"even though"},{"w":"le loyer soit élevé,","t":"the rent is high,"},{"w":"ils arrivent à","t":"they manage to"},{"w":"économiser un peu.","t":"save a little."}]}

items.fr: Si elle dépensait moins au restaurant, elle aurait plus d'économies.
items.en: If she spent less at restaurants, she'd have more savings.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Si elle dépensait moins","t":"if she spent less"},{"w":"au restaurant,","t":"at restaurants,"},{"w":"elle aurait","t":"she'd have"},{"w":"plus d'économies.","t":"more savings."}]}

items.fr: Le conseiller nous a expliqué comment réduire nos frais bancaires.
items.en: The advisor explained to us how to reduce our bank fees.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le conseiller","t":"the advisor"},{"w":"nous a expliqué","t":"explained to us"},{"w":"comment réduire","t":"how to reduce"},{"w":"nos frais bancaires.","t":"our bank fees."}]}

items.fr: Quand la facture est trop élevée, nous appelons le fournisseur.
items.en: When the bill is too high, we call the provider.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Quand la facture est trop élevée,","t":"when the bill is too high,"},{"w":"nous appelons","t":"we call"},{"w":"le fournisseur.","t":"the provider."}]}

items.fr: Il tient à jour un tableau pour suivre ses dépenses.
items.en: He keeps an updated spreadsheet to track his spending.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il tient à jour","t":"he keeps updated"},{"w":"un tableau","t":"a spreadsheet"},{"w":"pour suivre ses dépenses.","t":"to track his spending"}]}

items.fr: Puisqu'il avait dépensé tout son salaire, il a dû emprunter à sa sœur.
items.en: Since he had spent his whole paycheck, he had to borrow from his sister.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Puisqu'il avait dépensé","t":"since he had spent"},{"w":"tout son salaire,","t":"his whole paycheck,"},{"w":"il a dû emprunter","t":"he had to borrow"},{"w":"à sa sœur.","t":"from his sister."}]}

items.fr: Avant de signer le prêt, il vaut mieux lire toutes les conditions.
items.en: Before signing the loan, it's better to read all the terms.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Avant de signer le prêt,","t":"before signing the loan,"},{"w":"il vaut mieux","t":"it's better to"},{"w":"lire toutes les conditions.","t":"read all the terms"}]}

items.fr: Le montant qu'elle a économisé lui permettra de partir en voyage.
items.en: The amount she saved will let her go on a trip.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le montant qu'elle a économisé","t":"the amount she saved"},{"w":"lui permettra de","t":"will let her"},{"w":"partir en voyage.","t":"go on a trip."}]}

items.fr: Comme les charges augmentent, nous devons revoir notre budget mensuel.
items.en: Since expenses are rising, we need to revise our monthly budget.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Comme les charges augmentent,","t":"since expenses are rising,"},{"w":"nous devons revoir","t":"we need to revise"},{"w":"notre budget mensuel.","t":"our monthly budget."}]}

items.fr: Elle a dû attendre trois jours avant que le virement arrive.
items.en: She had to wait three days before the transfer arrived.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle a dû attendre","t":"she had to wait"},{"w":"trois jours","t":"three days"},{"w":"avant que le virement arrive.","t":"before the transfer arrived."}]}

items.fr: Même si son salaire a augmenté, ses dépenses ont augmenté aussi.
items.en: Even though her salary went up, her expenses went up too.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Même si","t":"even though"},{"w":"son salaire a augmenté,","t":"her salary went up,"},{"w":"ses dépenses ont augmenté","t":"her expenses went up"},{"w":"aussi.","t":"too."}]}

items.fr: Il vaut mieux mettre de l'argent de côté chaque mois plutôt que d'attendre.
items.en: It's better to set money aside every month rather than wait.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il vaut mieux","t":"it's better to"},{"w":"mettre de l'argent de côté","t":"set money aside"},{"w":"chaque mois","t":"every month"},{"w":"plutôt que d'attendre.","t":"rather than wait"}]}

items.fr: Dès qu'elle reçoit son salaire, elle paie ses factures en premier.
items.en: As soon as she gets paid, she pays her bills first.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Dès qu'elle reçoit son salaire,","t":"as soon as she gets paid,"},{"w":"elle paie ses factures","t":"she pays her bills"},{"w":"en premier.","t":"first"}]}

items.fr: Le banquier lui a conseillé d'ouvrir un livret pour les urgences.
items.en: The banker advised her to open a savings account for emergencies.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le banquier","t":"the banker"},{"w":"lui a conseillé d'ouvrir","t":"advised her to open"},{"w":"un livret","t":"a savings account"},{"w":"pour les urgences.","t":"for emergencies."}]}

items.fr: Nous avons discuté du budget familial pendant tout le dîner.
items.en: We discussed the family budget throughout dinner.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons discuté du budget familial","t":"we discussed the family budget"},{"w":"pendant tout le dîner.","t":"throughout dinner"}]}
The final “l” in “gentil” is silent, unlike in the feminine “gentille”.

items.fr: Ma copine adore les fleurs rouges.
items.ipa: ma kɔ.pin a.dɔʁ le flœʁ ʁuʒ
items.notes: “rouges” takes a final s to agree with the plural “fleurs”.

items.fr: Mon mari est amoureux de moi.
items.en: My husband is in love with me.
items.notes: The final “x” in “amoureux” is silent.
“infirmière” takes the feminine ending -ère to agree with “ma femme”.
“sommes” is the “nous” form of être, not “sont”.

items.fr: Il a rencontré sa copine à la fac.
items.en: He met his girlfriend at university.
items.ipa: il a ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe sa kɔ.pin a la fak
items.notes: “a” (from avoir) and “à” (preposition) sound identical, but only “a” fits before “rencontré”.

items.en: They love each other a lot.
items.notes: “s'aiment” elides “se” to avoid the vowel clash with “aiment”.

items.fr: On sort ensemble depuis un mois.
items.en: We've been dating for a month.
items.ipa: ɔ̃ sɔʁ ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl də.pɥi œ̃ mwa
items.notes: “on” (the pronoun) sounds like “ont” (they have), but only “on” fits as the subject here.

items.fr: Mon petit ami habite près de chez moi.
items.en: My boyfriend lives close to my place.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ pə.ti.t‿a.mi a.bit pʁɛ də ʃe mwa
items.notes: “petit ami” has a liaison: the t of “petit” is pronounced before the vowel of “ami”.

items.fr: Nous avons un rendez-vous ce soir.
items.notes: “nous avons” has a liaison: the s of “nous” is pronounced like a z before “avons”.

items.fr: Mon amoureux m'a offert des fleurs.
items.notes: “m'a” elides “me” before the vowel of the auxiliary “a”.

items.fr: Elle porte une bague de fiançailles.
items.ipa: ɛl pɔʁt yn bag də fjɑ̃.sɑj
items.notes: The cedilla on the “ç” keeps the soft s sound in “fiançailles” before the vowel a.

items.fr: Ils vont se marier en septembre.
items.ipa: il vɔ̃ sə ma.ʁje ɑ̃ sɛp.tɑ̃bʁ
items.notes: “vont se marier” uses aller plus the infinitive to express the near future.

items.fr: Ma copine et moi, nous voyageons souvent.
items.en: My girlfriend and I travel often.
items.ipa: ma kɔ.pin e mwa, nu vwa.ja.ʒɔ̃ su.vɑ̃
items.notes: “voyageons” keeps the extra e after the g to preserve the soft sound before o.
“adorent” ends in a silent -ent to agree with the plural “mes parents”.

items.fr: Nous nous sommes rencontrés en ligne.
items.ipa: nu nu sɔm ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe ɑ̃ liɲ
items.notes: “rencontrés” takes a plural s because the reflexive pronoun “nous” is the direct object.

items.fr: Elle a une nouvelle petite amie.
items.ipa: ɛl a yn nu.vɛl pə.tit a.mi
items.notes: “nouvelle” and “petite” both take the feminine form to agree with “amie”.
The final “t” in “patient” is silent.

items.fr: Ils se sont disputés hier soir.
items.en: They had an argument last night.
items.ipa: il sə sɔ̃ dis.py.te jɛʁ swaʁ
items.notes: “disputés” agrees in the plural because “se” is the direct object of the reflexive verb.

items.fr: Ma copine n'aime pas les films tristes.
items.en: My girlfriend doesn't like sad movies.
items.ipa: ma kɔ.pin nɛm pa le film tʁist
items.notes: “n'aime” elides “ne” before the vowel of “aime”.

items.fr: Mon copain oublie souvent notre anniversaire.
items.en: My boyfriend often forgets our anniversary.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ kɔ.pɛ̃ u.bli su.vɑ̃ nɔtʁ a.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ
items.notes: “notre” (our) and “nôtre” (ours) differ only by a circumflex, but the unstressed form fits here.

items.fr: Elle écrit une lettre à son copain.
items.en: She's writing a letter to her boyfriend.
items.ipa: ɛl e.kʁi yn lɛtʁ a sɔ̃ kɔ.pɛ̃
items.notes: “écrit” needs the accent aigu on the first e.

items.fr: Nous habitons ensemble depuis deux ans.
items.en: We've been living together for two years.
items.notes: “nous habitons” has a liaison, the s of “nous” sounds like z before the vowel.

items.fr: Mon mari me fait rire tous les jours.
items.en: My husband makes me laugh every day.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ ma.ʁi mə fɛ ʁiʁ tu le ʒuʁ
items.notes: “fait” keeps the irregular ai spelling from the verb faire.

items.fr: Est-ce que ton copain vient avec nous ?
items.en: Is your boyfriend coming with us?
items.ipa: ɛs kə tɔ̃ kɔ.pɛ̃ vjɛ̃.t‿a.vɛk nu
items.notes: French requires a space before the question mark: “nous ?” not “nous?”.

items.fr: Depuis notre rencontre, il m'appelle tous les soirs.
items.en: Since we met, he calls me every evening.
items.ipa: də.pɥi nɔtʁ ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃tʁ, il ma.pɛl tu le swaʁ
items.notes: The final s in “soirs” is silent, even though it marks the plural.

items.fr: Ma petite amie et moi avons emménagé ensemble.
items.en: My girlfriend and I moved in together.
items.ipa: ma pə.tit a.mi e mwa a.vɔ̃.z‿ɑ̃.me.na.ʒe ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl
items.notes: “avons” is required because “ma petite amie et moi” together mean “nous”.

items.fr: Il a demandé sa copine en mariage hier.
items.en: He proposed to his girlfriend yesterday.
items.ipa: il a də.mɑ̃.de sa kɔ.pin ɑ̃ ma.ʁjaʒ jɛʁ
items.notes: “a” (avoir) is easy to confuse with “à”, but the verb form is needed before “demandé”.

items.fr: Nous nous sommes fiancés le mois dernier.
items.ipa: nu nu sɔm fjɑ̃.se lə mwa dɛʁ.nje
items.notes: “fiancés” takes the plural s to agree with “nous”.

items.fr: Je pense qu'elle est la femme de ma vie.
items.en: I think she's the woman of my life.
items.ipa: ʒə pɑ̃s kɛl ɛ la fam də ma vi
items.notes: “qu'elle” elides “que” before the vowel of “elle”.

items.fr: Mon copain travaille loin, c'est une relation à distance.
items.en: My boyfriend works far away, it's a long-distance relationship.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ kɔ.pɛ̃ tʁa.vaj lwɛ̃, sɛ.t‿yn ʁə.la.sjɔ̃ a dis.tɑ̃s
items.notes: “à” needs its grave accent to distinguish it from “a” (has).

items.fr: Ils se sont réconciliés après leur dispute.
items.en: They made up after their argument.
items.ipa: il sə sɔ̃ ʁe.kɔ̃.si.lje a.pʁɛ lœʁ dis.pyt
items.notes: “réconciliés” carries two accents aigus, both from the infinitive “réconcilier”.

items.fr: Ma femme est plus âgée que moi de trois ans.
items.en: My wife is three years older than me.
items.ipa: ma fam ɛ ply.z‿ɑ.ʒe kə mwa də tʁwa.z‿ɑ̃
items.notes: “âgée” needs the circumflex on the a, inherited from “âge”.

items.fr: Mon mari et moi nous sommes séparés puis remis ensemble.
items.en: My husband and I separated and then got back together.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ ma.ʁi e mwa nu sɔm se.pa.ʁe pɥi ʁə.mi ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl
items.notes: “séparés” takes a plural s to agree with the reflexive subject “nous”.

items.fr: Elle a rompu avec son copain la semaine dernière.
items.en: She broke up with her boyfriend last week.
items.ipa: ɛl a ʁɔ̃.py a.vɛk sɔ̃ kɔ.pɛ̃ la sə.mɛn dɛʁ.njɛʁ
items.notes: “a” (verb avoir) here introduces the passé composé, unlike the preposition “à”.

items.fr: Nous vivons une belle histoire d'amour.
items.en: We're living a beautiful love story.
items.ipa: nu vi.vɔ̃ yn bɛl is.twaʁ da.muʁ
items.notes: “belle” takes the feminine form to agree with “histoire”.

items.fr: Mon petit ami est parti travailler à l'étranger.
items.en: My boyfriend left to work abroad.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ pə.ti.t‿a.mi ɛ paʁ.ti tʁa.va.je a le.tʁɑ̃.ʒe
items.notes: “à l'étranger” elides “le” to “l'” before the vowel of “étranger”.

items.fr: Ma copine et moi discutons de nos projets d'avenir.
items.en: My girlfriend and I talk about our future plans.
items.ipa: ma kɔ.pin e mwa dis.ky.tɔ̃ də no pʁɔ.ʒɛ da.vniʁ
items.notes: “discutons” has a single t, unlike the doubled consonant in “discussion”.

items.fr: Il lui a offert une bague en argent.
items.en: He gave her a silver ring.
items.ipa: il lɥi a ɔ.fɛʁ yn bag ɑ̃.n‿aʁ.ʒɑ̃
items.notes: “offert” has a double f, unlike the single f in “offrir”.

items.fr: Après leur rupture, ils ne se parlent plus.
items.en: After their breakup, they don't speak to each other anymore.
items.ipa: a.pʁɛ lœʁ ʁyp.tyʁ, il nə sə paʁl ply
items.notes: The negation “ne... plus” needs both parts in writing to mean “no longer”.

items.fr: Ma femme travaille de nuit, alors on se voit peu.
items.en: My wife works nights, so we don't see each other much.
items.ipa: ma fam tʁa.vaj də nɥi, a.lɔʁ ɔ̃ sə vwa pø
items.notes: The final s in “alors” is silent.

items.fr: Mon copain m'a écrit une lettre d'amour.
items.en: My boyfriend wrote me a love letter.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ kɔ.pɛ̃ ma e.kʁi yn lɛtʁ da.muʁ
items.notes: “m'a” elides “me” before the auxiliary “a”.

items.fr: Nous célébrons notre anniversaire de mariage ce week-end.
items.en: We're celebrating our wedding anniversary this weekend.
items.ipa: nu se.le.bʁɔ̃ nɔtʁ a.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ də ma.ʁjaʒ sə wik.ɛnd
items.notes: “célébrons” has two accents aigus, both required for the correct pronunciation.

items.fr: Ils se sont remis ensemble après six mois de séparation.
items.en: They got back together after six months apart.
items.ipa: il sə sɔ̃ ʁə.mi ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl a.pʁɛ si mwa də se.pa.ʁa.sjɔ̃
items.notes: “remis” stays the same in the masculine plural, it does not take an extra s.

items.fr: Quand vas-tu demander ta copine en mariage ?
items.en: When are you going to propose to your girlfriend?
items.ipa: kɑ̃ va ty də.mɑ̃.de ta kɔ.pin ɑ̃ ma.ʁjaʒ
items.notes: Inverted questions link “vas” and “tu” with a hyphen, and need a space before the final “?”.

items.fr: Je crois que nous sommes faits l'un pour l'autre.
items.en: I believe we are meant for each other.
items.ipa: ʒə kʁwa kə nu sɔm fɛ lœ̃ puʁ lotʁ
items.notes: Both “l'un” and “l'autre” elide “le” before a vowel.

items.fr: Mon copain, qui vit à Marseille, me manque énormément.
items.en: I really miss my boyfriend, who lives in Marseille.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ kɔ.pɛ̃, ki vi a maʁ.sɛj, mə mɑ̃k e.nɔʁ.me.mɑ̃
items.notes: “qui” introduces the relative clause and is the subject of “vit”.

items.fr: Si tu m'aimais vraiment, tu me le dirais.
items.en: If you really loved me, you would tell me.
items.ipa: si ty mɛ.mɛ vʁɛ.mɑ̃, ty mə lə di.ʁɛ
items.notes: The imperfect “aimais” after “si” pairs with the conditional “dirais”.

items.fr: Quand elle a rencontré son mari, elle savait déjà que c'était le bon.
items.en: When she met her husband, she already knew he was the one.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ ɛl a ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe sɔ̃ ma.ʁi, ɛl sa.vɛ de.ʒa kə se.tɛ lə bɔ̃
items.notes: “c'était” (it was) sounds like “s'était”, but only “c'était” fits before an adjective clause.

items.fr: Bien que nous soyons loin l'un de l'autre, notre amour reste fort.
items.en: Even though we're far from each other, our love stays strong.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃ kə nu swa.jɔ̃ lwɛ̃ lœ̃ də lotʁ, nɔtʁ a.muʁ ʁɛst fɔʁ
items.notes: “soyons” is the subjunctive of être, required after “bien que”.

items.fr: Ma femme et moi avons décidé de nous marier parce que nous nous aimons profondément.
items.en: My wife and I decided to get married because we love each other deeply.
items.ipa: ma fam e mwa a.vɔ̃ de.si.de də nu ma.ʁje paʁs kə nu nu.z‿ɛ.mɔ̃ pʁɔ.fɔ̃.de.mɑ̃
items.notes: “profondément” keeps the acute accent, unlike the base adjective “profond”.

items.fr: Il a fallu du temps pour que je lui pardonne son infidélité.
items.en: It took time for me to forgive his infidelity.
items.ipa: il a fa.ly dy tɑ̃ puʁ kə ʒə lɥi paʁ.dɔn sɔ̃.n‿ɛ̃.fi.de.li.te
items.notes: “pour que” triggers the subjunctive, here hidden in “pardonne”.

items.fr: Depuis que nous nous sommes réconciliés, tout va mieux entre nous.
items.en: Since we made up, everything's better between us.
items.ipa: də.pɥi kə nu nu sɔm ʁe.kɔ̃.si.lje, tu va mjø ɑ̃tʁ nu
items.notes: “réconciliés” agrees in the plural because “nous” is the reflexive direct object.

items.fr: Elle a fini par accepter la demande en mariage de son copain, même si elle avait des doutes.
items.en: She eventually accepted her boyfriend's marriage proposal, even though she had doubts.
items.ipa: ɛl a fi.ni paʁ ak.sɛp.te la də.mɑ̃d ɑ̃ ma.ʁjaʒ də sɔ̃ kɔ.pɛ̃, mɛm si ɛl a.vɛ de dut
items.notes: “a” (avoir) is easy to mix up with “à”, but “a fini” needs the unaccented verb form.

items.fr: Mon petit ami habite loin, ce qui rend notre relation difficile parfois.
items.en: My boyfriend lives far away, which makes our relationship hard sometimes.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ pə.ti.t‿a.mi a.bit lwɛ̃, sə ki ʁɑ̃ nɔtʁ ʁə.la.sjɔ̃ di.fi.sil paʁ.fwa
items.notes: “difficile” has no accent at all, unlike similar-sounding words with é or è.

items.fr: Nous avons rompu, puis nous nous sommes remis ensemble deux mois plus tard.
items.en: We broke up, then got back together two months later.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʁɔ̃.py, pɥi nu nu sɔm ʁə.mi ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl dø mwa ply taʁ
items.notes: “remis” already ends in s, so it stays the same in the masculine plural.

items.fr: Si elle n'avait pas déménagé, nous serions peut-être encore ensemble.
items.en: If she hadn't moved, we might still be together.
items.ipa: si ɛl na.vɛ pa de.me.na.ʒe, nu sə.ʁjɔ̃ pø.tɛtʁ ɑ̃.kɔʁ ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl
items.notes: “serions” is the conditional of être, matching the plus-que-parfait in the si-clause.

items.fr: Mon mari dit toujours qu'il m'aimera pour la vie.
items.en: My husband always says he'll love me for life.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ ma.ʁi di tu.ʒuʁ kil mɛ.mə.ʁa puʁ la vi
items.notes: “qu'il” elides “que” before the vowel sound of “il”.

items.fr: Quoiqu'ils se disputent souvent, ils restent très amoureux.
items.en: Even though they argue often, they remain very much in love.
items.ipa: kwa.kil sə dis.pyt su.vɑ̃, il ʁɛst tʁɛ.z‿a.mu.ʁø
items.notes: “quoique” is written as a single word here, unlike “quoi que” in other constructions.

items.fr: Est-ce que ta copine t'a pardonné, ou est-ce fini entre vous ?
items.en: Has your girlfriend forgiven you, or is it over between you?
items.ipa: ɛs kə ta kɔ.pin ta paʁ.dɔ.ne, u ɛs fi.ni ɑ̃tʁ vu
items.notes: The final question mark needs a preceding space, and “ou” (or) has no accent, unlike “où” (where).
