items.fr: On se retrouve devant le café à midi.
items.en: We're meeting in front of the café at noon.
items.ipa: ɔ̃ sə ʁə.tʁuv də.vɑ̃ lə ka.fe a mi.di
items.notes: “On” (we) sounds exactly like “ont” (they have), but only “on” fits as the subject pronoun here.

items.fr: Elle a un très joli sourire.
items.ipa: ɛl a ɛ̃ tʁɛ ʒɔ.li su.ʁiʁ
items.notes: “très” needs a grave accent on the e, without it “tres” would not be a real French word.

items.fr: C'est une nouvelle collègue très gentille.
items.en: She's a new colleague who's very kind.
items.notes: “nouvelle” and “gentille” both take the feminine ending to agree with “collègue”.

items.fr: Les nouveaux étudiants sont très sympas.
items.en: The new students are really nice.
items.ipa: le nu.vo e.ty.djɑ̃ sɔ̃ tʁɛ sɛ̃.pa
items.notes: “nouveaux” takes an x, not an s, in the masculine plural to agree with “étudiants”.

items.fr: Il est grand et il porte des lunettes.
items.en: He's tall and he wears glasses.
items.ipa: i.l‿ɛ ɡʁɑ̃ e il pɔʁt de ly.nɛt
items.notes: the final “d” in “grand” is silent, but it still has to be written.

items.fr: Nous avons échangé nos adresses e-mail.
items.notes: “nos adresses” requires a liaison, the s of “nos” is pronounced as a z before the vowel.

items.fr: Je l'ai rencontré à une soirée entre amis.
items.en: I met him at a party with friends.
items.ipa: ʒə l‿ɛ ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe a yn swa.ʁe ɑ̃.tʁə.z‿a.mi
items.notes: “le” elides to “l'” before the vowel of “ai” (avoir).

items.fr: Je suis content de faire ta connaissance.
items.ipa: ʒə sɥi kɔ̃.tɑ̃ də fɛʁ ta kɔ.nɛ.sɑ̃s
items.notes: after “content de”, the verb stays in the infinitive: “faire”, not a conjugated form.

items.fr: Elle est venue me parler après le cours.
items.en: She came to talk to me after class.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ və.ny mə paʁ.le a.pʁɛ lə kuʁ
items.notes: “venue” takes a feminine e because “venir” uses être and agrees with the subject “elle”.

items.en: How do you spell your first name?
items.notes: “écris” comes from “écrire” and is spelled with a c, not like the word “cri”.
a space is required before the question mark in French: “exactement ?” not “exactement?”.

items.fr: Quel est ton nom de famille ?
items.notes: “quel” (masculine) sounds like “quelle” (feminine), but “nom” is masculine so “quel” is correct.

items.fr: On s'est déjà vus quelque part, non ?
items.ipa: ɔ̃ sɛ de.ʒa vy kɛl.kə paʁ nɔ̃
items.notes: “déjà” carries two different accents, an acute on the first e and a grave on the a.

items.fr: C'est un ami très gentil que j'ai rencontré hier.
items.en: He's a really kind friend I met yesterday.
items.ipa: sɛ.t‿ɛ.n‿a.mi tʁɛ ʒɑ̃.ti kə ʒe ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe jɛʁ
items.notes: “un” and “gentil” must match the masculine noun “ami”; for a woman it would be “une amie gentille”.

items.fr: Mes nouveaux voisins sont très accueillants.
items.en: My new neighbors are very welcoming.
items.notes: “accueillants” takes a final s to agree with the plural “voisins”.

items.fr: Il travaille dans le même immeuble que moi.
items.en: He works in the same building as me.
items.ipa: il tʁa.vaj dɑ̃ lə mɛm i.mœbl kə mwa
items.notes: the final “e” of “même” is silent but changes how the vowel before it sounds.

items.fr: Nous nous sommes rencontrés en octobre dernier.
items.en: We met each other last October.
items.notes: “en octobre” requires a liaison, pronounced with an n sound linking the two words.

items.fr: J'aimerais bien garder contact avec toi.
items.en: I'd love to stay in touch with you.
items.ipa: ʒɛm.ʁɛ bjɛ̃ ɡaʁ.de kɔ̃.takt a.vɛk twa
items.notes: “je” elides to “j'” before the vowel sound of “aimerais”.

items.fr: Je ne connais personne ici, c'est ma première fois.
items.en: I don't know anyone here, it's my first time.
items.ipa: ʒə nə kɔ.nɛ pɛʁ.sɔn i.si sɛ ma pʁə.mjɛʁ fwa
items.notes: “ne ... personne” is a negative structure, both parts are needed even though “personne” also means “a person”.

items.fr: Elle vient de déménager dans mon quartier.
items.en: She just moved into my neighborhood.
items.ipa: ɛl vjɛ̃ də de.me.na.ʒe dɑ̃ mɔ̃ kaʁ.tje
items.notes: “vient de” plus infinitive expresses a recent action, not just a form of “venir” alone.

items.fr: Il s'appelle Guillaume, avec deux L.
items.en: His name is Guillaume, with two L's.
items.ipa: il sa.pɛl gi.jom a.vɛk dø ɛl
items.notes: “Guillaume” keeps the silent u after the g, part of the spelling even though it isn't pronounced.

items.fr: Quel plaisir de te rencontrer enfin !
items.en: What a pleasure to finally meet you!
items.ipa: kɛl plɛ.ziʁ də tə ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe ɑ̃.fɛ̃
items.notes: French requires a space before the exclamation mark: “enfin !” not “enfin!”.

items.fr: Ces amis-là m'ont présenté à toute la bande.
items.en: Those friends introduced me to the whole group.
items.ipa: se.z‿a.mi la mɔ̃ pʁe.zɑ̃.te a tut la bɑ̃d
items.notes: “ces” (these/those) sounds like “ses” (his/her), but the demonstrative “ces” is required before “amis-là”.

items.fr: Où est-ce que tu as grandi ?
items.ipa: u ɛs kə ty a ɡʁɑ̃.di
items.notes: “où” (where) needs a grave accent to distinguish it from “ou” (or).

items.en: My new friend is from Spain.
items.notes: “nouvelle” agrees with the feminine “amie”; it would be “nouveau” before a man's name.

items.fr: Tous les invités se sont présentés poliment.
items.en: All the guests introduced themselves politely.
items.ipa: tu le.z‿ɛ̃.vi.te sə sɔ̃ pʁe.zɑ̃.te po.li.mɑ̃
items.notes: “présentés” takes a final s to agree with the plural subject “les invités”.

items.fr: Il tend la main pour dire bonjour.
items.en: He holds out his hand to say hello.
items.ipa: il tɑ̃ la mɛ̃ puʁ diʁ bɔ̃.ʒuʁ
items.notes: the final “d” in “tend” is silent but must not be dropped in writing.

items.fr: Ils habitent ensemble depuis un an.
items.en: They've been living together for a year.
items.notes: “ils habitent” requires a liaison since the h in “habitent” is silent.

items.fr: L'homme que j'ai croisé au marché m'a souri.
items.en: The man I ran into at the market smiled at me.
items.ipa: lɔm kə ʒe kʁwa.ze o maʁ.ʃe ma su.ʁi
items.notes: “le” becomes “l'” before “homme” because its h is silent.

items.fr: Il faut toujours sourire quand on rencontre quelqu'un.
items.en: You should always smile when you meet someone.
items.ipa: il fo tu.ʒuʁ su.ʁiʁ kɑ̃.t‿ɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃tʁ kɛl.kœ̃
items.notes: “il faut” is followed here by an infinitive, not a conjugated verb.

items.fr: Il dit toujours bonjour avec le sourire.
items.en: He always says hello with a smile.
items.ipa: il di tu.ʒuʁ bɔ̃.ʒuʁ a.vɛk lə su.ʁiʁ
items.notes: “dit” (from “dire”) is irregular and takes no s in the third-person singular present.

items.fr: Elle s'appelle Camille, comme la chanteuse.
items.en: Her name is Camille, like the singer.
items.ipa: ɛl sa.pɛl ka.mij kɔm la ʃɑ̃.tøz
items.notes: “s'appelle” is written with a double l, unlike the single l in “appeler”.
the question mark needs a space before it: “t'appelles ?”.

items.fr: Son numéro de téléphone est facile à retenir.
items.en: His phone number is easy to remember.
items.ipa: sɔ̃ ny.me.ʁo də te.le.fɔn ɛ fa.sil a ʁə.tə.niʁ
items.notes: “son” (his/her) sounds like “sont” (are), but the possessive “son” is needed before “numéro”.

items.fr: Je préfère les gens curieux et ouverts.
items.en: I prefer people who are curious and open-minded.
items.ipa: ʒə pʁe.fɛʁ le ʒɑ̃ ky.ʁjø e u.vɛʁ
items.notes: “préfère” carries two different accents, acute then grave, on its two e's.

items.fr: Quand est-ce que tu l'as rencontré ?
items.notes: “quand” (when) sounds like “quant” (as for), but only “quand” works as a question word here.

items.fr: Leur conversation a duré plus d'une heure.
items.en: Their conversation lasted more than an hour.
items.ipa: lœʁ kɔ̃.vɛʁ.sa.sjɔ̃ a dy.ʁe ply dyn œʁ
items.notes: “leur” (their) sounds exactly like “leurs”, but no s is added before a singular noun like “conversation”.

items.fr: Elle m'a semblé très réservée au début.
items.en: She seemed very reserved at first.
items.ipa: ɛl ma sɑ̃.ble tʁɛ ʁe.zɛʁ.ve o de.by
items.notes: “réservée” carries an acute accent on both e's before the silent final e.

items.fr: Nous avons parlé de tout et de rien.
items.en: We talked about this and that.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ paʁ.le də tu e də ʁjɛ̃
items.notes: “parlé” needs the acute accent to mark its sound, unlike “parler” or “parlez”.

items.fr: C'est une personne assez timide au premier abord.
items.en: She's a fairly shy person at first.
items.ipa: sɛ.t‿yn pɛʁ.sɔn a.se ti.mid o pʁə.mje.ʁ‿a.bɔʁ
items.notes: “personne” is always feminine in French, even when describing a man, so “une” stays feminine.

items.fr: Son nouveau collègue est arrivé lundi dernier.
items.en: His new colleague arrived last Monday.
items.ipa: sɔ̃ nu.vo kɔ.lɛg ɛ.t‿a.ʁi.ve lœ̃.di dɛʁ.nje
items.notes: “nouveau” agrees with the masculine “collègue”; it would become “nouvelle” for a woman.

items.fr: Cette femme d'affaires m'a beaucoup impressionné.
items.ipa: sɛt fam da.fɛʁ ma bo.ku ɛ̃.pʁe.sjɔ.ne
items.notes: “cette” is the feminine form of “ce”, required before the feminine noun “femme”.

items.fr: Les premières impressions sont parfois trompeuses.
items.notes: “premières” and “trompeuses” both take a final s to agree with the plural “impressions”.

items.fr: Plusieurs nouveaux visages sont arrivés à la réunion.
items.en: Several new faces showed up at the meeting.
items.ipa: ply.zjœʁ nu.vo vi.zaʒ sɔ̃.t‿a.ʁi.ve a la ʁe.y.njɔ̃
items.notes: “arrivés” agrees in the plural with “visages” since it's a past participle with être.

items.fr: J'ai rencontré beaucoup de monde ce week-end.
items.en: I met a lot of people this weekend.
items.ipa: ʒe ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe bo.ku də mɔ̃d sə wik.ɛnd
items.notes: the final “p” in “beaucoup” is silent and must not be forgotten in spelling.

items.fr: Nous avons discuté longtemps dans le jardin.
items.en: We chatted for a long time in the garden.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ dis.ky.te lɔ̃.tɑ̃ dɑ̃ lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃
items.notes: the final “s” in “longtemps” is silent but essential in spelling to mark the word correctly.

items.fr: Mon ancien camarade de classe habite à Lyon maintenant.
items.en: My old classmate lives in Lyon now.
items.ipa: mɔ̃.n‿ɑ̃.sjɛ̃ ka.ma.ʁad də klas a.bit a ljɔ̃ mɛ̃t.nɑ̃
items.notes: “mon ancien” requires a liaison, the n of “mon” links to the vowel of “ancien”.

items.fr: Ils ont énormément de points communs.
items.en: They have a huge amount in common.
items.notes: “ont” requires a liaison, the t links to the vowel of “énormément”.

items.fr: Nous étions les seuls invités à ne pas se connaître.
items.en: We were the only guests who didn't know each other.
items.ipa: nu.z‿e.tjɔ̃ le sœl ɛ̃.vi.te a nə pa sə kɔ.nɛtʁ
items.notes: “nous étions” requires a liaison, the s of “nous” is pronounced as a z before the vowel.

items.fr: L'ami de Sarah m'a invité à sa fête d'anniversaire.
items.en: Sarah's friend invited me to her birthday party.
items.ipa: la.mi də sa.ʁa ma ɛ̃.vi.te a sa fɛt da.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ
items.notes: “le” becomes “l'” before “ami” since it starts with a vowel.

items.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu penses de notre nouveau voisin ?
items.en: What do you think of our new neighbor?
items.ipa: kɛs kə ty pɑ̃s də nɔtʁ nu.vo vwa.zɛ̃
items.notes: “que” elides to “qu'” before “est-ce”, a fixed contraction that must keep its apostrophe.

items.fr: Ça fait plaisir de rencontrer enfin quelqu'un comme toi.
items.en: It's so nice to finally meet someone like you.
items.ipa: sa fɛ plɛ.ziʁ də ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe ɑ̃.fɛ̃ kɛl.kœ̃ kɔm twa
items.notes: “quelqu'un” is written as one fixed word here, not as “quelqu” plus “un”.

items.fr: Je viens de faire la connaissance de tes parents.
items.ipa: ʒə vjɛ̃ də fɛʁ la kɔ.nɛ.sɑ̃s də te pa.ʁɑ̃
items.notes: “venir de” plus infinitive expresses a very recent action, here “faire”, which stays uninflected.

items.fr: Il vaut mieux se présenter avant de poser des questions.
items.en: It's better to introduce yourself before asking questions.
items.ipa: il vo mjø sə pʁe.zɑ̃.te a.vɑ̃ də po.ze de kɛs.tjɔ̃
items.notes: “il vaut mieux” is followed directly by an infinitive, not by “que” plus a conjugated verb.

items.fr: Nous nous sommes tout de suite bien entendus.
items.en: We hit it off right away.
items.ipa: nu nu sɔm tu də sɥit bjɛ̃.n‿ɑ̃.tɑ̃.dy
items.notes: “entendus” ends in s because this reflexive verb agrees with the plural subject “nous” in the passé composé.

items.fr: Elle connaissait déjà mon frère avant de me rencontrer.
items.en: She already knew my brother before meeting me.
items.ipa: ɛl kɔ.nɛ.sɛ de.ʒa mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ a.vɑ̃ də mə ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe
items.notes: “connaissait” is the imperfect form of “connaître”, spelled with two s and an i before the ending.

items.fr: Ils se reverront la semaine prochaine, j'en suis sûr.
items.en: They'll see each other again next week, I'm sure of it.
items.ipa: il sə ʁə.vɛ.ʁɔ̃ la sə.mɛn pʁɔ.ʃɛn ʒɑ̃ sɥi syʁ
items.notes: “reverront” is the future tense of “revoir”, built irregularly just like “voir” becomes “verront”.

items.fr: Il épelle son nom lettre par lettre pour être sûr.
items.en: He spells out his name letter by letter to be sure it's right.
items.ipa: il e.pɛl sɔ̃ nɔ̃ lɛtʁ paʁ lɛtʁ puʁ ɛtʁ syʁ
items.notes: “épelle” doubles the l, unlike the infinitive “épeler” which has only one.

items.fr: Nous avons échangé nos coordonnées avant de partir.
items.en: We exchanged contact details before leaving.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ e.ʃɑ̃.ʒe no kɔ.ɔʁ.dɔ.ne a.vɑ̃ də paʁ.tiʁ
items.notes: “coordonnées” has two o's in a row and a double n, easy to mistype.

items.fr: Tu te souviens de moi, non ?
items.ipa: ty tə su.vjɛ̃ də mwa nɔ̃
items.notes: a comma is needed before the tag question “non ?”, separating the two parts of the sentence.

items.fr: Son sourire chaleureux m'a tout de suite mis en confiance.

items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Son sourire chaleureux","t":"his warm smile"},{"w":"m'a tout de suite mis en confiance.","t":"immediately put me at ease"}]}

items.fr: La plupart des gens que je connais viennent de cette association.
items.en: Most of the people I know come from that club.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"La plupart des gens","t":"most of the people"},{"w":"que je connais","t":"that I know"},{"w":"viennent de","t":"come from"},{"w":"cette association.","t":"that club"}]}

items.fr: Elle n'a pas hésité une seconde à se présenter.
items.en: She didn't hesitate a second to introduce herself.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle n'a pas hésité","t":"she didn't hesitate"},{"w":"une seconde","t":"a second"},{"w":"à se présenter.","t":"to introduce herself"}]}

items.fr: Au lieu de rester seul, il a préféré aller lui parler.
items.en: Instead of staying alone, he decided to go talk to her.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Au lieu de rester seul,","t":"instead of staying alone"},{"w":"il a préféré","t":"he decided"},{"w":"aller lui parler.","t":"to go talk to her"}]}

items.fr: Nous avons entendu parler l'un de l'autre avant de nous rencontrer.
items.en: We'd heard of each other before we met.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons entendu parler","t":"we'd heard"},{"w":"l'un de l'autre","t":"of each other"},{"w":"avant de nous rencontrer.","t":"before we met"}]}

items.fr: Elle a tenu compte de mes conseils dès notre première rencontre.
items.en: She took my advice into account from our very first meeting.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle a tenu compte de","t":"she took into account"},{"w":"mes conseils","t":"my advice"},{"w":"dès notre première rencontre.","t":"from our very first meeting"}]}

items.fr: Petit à petit, nous sommes devenus de vrais amis.
items.en: Little by little, we became real friends.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Petit à petit,","t":"little by little"},{"w":"nous sommes devenus","t":"we became"},{"w":"de vrais amis.","t":"real friends"}]}

items.fr: En général, elle se souvient du prénom de tout le monde.
items.en: In general, she remembers everyone's first name.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"En général,","t":"in general"},{"w":"elle se souvient","t":"she remembers"},{"w":"du prénom","t":"the first name"},{"w":"de tout le monde.","t":"of everyone"}]}

items.fr: Je ne pensais pas du tout le rencontrer ici.
items.en: I really didn't expect to meet him here.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Je ne pensais pas du tout","t":"I really didn't expect"},{"w":"le rencontrer","t":"to meet him"},{"w":"ici.","t":"here"}]}

items.fr: Nous avons eu de la chance de nous croiser ce jour-là.
items.en: We were lucky to run into each other that day.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons eu de la chance","t":"we were lucky"},{"w":"de nous croiser","t":"to run into each other"},{"w":"ce jour-là.","t":"that day"}]}

items.fr: Ils se sont mis à discuter comme de vieux amis.
items.en: They started chatting like old friends.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Ils se sont mis à discuter","t":"they started chatting"},{"w":"comme de vieux amis.","t":"like old friends"}]}

items.fr: Elle avait hâte de rencontrer les nouveaux étudiants.
items.en: She couldn't wait to meet the new students.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle avait hâte de rencontrer","t":"she couldn't wait to meet"},{"w":"les nouveaux étudiants.","t":"the new students"}]}

items.fr: Ce genre de rencontre change parfois toute une vie.
items.en: That kind of meeting sometimes changes a whole life.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Ce genre de rencontre","t":"that kind of meeting"},{"w":"change parfois","t":"sometimes changes"},{"w":"toute une vie.","t":"a whole life"}]}

items.fr: Il pense que j'ai tort, mais il se trompe.
items.en: He thinks I'm wrong, but he's mistaken.
items.ipa: il pɑ̃s kə ʒe tɔʁ, mɛ il sə tʁɔ̃p
items.notes: “mais” (but) sounds close to “mes” (my), but only “mais” fits as the contrasting conjunction here.

items.fr: Mon frère a dit que c'était sa faute, pas la mienne.
items.en: My brother said it was his fault, not mine.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ a di kə se.tɛ sa fot, pa la mjɛn
items.notes: “c'était” (it was) can be confused with “s'était” (had... itself), but only “c'était” fits after “dit que”.

items.fr: Mes parents ont raison, on doit se réconcilier avant le dîner.
items.en: My parents are right, we need to make up before dinner.
items.ipa: me pa.ʁɑ̃ ɔ̃ ʁɛ.zɔ̃, ɔ̃ dwa sə ʁe.kɔ̃.si.lje a.vɑ̃ lə di.ne
items.notes: “ont” (have, from avoir) sounds like “on” (we), but only “ont” fits with “mes parents” as subject.

items.fr: Notre collègue a mal pris ce qu'on lui a dit hier.
items.en: Our colleague took what we told him the wrong way yesterday.
items.ipa: nɔtʁ kɔ.lɛg a mal pʁi sə kɔ̃ lɥi a di jɛʁ
items.notes: “a” (from avoir) is a homophone of “à” (to), but no accent is needed in this verb form.

items.fr: Mon coloc croit que c'est moi qui ai cassé son assiette préférée.
items.en: My roommate thinks I'm the one who broke his favorite plate.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ kɔ.lɔk kʁwa kə sɛ mwa ki e ka.se sɔ̃.n‿a.sjɛt pʁe.fe.ʁe
items.notes: “c'est” (it is) is easily confused with “s'est”, but only “c'est” fits before “moi qui”.

items.fr: Le voisin pense que nous sommes responsables du bruit, alors qu'en réalité, ce sont ses enfants.
items.en: The neighbor thinks we're responsible for the noise, when in reality, it's his kids.
items.ipa: lə vwa.zɛ̃ pɑ̃s kə nu sɔm ʁes.pɔ̃.sabl dy bʁɥi, a.lɔʁ kɑ̃ ʁe.a.li.te, sə sɔ̃ se.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃
items.notes: “qu'en” is easily confused with “quand”, but the clause needs “qu'en réalité”.

items.fr: Elle a fini par lui pardonner après leur dispute.
items.en: She eventually forgave him after their argument.
items.ipa: ɛl a fi.ni paʁ lɥi paʁ.dɔ.ne a.pʁɛ lœʁ dis.pyt
items.notes: “après” takes a grave accent, not an acute one, even though it sounds close to “é”.

items.fr: Ma sœur a été très blessée par mes mots.
items.en: My sister was really hurt by my words.
items.ipa: ma sœʁ a e.te tʁɛ ble.se paʁ me mo
items.notes: “été” keeps both acute accents in every form of the past participle.

items.fr: Mon meilleur ami préfère qu'on règle ce problème calmement.
items.en: My best friend would rather we settle this problem calmly.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ mɛ.jœʁ a.mi pʁe.fɛʁ kɔ̃ ʁɛgl sə pʁɔ.blɛm kalm.mɑ̃
items.notes: “règle” needs a grave accent on the first e, not an acute one.

items.fr: Mon père a très mal réagi quand je lui ai menti.
items.en: My father reacted very badly when I lied to him.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ pɛʁ a tʁɛ mal ʁe.a.ʒi kɑ̃ ʒə lɥi e mɑ̃.ti
items.notes: “réagi” keeps its acute accent even as a past participle.

items.fr: Notre chef a présenté ses excuses devant toute l'équipe.
items.en: Our boss apologized in front of the whole team.
items.ipa: nɔtʁ ʃɛf a pʁe.zɑ̃.te se.z‿ɛk.skyz də.vɑ̃ tut le.kip
items.notes: the first e in “présenté” takes an acute accent, unlike a silent e.

items.fr: Elle était vraiment fâchée contre son copain.
items.en: She was really angry with her boyfriend.
items.ipa: ɛl e.tɛ vʁɛ.mɑ̃ fɑ.ʃe kɔ̃tʁ sɔ̃ kɔ.pɛ̃
items.notes: “fâchée” needs the extra e to agree with the feminine subject “elle”.

items.fr: Ma sœur est restée silencieuse pendant toute la dispute.
items.en: My sister stayed silent through the whole argument.
items.ipa: ma sœʁ ɛs.te si.lɑ̃.sjøz pɑ̃.dɑ̃ tut la dis.pyt
items.notes: “silencieuse” takes the feminine ending because it describes “ma sœur”.

items.fr: Mon amie était surprise que je sois encore fâché.
items.en: My friend was surprised that I was still angry.
items.ipa: mɔ̃.n‿a.mi e.tɛ syʁ.pʁiz kə ʒə swa ɑ̃.kɔʁ fa.ʃe
items.notes: “amie” is feminine even though “mon” precedes it before a vowel, so “surprise” stays feminine.

items.fr: La mère était tellement déçue qu'elle n'a pas parlé à sa fille de la soirée.
items.en: The mother was so disappointed that she didn't speak to her daughter all evening.
items.ipa: la mɛʁ e.tɛ tɛl.mɑ̃ de.sy kɛl na pa paʁ.le a sa fij də la swa.ʁe
items.notes: “déçue” ends in “ue” to agree with the feminine subject “la mère”.

items.fr: Notre collègue Sophie est restée calme malgré la tension.
items.en: Our colleague Sophie stayed calm despite the tension.
items.ipa: nɔtʁ kɔ.lɛg sɔ.fi ɛs.te kalm mal.gʁe la tɑ̃.sjɔ̃
items.notes: “restée” ends in “ée” because the subject, Sophie, is feminine.

items.fr: La voisine était vexée par notre remarque.
items.en: The neighbor was offended by our comment.
items.ipa: la vwa.zin e.tɛ vɛk.se paʁ nɔtʁ ʁə.maʁk
items.notes: “vexée” takes the feminine e because “la voisine” is feminine.

items.fr: Les deux amoureux se sont enfin réconciliés.
items.en: The two lovers finally made up.
items.notes: “réconciliés” takes a plural s because it agrees with “les deux amoureux”.

items.fr: Mes frères se sont disputés parce qu'ils n'étaient pas d'accord sur les règles du jeu.
items.en: My brothers argued because they didn't agree on the rules of the game.
items.ipa: me fʁɛʁ sə sɔ̃ dis.py.te paʁ.skil ne.tɛ pa da.kɔʁ syʁ le ʁɛgl dy ʒø
items.notes: “disputés” needs the plural s to agree with “mes frères”.

items.fr: Les excuses qu'elle nous a présentées ont vraiment aidé à calmer les esprits.
items.en: The apologies she gave us really helped calm things down.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɛk.skyz kɛl nu.z‿a pʁe.zɑ̃.te ɔ̃ vʁɛ.mɑ̃ ɛ.de a kal.me le.z‿ɛs.pʁi
items.notes: “présentées” agrees with “les excuses”, the preceding direct object of “a présentées”.

items.fr: Nos collègues sont restés fâchés toute la journée.
items.en: Our colleagues stayed upset all day.
items.ipa: no kɔ.lɛg sɔ̃ ʁɛs.te fa.ʃe tut la ʒuʁ.ne
items.notes: “restés” and “fâchés” both take the plural s to agree with “nos collègues”.

items.fr: Les enfants se sont excusés auprès de leur père.
items.en: The children apologized to their father.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ sə sɔ̃.t‿ɛks.ky.ze o.pʁɛ də lœʁ pɛʁ
items.notes: “excusés” takes the plural s to agree with “les enfants”.

items.fr: Il n'a jamais vraiment compris pourquoi elle était fâchée.
items.en: He never really understood why she was angry.
items.ipa: il na ʒa.mɛ vʁɛ.mɑ̃ kɔ̃.pʁi puʁ.kwa ɛl e.tɛ fa.ʃe
items.notes: the final s in “compris” is silent.

items.fr: Mon petit frère ne dit jamais pardon, même quand il sait qu'il a tort.
items.en: My little brother never says sorry first, even when he knows he's wrong.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ pə.ti fʁɛʁ nə di ʒa.mɛ paʁ.dɔ̃, mɛm kɑ̃.t‿il sɛ kil a tɔʁ
items.notes: the final s of “jamais” is never pronounced.

items.fr: Elle a fini par accepter mes excuses, mais ça a pris du temps.
items.en: She eventually accepted my apology, but it took time.
items.ipa: ɛl a fi.ni paʁ ak.sɛp.te me.z‿ɛk.skyz, mɛ sa a pʁi dy tɑ̃
items.notes: “temps” ends in a silent p and s.

items.fr: Le conflit avec mon collègue s'est calmé au bout de quelques jours.
items.en: The conflict with my colleague settled down after a few days.
items.ipa: lə kɔ̃.fli a.vɛk mɔ̃ kɔ.lɛg sɛ kal.me o bu də kɛl.kə ʒuʁ
items.notes: the final t in “bout” is silent.

items.fr: Mes parents n'ont pas dit un mot pendant tout le repas.
items.en: My parents didn't say a word during the whole meal.
items.ipa: me pa.ʁɑ̃ nɔ̃ pa di œ̃ mo pɑ̃.dɑ̃ tu lə ʁə.pa
items.notes: the final t in “mot” is silent.

items.fr: Notre voisin a trop crié pendant la dispute.
items.en: Our neighbor shouted too much during the argument.
items.ipa: nɔtʁ vwa.zɛ̃ a tʁo kʁi.e pɑ̃.dɑ̃ la dis.pyt
items.notes: the final p in “trop” is silent.

items.fr: Ils ont eu une grosse dispute hier soir.
items.en: They had a big argument last night.
items.ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃.t‿y yn gʁos dis.pyt jɛʁ swaʁ
items.notes: “ils ont” requires a liaison, so the final s of “ils” is pronounced as a z.

items.fr: Mes deux enfants ne s'entendent plus du tout.
items.en: My two children don't get along at all anymore.
items.ipa: me dø.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ nə sɑ̃.tɑ̃d ply dy tu
items.notes: “deux enfants” requires a liaison between “deux” and the vowel of “enfants”.

items.fr: Nous avons eu un grand malentendu qui nous a beaucoup affectés.
items.en: We had a big misunderstanding that really affected us.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃.z‿y œ̃ gʁɑ̃.t‿ma.lɑ̃.tɑ̃.dy ki nu.z‿a bo.ku a.fɛk.te
items.notes: “grand” makes a liaison with “malentendu”, pronounced with a t sound.

items.fr: Les autres employés ont pris son parti dans le conflit.
items.en: The other employees took his side in the conflict.
items.ipa: le.z‿otʁ.z‿ɑ̃.plwa.je ɔ̃ pʁi sɔ̃ paʁ.ti dɑ̃ lə kɔ̃.fli
items.notes: “les autres” carries a liaison, the s sounding like z before the vowel.

items.fr: Mes grands-parents ont eu une dispute dont ils ne se souviennent même plus.
items.en: My grandparents had an argument that they don't even remember anymore.
items.ipa: me gʁɑ̃.pa.ʁɑ̃.z‿ɔ̃.t‿y yn dis.pyt dɔ̃.t‿il nə sə su.vjɛn mɛm ply
items.notes: “parents ont” requires a liaison, so the final s of “parents” is pronounced as z.

items.fr: Je ne l'ai pas cru quand il m'a dit qu'il regrettait.
items.en: I didn't believe him when he told me he was sorry.
items.ipa: ʒə nə le pa kʁy kɑ̃.t‿il ma di kil ʁə.gʁɛ.tɛ
items.notes: “que” elides to “qu'” before the vowel sound of “il”.

items.fr: Elle ne s'attendait pas à ce que je m'excuse si vite.
items.en: She didn't expect me to apologize so quickly.
items.ipa: ɛl nə sa.tɑ̃.dɛ pa a sə kə ʒə mɛk.skyz si vit
items.notes: “se” elides to “s'” before a vowel, giving “s'attendait”.

items.fr: J'ai essayé de lui expliquer, mais elle n'a rien voulu entendre.
items.en: I tried to explain to her, but she wouldn't listen to anything.
items.ipa: ʒe e.se.je də lɥi ɛk.spli.ke, mɛ ɛl na ʁjɛ̃ vu.ly ɑ̃.tɑ̃dʁ
items.notes: “je” elides to “j'” before the vowel of “ai”.

items.fr: Quoiqu'il ait eu tort, personne n'a osé le lui dire en réunion.
items.en: Even though he was wrong, no one dared to tell him in the meeting.
items.ipa: kwa.kil ɛ.t‿y tɔʁ, pɛʁ.sɔn na o.ze lə lɥi diʁ ɑ̃ ʁe.y.njɔ̃
items.notes: “quoique” elides to “quoiqu'” before “il”.

items.fr: L'enfant a pleuré après la dispute avec sa mère.
items.en: The child cried after the argument with his mother.
items.ipa: lɑ̃.fɑ̃ a plø.ʁe a.pʁɛ la dis.pyt a.vɛk sa mɛʁ
items.notes: “le” or “la” elides to “l'” before the vowel of “enfant”.

items.fr: J'aurais dû m'excuser plus tôt auprès d'elle.
items.en: I should have apologized to her sooner.
items.ipa: ʒo.ʁɛ dy mɛk.sky.ze ply to o.pʁɛ dɛl
items.notes: “de” elides to “d'” before “elle” because it starts with a vowel sound.

items.fr: Bien qu'ils se soient réconciliés, la confiance n'est pas totalement revenue.
items.en: Although they've made up, the trust hasn't fully come back.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃ kil sə swa.t‿ʁe.kɔ̃.si.lje, la kɔ̃.fjɑ̃s nɛ pa to.ta.lə.mɑ̃ ʁə.və.ny
items.notes: “bien que” always triggers the subjunctive, hence “se soient réconciliés”.

items.fr: Il faut que tu fasses des excuses à ta sœur.
items.en: You need to apologize to your sister.
items.ipa: il fo kə ty fas de.z‿ɛk.skyz a ta sœʁ
items.notes: “il faut que” requires the subjunctive “fasses”, not the indicative “fais”.

items.fr: Si tu m'écoutais, on ne se disputerait pas autant.
items.en: If you listened to me, we wouldn't argue so much.
items.ipa: si ty me.ku.tɛ, ɔ̃ nə sə dis.py.tə.ʁɛ pa o.tɑ̃
items.notes: after “si” plus imparfait, the main clause needs the conditional “disputerait”, not the future.

items.fr: Elle a agi comme si de rien n'était après notre dispute.
items.en: She acted as if nothing had happened after our argument.
items.ipa: ɛl a a.ʒi kɔm si də ʁjɛ̃ ne.tɛ a.pʁɛ nɔtʁ dis.pyt
items.notes: “comme si de rien n'était” is a fixed expression that always keeps this exact form.

items.fr: Mon fils refuse de reconnaître qu'il a tort.
items.en: My son refuses to admit he's wrong.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fis ʁə.fyz də ʁə.kɔ.nɛtʁ kil a tɔʁ
items.notes: “reconnaître que” takes the indicative “a”, not the subjunctive “ait”.

items.fr: Nous nous sommes réconciliés après avoir discuté pendant des heures.
items.en: We made up after talking for hours.
items.ipa: nu nu sɔm ʁe.kɔ̃.si.lje a.pʁɛ a.vwaʁ dis.ky.te pɑ̃.dɑ̃ de.z‿œʁ
items.notes: reflexive verbs use “être” in the passé composé, so “réconciliés” agrees with the subject.

items.fr: Mon frère m'a pardonné, mais il ne l'a pas oublié.
items.en: My brother forgave me, but he hasn't forgotten it.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ ma paʁ.dɔ.ne, mɛ il nə la pa u.bli.e
items.notes: “pardonné” ends in é as the past participle, not like the infinitive “pardonner”.

items.fr: Si elle avait su à quel point ça m'avait blessé, elle se serait excusée plus tôt.
items.en: If she had known how much it hurt me, she would have apologized sooner.
items.ipa: si ɛl a.vɛ sy a kɛl pwɛ̃ sa ma.vɛ ble.se, ɛl sə sə.ʁɛ.t‿ɛk.sky.ze ply to
items.notes: the “si” clause needs the plus-que-parfait “avait su”, paired with the conditional perfect “se serait excusée”.

items.fr: Nous avons réglé le malentendu dès le lendemain.
items.en: We resolved the misunderstanding the very next day.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʁe.gle lə ma.lɑ̃.tɑ̃.dy dɛ lə lɑ̃d.mɛ̃
items.notes: “réglé” ends in é, the past participle of the ‑er verb “régler”.

items.fr: Tu dois t'excuser avant qu'il ne soit trop tard.
items.en: You need to apologize before it's too late.
items.ipa: ty dwa tɛk.sky.ze a.vɑ̃ kil nə swa tʁo taʁ
items.notes: “avant que” often takes an optional expletive “ne”, which doesn't make the sentence negative.

items.fr: Depuis qu'ils se sont parlé, la tension a beaucoup diminué.
items.en: Since they talked to each other, the tension has eased a lot.
items.ipa: də.pɥi kil sə sɔ̃ paʁ.le, la tɑ̃.sjɔ̃ a bo.ku di.mi.nɥe
items.notes: “parlé” stays invariable here because “se” is an indirect object, as in “parler à quelqu'un”.

items.fr: Elle a écrit une lettre pour s'excuser après leur dispute.
items.en: She wrote a letter to apologize after their argument.
items.ipa: ɛl a e.kʁi yn lɛtʁ puʁ sɛk.sky.ze a.pʁɛ lœʁ dis.pyt
items.notes: “écrit” is spelled with a final t, not an s like the present tense “écris”.

items.fr: Ma sœur a toujours raison, du moins c'est ce qu'elle croit.
items.en: My sister is always right, or at least that's what she thinks.
items.ipa: ma sœʁ a tu.ʒuʁ ʁɛ.zɔ̃, dy mwɛ̃ sɛ sə kɛl kʁwa
items.notes: “toujours” is spelled with “ou”, not with “u” alone as it might sound.

items.fr: Nous avons eu un désaccord à propos d'un cadeau d'anniversaire.
items.en: We had a disagreement about a birthday present.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃.z‿y œ̃ de.za.kɔʁ a pʁɔ.po dœ̃ ka.do da.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ
items.notes: “désaccord” has a double c, not a double s.

items.fr: Le désaccord entre les deux équipes a fini par s'apaiser grâce à la médiation.
items.en: The disagreement between the two teams eventually settled thanks to mediation.
items.ipa: lə de.za.kɔʁ ɑ̃tʁ le dø.z‿e.kip a fi.ni paʁ sa.pɛ.ze gʁɑs a la me.dja.sjɔ̃
items.notes: “grâce” requires a circumflex on the a, unlike English “grace”.

items.fr: Ma fille a exagéré en disant que je ne l'écoutais jamais.
items.en: My daughter exaggerated when she said I never listen to her.
items.ipa: ma fij a ɛg.za.ʒe.ʁe ɑ̃ di.zɑ̃ kə ʒə nə le.ku.tɛ ʒa.mɛ
items.notes: “exagéré” is spelled with an x, not the “gz” sound it might suggest.

items.fr: Pourquoi tu ne m'as rien dit avant ?
items.en: Why didn't you tell me anything before?
items.ipa: puʁ.kwa ty nə ma ʁjɛ̃ di a.vɑ̃
items.notes: French requires a space before the question mark: “avant ?”.

items.fr: Arrête de crier, s'il te plaît !
items.ipa: a.ʁɛt də kʁi.je, sil tə plɛ
items.notes: an exclamation mark in French needs a space before it: “plaît !”.

items.fr: Est-ce que tu m'en veux encore ?
items.en: Are you still mad at me?

items.fr: Le mariage a lieu samedi prochain.
items.en: The wedding is happening next Saturday.
items.ipa: lə ma.ʁjaʒ a ljø sam.di pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃
items.notes: “a” (from avoir) has no accent, unlike the preposition “à”.
“mariée” takes a final e because the reflexive subject “sœur” is feminine.

items.fr: Le bébé est né hier soir.
items.en: The baby was born last night.
items.ipa: lə be.be ɛ ne jɛʁ swaʁ
items.notes: “né” stays masculine here because “bébé” is grammatically masculine, whatever the baby's sex.
“anniversaire” has two n's and two r's, easy to drop one.

items.fr: Toute la famille est réunie ce soir.
items.en: The whole family is together tonight.
items.ipa: tut la fa.mij ɛ ʁe.y.ni sə swaʁ
items.notes: “toute” takes the feminine e to agree with “la famille”.

items.en: The guests are arriving at noon.
items.notes: the s of “les” links to “invités”, making a z sound.

items.fr: C'est le baptême de mon neveu.
items.ipa: sɛ lə ba.tɛm də mɔ̃ nə.vø
items.notes: the “p” in “baptême” is silent.

items.fr: On va chanter pour son anniversaire.
items.en: We're going to sing for his birthday.
items.notes: “son” agrees with the masculine noun “anniversaire”, not with the person's gender.

items.fr: Les mariés dansent devant tout le monde.
items.en: The newlyweds are dancing in front of everyone.
items.ipa: le ma.ʁje dɑ̃s də.vɑ̃ tu lə mɔ̃d
items.notes: “mariés” takes a plural s because it refers to both newlyweds together.

items.fr: Est-ce que tu viens à la fête ?
items.en: Are you coming to the party?
items.ipa: ɛs kə ty vjɛ̃ a la fɛt
items.notes: French requires a space before the question mark, unlike English.

items.fr: Mes grands-parents fêtent leurs noces d'or.
items.en: My grandparents are celebrating their golden wedding anniversary.
items.ipa: me ɡʁɑ̃.pa.ʁɑ̃ fɛt lœʁ nɔs dɔʁ
items.notes: “grands-parents” takes an s on both words in the plural.
“gâteau” needs a circumflex accent on the a.

items.fr: Nous sommes tristes pour cette perte.
items.en: We are sad about this loss.
items.ipa: nu sɔm tʁist puʁ sɛt pɛʁt
items.notes: “sommes” is the “nous” form of être, not “somme”.

items.fr: La cérémonie commence à quatorze heures.
items.en: The ceremony starts at two in the afternoon.
items.notes: “cérémonie” has two accented é's.

items.fr: Il porte un costume noir pour l'enterrement.
items.en: He's wearing a black suit for the funeral.
items.ipa: il pɔʁt œ̃ kɔs.tym nwaʁ puʁ lɑ̃.tɛʁ.mɑ̃
items.notes: “le” becomes “l’” before the vowel in “enterrement”.

items.fr: On allume une bougie pour grand-père.
items.en: We're lighting a candle for grandpa.
items.notes: “on” (pronoun) is not “ont” (from avoir), even though they sound the same.

items.fr: Les enfants jouent pendant le repas de famille.
items.en: The children are playing during the family meal.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ ʒu pɑ̃.dɑ̃ lə ʁə.pa də fa.mij
items.notes: “jouent” ends in a silent “-ent” for the plural ils/elles form.

items.fr: C'est un jour heureux pour nous tous.
items.en: It's a happy day for all of us.
items.ipa: sɛ.t‿œ̃ ʒuʁ œ.ʁø puʁ nu tus
items.notes: “c'” elides with “est” to avoid the vowel clash.

items.fr: Le parrain tient le bébé dans ses bras.
items.en: The godfather is holding the baby in his arms.
items.ipa: lə pa.ʁɛ̃ tjɛ̃ lə be.be dɑ̃ se bʁa
items.notes: the final “t” of “tient” is silent.

items.fr: La mariée porte une robe blanche.
items.en: The bride is wearing a white dress.
items.ipa: la ma.ʁje pɔʁt yn ʁɔb blɑ̃ʃ
items.notes: “blanche” is the feminine form of “blanc”, agreeing with “robe”.

items.fr: Nous avons offert des fleurs pour ses funérailles.
items.en: We brought flowers for her funeral.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃.z‿ɔ.fɛʁ de flœʁ puʁ se fy.ne.ʁaj
items.notes: “offert” stays unchanged because the direct object “des fleurs” comes after the verb.

items.fr: Le repas de fête dure trois heures.
items.en: The celebration meal lasts three hours.
items.ipa: lə ʁə.pa də fɛt dyʁ tʁwa.z‿œʁ
items.notes: “trois” links to “heures” with a z sound.

items.fr: Mes cousins viennent pour la fête de famille.
items.en: My cousins are coming for the family gathering.
items.ipa: me ku.zɛ̃ vjɛn puʁ la fɛt də fa.mij
items.notes: the final “s” of “cousins” is silent.

items.fr: La famille se recueille au cimetière en silence.
items.en: The family gathers quietly at the cemetery.
items.ipa: la fa.mij sə ʁə.kœj o sim.tjɛʁ ɑ̃ si.lɑ̃s
items.notes: “cimetière” has a grave accent on the second e.

items.fr: Elle porte le deuil depuis un mois.
items.en: She has been in mourning for a month.
items.ipa: ɛl pɔʁt lə dœj də.pɥi œ̃ mwa
items.notes: “depuis” marks an action still continuing, not “pendant”.

items.fr: Nous avons organisé une grande fête pour ses cinquante ans.
items.en: We organized a big party for his fiftieth birthday.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃.z‿ɔʁ.ɡa.ni.ze yn ɡʁɑ̃d fɛt puʁ se sɛ̃.kɑ̃t‿ɑ̃
items.notes: “organisé” doesn't change form because there's no preceding direct object with avoir.

items.fr: Les mariés ont échangé leurs alliances devant tout le monde.
items.en: The newlyweds exchanged rings in front of everyone.
items.ipa: le ma.ʁje ɔ̃.t‿e.ʃɑ̃.ʒe lœʁ.z‿a.ljɑ̃s də.vɑ̃ tu lə mɔ̃d
items.notes: “échangé” stays singular masculine since the object “leurs alliances” follows the verb.

items.fr: Ma tante a pleuré de joie en voyant le bébé.
items.en: My aunt cried tears of joy when she saw the baby.
items.ipa: ma tɑ̃t a plø.ʁe də ʒwa ɑ̃ vwa.jɑ̃ lə be.be
items.notes: “voyant” keeps the y from “voir” even though it's pronounced like “vwa-yan”.

items.fr: Le curé a béni les jeunes mariés à l'église.
items.en: The priest blessed the newlyweds at the church.
items.ipa: lə ky.ʁe a be.ni le ʒœn ma.ʁje a le.ɡliz
items.notes: “la” becomes “l’” before the vowel of “église”.

items.fr: Les grands-parents racontent des souvenirs de leur mariage.
items.en: The grandparents are sharing memories from their wedding.
items.ipa: le ɡʁɑ̃.pa.ʁɑ̃ ʁa.kɔ̃t de su.və.niʁ də lœʁ ma.ʁjaʒ
items.notes: “racontent” ends in the silent “-ent” of the ils/elles form.

items.fr: Pour son mariage, elle porte le collier de sa grand-mère.
items.en: For her wedding, she's wearing her grandmother's necklace.
items.ipa: puʁ sɔ̃ ma.ʁjaʒ ɛl pɔʁt lə kɔ.lje də sa ɡʁɑ̃ mɛʁ
items.notes: “collier” is spelled with a double l.

items.fr: Nous avons reçu un faire-part de naissance ce matin.
items.en: We received a birth announcement this morning.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʁə.sy œ̃ fɛʁ.paʁ də nɛ.sɑ̃s sə ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: “reçu” needs a cedilla under the c to keep the soft s sound.

items.fr: Les cousines se sont retrouvées après dix ans.
items.en: The cousins saw each other again after ten years.
items.ipa: le ku.zin sə sɔ̃ ʁə.tʁu.ve a.pʁɛ di.z‿ɑ̃
items.notes: “retrouvées” takes -ées to agree with the feminine plural subject “les cousines”.

items.fr: On a envoyé des faire-part à tous les invités.
items.en: We sent invitations to all the guests.
items.ipa: ɔ̃.n‿a ɑ̃.vwa.je de fɛʁ.paʁ a tu le.z‿ɛ̃.vi.te
items.notes: “faire-part” stays the same in the plural, it never takes an s.

items.fr: Mon oncle a proposé un toast en l'honneur des mariés.
items.en: My uncle raised a toast in honor of the newlyweds.
items.ipa: mɔ̃.n‿ɔ̃kl a pʁɔ.po.ze œ̃ tost ɑ̃ lɔ.nœʁ de ma.ʁje
items.notes: the h in “honneur” is silent, which is why “le” elides to “l’”.

items.fr: Ma cousine était bouleversée en apprenant la triste nouvelle.
items.en: My cousin was overwhelmed when she heard the sad news.
items.ipa: ma ku.zin e.tɛ bul.vɛʁ.se ɑ̃ a.pʁə.nɑ̃ la tʁist nu.vɛl
items.notes: “bouleversée” takes a final e to agree with the feminine “cousine”.

items.fr: Ils ont soufflé les bougies ensemble.
items.en: They blew out the candles together.
items.notes: “soufflé” is spelled with a double f.
French puts a space before the exclamation mark, unlike English.

items.fr: Nous nous sommes tous embrassés en pleurant de joie.
items.en: We all hugged each other, crying with joy.
items.ipa: nu nu sɔm tu.z‿ɑ̃.bʁa.se ɑ̃ plø.ʁɑ̃ də ʒwa
items.notes: “embrassés” takes the plural s agreeing with the reciprocal “nous”.

items.fr: Le vieil oncle raconte toujours la même histoire à Noël.
items.en: The old uncle always tells the same story at Christmas.
items.ipa: lə vjɛj ɔ̃kl ʁa.kɔ̃t tu.ʒuʁ la mɛm is.twaʁ a nɔ.ɛl
items.notes: “vieux” becomes “vieil” before a vowel sound like in “oncle”.

items.fr: Les enfants ont couru partout pendant la réception.
items.en: The children ran everywhere during the reception.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃.z‿ɔ̃ ku.ʁy paʁ.tu pɑ̃.dɑ̃ la ʁe.sɛp.sjɔ̃
items.notes: “couru” is the irregular past participle of “courir”, not “couri”.

items.fr: Ma grand-mère a cent ans aujourd'hui.
items.en: My grandmother turns a hundred today.
items.ipa: ma ɡʁɑ̃ mɛʁ a sɑ̃.z‿ɑ̃ o.ʒuʁ.dɥi
items.notes: “cent” (hundred) sounds like “sans” and “sang” but is spelled differently.

items.fr: Nous avons dansé jusqu'à minuit pour célébrer leurs noces.
items.en: We danced until midnight to celebrate their wedding.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ dɑ̃.se ʒys.ka mi.nɥi puʁ se.le.bʁe lœʁ nɔs
items.notes: “jusque” elides to “jusqu'” before “à”.

items.fr: Le vieux couple fête ses noces de diamant cette année.
items.en: The elderly couple is celebrating their diamond wedding anniversary this year.
items.ipa: lə vjø kupl fɛt se nɔs də dja.mɑ̃ sɛt a.ne
items.notes: “vieux” stays masculine to agree with “le couple”, which is grammatically masculine.

items.fr: Elle a été très émue pendant le discours de son père.
items.en: She was very moved during her father's speech.
items.ipa: ɛl a e.te tʁɛ.z‿e.my pɑ̃.dɑ̃ lə dis.kuʁ də sɔ̃ pɛʁ
items.notes: “émue” takes an e to agree with the feminine subject “elle”.

items.fr: Bien que la cérémonie ait été courte, tout le monde était ému.
items.en: Although the ceremony was short, everyone was moved.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃ kə la se.ʁe.mɔ.ni ɛ e.te kuʁt tu lə mɔ̃d e.tɛ e.my
items.notes: “bien que” requires the subjunctive, hence “ait été” rather than “a été”.

items.fr: Quand ma grand-mère est décédée, toute la famille s'est rassemblée pour l'enterrement.
items.en: When my grandmother passed away, the whole family gathered for the funeral.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ ma ɡʁɑ̃ mɛʁ ɛ de.se.de tut la fa.mij sɛ ʁa.sɑ̃.ble puʁ lɑ̃.tɛʁ.mɑ̃
items.notes: “décédée” takes a final e because it agrees with the feminine subject “ma grand-mère”.

items.fr: Si nous avions su plus tôt, nous aurions organisé une plus grande fête.
items.en: If we had known sooner, we would have organized a bigger party.
items.ipa: si nu.z‿a.vjɔ̃ sy ply to nu.z‿o.ʁjɔ̃ ɔʁ.ɡa.ni.ze yn ply ɡʁɑ̃d fɛt
items.notes: the “si” clause takes the pluperfect (“avions su”) while the result uses the past conditional (“aurions organisé”).

items.fr: C'est grâce à toi que ce mariage a pu avoir lieu.
items.en: It's thanks to you that this wedding was able to happen.
items.ipa: sɛ ɡʁɑs a twa kə sə ma.ʁjaʒ a py a.vwaʁ ljø
items.notes: “grâce” has a circumflex on the a.

items.fr: Les invités qui viennent de loin dormiront à l'hôtel.
items.en: The guests who are coming from far away will stay at the hotel.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɛ̃.vi.te ki vjɛn də lwɛ̃ dɔʁ.mi.ʁɔ̃ a lo.tɛl
items.notes: the h at the start of “hôtel” is silent.

items.fr: Bien qu'elle soit en deuil, elle a tenu à assister à la fête.
items.en: Even though she is in mourning, she insisted on attending the party.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃ kɛl swa ɑ̃ dœj ɛl a tə.ny a a.sis.te a la fɛt
items.notes: “bien que” triggers the subjunctive “soit”, not the indicative “est”.

items.fr: Le prêtre a demandé aux parrains et marraines de s'avancer.
items.en: The priest asked the godparents to step forward.
items.ipa: lə pʁɛtʁ a də.mɑ̃.de o pa.ʁɛ̃ e ma.ʁɛn də sa.vɑ̃.se
items.notes: “prêtre” has a circumflex accent on the e.

items.fr: Quoiqu'ils se soient disputés autrefois, les deux frères se sont réconciliés aux funérailles.
items.en: Although they had argued in the past, the two brothers reconciled at the funeral.
items.ipa: kwa.kil sə swa.tje dis.py.te o.tʁə.fwa le dø fʁɛʁ sə sɔ̃ ʁe.kɔ̃.si.lje o fy.ne.ʁaj
items.notes: “quoique” requires the subjunctive, hence “se soient disputés”.

items.fr: Il vaut mieux annoncer la naissance après la sortie de la maternité.
items.en: It's better to announce the birth after leaving the maternity ward.
items.ipa: il vo mjø a.nɔ̃.se la nɛ.sɑ̃s a.pʁɛ la sɔʁ.ti də la ma.tɛʁ.ni.te
items.notes: “il vaut mieux” is an impersonal expression always followed by the infinitive here.

items.fr: Les grands-parents, dont c'était les noces d'or, ont reçu de nombreux cadeaux.
items.en: The grandparents, whose golden wedding anniversary it was, received many gifts.
items.ipa: le ɡʁɑ̃.pa.ʁɑ̃ dɔ̃ se.tɛ le nɔs dɔʁ ɔ̃ ʁə.sy də nɔ̃.bʁø ka.do
items.notes: “dont” replaces “de qui/de quoi” to show possession, linking back to “les grands-parents”.

items.fr: Ce sont ces photos de famille que nous chérirons toujours.
items.en: These are the family photos that we'll always treasure.
items.ipa: sə sɔ̃ se fo.to də fa.mij kə nu ʃe.ʁi.ʁɔ̃ tu.ʒuʁ
items.notes: “ces” (these) is not “ses” (his/her) or “c'est”, even though all three sound alike.

items.fr: Depuis que son fils est né, elle sourit tout le temps.
items.en: Ever since her son was born, she smiles all the time.
items.ipa: də.pɥi kə sɔ̃ fis ɛ ne ɛl su.ʁi tu lə tɑ̃
items.notes: the final “t” of “sourit” is silent.

items.fr: Malgré la tristesse, les proches ont su trouver des mots réconfortants.
items.en: Despite the sadness, the relatives managed to find comforting words.
items.ipa: mal.ɡʁe la tʁis.tɛs le pʁɔʃ ɔ̃ sy tʁu.ve de mo ʁe.kɔ̃.fɔʁ.tɑ̃
items.notes: “réconfortants” takes a plural s to agree with the masculine plural “mots”.

items.fr: Une fois que le faire-part sera envoyé, il n'y aura plus qu'à attendre les réponses.
items.en: Once the invitation has been sent, all that's left is to wait for the replies.
items.ipa: yn fwa kə lə fɛʁ.paʁ sə.ʁa ɑ̃.vwa.je il nja o.ʁa ply ka a.tɑ̃dʁ le ʁe.pɔ̃s
items.notes: after “une fois que” referring to the future, French uses the future tense, unlike English.

items.fr: C'est en réunissant toute la famille qu'on se souvient vraiment de ceux qu'on a perdus.
items.en: It's by bringing the whole family together that we truly remember those we've lost.
items.ipa: sɛ.t‿ɑ̃ ʁe.y.ni.sɑ̃ tut la fa.mij kɔ̃ sə su.vjɛ̃ vʁɛ.mɑ̃ də sø kɔ̃.n‿a pɛʁ.dy
items.notes: “réunissant” is the present participle form of “réunir”, built like other -ir verbs.

items.en: The wedding starts at three in the afternoon.

items.fr: Mes parents fêtent leurs vingt-cinq ans de mariage ce week-end.
items.en: My parents are celebrating their twenty-fifth wedding anniversary this weekend.

items.fr: De temps en temps, toute la famille se retrouve pour un grand repas.
items.en: From time to time, the whole family gets together for a big meal.

items.fr: Les invités doivent confirmer leur présence avant la fin du mois.
items.en: The guests need to confirm their attendance before the end of the month.

items.fr: Ma grand-mère a hâte de rencontrer son arrière-petit-fils.
items.en: My grandmother can't wait to meet her great-grandson.

items.fr: Mon frère a préparé un discours émouvant pour le mariage.
items.en: My brother prepared a moving speech for the wedding.

items.fr: Les cousins se voient rarement, alors ces réunions comptent beaucoup.
items.en: The cousins rarely see each other, so these gatherings matter a lot.

items.fr: Grâce à l'aide de tous, la fête a été un vrai succès.
items.en: Thanks to everyone's help, the party was a real success.

items.fr: La famille se recueille un instant avant de disperser les cendres.
items.en: The family pauses for a moment before scattering the ashes.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"La famille","t":"the family"},{"w":"se recueille un instant","t":"pauses for a moment"},{"w":"avant de disperser","t":"before scattering"},{"w":"les cendres.","t":"the ashes"}]}

items.fr: Il faut réserver le traiteur plusieurs mois à l'avance.
items.en: You need to book the caterer several months in advance.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il faut réserver","t":"you need to book"},{"w":"le traiteur","t":"the caterer"},{"w":"plusieurs mois à l'avance.","t":"several months in advance"}]}

items.fr: Elle porte le deuil de son mari depuis plusieurs semaines.
items.en: She has been mourning her husband for several weeks.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle porte le deuil","t":"she has been mourning"},{"w":"de son mari","t":"her husband"},{"w":"depuis plusieurs semaines.","t":"for several weeks"}]}

items.fr: Au bout d'un moment, tout le monde s'est mis à danser.
items.en: After a while, everyone started dancing.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Au bout d'un moment,","t":"after a while,"},{"w":"tout le monde","t":"everyone"},{"w":"s'est mis à danser.","t":"started dancing"}]}

items.fr: Les jeunes mariés partent en voyage de noces demain matin.
items.en: The newlyweds are leaving on their honeymoon tomorrow morning.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Les jeunes mariés","t":"the newlyweds"},{"w":"partent en voyage de noces","t":"are leaving on their honeymoon"},{"w":"demain matin.","t":"tomorrow morning"}]}

items.fr: Mon père tenait à porter un toast en mémoire de mon grand-père.
items.en: My father insisted on raising a toast in memory of my grandfather.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Mon père","t":"my father"},{"w":"tenait à","t":"insisted on"},{"w":"porter un toast","t":"raising a toast"},{"w":"en mémoire de mon grand-père.","t":"in memory of my grandfather"}]}

items.fr: Toute la famille garde de beaux souvenirs de cette réunion.
items.en: The whole family has fond memories of that reunion.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Toute la famille","t":"the whole family"},{"w":"garde de beaux souvenirs","t":"has fond memories"},{"w":"de cette réunion.","t":"of that reunion"}]}

items.fr: Nous avons hâte de fêter le baptême de notre nièce.
items.en: We can't wait to celebrate our niece's baptism.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons hâte de","t":"we can't wait to"},{"w":"fêter","t":"celebrate"},{"w":"le baptême","t":"the baptism"},{"w":"de notre nièce.","t":"of our niece"}]}

items.fr: Le curé a insisté sur l'importance de l'amour et de la patience.
items.en: The priest emphasized the importance of love and patience.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Le curé","t":"the priest"},{"w":"a insisté sur","t":"emphasized"},{"w":"l'importance","t":"the importance"},{"w":"de l'amour et de la patience.","t":"of love and patience"}]}

items.fr: Les enfants font partie du cortège pendant le mariage.
items.en: The children are part of the procession during the wedding.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Les enfants font partie du cortège","t":"the children are part of the procession"},{"w":"pendant le mariage.","t":"during the wedding"}]}

items.fr: Bien que la cérémonie ait duré longtemps, personne ne s'est ennuyé.
items.en: Although the ceremony lasted a long time, no one got bored.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Bien que","t":"although"},{"w":"la cérémonie ait duré longtemps,","t":"the ceremony lasted a long time,"},{"w":"personne","t":"no one"},{"w":"ne s'est ennuyé.","t":"got bored"}]}

items.fr: Il vaut mieux tenir compte des allergies alimentaires avant de choisir le menu.
items.en: It's better to take food allergies into account before choosing the menu.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il vaut mieux","t":"it's better to"},{"w":"tenir compte des allergies alimentaires","t":"take food allergies into account"},{"w":"avant de choisir le menu.","t":"before choosing the menu"}]}

items.fr: Depuis que sa fille s'est mariée, elle se sent un peu seule à la maison.
items.en: Since her daughter got married, she has felt a bit lonely at home.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Depuis que","t":"since"},{"w":"sa fille s'est mariée,","t":"her daughter got married,"},{"w":"elle se sent","t":"she has felt"},{"w":"un peu seule","t":"a bit lonely"},{"w":"à la maison.","t":"at home"}]}

items.fr: Quand on perd un proche, chaque petite tradition familiale prend un sens nouveau.
items.en: When you lose a loved one, every little family tradition takes on new meaning.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Quand on perd","t":"when you lose"},{"w":"un proche,","t":"a loved one,"},{"w":"chaque petite tradition familiale","t":"every little family tradition"},{"w":"prend un sens nouveau.","t":"takes on new meaning"}]}

items.fr: Même si les cousins se disputent parfois, ils s'entraident dans les moments difficiles.
items.en: Even if the cousins argue sometimes, they support each other in tough times.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Même si","t":"even if"},{"w":"les cousins se disputent parfois,","t":"the cousins argue sometimes,"},{"w":"ils s'entraident","t":"they support each other"},{"w":"dans les moments difficiles.","t":"in tough times"}]}

items.fr: C'est en partageant ces souvenirs que la famille reste soudée malgré la distance.
items.en: It's by sharing these memories that the family stays close despite the distance.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"C'est en partageant","t":"it's by sharing"},{"w":"ces souvenirs","t":"these memories"},{"w":"que la famille","t":"that the family"},{"w":"reste soudée","t":"stays close"},{"w":"malgré la distance.","t":"despite the distance"}]}

items.fr: Avant de se marier, ils ont pris le temps de bien se connaître.
items.en: Before getting married, they took the time to really get to know each other.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Avant de se marier,","t":"before getting married,"},{"w":"ils ont pris le temps","t":"they took the time"},{"w":"de bien se connaître.","t":"to really get to know each other"}]}

items.fr: Une fois que le deuil s'apaise, les souvenirs heureux reviennent peu à peu.
items.en: Once the grief eases, the happy memories gradually come back.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Une fois que","t":"once"},{"w":"le deuil s'apaise,","t":"the grief eases,"},{"w":"les souvenirs heureux","t":"the happy memories"},{"w":"reviennent peu à peu.","t":"gradually come back"}]}

items.fr: Les grands-parents, dont c'était le soixantième anniversaire de mariage, ont reçu toute la famille.
items.en: The grandparents, whose sixtieth wedding anniversary it was, hosted the whole family.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Les grands-parents,","t":"the grandparents,"},{"w":"dont c'était","t":"whose it was"},{"w":"le soixantième anniversaire de mariage,","t":"the sixtieth wedding anniversary,"},{"w":"ont reçu","t":"hosted"},{"w":"toute la famille.","t":"the whole family"}]}

items.fr: Quoiqu'elle habite loin, ma tante n'a manqué aucun mariage dans la famille.
items.en: Even though she lives far away, my aunt has never missed a family wedding.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Quoiqu'elle habite loin,","t":"even though she lives far away,"},{"w":"ma tante","t":"my aunt"},{"w":"n'a manqué","t":"has never missed"},{"w":"aucun mariage","t":"a wedding"},{"w":"dans la famille.","t":"in the family"}]}

items.fr: Si les enfants n'avaient pas chanté, la fête aurait paru bien triste.
items.en: If the children hadn't sung, the party would have felt quite sad.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Si les enfants n'avaient pas chanté,","t":"if the children hadn't sung,"},{"w":"la fête","t":"the party"},{"w":"aurait paru","t":"would have felt"},{"w":"bien triste.","t":"quite sad"}]}

items.fr: Il a fallu attendre la fin du repas pour que le discours commence.
items.en: We had to wait until the end of the meal for the speech to begin.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il a fallu attendre","t":"we had to wait"},{"w":"la fin du repas","t":"until the end of the meal"},{"w":"pour que le discours commence.","t":"for the speech to begin"}]}

items.fr: Pendant que les adultes discutaient, les petits-enfants jouaient dans le jardin.
items.en: While the adults were chatting, the grandchildren were playing in the garden.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Pendant que","t":"while"},{"w":"les adultes discutaient,","t":"the adults were chatting,"},{"w":"les petits-enfants","t":"the grandchildren"},{"w":"jouaient","t":"were playing"},{"w":"dans le jardin.","t":"in the garden"}]}

items.fr: Ce qui compte le plus, c'est que toute la famille est réunie ce jour-là.
items.en: What matters most is that the whole family is together that day.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Ce qui compte le plus,","t":"what matters most,"},{"w":"c'est que","t":"is that"},{"w":"toute la famille","t":"the whole family"},{"w":"est réunie","t":"is together"},{"w":"ce jour-là.","t":"that day"}]}

items.fr: Malgré la tristesse des funérailles, les proches ont su trouver un peu de réconfort ensemble.
items.en: Despite the sadness of the funeral, the relatives managed to find some comfort together.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Malgré la tristesse des funérailles,","t":"despite the sadness of the funeral,"},{"w":"les proches","t":"the relatives"},{"w":"ont su trouver","t":"managed to find"},{"w":"un peu de réconfort","t":"some comfort"},{"w":"ensemble.","t":"together"}]}

items.fr: Mon voisin m'a aidé à porter mes courses.
items.en: My neighbor helped me carry my groceries.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ vwa.zɛ̃ ma ɛ.de a pɔʁ.te me kuʁs
items.notes: “a” (from avoir) and “à” sound identical, but only “a” fits before “aidé”.

items.fr: Mon père a réparé la fenêtre de notre voisine âgée.
items.en: My dad fixed our elderly neighbor's window.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ pɛʁ a ʁe.pa.ʁe la fə.nɛtʁ də nɔtʁ vwa.zin a.ʒe
items.notes: “âgée” needs a circumflex accent on the a, easy to forget.

items.fr: Elle est très généreuse avec ses voisins.
items.en: She's very generous with her neighbors.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ tʁɛ ʒe.ne.ʁøz a.vɛk se vwa.zɛ̃
items.notes: “généreuse” takes an extra e because the subject “elle” is feminine.

items.fr: Tous mes voisins sont prêts à donner un coup de main.
items.en: All my neighbors are ready to lend a hand.
items.ipa: tu me vwa.zɛ̃ sɔ̃ pʁɛ a dɔ.ne œ̃ ku də mɛ̃
items.notes: “prêts” takes a final s to agree with the plural “voisins”.

items.fr: Elle a pris beaucoup de temps pour m'écouter.
items.en: She took a lot of time to listen to me.
items.ipa: ɛl a pʁi bo.ku də tɑ̃ puʁ me.ku.te
items.notes: In “temps”, the final -ps is silent.

items.fr: Ils ont offert leur aide sans hésiter.
items.en: They offered their help without hesitating.
items.ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃ ɔ.fɛʁ lœʁ ɛd sɑ̃ e.zi.te
items.notes: There's a liaison between “ils” and “ont”, pronounced “ils_ont”.

items.fr: Elle m'a proposé de garder mon chat ce week-end.
items.en: She offered to look after my cat this weekend.
items.ipa: ɛl ma pʁɔ.po.ze də gaʁ.de mɔ̃ ʃa sə wik.ɛnd
items.notes: “me” becomes “m'” before the vowel in “a”.

items.fr: Il faut que tu demandes de l'aide si tu en as besoin.
items.en: You need to ask for help if you need it.
items.ipa: il fo kə ty də.mɑ̃d də lɛd si ty ɑ̃.n‿a bə.zwɛ̃
items.notes: After “il faut que”, the verb goes in the subjunctive: “que tu demandes”.

items.fr: Je t'aiderai à déménager samedi prochain.
items.en: I'll help you move next Saturday.
items.ipa: ʒə tɛ.dʁe a de.me.na.ʒe sam.di pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃
items.notes: “aiderai” is the futur simple form of “aider”, ending in -ai.

items.fr: Nous nous entraidons souvent dans notre quartier.
items.en: We often help each other out in our neighborhood.
items.ipa: nu nu.z‿ɑ̃.tʁɛ.dɔ̃ su.vɑ̃ dɑ̃ nɔtʁ kaʁ.tje
items.notes: “entraidons” is written as one word: no hyphen between “entre” and “aider”.

items.fr: Mes voisins sont toujours là quand j'ai un problème.
items.en: My neighbors are always there when I have a problem.
items.ipa: me vwa.zɛ̃ sɔ̃ tu.ʒuʁ la kɑ̃ ʒe œ̃ pʁɔ.blɛm
items.notes: “sont” (from être) and “son” sound the same, but only “sont” fits here.

items.fr: J'ai prêté mon échelle à mon voisin.
items.en: I lent my ladder to my neighbor.
items.ipa: ʒe pʁɛ.te mɔ̃.n‿e.ʃɛl a mɔ̃ vwa.zɛ̃
items.notes: “prêté” keeps the circumflex accent from “prêter”, don't drop it.

items.fr: Ma voisine est toujours prête à rendre service.
items.en: My neighbor is always ready to help out.
items.ipa: ma vwa.zin ɛ tu.ʒuʁ pʁɛt a ʁɑ̃dʁ sɛʁ.vis
items.notes: “prête” ends in e to agree with the feminine “voisine”.

items.fr: Toutes les voisines se sont réunies pour aider Mme Dubois après son opération.
items.en: All the neighbors got together to help Mrs. Dubois after her surgery.
items.ipa: tut le vwa.zin sə sɔ̃ ʁe.y.ni puʁ ɛ.de ma.dam dy.bwa a.pʁɛ sɔ̃.n‿ɔ.pe.ʁa.sjɔ̃
items.notes: “réunies” takes -es to agree with the feminine plural subject “voisines”.

items.fr: Les gens du quartier s'entraident beaucoup.
items.en: People in the neighborhood help each other out a lot.
items.ipa: le ʒɑ̃ dy kaʁ.tje sɑ̃.tʁɛd bo.ku
items.notes: The final -s in “gens” is silent.

items.fr: Nous avons offert notre aide immédiatement.
items.en: We offered our help right away.
items.notes: There's a liaison between “nous” and “avons”: “nous_avons”.

items.fr: Elle a besoin d'aide pour finir ses cartons.
items.en: She needs help finishing her boxes.
items.ipa: ɛl a bə.zwɛ̃ dɛd puʁ fi.niʁ se kaʁ.tɔ̃
items.notes: “de” becomes “d'” before the vowel in “aide”.

items.fr: Si tu as besoin, appelle-moi sans hésiter.
items.en: If you need anything, just call me.
items.ipa: si ty a bə.zwɛ̃ a.pɛl.mwa sɑ̃ e.zi.te
items.notes: After “si” in this kind of sentence, the verb stays in the present: “tu as”.

items.fr: Elle nous a beaucoup aidés cette semaine.
items.en: She helped us a lot this week.
items.ipa: ɛl nu.z‿a bo.ku ɛ.de sɛt sə.mɛn
items.notes: “aidés” agrees with “nous” because the direct object comes before the verb in the passé composé.

items.fr: C'est agréable de pouvoir compter sur ses proches.
items.en: It's nice to be able to count on the people close to you.
items.ipa: sɛ.t‿a.gʁe.abl də pu.vwaʁ kɔ̃.te syʁ se pʁɔʃ
items.notes: “agréable” is spelled with é, not è, even though it sounds similar.

items.fr: Mon voisin se propose souvent pour garder les enfants.
items.en: My neighbor often offers to look after the kids.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ vwa.zɛ̃ sə pʁɔ.poz su.vɑ̃ puʁ gaʁ.de le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃
items.notes: “se propose” uses the reflexive pronoun “se”, not the demonstrative “ce”.

items.fr: J'ai été très touché par sa générosité.
items.en: I was really touched by her generosity.
items.ipa: ʒe e.te tʁɛ tu.ʃe paʁ sa ʒe.ne.ʁo.zi.te
items.notes: “été” has two accents aigus, don't confuse it with the unaccented “ete”.

items.fr: Notre voisine est très dévouée envers sa famille.
items.en: Our neighbor is very devoted to her family.
items.ipa: nɔtʁ vwa.zin ɛ tʁɛ de.vwe ɑ̃.vɛʁ sa fa.mij
items.notes: “dévouée” ends in -ée to agree with the feminine “voisine”.

items.fr: Les voisins se sont entraidés pendant la tempête.
items.en: The neighbors helped each other during the storm.
items.ipa: le vwa.zɛ̃ sə sɔ̃.t‿ɑ̃.tʁɛ.de pɑ̃.dɑ̃ la tɑ̃.pɛt
items.notes: “entraidés” takes a final s to agree with the plural subject “les voisins”.

items.fr: Il nous a beaucoup aidés, c'est un homme fiable.
items.en: He helped us a lot, he's a reliable man.
items.ipa: il nu.z‿a bo.ku ɛ.de sɛ.t‿œ̃.n‿ɔm fjabl
items.notes: The h in “homme” is silent.

items.fr: Elles ont accepté immédiatement de nous aider.
items.en: They immediately agreed to help us.
items.notes: There's a liaison between “elles” and “ont”: “elles_ont”.

items.fr: Je n'hésite jamais à aider mes voisins.
items.en: I never hesitate to help my neighbors.
items.ipa: ʒə ne.zit ʒa.mɛ a ɛ.de me vwa.zɛ̃
items.notes: “ne” becomes “n'” before “hésite” because the h is silent.

items.fr: Il vaut mieux demander de l'aide que rester bloqué.
items.en: It's better to ask for help than to stay stuck.
items.ipa: il vo mjø də.mɑ̃.de də lɛd kə ʁɛs.te blɔ.ke
items.notes: After “il vaut mieux”, the next verb stays in the infinitive: “demander”.

items.fr: Nous les aiderons dès que possible.
items.en: We'll help them as soon as possible.
items.notes: “aiderons” is the nous-form of the futur simple of “aider”.

items.fr: Mon amie m'a beaucoup soutenue cette année.
items.en: My friend supported me a lot this year.
items.notes: “soutenue” keeps the u from “soutenir” before adding the feminine ending.

items.fr: Tu veux que je t'aide à porter ça ?
items.en: Do you want me to help you carry that?
items.ipa: ty vø kə ʒə tɛd a pɔʁ.te sa
items.notes: French requires a space before the question mark: “ça ?”.

items.fr: On peut toujours compter sur nos voisins.
items.en: We can always count on our neighbors.
items.ipa: ɔ̃ pø tu.ʒuʁ kɔ̃.te syʁ no vwa.zɛ̃
items.notes: “on” (subject pronoun) sounds like “ont” (from avoir), but only “on” fits here.

items.fr: Mon père a réparé le vélo de mon frère aîné.
items.en: My dad fixed my older brother's bike.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ pɛʁ a ʁe.pa.ʁe lə ve.lo də mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ ɛ.ne
items.notes: “aîné” needs a circumflex accent on the i.

items.fr: Sa cousine est venue l'aider à peindre sa chambre.
items.en: Her cousin came to help her paint her room.
items.ipa: sa ku.zin ɛ və.ny lɛ.de a pɛ̃dʁ sa ʃɑ̃bʁ
items.notes: “venue” ends in e to agree with the feminine subject “sa cousine”.

items.fr: Mes deux sœurs sont venues m'aider à cuisiner.
items.en: My two sisters came to help me cook.
items.ipa: me dø sœʁ sɔ̃ və.ny mɛ.de a kɥi.zi.ne
items.notes: “venues” takes -es to agree with the feminine plural subject “mes deux sœurs”.

items.fr: Elle sait qu'elle peut toujours compter sur nous.
items.en: She knows she can always count on us.
items.ipa: ɛl sɛ kɛl pø tu.ʒuʁ kɔ̃.te syʁ nu
items.notes: The final t in “sait” is silent.

items.fr: Vous avez besoin d'un coup de main ?
items.ipa: vu.z‿a.ve bə.zwɛ̃ dœ̃ ku də mɛ̃
items.notes: There's a liaison between “vous” and “avez”: “vous_avez”.

items.fr: Je l'ai aidée à trouver du travail.
items.en: I helped her find a job.
items.ipa: ʒə lɛ ɛ.de a tʁu.ve dy tʁa.vaj
items.notes: “la” becomes “l'” before “ai”, and “aidée” agrees with the feminine “l'” (her).

items.fr: Elle aide toujours ceux qui en ont besoin.
items.en: She always helps those who need it.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛd tu.ʒuʁ sø ki ɑ̃.n‿ɔ̃ bə.zwɛ̃
items.notes: “qui” is the relative pronoun used because it's the subject of “ont besoin”.

items.fr: Ils nous aident chaque fois que nous en avons besoin.
items.en: They help us every time we need it.
items.ipa: il nu.z‿ɛd ʃak fwa kə nu.z‿ɑ̃.n‿a.vɔ̃ bə.zwɛ̃
items.notes: “aident” ends in -ent for the ils/elles form of “aider”.

items.fr: Ses proches l'ont beaucoup soutenu quand il a perdu son emploi.
items.en: His loved ones supported him a lot when he lost his job.
items.ipa: se pʁɔʃ lɔ̃ bo.ku sut.ny kɑ̃.t‿il a pɛʁ.dy sɔ̃.n‿ɑ̃.plwa
items.notes: “ses” (his/her) and “ces” (these) sound the same, but only “ses” fits before “proches” here.

items.fr: Elle a été présente à chaque étape, même dans les moments les plus difficiles.
items.en: She was there every step of the way, even during the hardest moments.
items.ipa: ɛl a e.te pʁe.zɑ̃t a ʃak e.tap mɛm dɑ̃ le mɔ.mɑ̃ le ply di.fi.sil
items.notes: “étape” needs an accent aigu on the first e.

items.fr: Sa meilleure amie s'est montrée particulièrement attentionnée quand elle traversait une période difficile.
items.en: Her best friend was especially caring while she was going through a rough patch.
items.ipa: sa mɛ.jœʁ a.mi sɛ mɔ̃.tʁe paʁ.ti.ky.ljɛʁ.mɑ̃ a.tɑ̃.sjɔ.ne kɑ̃.t‿ɛl tʁa.vɛʁ.sɛ yn pe.ʁjɔd di.fi.sil
items.notes: “montrée” and “attentionnée” both agree in the feminine with “amie”.

items.fr: Les voisines se sont relayées pour s'occuper des enfants pendant son hospitalisation.
items.en: The neighbors took turns looking after the kids while she was in the hospital.
items.ipa: le vwa.zin sə sɔ̃ ʁə.lɛ.je puʁ sɔ.ky.pe de.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ pɑ̃.dɑ̃ sɔ̃.n‿ɔs.pi.ta.li.za.sjɔ̃
items.notes: “relayées” agrees in the feminine plural with “les voisines”.

items.fr: Elle ne voulait pas être un poids pour ses amis, mais elle a fini par accepter leur aide.
items.en: She didn't want to be a burden on her friends, but she ended up accepting their help.
items.ipa: ɛl nə vu.lɛ pa ɛtʁ œ̃ pwa puʁ se.z‿a.mi mɛ ɛl a fi.ni paʁ ak.sɛp.te lœʁ ɛd
items.notes: The final d in “poids” is silent.

items.fr: Ils ont énormément aidé leur voisine après son accident.
items.en: They helped their neighbor enormously after her accident.
items.ipa: il.z‿ɔ̃.t‿e.nɔʁ.me.mɑ̃ ɛ.de lœʁ vwa.zin a.pʁɛ sɔ̃.n‿ak.si.dɑ̃
items.notes: There's a liaison between “ont” and “énormément”: “ont_énormément”.

items.fr: Puisqu'elle n'avait personne pour l'aider, ses collègues se sont proposés spontanément.
items.en: Since she had no one to help her, her coworkers stepped in on their own.
items.ipa: pɥis.kɛl na.vɛ pɛʁ.sɔn puʁ lɛ.de se kɔ.lɛg sə sɔ̃ pʁɔ.po.ze spɔ̃.ta.ne.mɑ̃
items.notes: “puisque” becomes “puisqu'” before the vowel in “elle”.

items.fr: Il aurait aimé qu'on l'aide davantage à l'époque.
items.en: He would have liked to be helped more back then.
items.ipa: il o.ʁɛ ɛ.me kɔ̃ lɛd da.vɑ̃.taʒ a le.pɔk
items.notes: After “il aurait aimé que”, the verb goes in the subjunctive: “qu'on l'aide”.

items.fr: Si elle avait demandé de l'aide plus tôt, elle aurait évité bien des soucis.

items.ipa: si ɛl a.vɛ də.mɑ̃.de də lɛd ply to ɛl o.ʁɛ e.vi.te bjɛ̃ de su.si
items.notes: The “si” clause uses the plus-que-parfait “avait demandé”, paired with the conditionnel passé.

items.fr: Leur solidarité nous a profondément touchés pendant cette épreuve.

items.ipa: lœʁ sɔ.li.da.ʁi.te nu.z‿a pʁɔ.fɔ̃.de.mɑ̃ tu.ʃe pɑ̃.dɑ̃ sɛ.t‿e.pʁœv

items.fr: Pourquoi ne m'as-tu pas demandé de l'aide plus tôt ?

items.ipa: puʁ.kwa nə ma.ty pa də.mɑ̃.de də lɛd ply to
items.notes: There must be a space before the question mark, and a hyphen links “as-tu” in the inversion.

items.fr: Quand on l'a vu si fatigué, on a tout de suite proposé de l'aider.

items.fr: Grâce à l'entraide de ses collègues, elle a pu terminer le projet à temps.

items.fr: Elle s'est sentie soutenue dès qu'elle a expliqué sa situation à ses amis.

items.fr: Les habitants du quartier se sont mobilisés pour aider la famille sinistrée.
