items.fr: Elle a fini par savoir ce qui s'était vraiment passé.
items.en: She eventually found out what had really happened.

items.fr: Il est huit heures et quart.
items.notes: The liaison in “huit heures” makes the final “t” of “huit” pronounced.

items.fr: Le magasin ouvre à neuf heures.
items.en: The store opens at nine o'clock.
items.notes: The liaison in “neuf heures” pronounces “neuf” as [nœv], not the usual [nœf].

items.fr: Nous nous levons tous les jours à sept heures.
items.en: We get up every day at seven o'clock.
items.ipa: nu nu lə.vɔ̃ tu le ʒuʁ a sɛ.t‿œʁ
items.notes: In “tous les jours”, the final “s” of “tous” stays silent because it comes right before the noun.
The inverted “est-il” needs the linking “t” between “est” and “il”.
“midi” never takes an article after “à”, unlike “le matin” or “le soir”.
“minuit” is masculine, so avoid writing “la minuit”.
The final “s” in “toujours” stays silent, unlike the plural noun “jours”.

items.fr: Il est une heure de l'après-midi.
items.en: It's one o'clock in the afternoon.
items.notes: “après” needs its grave accent on the “è”, easy to drop when writing fast.

items.fr: Le cours commence à quatorze heures.
items.en: The class starts at two o'clock in the afternoon.
items.notes: Official schedules use “quatorze heures”, not “deux heures”, to avoid ambiguity.

items.fr: Nous avons rendez-vous à seize heures trente.
items.en: We have an appointment at four thirty in the afternoon.
items.notes: “rendez-vous” keeps its hyphens and stays singular even though it names one meeting.

items.fr: Le musée est fermé le lundi.
items.en: The museum is closed on Mondays.
items.ipa: lə my.ze ɛ fɛʁ.me lə lœ̃.di
items.notes: Days of the week like “lundi” never take a capital letter in French.

items.fr: Je fais du sport tous les mardis.
items.ipa: ʒə fɛ dy spɔʁ tu le maʁ.di
items.notes: “mardis” takes an “s” here because “tous les” makes the day plural and habitual.

items.fr: Il travaille du lundi au vendredi.
items.en: He works from Monday to Friday.
items.ipa: il tʁa.vaj dy lœ̃.di o vɑ̃.dʁə.di
items.notes: “au” is the required contraction of “à” and “le” before “vendredi”, not “à le”.

items.fr: Le dimanche, nous restons à la maison.
items.ipa: lə di.mɑ̃ʃ nu ʁɛs.tɔ̃ a la mɛ.zɔ̃
items.notes: “dimanche” with “le” in front expresses a habit, not one specific Sunday.

items.fr: Quelle est l'heure de fermeture du magasin ?
items.en: What is the store's closing time?
items.ipa: kɛ.l ɛ l‿œʁ də fɛʁ.mə.tyʁ dy ma.ga.zɛ̃
items.notes: “l'heure” elides “la” before the vowel sound of “heure”.

items.fr: Le réveil sonne à six heures et demie.
items.en: The alarm clock rings at half past six.
items.ipa: lə ʁe.vɛj sɔn a si.z‿œʁ e də.mi
items.notes: “demie” agrees in the feminine because it refers back to “heure”.

items.fr: Il est presque l'heure du déjeuner.
items.ipa: i.l ɛ pʁɛs.k l‿œʁ dy de.ʒœ.ne
items.notes: “l'heure” takes the elided article, never “la heure”.
“chaque” stays singular and never adds an “s”, even though it implies repetition.

items.fr: Le bus arrive à sept heures moins le quart.
items.en: The bus arrives at a quarter to seven.
items.ipa: lə bys a.ʁiv a sɛ.t‿œʁ mwɛ̃ lə kaʁ
items.notes: The final “t” of “quart” stays silent.

items.fr: Es-tu à l'heure pour le travail ?
items.en: Are you on time for work?
items.ipa: ɛ.ty a l‿œʁ puʁ lə tʁa.vaj
items.notes: “à l'heure” means “on time” and never drops its elided article.

items.fr: Le film commence dans dix minutes.
items.en: The movie starts in ten minutes.
items.ipa: lə film kɔ.mɑ̃s dɑ̃ di mi.nyt
items.notes: “dix” loses its final consonant sound before a consonant like “minutes”.

items.fr: À quelle heure pars-tu le matin ?
items.en: What time do you leave in the morning?
items.ipa: a kɛ.l œʁ paʁ ty lə ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: “à” needs its accent to mean “at”, unlike “a” from the verb “avoir”.

items.fr: Le matin, je bois du café avant de partir.
items.en: In the morning, I drink coffee before leaving.
items.ipa: lə ma.tɛ̃ ʒə bwa dy ka.fe a.vɑ̃ də paʁ.tiʁ
items.notes: “matin” is masculine, so it takes “le”, never “la”.

items.fr: Ils dorment jusqu'à neuf heures le week-end.
items.en: They sleep until nine o'clock on weekends.
items.ipa: il dɔʁm ʒys.k‿a nœ.v‿œʁ lə wik.ɛnd
items.notes: “jusqu'à” elides “jusque” before the vowel of “à”.
“horaire” starts with a mute “h”, so “notre” never becomes “not'”.

items.fr: La réunion dure une heure entière.
items.en: The meeting lasts a whole hour.
items.ipa: la ʁe.y.njɔ̃ dyʁ y.n œʁ ɑ̃.tjɛʁ
items.notes: “entière” agrees in the feminine with “heure”, not “entier”.

items.fr: Le magasin est ouvert de neuf heures à dix-neuf heures.
items.en: The store is open from nine to seven in the evening.
items.ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ ɛ.t‿u.vɛʁ də nœ.v‿œʁ a diz.nœ.v‿œʁ
items.notes: “ouvert” must agree with the masculine “magasin”, not “ouverte”.

items.fr: Chaque jour, il vérifie l'heure sur son téléphone.
items.en: Every day, he checks the time on his phone.
items.ipa: ʃak ʒuʁ i.l ve.ʁi.fi l‿œʁ syʁ sɔ̃ te.le.fɔn
items.notes: “chaque jour” is singular, unlike “tous les jours” which uses the plural noun.

items.fr: D'habitude, l'équipe se réunit à dix heures précises.
items.en: Usually, the team meets at exactly ten o'clock.
items.ipa: da.by.tyd le.kip sə ʁe.y.ni a di.z‿œʁ pʁe.siz
items.notes: “précises” agrees in the feminine plural with “heures”.

items.fr: Le vol décolle à vingt heures dix.
items.en: The flight takes off at eight ten in the evening.
items.ipa: lə vɔl de.kɔl a vɛ̃.t‿œʁ dis
items.notes: The liaison before “heures” makes the “t” of “vingt” pronounced.

items.fr: Elle change souvent son emploi du temps.
items.ipa: ɛl ʃɑ̃ʒ su.vɑ̃ sɔ.n‿ɑ̃.plwa dy tɑ̃
items.notes: “emploi” takes “son” because it is masculine, not “sa emploi”.

items.fr: Nous avons cours tous les jours sauf le dimanche.
items.en: We have class every day except Sunday.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ kuʁ tu le ʒuʁ so lə di.mɑ̃ʃ
items.notes: “sauf” never changes form, whatever the gender or number that follows.

items.fr: À quelle heure ferme la pharmacie le samedi ?
items.en: What time does the pharmacy close on Saturdays?
items.ipa: a kɛ.l œʁ fɛʁm la faʁ.ma.si lə sam.di
items.notes: “samedi” never gets a capital letter, even meaning “on Saturdays”.

items.fr: Le directeur arrive rarement avant huit heures.
items.en: The director rarely arrives before eight o'clock.
items.ipa: lə di.ʁɛk.tœʁ a.ʁiv ʁaʁ.mɑ̃ a.vɑ̃ ɥi.t‿œʁ
items.notes: “rarement” keeps the base adjective's spelling “rare” plus “ment”, with no extra “e”.

items.fr: Ils se retrouvent chaque vendredi soir au café.
items.en: They meet up every Friday evening at the café.
items.ipa: il sə ʁə.tʁuv ʃak vɑ̃.dʁə.di swaʁ o ka.fe
items.notes: “chaque” is invariable, whether the noun after it is masculine or feminine.

items.fr: Le magasin reste ouvert jusqu'à vingt-deux heures.
items.en: The store stays open until ten in the evening.
items.notes: “vingt” pronounces its final “t” inside compound numbers like “vingt-deux”, even though it stays silent when used alone.

items.fr: Elle a deux rendez-vous cet après-midi.
items.en: She has two appointments this afternoon.
items.notes: “cet” replaces “ce” before the vowel sound of “après-midi”.

items.fr: Nous nous voyons une fois par semaine.
items.en: We see each other once a week.
items.ipa: nu nu vwa.jɔ̃ yn fwa paʁ sə.mɛn
items.notes: “fois” sounds like “foie” and “foi”, but only “fois” fits after “une”.
“quarante” ends in “-ante”, not “-ente” as “trente” might suggest.

items.fr: À quelle heure te lèves-tu d'habitude ?
items.en: What time do you usually get up?
items.ipa: a kɛ.l œʁ tə lɛv ty da.by.tyd
items.notes: “lèves” takes a grave accent because the stem vowel is stressed in this conjugation.

items.fr: Ils ont changé l'horaire des trains ce mois-ci.
items.en: They changed the train schedule this month.
items.ipa: i.l ɔ̃ ʃɑ̃.ʒe lɔ.ʁɛʁ de tʁɛ̃ sə mwa.si
items.notes: “ont” (from avoir) sounds like “on”, but only “ont” fits before the past participle.

items.fr: Le lundi matin, les bureaux ouvrent plus tard.
items.en: On Monday mornings, the offices open later.
items.ipa: lə lœ̃.di ma.tɛ̃ le by.ʁo u.vʁ ply taʁ
items.notes: “ouvrent” keeps a silent “-ent” ending, typical of third-person plural verbs.

items.fr: Il faut arriver avant l'heure prévue pour la réunion.
items.en: You must arrive before the scheduled time for the meeting.
items.ipa: il fo a.ʁi.ve a.vɑ̃ l‿œʁ pʁe.vy puʁ la ʁe.y.njɔ̃
items.notes: “avant” takes a noun directly here, without needing “que” and a subjunctive verb.

items.fr: Le déjeuner est servi à midi et demi.
items.en: Lunch is served at half past noon.
items.ipa: lə de.ʒœ.ne ɛ sɛʁ.vi a mi.di e də.mi
items.notes: “demi” stays masculine here because it follows “midi”, unlike “et demie” after “heure”.

items.fr: Chaque matin, elle vérifie deux fois son réveil.
items.en: Every morning, she checks her alarm clock twice.
items.ipa: ʃak ma.tɛ̃ ɛl ve.ʁi.fi dø fwa sɔ̃ ʁe.vɛj
items.notes: “deux fois” needs no article, unlike “les deux fois” which would refer to specific occasions.

items.fr: L'horaire d'ouverture affiché est-il à jour ?
items.en: Is the posted opening schedule up to date?
items.ipa: lɔ.ʁɛʁ du.vɛʁ.tyʁ a.fi.ʃe ɛ.til a ʒuʁ
items.notes: “affiché” agrees with the masculine “horaire”, so no extra “e” is added.

items.fr: Nous répétons cet exercice trois fois par jour.
items.en: We repeat this exercise three times a day.
items.ipa: nu ʁe.pe.tɔ̃ sɛ.t‿ɛg.zɛʁ.sis tʁwa fwa paʁ ʒuʁ
items.notes: “répétons” needs an acute accent on both “e”s of the stem “répét-”.

items.fr: Son emploi du temps est plus chargé que le mien.
items.en: Her schedule is busier than mine.
items.ipa: sɔ.n‿ɑ̃.plwa dy tɑ̃ ɛ ply ʃaʁ.ʒe kə lə mjɛ̃
items.notes: “temps” ends in a silent “p” and “s”, both unpronounced.

items.fr: Le vol atterrit à vingt et une heures.
items.en: The flight lands at nine in the evening.
items.ipa: lə vɔl a.tɛ.ʁi a vɛ̃.t‿e yn œʁ
items.notes: “une” agrees with the feminine “heures”, so it is “vingt et une”, not “vingt et un”.

items.fr: Ils travaillent en horaires décalés cette semaine.
items.en: They are working staggered hours this week.
items.ipa: il tʁa.vaj ɑ̃.n‿ɔ.ʁɛʁ de.ka.le sɛt sə.mɛn
items.notes: “décalés” agrees in the masculine plural with “horaires”.

items.fr: Le magasin n'ouvre jamais avant huit heures.
items.en: The store never opens before eight o'clock.
items.ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ nu.vʁ ʒa.mɛ a.vɑ̃ ɥi.t‿œʁ
items.notes: “n'ouvre” needs both parts of the negation, “ne” and “jamais”, even in speech.

items.fr: À quelle heure est prévu le prochain rendez-vous ?
items.en: What time is the next appointment scheduled for?
items.ipa: a kɛ.l œʁ ɛ pʁe.vy lə pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃ ʁɑ̃.de.vu
items.notes: “prévu” agrees with the masculine “rendez-vous”, so it stays without a final “e”.

items.fr: Bien qu'il soit déjà tard, le magasin reste ouvert.
items.en: Even though it's already late, the store stays open.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃ ki.l swa de.ʒa taʁ lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ ʁɛs.t‿u.vɛʁ
items.notes: “bien que” triggers the subjunctive, so “soit” replaces “est”.

items.fr: Si j'avais su l'horaire, je serais arrivé à l'heure.
items.en: If I had known the schedule, I would have arrived on time.
items.ipa: si ʒa.vɛ sy lɔ.ʁɛʁ ʒə sə.ʁɛ.z‿a.ʁi.ve a l‿œʁ
items.notes: The hypothesis in “si j'avais su” takes the pluperfect, paired with the past conditional.

items.fr: Quel que soit l'horaire, elle arrive toujours en avance.
items.en: Whatever the schedule is, she always arrives early.
items.ipa: kɛl kə swa lɔ.ʁɛʁ ɛl a.ʁiv tu.ʒuʁ ɑ̃.n‿a.vɑ̃s
items.notes: “quel” agrees with “horaire” in “quel que soit”, not with the following clause.

items.fr: Le train aurait dû partir à quinze heures pile.
items.en: The train was supposed to leave at exactly three in the afternoon.
items.ipa: lə tʁɛ̃ o.ʁɛ dy paʁ.tiʁ a kɛ̃.z‿œʁ pil
items.notes: “aurait dû” uses the past conditional of “devoir” to express an unmet obligation.

items.fr: Dès que l'horloge sonnera, la réunion commencera.
items.en: As soon as the clock strikes, the meeting will start.
items.ipa: dɛ kə lɔʁ.lɔʒ sɔ.nə.ʁa la ʁe.y.njɔ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃.sə.ʁa
items.notes: After “dès que” referring to the future, French uses the future tense, not the present.

items.fr: L'horaire dont je te parlais a encore changé.
items.en: The schedule I was telling you about has changed again.
items.ipa: lɔ.ʁɛʁ dɔ̃ ʒə tə paʁ.lɛ a ɑ̃.kɔʁ ʃɑ̃.ʒe
items.notes: “dont” replaces “de + horaire”, so “de” is never repeated afterward.

items.fr: Quoique la réunion soit prévue à midi, elle commence souvent en retard.
items.en: Although the meeting is scheduled for noon, it often starts late.
items.ipa: kwa.kə la ʁe.y.njɔ̃ swa pʁe.vy a mi.di ɛl kɔ.mɑ̃s su.vɑ̃ ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ
items.notes: “quoique” is one word meaning “although” and takes the subjunctive, unlike “quoi que” (whatever).

items.fr: Nous nous demandions à quelle heure ils arriveraient.
items.en: We were wondering what time they would arrive.
items.ipa: nu nu də.mɑ̃.djɔ̃ a kɛ.l œʁ i.l a.ʁi.və.ʁɛ
items.notes: “arriveraient” is the conditional, matching the reported future inside a past sentence.

items.fr: C'est l'horaire le plus chargé que nous ayons jamais eu.
items.en: It's the busiest schedule we've ever had.
items.ipa: sɛ lɔ.ʁɛʁ lə ply ʃaʁ.ʒe kə nu.z‿ɛ.jɔ̃ ʒa.mɛ y
items.notes: The superlative “le plus chargé que” calls for the subjunctive “ayons”, not “avons”.

items.fr: Au cas où l'horaire changerait, préviens-nous à temps.
items.en: In case the schedule changes, let us know in time.
items.ipa: o ka u lɔ.ʁɛʁ ʃɑ̃ʒ.ʁɛ pʁe.vjɛ̃ nu a tɑ̃
items.notes: “au cas où” is followed by the conditional, not the present or future.

items.fr: Plus l'heure du départ approche, plus il devient nerveux.
items.en: The closer the departure time gets, the more nervous he becomes.
items.ipa: ply l‿œʁ dy de.paʁ a.pʁɔʃ ply i.l də.vjɛ̃ nɛʁ.vø
items.notes: The construction “plus... plus...” needs no “que” between the two clauses, unlike English.

items.fr: L'employé auquel je me suis adressé connaissait l'horaire par cœur.
items.en: The employee I spoke to knew the schedule by heart.
items.ipa: lɑ̃.plwa.je o.kɛl ʒə mə sɥi.z‿a.dʁɛ.se kɔ.nɛ.sɛ lɔ.ʁɛʁ paʁ kœʁ
items.notes: “auquel” contracts “à” and “lequel” to refer back to “l'employé”, agreeing in gender and number.

items.fr: Il se peut que l'horaire soit encore modifié d'ici demain.
items.en: It's possible that the schedule will be changed again by tomorrow.
items.ipa: il sə pø kə lɔ.ʁɛʁ swa ɑ̃.kɔʁ mɔ.di.fje di.si də.mɛ̃
items.notes: “il se peut que” always requires the subjunctive “soit”, never the indicative “est”.

items.fr: Je bois toujours un café le matin.
items.en: I always drink coffee in the morning.
items.ipa: ʒə bwa tu.ʒuʁ ɛ̃ ka.fe lə ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: “bois” is a homophone of “bois” (wood), but here it's the verb “boire” conjugated for “je”.

items.fr: Elle ne sort jamais le soir.
items.en: She never goes out in the evening.
items.ipa: ɛl nə sɔʁ ʒa.mɛ lə swaʁ
items.notes: “jamais” needs “ne” before the verb to form a complete negation.

items.en: We sometimes eat at a restaurant.
items.notes: “parfois” is spelled as one single word.
“souvent” ends in a silent “t”, not pronounced as in “vent”.

items.en: I have been living here for two years.
items.notes: “depuis” pairs with the present tense here, not the passé composé.

items.fr: Nous avons vécu à Lyon pendant trois ans.
items.en: We lived in Lyon for three years.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ve.ky a ljɔ̃ pɑ̃.dɑ̃ tʁwa.z‿ɑ̃
items.notes: “pendant” works with a finished action, unlike “depuis” which needs an ongoing one.

items.fr: Il est parti il y a une heure.
items.ipa: i.l ɛ paʁ.ti i.l i a yn œʁ
items.notes: “il y a” placed before a duration means “ago”, not “there is”.

items.fr: Je fais rarement la grasse matinée.
items.ipa: ʒə fɛ ʁaʁ.mɑ̃ la gʁas ma.ti.ne
items.notes: “matinée” takes a final “e” because it is feminine, unlike “matin”.

items.fr: Elle est toujours en retard le lundi.
items.en: She is always late on Mondays.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛ tu.ʒuʁ ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ lə lœ̃.di
items.notes: “toujours” placed after “est” describes a habit, so it needs no extra “que”.

items.fr: Nous nous voyons de temps en temps.
items.en: We see each other from time to time.
items.ipa: nu nu vwa.jɔ̃ də tɑ̃.z‿ɑ̃ tɑ̃
items.notes: “temps” keeps the same silent spelling in both parts of this fixed phrase.

items.fr: Il travaille chaque jour sauf le week-end.
items.en: He works every day except on weekends.
items.ipa: il tʁa.vaj ʃak ʒuʁ so lə wik.ɛnd
items.notes: “chaque” never adds an “s”, even before a noun implying repetition.

items.fr: Elle fume encore, mais moins souvent qu'avant.
items.en: She still smokes, but less often than before.
items.ipa: ɛl fym ɑ̃.kɔʁ mɛ mwɛ̃ su.vɑ̃ ka.vɑ̃
items.notes: “qu'avant” elides “que” before the vowel sound of “avant”.

items.fr: Ils vivent en France depuis longtemps.
items.en: They have been living in France for a long time.
items.ipa: il viv ɑ̃ fʁɑ̃s də.pɥi lɔ̃.tɑ̃
items.notes: “longtemps” is written as a single word, not “long temps”.

items.fr: Je ne bois plus jamais de soda.
items.ipa: ʒə nə bwa ply ʒa.mɛ də sɔ.da
items.notes: “plus jamais” combines two negative words together correctly, without “pas”.

items.fr: Nous allons au marché tous les samedis.
items.en: We go to the market every Saturday.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ o maʁ.ʃe tu le sam.di
items.notes: “tous” keeps its final “s” silent because it comes right before “les”.

items.fr: Elle range sa chambre deux fois par mois.
items.en: She tidies her room twice a month.
items.ipa: ɛl ʁɑ̃ʒ sa ʃɑ̃bʁ dø fwa paʁ mwa
items.notes: “fois” never changes spelling between singular and plural, so “deux fois” looks just like “une fois”.

items.fr: Ils sont mariés depuis dix ans.
items.en: They have been married for ten years.
items.notes: “sont” (from être) sounds like “son”, but only “sont” fits with “mariés”.

items.fr: Je révise mes leçons chaque soir avant de dormir.
items.en: I review my lessons every evening before sleeping.
items.ipa: ʒə ʁe.viz me lə.sɔ̃ ʃak swaʁ a.vɑ̃ də dɔʁ.miʁ
items.notes: “chaque” agrees with nothing, staying identical before masculine “soir” or a feminine noun.

items.fr: Nous avons attendu pendant deux heures.
items.notes: “pendant” introduces a completed span of waiting, matched here with the passé composé.

items.fr: Il ne pleut presque jamais ici en été.
items.en: It almost never rains here in summer.
items.ipa: il nə plø pʁɛs.k ʒa.mɛ i.si ɑ̃.n‿e.te
items.notes: “presque” keeps its final “e”, unlike “quelque” before a vowel.

items.fr: Elle arrive toujours à l'heure, jamais en retard.
items.en: She always arrives on time, never late.
items.ipa: ɛl a.ʁiv tu.ʒuʁ a l‿œʁ ʒa.mɛ ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ
items.notes: “à l'heure” elides its article, unlike “en retard” which uses no article at all.

items.en: We are leaving in two days.
items.notes: “dans” before a future duration means “in”, not “during” like “pendant”.

items.fr: D'habitude, elle ne travaille jamais le week-end.
items.en: Usually, she never works on weekends.
items.ipa: da.by.tyd ɛl nə tʁa.vaj ʒa.mɛ lə wik.ɛnd
items.notes: “d'habitude” elides “de” before the vowel of “habitude”.

items.fr: Il fait souvent la même erreur, encore et encore.
items.en: He often makes the same mistake, again and again.
items.ipa: il fɛ su.vɑ̃ la mɛm ɛ.ʁœʁ ɑ̃.kɔ.ʁ e ɑ̃.kɔʁ
items.notes: “même” needs a circumflex accent, unlike “meme” without one.

items.fr: Cela fait trois ans que nous habitons ici.
items.en: We have been living here for three years.
items.ipa: sə.la fɛ tʁwa.z‿ɑ̃ kə nu.z‿a.bi.tɔ̃ i.si
items.notes: “cela fait... que” takes the present tense, just like “depuis”, to show an ongoing state.

items.fr: Nous nous appelons de temps à autre.
items.en: We call each other from time to time.
items.notes: “de temps à autre” keeps “autre” invariable, without a final “s”.

items.fr: Elle n'a pas revu ses amis depuis des mois.
items.en: She hasn't seen her friends again for months.
items.ipa: ɛl na pa ʁə.vy se.z‿a.mi də.pɥi de mwa
items.notes: In a negative sentence, “depuis” can pair with the passé composé, unlike in a positive one.

items.fr: Il conduit prudemment, il n'a jamais eu d'accident.
items.en: He drives carefully, he has never had an accident.
items.ipa: il kɔ̃.dɥi pʁy.da.mɑ̃ i.l na ʒa.mɛ y dak.si.dɑ̃
items.notes: “prudemment” is built from “prudent” but written with “-emment”, not “-amment”.

items.fr: Nous partirons dans quelques jours seulement.
items.en: We will leave in just a few days.
items.ipa: nu paʁ.ti.ʁɔ̃ dɑ̃ kɛl.kə ʒuʁ sœl.mɑ̃
items.notes: “quelques” takes an “s” here because it modifies the plural “jours”.

items.fr: Ils se disputent rarement, mais quand ça arrive, c'est bruyant.
items.en: They rarely argue, but when it happens, it's loud.
items.ipa: il sə dis.pyt ʁaʁ.mɑ̃ mɛ kɑ̃ sa a.ʁiv sɛ bʁɥi.jɑ̃
items.notes: “quand” sounds like “qu'en”, but only “quand” fits as a time conjunction here.

items.fr: Depuis combien de temps apprends-tu le français ?
items.en: How long have you been learning French?
items.ipa: də.pɥi kɔ̃.bjɛ̃ də tɑ̃ a.pʁɑ̃ ty lə fʁɑ̃.sɛ
items.notes: “depuis combien de temps” asks about an ongoing duration, unlike “depuis quand” which asks for a starting point.

items.fr: Il a plu pendant toute la journée hier.
items.ipa: i.l a ply pɑ̃.dɑ̃ tut la ʒuʁ.ne jɛʁ
items.notes: “toute” agrees in the feminine with “journée”, not “tout”.

items.fr: Nous sortons rarement en semaine, seulement le week-end.
items.en: We rarely go out on weekdays, only on weekends.
items.ipa: nu sɔʁ.tɔ̃ ʁaʁ.mɑ̃ ɑ̃ sə.mɛn sœl.mɑ̃ lə wik.ɛnd
items.notes: “rarement” is formed from “rare” plus “-ment”, with no doubled consonant.

items.fr: Elle a toujours été ponctuelle, même enfant.
items.en: She has always been punctual, even as a child.
items.ipa: ɛl a tu.ʒuʁ e.te pɔ̃k.tɥɛl mɛ.m‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃
items.notes: “ponctuelle” doubles the “l” and adds “e” to agree with the feminine “elle”.

items.fr: Je n'ai pas vu ce film depuis des années.
items.en: I haven't seen this movie in years.
items.ipa: ʒə nɛ pa vy sə film də.pɥi de.z‿a.ne
items.notes: “ce” agrees with the masculine “film”, not “cette”.

items.fr: Il vérifie ses messages sans cesse, presque toutes les cinq minutes.
items.en: He checks his messages constantly, almost every five minutes.
items.ipa: il ve.ʁi.fi se me.saʒ sɑ̃ sɛs pʁɛs.k tut le sɛ̃k mi.nyt
items.notes: “toutes” agrees in the feminine plural with “minutes”, not “tous”.

items.fr: Nous avons déménagé il y a six mois.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ de.me.na.ʒe i.l i a si mwa
items.notes: “il y a” here means “ago” and never takes an accent on “a”.

items.fr: Elle apprend le français depuis peu de temps.
items.en: She has been learning French for a short time.
items.ipa: ɛl a.pʁɑ̃ lə fʁɑ̃.sɛ də.pɥi pø də tɑ̃
items.notes: “depuis peu” means “recently”, not “a little” like “un peu” alone.

items.fr: Je passe généralement mes soirées à lire.
items.en: I generally spend my evenings reading.
items.ipa: ʒə pas ʒe.ne.ʁal.mɑ̃ me swa.ʁe a liʁ
items.notes: “généralement” keeps the accents from “général” on both “e”s.

items.fr: Ils ont vécu ensemble pendant cinq ans avant de se marier.
items.en: They lived together for five years before getting married.
items.ipa: i.l ɔ̃ ve.ky ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl pɑ̃.dɑ̃ sɛ̃.k‿ɑ̃ a.vɑ̃ də sə ma.ʁje
items.notes: “avant de” is followed by an infinitive, never a conjugated verb.

items.fr: Elle ne se plaint presque jamais de son travail.
items.en: She almost never complains about her job.
items.ipa: ɛl nə sə plɛ̃ pʁɛs.k ʒa.mɛ də sɔ̃ tʁa.vaj
items.notes: “se plaint” keeps a silent “t” at the end, typical of third-person singular verbs.

items.fr: Nous nous téléphonons chaque semaine sans faute.
items.en: We phone each other without fail every week.
items.ipa: nu nu te.le.fɔ.nɔ̃ ʃak sə.mɛn sɑ̃ fot
items.notes: “téléphonons” carries two accents close together on the “e”s of “télé-”, easy to miss when writing quickly.

items.fr: Depuis qu'il a déménagé, nous nous voyons beaucoup moins souvent.
items.en: Since he moved, we see each other much less often.
items.ipa: də.pɥi ki.l a de.me.na.ʒe nu nu vwa.jɔ̃ bo.ku mwɛ̃ su.vɑ̃
items.notes: “depuis que” introduces a clause with a conjugated verb, unlike “depuis” alone before a noun.

items.fr: Il y a longtemps que je n'ai pas pris de vacances.
items.en: It's been a long time since I took a vacation.
items.ipa: i.l i a lɔ̃.tɑ̃ kə ʒə nɛ pa pʁi də va.kɑ̃s
items.notes: “il y a... que” at the start of a sentence expresses duration, paired here with the negative passé composé.

items.fr: Plus je le vois, plus je l'apprécie, et pourtant nous nous voyons rarement.
items.en: The more I see him, the more I like him, yet we rarely see each other.
items.ipa: ply ʒə lə vwa ply ʒə la.pʁe.si e puʁ.tɑ̃ nu nu vwa.jɔ̃ ʁaʁ.mɑ̃
items.notes: “pourtant” means “yet, however” and should not be confused with the different fixed phrase “pour autant”.

items.fr: Bien qu'elle vive ici depuis peu, elle connaît déjà tout le quartier.
items.en: Although she has lived here for only a short time, she already knows the whole neighborhood.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃ kɛl viv i.si də.pɥi pø ɛl kɔ.nɛ de.ʒa tu lə kaʁ.tje
items.notes: “bien que” triggers the subjunctive “vive”, not the indicative “vit”.

items.fr: Tant qu'il n'aura pas fini, il ne sortira jamais avant l'heure prévue.
items.en: As long as he hasn't finished, he will never leave before the scheduled time.
items.ipa: tɑ̃ ki.l no.ʁa pa fi.ni il nə sɔʁ.ti.ʁa ʒa.mɛ a.vɑ̃ l‿œʁ pʁe.vy
items.notes: After “tant que” referring to the future, the future perfect is required, not the present.

items.fr: Si souvent qu'il s'excuse, elle ne lui pardonne jamais vraiment.
items.en: However often he apologizes, she never really forgives him.
items.ipa: si su.vɑ̃ ki.l sɛk.skyz ɛl nə lɥi paʁ.dɔn ʒa.mɛ vʁɛ.mɑ̃
items.notes: “si souvent que” here means “however often”, and takes the indicative, not the subjunctive.

items.fr: Nous nous connaissons depuis si longtemps que nous finissons nos phrases.
items.en: We have known each other for so long that we finish each other's sentences.
items.ipa: nu nu kɔ.nɛ.sɔ̃ də.pɥi si lɔ̃.tɑ̃ kə nu fi.ni.sɔ̃ no fʁaz
items.notes: “depuis si longtemps” still requires the present tense “connaissons”, not a past tense.

items.fr: Quoi qu'il fasse, il finit toujours par arriver en retard.
items.en: Whatever he does, he always ends up arriving late.
items.ipa: kwa ki.l fas i.l fi.ni tu.ʒuʁ paʁ a.ʁi.ve ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ
items.notes: “quoi que” written in two words means “whatever”, unlike “quoique” which means “although”.

items.fr: Cela faisait des années qu'elle n'était pas retournée dans sa ville natale.
items.en: It had been years since she had gone back to her hometown.
items.ipa: sə.la fə.zɛ de.z‿a.ne kɛl ne.tɛ pa ʁə.tuʁ.ne dɑ̃ sa vil na.tal
items.notes: “cela faisait... que” in the imperfect matches the pluperfect “n'était pas retournée” to describe a past duration.

items.fr: Même s'il pleut souvent ce mois-ci, la réunion en plein air aura lieu comme prévu.
items.en: Even if it often rains this month, the outdoor meeting will happen as planned.
items.ipa: mɛ.m si.l plø su.vɑ̃ sə mwa.si la ʁe.y.njɔ̃ ɑ̃ plɛ.n‿ɛʁ o.ʁa ljø kɔm pʁe.vy
items.notes: “même si” is always followed by the indicative “pleut”, never the subjunctive.

items.fr: Aussi souvent qu'elle le lui répète, il continue d'arriver en retard.
items.en: However often she repeats it to him, he keeps arriving late.
items.ipa: o.si su.vɑ̃ kɛl lə lɥi ʁe.pɛt il kɔ̃.tiny da.ʁi.ve ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ
items.notes: “aussi souvent que” at the start of a clause keeps its usual word order, without inversion.

items.fr: Ça faisait un moment qu'il n'avait pas donné de nouvelles, ce qui l'inquiétait.
items.en: It had been a while since he had given any news, which worried her.
items.ipa: sa fə.zɛ ɛ̃ mɔ.mɑ̃ ki.l na.vɛ pa dɔ.ne də nu.vɛl sə ki lɛ̃.kje.tɛ
items.notes: “ça faisait... que” in the imperfect signals a duration measured from a past reference point.

items.fr: Loin d'être toujours ponctuel, il arrive parfois avec une heure de retard.
items.en: Far from always being punctual, he sometimes arrives an hour late.
items.ipa: lwɛ̃ dɛtʁ tu.ʒuʁ pɔ̃k.tɥɛl i.l a.ʁiv paʁ.fwa a.vɛ.k‿yn œʁ də ʁə.taʁ
items.notes: “loin de” is followed by the infinitive “être”, never a conjugated verb.

items.fr: Il faut encore qu'il se souvienne de l'heure exacte du rendez-vous.
items.en: He still needs to remember the exact time of the appointment.
items.ipa: il fo ɑ̃.kɔʁ ki.l sə su.vjɛn də l‿œʁ ɛg.zakt dy ʁɑ̃.de.vu
items.notes: “il faut que” always requires the subjunctive “se souvienne”, never the indicative “se souvient”.

items.fr: Depuis lors, elle ne manque plus jamais une réunion, même à la dernière minute.
items.en: Since then, she never misses a meeting anymore, even at the last minute.
items.ipa: də.pɥi lɔʁ ɛl nə mɑ̃k ply ʒa.mɛ yn ʁe.y.njɔ̃ mɛ.m‿a la dɛʁ.njɛʁ mi.nyt
items.notes: “depuis lors” means “since then” and stays invariable, unlike an adjective.

items.fr: Les fois où il arrive en avance plutôt qu'en retard sont rares.
items.en: The times when he arrives early rather than late are rare.
items.ipa: le fwa u i.l a.ʁiv ɑ̃.n‿a.vɑ̃s ply.to.k‿ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ sɔ̃ ʁaʁ
items.notes: “rares” agrees in the plural with “fois”, the noun it describes.

items.fr: Il aurait fallu qu'il vérifie l'heure avant de partir précipitamment.
items.en: He should have checked the time before rushing off like that.
items.ipa: i.l o.ʁɛ fa.ly ki.l ve.ʁi.fi l‿œʁ a.vɑ̃ də paʁ.tiʁ pʁe.si.pi.ta.mɑ̃
items.notes: “aurait fallu que” takes the present subjunctive “vérifie” afterward, not the indicative “vérifiait”.

items.fr: Toutes les fois qu'elle a essayé d'arriver à l'heure, un imprévu l'en a empêchée.
items.en: Every time she tried to arrive on time, something unexpected stopped her.
items.ipa: tut le fwa kɛl a e.sɛ.je da.ʁi.ve a l‿œʁ ɛ̃.n‿ɛ̃.pʁe.vy lɑ̃.n‿a ɑ̃.pe.ʃe
items.notes: “empêchée” agrees with the preceding direct object “l'” referring to “elle”, so it takes a feminine ending.

items.en: We will keep seeing each other from time to time, despite everything.

items.notes: “Excuse-moi” is the informal “tu” form, not the same register as “excusez-moi”.
“Excusez” (command) and “excusé” (excused) sound identical despite their different endings.

items.en: Excuse me, could you repeat the question?
items.notes: Both “excusez-moi” and “pourriez-vous” require a hyphen before the pronoun.

items.fr: Elle s'est excusée d'être arrivée en retard.
items.ipa: ɛl sɛt ɛkskyze dɛtʁ aʁive ɑ̃ ʁətaʁ
items.notes: With the pronominal verb “s'excuser”, the past participle “excusée” agrees with the subject.

items.fr: Nous nous excusons du dérangement que cette situation a pu causer.
items.en: We apologize for the inconvenience this situation may have caused.
items.ipa: nu nuz ɛkskyzɔ̃ dy deʁɑ̃ʒmɑ̃ kə sɛt sitɥasjɔ̃ a py koze
items.notes: Despite the “que” clause, this relative clause takes the indicative, not the subjunctive.

items.fr: Il s'excuserait volontiers s'il comprenait vraiment son erreur.
items.en: He would gladly apologize if he truly understood his mistake.
items.ipa: il sɛkskyzəʁɛ vɔlɔ̃tje sil kɔ̃pʁənɛ vʁɛmɑ̃ sɔ̃n eʁœʁ
items.notes: The conditional “s'excuserait” pairs with the imperfect “comprenait” in this hypothesis.

items.fr: Ça ne fait rien, ce n'est pas grave.
items.en: It doesn't matter, it's not a big deal.
items.ipa: sa nə fɛ ʁjɛ̃, sə nɛ pa gʁav
items.notes: “Ne … rien” forms a single negative pair; “rien” never needs “pas” added too.

items.fr: Tu as cassé le verre ? Ça ne fait rien.
items.en: You broke the glass? It's fine.
items.ipa: ty a kase lə vɛʁ, sa nə fɛ ʁjɛ̃
items.notes: “Ça” needs its cedilla to keep the soft “s” sound of the word.

items.fr: Ça ne fait rien si tu arrives un peu en retard.
items.en: It's fine if you arrive a little late.
items.ipa: sa nə fɛ ʁjɛ̃ si ty aʁiv œ̃ pø ɑ̃ ʁətaʁ
items.notes: After “si” in this kind of clause, French uses the present indicative “arrives”, not the subjunctive.

items.fr: Elle a dit que ça ne faisait rien, mais elle avait l'air déçue.
items.en: She said it was fine, but she seemed disappointed.
items.ipa: ɛl a di kə sa nə fəzɛ ʁjɛ̃, mɛ ɛl avɛ lɛʁ desy
items.notes: “Faisait” is pronounced [fə.zɛ], not the way its letters might suggest.

items.fr: Ça ne ferait rien si vous changiez la date, du moment que vous nous prévenez à l'avance.
items.en: It wouldn't matter if you changed the date, as long as you let us know in advance.
items.ipa: sa nə fəʁɛ ʁjɛ̃ si vu ʃɑ̃ʒje la dat, dy mɔmɑ̃ kə vu nu pʁevne a lavɑ̃s
items.notes: After “si” expressing a hypothesis, French requires the imperfect “changiez”, not the present.

items.fr: Ça n'aurait rien changé même si nous étions arrivés plus tôt.
items.en: It wouldn't have changed anything even if we had arrived earlier.
items.ipa: sa noʁɛ ʁjɛ̃ ʃɑ̃ʒe mɛm si nuz etjɔ̃z aʁive ply to
items.notes: “Arrivés” takes the plural “s” to agree with “nous” in this pluperfect with être.

items.fr: Tant pis, on ira une autre fois.
items.en: Too bad, we'll go another time.
items.ipa: tɑ̃ pi, ɔ̃n iʁa yn otʁ fwa
items.notes: “Tant” and “temps” are pronounced the same, despite their different meanings.

items.fr: Il pleut ? Tant pis, on reste à la maison.
items.en: It's raining? Too bad, we're staying home.
items.ipa: il plø, tɑ̃ pi, ɔ̃ ʁɛst a la mɛzɔ̃
items.notes: “On” always takes a singular verb form like “reste”, even when it means “we”.

items.fr: Tant pis pour lui s'il n'a pas réservé à temps.
items.en: Too bad for him if he didn't book in time.
items.ipa: tɑ̃ pi puʁ lɥi sil na pa ʁezɛʁve a tɑ̃
items.notes: “À temps” (in time) is spelled with “temps”, not with “tant”, despite the identical sound.

items.fr: Elle a raté le bus, tant pis, elle prendra le suivant.
items.en: She missed the bus, too bad, she'll take the next one.
items.ipa: ɛl a ʁate lə bys, tɑ̃ pi, ɛl pʁɑ̃dʁa lə sɥivɑ̃
items.notes: “Prendra” keeps the irregular stem of “prendre” in the future tense.

items.fr: Tant pis si cela déplaît à certains, la décision est déjà prise.
items.en: Too bad if that displeases some people, the decision has already been made.
items.ipa: tɑ̃ pi si səla deplɛ a sɛʁtɛ̃, la desizjɔ̃ ɛ deʒa pʁiz
items.notes: “Déplaît” keeps the circumflex accent on the “i”, inherited from “plaît”.

items.fr: Tant pis pour ceux qui n'auraient pas lu le règlement à temps.
items.en: Too bad for those who might not have read the rules in time.
items.ipa: tɑ̃ pi puʁ sø ki noʁɛ pa ly lə ʁɛgləmɑ̃ a tɑ̃
items.notes: “N'auraient pas lu” is a past conditional, used here for a hypothetical past situation.
“De” plus “le” contracts to “du”, never “de le”.
The final “d” of “dépend” is silent.

items.fr: Ça dépend si tu es libre ce week-end.
items.en: It depends if you're free this weekend.
items.ipa: sa depɑ̃ si ty ɛ libʁ sə wikɛnd
items.notes: After “si” here, French keeps the present indicative “es”, not the subjunctive.

items.fr: Le prix dépend de la saison où vous voyagez.
items.en: The price depends on the season in which you travel.
items.ipa: lə pʁi depɑ̃ də la sɛzɔ̃ u vu vwajaʒe
items.notes: “Où” can refer to a moment in time, as in “la saison où”, not only to a place.

items.fr: Ça dépendait beaucoup de l'humeur du directeur.
items.en: It depended a lot on the director's mood.
items.ipa: sa depɑ̃dɛ boku də lymœʁ dy diʁɛktœʁ
items.notes: The ending of “dépendait” is pronounced as a single vowel sound, not spelled letter by letter.

items.fr: Tout dépendra de la manière dont les négociations se dérouleront.
items.en: Everything will depend on how the negotiations unfold.
items.ipa: tu depɑ̃dʁa də la manjɛʁ dɔ̃ le negɔsjasjɔ̃ sə deʁulʁɔ̃
items.notes: “Dont” replaces “de laquelle” here, since “dépendre de” requires the preposition “de”.

items.fr: Ça dépendrait de vous si le projet était reporté à l'année prochaine.
items.en: It would depend on you if the project were postponed to next year.
items.ipa: sa depɑ̃dʁɛ də vu si lə pʁɔʒɛ etɛ ʁəpɔʁte a lane pʁɔʃɛn
items.notes: The conditional “dépendrait” pairs with the imperfect “était” in this hypothesis.

items.en: Thank you very much! You're welcome.
items.notes: French places a space before the exclamation mark, unlike in English.

items.en: You're welcome, it's the least I could do.
items.notes: The letters “ien” together form one single nasal sound in “rien”, not two separate sounds.

items.fr: Merci pour ton aide. De rien !
items.en: Thanks for your help. No problem!
items.ipa: mɛʁsi puʁ tɔ̃n ɛd, də ʁjɛ̃
items.notes: “Ton” (your) and “thon” (tuna) are pronounced the same, despite very different meanings.

items.fr: De rien, ça m'a fait plaisir.
items.en: You're welcome, it was my pleasure.
items.ipa: də ʁjɛ̃, sa ma fɛ plɛziʁ
items.notes: “M'a” fuses “me” and “a” with an apostrophe that must not be dropped.

items.fr: Ne me remerciez pas, de rien vraiment.
items.en: Don't thank me, really, it's nothing.
items.ipa: nə mə ʁəmɛʁsje pa, də ʁjɛ̃ vʁɛmɑ̃
items.notes: In a negative command, the pronoun “me” stays before the verb, unlike in an affirmative one.

items.fr: Il a répondu « de rien » avec un grand sourire.
items.en: He replied 'you're welcome' with a big smile.
items.ipa: il a ʁepɔ̃dy də ʁjɛ̃ avɛk œ̃ gʁɑ̃ suʁiʁ
items.notes: French uses guillemets, « » with inner spaces, rather than plain quotation marks for reported speech.

items.fr: Elle aurait pu accepter des remerciements, mais elle a simplement répondu que ce n'était rien.
items.en: She could have accepted the thanks, but she simply replied that it was nothing.
items.ipa: ɛl oʁɛ py aksɛpte de ʁəmɛʁsimɑ̃, mɛ ɛl a sɛ̃pləmɑ̃ ʁepɔ̃dy kə sə netɛ ʁjɛ̃
items.notes: The imperfect “était” describes an ongoing state here, unlike a passé composé, which would suggest one finished event.

items.fr: Tu viens avec nous ? Avec plaisir !
items.en: Are you coming with us? Gladly!
items.ipa: ty vjɛ̃ avɛk nu, avɛk plɛziʁ
items.notes: “Avec” never elides, even before a vowel, unlike “de” or “le”.
“Aiderai” (future) and “aiderais” (conditional) differ only by a final “s”, yet they are not interchangeable.

items.fr: Elle a accepté l'invitation avec plaisir.
items.en: She accepted the invitation with pleasure.
items.ipa: ɛl a aksɛpte lɛ̃vitasjɔ̃ avɛk plɛziʁ
items.notes: “Le” elides to “l'” before the vowel sound of “invitation”.

items.fr: Nous vous recevrons avec plaisir la semaine prochaine.
items.en: We will welcome you gladly next week.
items.ipa: nu vu ʁəsəvʁɔ̃ avɛk plɛziʁ la səmɛn pʁɔʃɛn
items.notes: “Recevrons” keeps the irregular stem of “recevoir” in the future tense.

items.fr: C'est avec plaisir que je vous présente notre nouveau projet.
items.en: It is with pleasure that I present our new project to you.
items.ipa: sɛt avɛk plɛziʁ kə ʒə vu pʁezɑ̃t nɔtʁ nuvo pʁɔʒɛ
items.notes: The structure “c'est … que” places emphasis on “avec plaisir” right after “c'est”.

items.fr: C'est avec grand plaisir que nous aurions accueilli votre proposition, si elle nous était parvenue à temps.
items.en: It would have been with great pleasure that we welcomed your proposal, had it reached us in time.
items.ipa: sɛt avɛk gʁɑ̃ plɛziʁ kə nuz oʁjɔ̃ akœji vɔtʁ pʁɔpozisjɔ̃, si ɛl nuz etɛ paʁvəny a tɑ̃
items.notes: “Parvenue” agrees in the feminine because the subject “elle” refers to “la proposition”.

items.fr: Pas de problème, je peux t'aider.
items.en: No problem, I can help you.
items.ipa: pa də pʁɔblɛm, ʒə pø tɛde
items.notes: “Problème” takes a grave accent on the “è”, not an acute one.

items.fr: Il n'y a pas de problème avec ta réservation.
items.en: There's no problem with your reservation.
items.ipa: il nja pa də pʁɔblɛm avɛk ta ʁezɛʁvasjɔ̃
items.notes: After a negative like “pas de”, the article disappears and “de” alone remains.
“Problème” is masculine even though it ends in “e”: “un problème”, never “une problème”.

items.fr: Ça ne pose pas de problème si tu changes d'avis.
items.en: It's not a problem if you change your mind.
items.ipa: sa nə poz pa də pʁɔblɛm si ty ʃɑ̃ʒ davi
items.notes: “Poser problème” is used without any article before “problème”.

items.fr: Nous n'avons eu aucun problème pendant le voyage.
items.en: We had no problem during the trip.
items.ipa: nu navɔ̃z y okœ̃ pʁɔblɛm pɑ̃dɑ̃ lə vwajaʒ
items.notes: “Aucun” stays singular even though it can imply “none at all” among many things.

items.fr: Il y aura peut-être un petit problème avec les billets.
items.en: There might be a small problem with the tickets.
items.ipa: il i oʁa pøtɛtʁ œ̃ pəti pʁɔblɛm avɛk le bijɛ
items.notes: “Aura” (future) should not be confused with the conditional “aurait” in this sentence.

items.fr: Il n'y aurait aucun problème à reporter la réunion, du moment que tout le monde est prévenu.
items.en: There would be no problem postponing the meeting, as long as everyone is informed.
items.ipa: il njoʁɛ okœ̃ pʁɔblɛm a ʁəpɔʁte la ʁeynjɔ̃, dy mɔmɑ̃ kə tu lə mɔ̃d ɛ pʁevny
items.notes: “Du moment que” is followed by the indicative “est”, not the subjunctive, even though it expresses a condition.
“Il y a” never changes with the subject's number, even before a plural noun.

items.fr: Il y a beaucoup de monde ici.
items.en: There are a lot of people here.
items.ipa: il ja boku də mɔ̃d isi
items.notes: The “y” in “il y a” is a fixed pronoun that can never be dropped.

items.fr: Il y avait moins de circulation ce matin.
items.en: There was less traffic this morning.
items.ipa: il javɛ mwɛ̃ də siʁkylasjɔ̃ sə matɛ̃
items.notes: “Y avait” keeps the same fixed “y” even in the imperfect tense.

items.fr: Il y aurait sans doute plus de solutions si nous cherchions ensemble.
items.en: There would probably be more solutions if we searched together.
items.ipa: il joʁɛ sɑ̃ dut plys də sɔlysjɔ̃ si nu ʃɛʁʃjɔ̃ ɑ̃sɑ̃bl
items.notes: “Cherchions” keeps the “i” from the verb stem, even though it isn't heard clearly.
“Ça y est” is a fixed expression whose three words are never reordered.

items.fr: Ça y est, le film commence.
items.en: Here we go, the movie is starting.
items.ipa: sa j ɛ, lə film kɔmɑ̃s
items.notes: “Commence” ends in a silent “e” marking the third-person singular.

items.fr: Ça y était presque fini quand tu es arrivé.
items.en: It was almost finished when you arrived.
items.ipa: sa j etɛ pʁɛsk fini kɑ̃ ty ɛ aʁive
items.notes: “Arrivé” agrees in gender here, adding an “e” only for a feminine subject.

items.fr: Ça y est, elle a enfin réussi son examen après plusieurs tentatives.
items.en: That's it, she finally passed her exam after several attempts.
items.ipa: sa j ɛ, ɛl a ɑ̃fɛ̃ ʁeysi sɔ̃n ɛgzamɛ̃ apʁɛ plyzjœʁ tɑ̃tativ
items.notes: “Réussi” takes a double “s” to keep the unvoiced sound, unlike words spelled with a single one.

items.fr: Il pleut, mais on sort quand même.
items.en: It's raining, but we're going out anyway.
items.ipa: il plø, mɛ ɔ̃ sɔʁ kɑ̃ mɛm
items.notes: “Quand” ends in a silent “d”, pronounced only in liaison before a vowel.

items.fr: C'est cher, mais j'achète quand même.
items.en: It's expensive, but I'm buying it anyway.
items.ipa: sɛ ʃɛʁ, mɛ ʒaʃɛt kɑ̃ mɛm
items.notes: “J'achète” elides “je” before the vowel in “achète”.

items.fr: Il fait froid, mais elle sort quand même sans manteau.
items.en: It's cold, but she goes out anyway without a coat.
items.ipa: il fɛ fʁwa, mɛ ɛl sɔʁ kɑ̃ mɛm sɑ̃ mɑ̃to
items.notes: “Manteau” ends in “-eau”, a common masculine noun ending.

items.fr: Même si les résultats étaient décevants, ils ont continué quand même leurs recherches.
items.en: Even though the results were disappointing, they continued their research anyway.
items.ipa: mɛm si le ʁezylta etɛ desəvɑ̃, ilz ɔ̃ kɔ̃tinye kɑ̃ mɛm lœʁ ʁəʃɛʁʃ
items.notes: “Décevants” agrees in the plural with “résultats”, adding an “s”.

items.fr: En fait, je préfère le thé au café.
items.en: Actually, I prefer tea to coffee.
items.ipa: ɑ̃ fɛt, ʒə pʁefɛʁ lə te o kafe
items.notes: There is a liaison between “en” and “fait”: pronounce a “t” sound.

items.fr: En fait, il n'habite plus ici.
items.en: Actually, he doesn't live here anymore.
items.ipa: ɑ̃ fɛt, il nabit ply isi
items.notes: “N'habite” elides “ne” before the silent “h” of “habite”.

items.fr: En fait, nous avons changé nos plans pour ce week-end.
items.en: Actually, we changed our plans for this weekend.
items.ipa: ɑ̃ fɛt, nuz avɔ̃ ʃɑ̃ʒe no plɑ̃ puʁ sə wikɛnd
items.notes: “Changé” ends in “é” because it follows “avons” in the passé composé.

items.fr: En fait, la réunion avait été reportée sans que personne ne soit prévenu.
items.en: Actually, the meeting had been postponed without anyone being informed.
items.ipa: ɑ̃ fɛt, la ʁeynjɔ̃ avɛ ete ʁəpɔʁte sɑ̃ kə pɛʁsɔn nə swa pʁevny
items.notes: “Soit” is the subjunctive form of “être” required after “sans que”.

items.fr: Au fait, tu as vu Marie récemment ?
items.en: By the way, have you seen Marie recently?
items.ipa: o fɛt, ty a vy maʁi ʁesamɑ̃
items.notes: “Au fait” links with a liaison “t” sound before the vowel that follows.

items.fr: Au fait, j'ai oublié de te dire quelque chose.
items.en: By the way, I forgot to tell you something.
items.ipa: o fɛt, ʒe ublije də tə diʁ kɛlkə ʃoz
items.notes: “Oublié” takes an accent aigu, not a grave one.

items.fr: Au fait, est-ce que tu as reçu mon message ?
items.en: By the way, did you get my message?
items.ipa: o fɛt, ɛs kə ty a ʁəsy mɔ̃ mesaʒ
items.notes: “Reçu” keeps the cedilla under the “c” to preserve the soft sound before “u”.

items.fr: Au fait, je voulais vous informer que la réunion avait été avancée.
items.en: By the way, I wanted to inform you that the meeting had been moved up.
items.ipa: o fɛt, ʒə vulɛ vuz ɛ̃fɔʁme kə la ʁeynjɔ̃ avɛ ete avɑ̃se
items.notes: “Avancée” agrees in gender with “réunion”, the feminine subject.

items.en: Of course, I can help you.
items.notes: “Sûr” takes a circumflex accent to distinguish it from “sur” (on).

items.fr: Bien sûr que non, ce n'est pas grave.
items.en: Of course not, it's not a big deal.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃ syʁ kə nɔ̃, sə nɛ pa gʁav
items.notes: “Grave” ends in a silent final “e” that does not change its pronunciation.

items.fr: Bien sûr, nous serons présents à la réunion.
items.en: Of course, we will be present at the meeting.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃ syʁ, nu səʁɔ̃ pʁezɑ̃ a la ʁeynjɔ̃
items.notes: “Serons” is the “nous” form of the future of “être”, not to be confused with “seront” (ils).

items.fr: Bien sûr, il aurait accepté si on le lui avait proposé plus tôt.
items.en: Of course, he would have accepted if it had been offered to him earlier.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃ syʁ, il oʁɛ aksɛpte si ɔ̃ lə lɥi avɛ pʁopoze ply to
items.notes: “Proposé” ends in “é” because it follows “avait” in the pluperfect.

items.fr: Tout à fait, tu as raison.
items.ipa: tut a fɛ, ty a ʁɛzɔ̃
items.notes: “Tout à fait” links with a liaison “t” sound between “tout” and “à”.

items.fr: Tout à fait d'accord avec toi.
items.ipa: tut a fɛ dakɔʁ avɛk twa
items.notes: “D'accord” elides “de” before the vowel in “accord”.

items.fr: C'est tout à fait normal de se sentir fatigué après ce voyage.
items.en: It's completely normal to feel tired after this trip.
items.ipa: sɛ tut a fɛ nɔʁmal də sə sɑ̃tiʁ fatige apʁɛ sə vwajaʒ
items.notes: “Fatigué” ends in “é”, the past participle used here as an adjective.

items.fr: Ce que vous dites est tout à fait exact, même si cela reste difficile à admettre.
items.en: What you're saying is entirely correct, even if it remains hard to admit.
items.ipa: sə kə vu dit ɛ tut a fɛ ɛgzakt, mɛm si səla ʁɛst difisil a admɛtʁ
items.notes: “Exact” ends in a silent “t” that is not pronounced on its own.

items.en: That is to say, he won't be coming.
items.ipa: sɛt a diʁ kil nə vjɛ̃dʁa pa
items.notes: “C'est-à-dire” is written with two hyphens, never as separate words.

items.fr: Je suis libre demain, c'est-à-dire mardi.
items.en: I'm free tomorrow, that is, Tuesday.
items.ipa: ʒə sɥi libʁ dəmɛ̃, sɛt a diʁ maʁdi
items.notes: “Mardi” is never capitalized in French, unlike English day names.

items.fr: Il a changé d'avis, c'est-à-dire qu'il ne partira plus en voyage.
items.en: He changed his mind, meaning he's no longer going on the trip.
items.ipa: il a ʃɑ̃ʒe davi, sɛt a diʁ kil nə paʁtiʁa ply ɑ̃ vwajaʒ
items.notes: “Partira” is the future of “partir”, not to be confused with “partirait” (conditional).

items.fr: Le contrat prendra fin en juin, c'est-à-dire dans à peine trois mois.
items.en: The contract will end in June, that is, in barely three months.
items.ipa: lə kɔ̃tʁa pʁɑ̃dʁa fɛ̃ ɑ̃ ʒɥɛ̃, sɛt a diʁ dɑ̃z a pɛn tʁwa mwa
items.notes: “Juin” is never capitalized, unlike month names in English.

items.fr: De toute façon, je dois partir maintenant.
items.en: Anyway, I have to leave now.
items.ipa: də tut fasɔ̃, ʒə dwa paʁtiʁ mɛ̃tnɑ̃
items.notes: “Façon” takes a cedilla under the “c” to keep the soft sound before “o”.

items.fr: De toute façon, il ne m'écoute jamais.
items.en: Anyway, he never listens to me.
items.ipa: də tut fasɔ̃, il nə mekut ʒamɛ
items.notes: “M'écoute” elides “me” before the vowel of “écoute”.

items.fr: De toute façon, nous n'avions pas le choix.
items.ipa: də tut fasɔ̃, nu navjɔ̃ pa lə ʃwa
items.notes: “Choix” ends in a silent “x”, never pronounced.

items.fr: De toute façon, cette décision aurait été prise, que vous soyez d'accord ou non.
items.en: Anyway, this decision would have been made, whether you agreed or not.
items.ipa: də tut fasɔ̃, sɛt desizjɔ̃ oʁɛ ete pʁiz, kə vu swaje dakɔʁ u nɔ̃
items.notes: “Soyez” is the subjunctive form of “être” required after “que” here.

items.fr: En tout cas, merci pour ton aide.
items.en: In any case, thanks for your help.
items.ipa: ɑ̃ tu ka, mɛʁsi puʁ tɔ̃n ɛd
items.notes: The final “s” of “cas” is always silent.

items.fr: En tout cas, moi je ne viendrai pas.
items.en: In any case, I'm not coming.
items.ipa: ɑ̃ tu ka, mwa ʒə nə vjɛ̃dʁe pa
items.notes: “Viendrai” is the future tense, ending in “-ai”, not “-ais” like the conditional.

items.fr: En tout cas, les billets sont déjà réservés.
items.en: In any case, the tickets are already booked.
items.ipa: ɑ̃ tu ka, le bijɛ sɔ̃ deʒa ʁezɛʁve
items.notes: “Réservés” agrees in the plural with “billets”, adding an “s”.

items.fr: En tout cas, personne n'aurait pu prévoir un tel changement de situation.
items.en: In any case, no one could have foreseen such a change of situation.
items.ipa: ɑ̃ tu ka, pɛʁsɔn noʁɛ py pʁevwaʁ œ̃ tɛl ʃɑ̃ʒmɑ̃ də sitɥasjɔ̃
items.notes: “Prévoir” keeps its irregular form, do not confuse it with “prévenir”.

items.fr: J'aime le café, par contre je n'aime pas le thé.
items.en: I like coffee, but I don't like tea.
items.ipa: ʒɛm lə kafe, paʁ kɔ̃tʁ ʒə nɛm pa lə te
items.notes: “Par contre” is written as two words, never joined together.

items.fr: Il est gentil, par contre il est souvent en retard.
items.en: He's nice, but he's often late.
items.ipa: il ɛ ʒɑ̃ti, paʁ kɔ̃tʁ il ɛ suvɑ̃ ɑ̃ ʁətaʁ
items.notes: The final “l” of “gentil” is silent in the masculine form.

items.fr: Le loyer est raisonnable, par contre le quartier est très bruyant.
items.en: The rent is reasonable, but the neighborhood is very noisy.
items.ipa: lə lwaje ɛ ʁɛzɔnabl, paʁ kɔ̃tʁ lə kaʁtje ɛ tʁɛ bʁɥijɑ̃
items.notes: “Raisonnable” takes a double “n”, a common spelling slip.

items.fr: Le projet avance bien, par contre le budget dépasse déjà largement les prévisions initiales.
items.en: The project is progressing well, but the budget already largely exceeds the initial forecasts.
items.ipa: lə pʁɔʒɛ avɑ̃s bjɛ̃, paʁ kɔ̃tʁ lə byʒɛ depas deʒa laʁʒəmɑ̃ le pʁevizjɔ̃ inisjal
items.notes: “Dépasse” is spelled with a double “s” to keep the unvoiced sound.

items.fr: Elle est intelligente, et en plus très gentille.
items.en: She's smart, and also very kind.
items.ipa: ɛl ɛt ɛ̃tɛliʒɑ̃t, e ɑ̃ plys tʁɛ ʒɑ̃ti
items.notes: “Gentille” doubles the “l” and adds an “e” to agree with the feminine subject.

items.en: On top of that, it's raining today.
items.notes: “Aujourd'hui” is always written as one word with an apostrophe.

items.fr: Ce restaurant est cher, et en plus le service est lent.
items.en: This restaurant is expensive, and on top of that the service is slow.
items.ipa: sə ʁɛstoʁɑ̃ ɛ ʃɛʁ, e ɑ̃ plys lə sɛʁvis ɛ lɑ̃
items.notes: “Lent” ends in a silent “t”, from the adjective meaning slow.

items.fr: En plus d'être en retard, il avait complètement oublié ses documents importants.
items.en: On top of being late, he had completely forgotten his important documents.
items.ipa: ɑ̃ plys dɛtʁ ɑ̃ ʁətaʁ, il avɛ kɔ̃plɛtmɑ̃ ublije se dɔkymɑ̃ ɛ̃pɔʁtɑ̃
items.notes: “Complètement” takes an accent grave on the “e”, from the adjective “complète”.

items.fr: D'ailleurs, je n'ai pas encore mangé.
items.ipa: dajœʁ, ʒə nɛ pa ɑ̃kɔʁ mɑ̃ʒe
items.notes: “D'ailleurs” elides “de” before the vowel sound of “ailleurs”.

items.fr: Elle ne répond jamais, d'ailleurs elle n'a même pas de téléphone.
items.en: She never answers, besides she doesn't even have a phone.
items.ipa: ɛl nə ʁepɔ̃ ʒamɛ, dajœʁ ɛl na mɛm pa də telefɔn
items.notes: “Téléphone” takes two accents aigus, keep both.

items.fr: Ce quartier me plaît beaucoup, d'ailleurs j'envisage d'y déménager.
items.en: I really like this neighborhood, in fact I'm considering moving there.
items.ipa: sə kaʁtje mə plɛ boku, dajœʁ ʒɑ̃vizaʒ di demenaʒe
items.notes: “Plaît” keeps its circumflex accent on the “i”, inherited from “plaire”.

items.fr: Il n'a jamais accepté cette proposition, d'ailleurs il l'avait clairement refusée dès le départ.
items.en: He never accepted this proposal, in fact he had clearly refused it from the start.
items.ipa: il na ʒamɛ aksɛpte sɛt pʁopozisjɔ̃, dajœʁ il lavɛ klɛʁmɑ̃ ʁəfyze dɛ lə depaʁ
items.notes: “Refusée” agrees in gender with “proposition”, the feminine object placed before the verb.
“Faut” ends in a silent “t”, from the impersonal verb “falloir”.

items.fr: Il faut que tu manges quelque chose.
items.ipa: il fo kə ty mɑ̃ʒ kɛlkə ʃoz
items.notes: After “il faut que”, the verb goes into the subjunctive, here “manges”.

items.fr: Il faudra réserver les billets à l'avance.
items.en: We'll need to book the tickets in advance.
items.ipa: il fodʁa ʁezɛʁve le bijɛ a lavɑ̃s
items.notes: “Faudra” is the future form of “falloir”, spelled with “d”, not “t”.

items.fr: Il aurait fallu prévenir tout le monde avant de changer les horaires.
items.en: We should have warned everyone before changing the schedule.
items.ipa: il oʁɛ faly pʁevəniʁ tu lə mɔ̃d avɑ̃ də ʃɑ̃ʒe lez ɔʁɛʁ
items.notes: “Fallu” is the irregular past participle of “falloir”, unlike “fallait”, the imperfect.

items.fr: Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît.
items.en: I would like a coffee, please.
items.ipa: ʒə vudʁɛ œ̃ kafe, sil vu plɛ
items.notes: “Voudrais” is the conditional of “vouloir”, spelled with “dr”, not “dr” doubled.

items.fr: Je voudrais réserver une table pour deux.
items.en: I would like to book a table for two.
items.ipa: ʒə vudʁɛ ʁezɛʁve yn tabl puʁ dø
items.notes: “Réserver” keeps its accent aigu on both “e”s.

items.fr: Nous voudrions changer notre vol pour demain matin.
items.en: We would like to change our flight to tomorrow morning.
items.ipa: nu vudʁjɔ̃ ʃɑ̃ʒe nɔtʁ vɔl puʁ dəmɛ̃ matɛ̃
items.notes: “Voudrions” is the “nous” form of the conditional, ending in “-ions”.

items.fr: J'aurais voulu vous prévenir plus tôt, mais je n'ai trouvé votre numéro qu'hier.
items.en: I would have liked to warn you sooner, but I only found your number yesterday.
items.ipa: ʒoʁɛ vuly vu pʁevəniʁ ply to, mɛ ʒə nɛ tʁuve vɔtʁ nymeʁo kjɛʁ
items.notes: “Voulu” is the past participle of “vouloir”, used here after “aurais” for the past conditional.

items.en: You choose, it doesn't matter to me.
items.notes: “Égal” takes an accent aigu on the first “e”.

items.fr: Peu importe l'heure, ça m'est égal.
items.en: Whatever time, it's fine by me.
items.ipa: pø ɛ̃pɔʁt lœʁ, sa mɛ egal
items.notes: “L'heure” elides “la” before the silent “h” of “heure”.

items.fr: Que vous partiez maintenant ou plus tard, cela m'est complètement égal.
items.en: Whether you leave now or later, it's completely the same to me.
items.ipa: kə vu paʁtje mɛ̃tnɑ̃ u ply taʁ, səla mɛ kɔ̃plɛtmɑ̃ egal
items.notes: “Partiez” is the subjunctive form required after “que” here.

items.fr: Peu m'importe ce que les autres pensent de ma décision.
items.en: I don't care what others think of my decision.
items.ipa: pø mɛ̃pɔʁt sə kə lez otʁ pɑ̃s də ma desizjɔ̃
items.notes: “M'importe” elides “me” before the vowel of “importe”.
“Tout de suite” is three separate words, never joined.
“Reviens” comes from “revenir”, conjugated like “venir”.

items.fr: Il faut répondre tout de suite à ce message.
items.en: You need to reply to this message right away.
items.ipa: il fo ʁepɔ̃dʁ tu də sɥit a sə mesaʒ
items.notes: “Répondre” keeps a silent final “e” after the consonant cluster.

items.fr: Dès qu'elle a appris la nouvelle, elle a réagi tout de suite sans hésiter.
items.en: As soon as she heard the news, she reacted right away without hesitating.
items.ipa: dɛ kɛl a apʁi la nuvɛl, ɛl a ʁeaʒi tu də sɥit sɑ̃z eziteʁ
items.notes: “Réagi” keeps a hiatus between “é” and “a”, both pronounced separately.

items.fr: À mon avis, il a raison.
items.ipa: a mɔ̃n avi, il a ʁɛzɔ̃
items.notes: “À” takes a grave accent to distinguish it from “a” (the verb avoir).

items.fr: À mon avis, ce film est trop long.
items.en: In my opinion, this movie is too long.
items.ipa: a mɔ̃n avi, sə film ɛ tʁo lɔ̃
items.notes: “Trop” ends in a silent “p”, never pronounced.

items.fr: À notre avis, cette solution n'est pas la meilleure.
items.en: In our opinion, this solution isn't the best.
items.ipa: a nɔtʁ avi, sɛt sɔlysjɔ̃ nɛ pa la mɛjœʁ
items.notes: “Meilleure” agrees in gender with “solution”, the feminine noun.

items.fr: À mon avis, il aurait mieux valu attendre les résultats avant d'annoncer quoi que ce soit.
items.en: In my opinion, it would have been better to wait for the results before announcing anything.
items.ipa: a mɔ̃n avi, il oʁɛ mjø valy atɑ̃dʁ le ʁezylta avɑ̃ danɔ̃se kwa kə sə swa
items.notes: “Valu” is the past participle of “valoir”, irregular like “fallu”.

items.fr: Comment ça va ? Comme ci, comme ça.
items.ipa: kɔmɑ̃ sa va, kɔm si, kɔm sa
items.notes: “Comme ci, comme ça” is a fixed expression with a comma between each part.

items.fr: Ce n'est pas mal du tout.
items.ipa: sə nɛ pa mal dy tu
items.notes: “Mal” never takes a feminine or plural form when used as an adverb.

items.fr: Le film n'était pas mal, mais un peu long.
items.en: The movie wasn't bad, but a bit long.
items.ipa: lə film netɛ pa mal, mɛz œ̃ pø lɔ̃
items.notes: “N'était” elides “ne” before the vowel in “était”.

items.fr: Ses résultats n'étaient pas mal, compte tenu du peu de temps qu'il avait eu pour réviser.
items.en: His results weren't bad, given the little time he had to study.
items.ipa: se ʁezylta netɛ pa mal, kɔ̃t təny dy pø də tɑ̃ kil avɛ y puʁ ʁevize
items.notes: “Compte tenu de” is an invariable fixed expression, “tenu” never agrees.
“Bientôt” takes a circumflex accent on the “o”.

items.en: Goodbye ma'am, have a good day.
items.notes: “Madame” is never abbreviated with a capital letter mid-sentence.

items.fr: Elle nous a dit au revoir avant de partir en vacances.
items.en: She said goodbye to us before leaving on vacation.
items.ipa: ɛl nuz a di o ʁəvwaʁ avɑ̃ də paʁtiʁ ɑ̃ vakɑ̃s
items.notes: “Vacances” is always plural in French, even for one trip.

items.fr: Après s'être longuement dit au revoir sur le quai, ils sont enfin montés dans le train.
items.en: After saying a long goodbye on the platform, they finally boarded the train.
items.ipa: apʁɛ sɛtʁ lɔ̃gəmɑ̃ di o ʁəvwaʁ syʁ lə kɛ, il sɔ̃t ɑ̃fɛ̃ mɔ̃te dɑ̃ lə tʁɛ̃
items.notes: “Montés” agrees in the plural with “ils”, adding an “s” to the past participle.

items.fr: Il y a du pain sur la table.
items.en: There is bread on the table.

items.fr: Il y a un chat dans le jardin.
items.en: There is a cat in the garden.

items.fr: Il y a beaucoup de monde ici.
items.en: There are a lot of people here.

items.fr: Il y a trois ans, j'habitais à Paris.
items.en: Three years ago, I was living in Paris.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il y a trois ans,","t":"three years ago,"},{"w":"j'habitais","t":"I was living"},{"w":"à Paris.","t":"in Paris"}]}

items.fr: Il y a un problème avec la voiture.
items.en: There is a problem with the car.

items.fr: Il y a une pharmacie au coin de la rue.
items.en: There is a pharmacy at the corner of the street.

items.fr: Il y a des moments où il vaut mieux se taire.
items.en: There are moments when it's better to stay quiet.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il y a des moments","t":"there are moments"},{"w":"où il vaut mieux","t":"when it's better"},{"w":"se taire.","t":"to stay quiet"}]}

items.fr: Il y a longtemps que nous ne nous sommes pas vus.
items.en: It has been a long time since we last saw each other.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il y a longtemps","t":"it's been a long time"},{"w":"que nous ne nous sommes pas vus.","t":"since we haven't seen each other"}]}

items.en: You need to close the door.

items.fr: Il faut réserver une table à l'avance.
items.en: You need to book a table in advance.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il faut","t":"you need to"},{"w":"réserver une table","t":"book a table"},{"w":"à l'avance.","t":"in advance"}]}

items.fr: Il faut du temps pour apprendre une langue.
items.en: It takes time to learn a language.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il faut du temps","t":"it takes time"},{"w":"pour apprendre une langue.","t":"to learn a language"}]}

items.fr: Il ne faut pas oublier les clés.
items.en: You must not forget the keys.

items.fr: Il faudrait que tu prennes une décision rapidement.
items.en: You should make a decision quickly.

items.fr: Il faut faire preuve de patience avec les enfants.
items.en: You have to show patience with children.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il faut faire preuve de patience","t":"you have to show patience"},{"w":"avec les enfants.","t":"with children"}]}

items.en: It's going to get better tomorrow.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Ça va aller mieux","t":"it's going to get better"},{"w":"demain.","t":"tomorrow"}]}

items.fr: Ça ne va pas du tout ce matin.
items.en: Things are not going well at all this morning.

items.fr: Ça va prendre plus de temps que prévu.
items.en: It's going to take more time than expected.

items.fr: Ça va être compliqué d'organiser la réunion à temps.
items.en: It's going to be complicated to organize the meeting on time.

items.fr: Elle a besoin de nouvelles chaussures.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle a besoin de","t":"she needs"},{"w":"nouvelles chaussures.","t":"new shoes"}]}

items.fr: Il a besoin de parler à quelqu'un.
items.en: He needs to talk to someone.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il a besoin de","t":"he needs"},{"w":"parler à quelqu'un.","t":"to talk to someone"}]}

items.fr: Vous avez besoin d'un stylo pour l'examen.
items.en: You need a pen for the exam.

items.fr: Nous avons besoin de réfléchir avant de répondre.
items.en: We need to think before answering.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons besoin de réfléchir","t":"we need to think"},{"w":"avant de répondre.","t":"before answering"}]}

items.fr: Ils ont besoin d'un plan plus précis.
items.en: They need a more precise plan.
She feels like having a coffee.

items.fr: Nous avons envie de voyager cet été.
items.en: We feel like traveling this summer.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons envie de voyager","t":"we feel like traveling"},{"w":"cet été.","t":"this summer"}]}

items.fr: Il a envie de changer de travail.
As-tu envie de sortir ce soir ?
items.en: Do you feel like going out tonight?

items.fr: J'ai vraiment envie de découvrir de nouvelles cultures.
items.en: I really feel like discovering new cultures.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"J'ai vraiment envie de découvrir","t":"I really feel like discovering"},{"w":"de nouvelles cultures.","t":"new cultures"}]}

items.fr: Elle n'a pas envie de discuter de ce sujet.
items.en: She doesn't feel like discussing that topic.

items.fr: Le chien a peur de l'orage.
items.en: The dog is afraid of thunderstorms.

items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle a peur","t":"she is afraid"},{"w":"des araignées.","t":"of spiders"}]}

items.fr: Nous avons peur de rater le train.
items.en: We are afraid of missing the train.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons peur de rater","t":"we're afraid of missing"},{"w":"le train.","t":"the train"}]}

items.fr: Il a peur de parler en public.
items.en: He is afraid of speaking in public.

items.fr: Beaucoup de gens ont peur de l'échec.
items.en: Many people are afraid of failure.

items.fr: Ils avaient peur que la réunion soit annulée.
items.en: They were afraid the meeting would be canceled.

items.fr: Elle a raison de partir tôt.
items.en: She is right to leave early.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle a raison de partir","t":"she is right to leave"},{"w":"tôt.","t":"early"}]}

items.fr: Nous avons raison sur ce point.
items.en: We are right about this point.

items.fr: Tu as eu raison de refuser cette offre.
items.en: You were right to refuse that offer.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Tu as eu raison de refuser","t":"you were right to refuse"},{"w":"cette offre.","t":"that offer"}]}

items.fr: Il n'a pas tort, il faut l'admettre.
items.en: He isn't wrong, we have to admit it.

items.fr: Il faut faire attention en traversant la rue.
items.en: You must be careful when crossing the street.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il faut faire attention","t":"you must be careful"},{"w":"en traversant la rue.","t":"when crossing the street"}]}

items.fr: Elle fait attention à son alimentation.
items.en: She pays attention to her diet.

items.fr: Faites attention aux marches, elles sont glissantes.
items.en: Be careful of the steps, they are slippery.

items.fr: Nous devons faire attention à ne pas gaspiller l'eau.
items.en: We must be careful not to waste water.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous devons faire attention","t":"we must be careful"},{"w":"à ne pas gaspiller l'eau.","t":"not to waste water"}]}

items.fr: Il fait attention à chaque détail de son travail.
items.en: He pays attention to every detail of his work.
I can't wait to see you.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"J'ai hâte de","t":"I can't wait to"},{"w":"te voir.","t":"see you"}]}

items.fr: Elle a hâte de partir en vacances.
items.en: She can't wait to go on vacation.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle a hâte de partir","t":"she can't wait to go"},{"w":"en vacances.","t":"on vacation"}]}

items.fr: Nous avons hâte de découvrir la nouvelle maison.
items.en: We can't wait to discover the new house.

items.fr: Il a hâte de commencer son nouveau travail.
items.en: He can't wait to start his new job.

items.fr: J'ai hâte que ce projet soit enfin terminé.
items.en: I can't wait for this project to finally be finished.

items.fr: Ils ont hâte de retrouver leurs amis après le voyage.
items.en: They can't wait to see their friends again after the trip.

items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Un café,","t":"a coffee,"},{"w":"s'il vous plaît.","t":"please"}]}

items.fr: Fermez la porte, s'il vous plaît.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Fermez la porte,","t":"close the door,"},{"w":"s'il vous plaît.","t":"please"}]}

items.fr: Passez-moi le sel, s'il vous plaît.

items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Pourriez-vous m'aider,","t":"could you help me,"},{"w":"s'il vous plaît ?","t":"please?"}]}

items.fr: Parlez plus lentement, s'il vous plaît.
Nous vous demandons de patienter quelques minutes, s'il vous plaît.
items.en: We kindly ask you to wait a few minutes, please.

items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Je voudrais","t":"I would like"},{"w":"un thé.","t":"a tea"}]}

items.en: I would like to book a room.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Je voudrais","t":"I would like"},{"w":"réserver une chambre.","t":"to book a room"}]}

items.en: I would like to speak to the manager.

items.fr: Je voudrais changer mon billet de train.
items.en: I would like to change my train ticket.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Je voudrais changer","t":"I would like to change"},{"w":"mon billet de train.","t":"my train ticket"}]}

items.fr: Nous voudrions visiter le musée demain.
items.en: We would like to visit the museum tomorrow.

items.fr: Je voudrais savoir pourquoi la livraison a été retardée.
items.en: I would like to know why the delivery was delayed.
Excuse me, where is the restroom?
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Excusez-moi,","t":"excuse me,"},{"w":"où sont les toilettes ?","t":"where is the restroom?"}]}
{"tiles":[{"w":"Excusez-moi","t":"excuse me"},{"w":"du retard.","t":"for being late"}]}

items.fr: Excusez-moi de vous déranger si tard.
items.en: Sorry to bother you so late.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Excusez-moi de vous déranger","t":"sorry to bother you"},{"w":"si tard.","t":"so late"}]}

items.en: Excuse me, could you repeat the question?

items.fr: Excusez-moi de vous interrompre, mais c'est urgent.
items.en: Excuse me for interrupting you, but it's urgent.

items.fr: Ça ne fait rien, ne t'inquiète pas.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Ça ne fait rien,","t":"it's okay,"},{"w":"ne t'inquiète pas.","t":"don't worry"}]}

items.fr: Tu es en retard ? Ça ne fait rien.
Ça ne fait rien si tu ne peux pas venir.
items.en: It's fine if you can't come.

items.fr: Ça ne fait rien, on recommencera demain.
items.en: It's okay, we'll start again tomorrow.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Ça ne fait rien,","t":"it's okay,"},{"w":"on recommencera","t":"we'll start again"},{"w":"demain.","t":"tomorrow"}]}

items.fr: Il a oublié son parapluie, mais ça ne fait rien.
items.en: He forgot his umbrella, but it doesn't matter.

items.fr: Ça ne fait rien si le résultat n'est pas parfait.
items.en: It doesn't matter if the result isn't perfect.

items.fr: Il n'y a plus de gâteau ? Tant pis.
items.en: There's no more cake? Oh well.

items.fr: Tant pis, on essaiera une autre fois.
items.en: Too bad, we'll try another time.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Tant pis,","t":"too bad,"},{"w":"on essaiera","t":"we'll try"},{"w":"une autre fois.","t":"another time"}]}

items.fr: Tant pis pour lui, il n'a pas écouté.
items.en: Too bad for him, he didn't listen.

items.fr: Si personne ne veut venir, tant pis.
items.en: If nobody wants to come, too bad.

items.fr: Tant pis si cela prend plus de temps que prévu.
items.en: Too bad if it takes longer than expected.

items.fr: Tant pis pour les regrets, il fallait décider plus tôt.
items.en: Too bad for regrets, one had to decide earlier.
Are you coming tomorrow? It depends.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Tu viens demain ?","t":"are you coming tomorrow?"},{"w":"Ça dépend.","t":"it depends"}]}

items.fr: Ça dépend du temps qu'il fait.
Ça dépend si nous avons assez d'argent.
items.en: It depends whether we have enough money.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Ça dépend","t":"it depends"},{"w":"si nous avons assez d'argent.","t":"on whether we have enough money"}]}

items.fr: Le prix dépend de la saison.
items.en: The price depends on the season.

items.fr: Ça dépend des circonstances dans lesquelles nous nous trouvons.
items.en: It depends on the circumstances we find ourselves in.

items.fr: Tout dépend de la manière dont on présente les choses.
items.en: Everything depends on how things are presented.
Thank you very much! You're welcome.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Merci beaucoup !","t":"thank you very much!"},{"w":"De rien.","t":"you're welcome"}]}

items.en: You're welcome, it was a pleasure.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"De rien,","t":"you're welcome,"},{"w":"c'était un plaisir.","t":"it was a pleasure"}]}

items.en: You're welcome, call me if you need to.

items.fr: De rien, je suis content d'avoir pu aider.
items.en: You're welcome, I'm glad I could help.

items.fr: Merci pour ton aide. De rien du tout.
items.en: Thanks for your help. Not at all.

items.fr: De rien, cela m'a fait plaisir de vous rendre service.
items.en: You're welcome, it was my pleasure to help you.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"De rien,","t":"you're welcome,"},{"w":"cela m'a fait plaisir","t":"it was my pleasure"},{"w":"de vous rendre service.","t":"to help you"}]}

items.fr: De rien, n'hésitez pas à revenir si vous avez des questions.
items.en: You're welcome, feel free to come back if you have questions.

items.fr: Tu veux venir dîner ? Avec plaisir !
items.en: Do you want to come for dinner? With pleasure!
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Tu veux venir dîner ?","t":"do you want to come for dinner?"},{"w":"Avec plaisir !","t":"with pleasure!"}]}
{"tiles":[{"w":"Je t'aiderai","t":"I will help you"},{"w":"avec plaisir.","t":"gladly"}]}

items.fr: Elle a accepté l'invitation avec plaisir.
Nous vous accueillerons avec plaisir la semaine prochaine.
items.en: We will gladly welcome you next week.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous vous accueillerons avec plaisir","t":"we will gladly welcome you"},{"w":"la semaine prochaine.","t":"next week"}]}

items.fr: C'est avec plaisir que je vous présente notre nouvelle équipe.
items.en: It is with pleasure that I introduce our new team to you.

items.fr: Tu peux venir plus tard ? Pas de problème.
items.en: Can you come later? No problem.

items.fr: Pas de problème, je m'en occupe.
items.en: No problem, I'll take care of it.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Pas de problème,","t":"no problem,"},{"w":"je m'en occupe.","t":"I'll take care of it"}]}

items.fr: Pas de problème, nous avons encore le temps.
items.en: No problem, we still have time.

items.fr: Il n'y a pas de problème avec cette solution.
items.en: There's no problem with this solution.

items.fr: Pas de problème, nous trouverons une solution ensemble.
items.en: No problem, we'll find a solution together.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Pas de problème,","t":"no problem,"},{"w":"nous trouverons une solution","t":"we'll find a solution"},{"w":"ensemble.","t":"together"}]}

items.fr: Il n'y aura pas de problème tant que tout le monde respecte les règles.
items.en: There won't be a problem as long as everyone follows the rules.

items.fr: Mon frère est plus grand que moi.
items.en: My brother is taller than me.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ ɛ ply ɡʁɑ̃ kə mwa
items.notes: The s in “plus” stays silent before a consonant like “grand”.
“Plus” links with a z sound before the vowel of “âgé”.

items.fr: Cette voiture est moins rapide que la mienne.
items.en: This car is slower than mine.
items.ipa: sɛt vwa.tyʁ ɛ mwɛ̃ ʁa.pid kə la mjɛn
items.notes: “Mienne” must agree with the feminine “voiture”, never written as “mien” here.

items.fr: Ma sœur est aussi grande que moi.
items.en: My sister is just as tall as me.
items.ipa: ma sœʁ ɛ o.si ɡʁɑ̃d kə mwa
items.notes: “Grande” takes a final e to agree with the feminine “sœur”.

items.fr: Ce livre est plus intéressant que le film.
items.en: This book is more interesting than the movie.
items.ipa: sə livʁ ɛ plyz‿ɛ̃.te.ʁɛ.sɑ̃ kə lə film
items.notes: Liaison makes “plus” sound like “plyz” before “intéressant”.

items.en: It is less cold than yesterday.
items.notes: “Que” drops its e and becomes “qu'” before the vowel sound of “hier”.

items.fr: Cette ville a plus d'habitants que la nôtre.
items.en: This city has more inhabitants than ours.
items.ipa: sɛt vil a plyz‿a.bi.tɑ̃ kə la notʁ
items.notes: Before a noun, French needs “de” rather than a bare “que”, giving “plus d'habitants”.

items.fr: Il gagne moins d'argent que son collègue.
items.en: He earns less money than his colleague.
items.ipa: il ɡaɲ mwɛ̃ daʁ.ʒɑ̃ kə sɔ̃ kɔ.lɛɡ
items.notes: “D'argent” uses the elided form of “de” because “argent” starts with a vowel.

items.fr: Ce gâteau est meilleur que l'autre.
items.en: This cake is better than the other one.
items.ipa: sə ɡɑ.to ɛ mɛ.jœʁ kə lotʁ
items.notes: “Meilleur” is the irregular comparative of “bon”; never write “plus bon”.

items.fr: Cette tarte est meilleure que la mienne.
items.en: This tart is better than mine.
items.ipa: sɛt taʁt ɛ mɛ.jœʁ kə la mjɛn
items.notes: “Meilleure” adds an e to agree with the feminine “tarte”.

items.fr: Ses résultats sont pires que les nôtres.
items.en: His results are worse than ours.
items.ipa: se ʁe.zyl.ta sɔ̃ piʁ kə le notʁ
items.notes: “Pire” takes an s in the plural to agree with “résultats”.

items.fr: Ce quartier est plus calme que le centre-ville.
items.en: This neighborhood is quieter than downtown.
items.ipa: sə kaʁ.tje ɛ ply kalm kə lə sɑ̃tʁ vil
items.notes: The final t of “quartier” is never pronounced.

items.fr: Mon chien est plus obéissant que le tien.
items.en: My dog is more obedient than yours.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ ʃjɛ̃ ɛ plyz‿ɔ.be.i.sɑ̃ kə lə tjɛ̃
items.notes: Liaison turns “plus obéissant” into “plyzɔbeisɑ̃”.

items.fr: Cette rue est plus longue que l'avenue.
items.en: This street is longer than the avenue.
items.ipa: sɛt ʁy ɛ ply lɔ̃ɡ kə lav.ny
items.notes: “Longue” keeps the u after g to preserve the hard sound before the feminine e.

items.fr: Les enfants sont plus curieux que les adultes.
items.en: Children are more curious than adults.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ sɔ̃ ply ky.ʁjø kə le.z‿a.dylt
items.notes: “Curieux” already ends in x, so no extra s is added in the plural.

items.fr: Ce café est moins fort que le tien.
items.en: This coffee is less strong than yours.
items.ipa: sə ka.fe ɛ mwɛ̃ fɔʁ kə lə tjɛ̃
items.notes: “Moins” always keeps its written s even though it is silent here.

items.fr: Notre équipe joue mieux que la vôtre.
items.en: Our team plays better than yours.
items.ipa: nɔtʁ e.kip ʒu mjø kə la votʁ
items.notes: “Mieux” is the irregular comparative of the adverb “bien” and never becomes “plus bien”.

items.fr: Ton idée est plus originale que la sienne.
items.en: Your idea is more original than his.
items.ipa: tɔ̃.n‿i.de ɛ plyz‿ɔ.ʁi.ʒi.nal kə la sjɛn
items.notes: “Originale” adds an e to agree with the feminine “idée”.

items.fr: Ce travail est plus fatigant que le précédent.
items.en: This job is more tiring than the previous one.
items.ipa: sə tʁa.vaj ɛ ply fa.ti.ɡɑ̃ kə lə pʁe.se.dɑ̃
items.notes: The adjective “fatigant” drops the u found in the verb form “fatiguant”.

items.fr: Ma valise est plus lourde que la tienne.
items.en: My suitcase is heavier than yours.
items.ipa: ma va.liz ɛ ply luʁd kə la tjɛn
items.notes: “Lourde” needs the final e to agree with the feminine “valise”.

items.fr: Il conduit plus vite que moi.
items.ipa: il kɔ̃.dɥi ply vit kə mwa
items.notes: “Vite” is an invariable adverb here, so it never takes an s.

items.fr: Cette réunion est moins longue que la dernière.
items.en: This meeting is shorter than the last one.
items.ipa: sɛt ʁe.y.njɔ̃ ɛ mwɛ̃ lɔ̃ɡ kə la dɛʁ.njɛʁ
items.notes: “Réunion” needs an accent on both e's and is never written without them.

items.fr: Ce problème est plus simple qu'on ne le pensait.
items.en: This problem is simpler than one thought.
items.ipa: sə pʁɔ.blɛm ɛ ply sɛ̃pl kɔ̃ nə lə pɑ̃.sɛ
items.notes: “Que” elides to “qu'” before “on” because “on” starts with a vowel.

items.fr: Cette chambre est plus claire que la mienne.
items.en: This bedroom is brighter than mine.
items.ipa: sɛt ʃɑ̃bʁ ɛ ply klɛʁ kə la mjɛn
items.notes: “Claire” needs the final e to agree with the feminine “chambre”.

items.fr: Mon voisin est moins bavard que le tien.
items.en: My neighbor is less talkative than yours.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ vwa.zɛ̃ ɛ mwɛ̃ ba.vaʁ kə lə tjɛ̃
items.notes: The final d of “bavard” is silent, unlike in its feminine form “bavarde”.

items.fr: Ces exercices sont plus faciles que les précédents.
items.en: These exercises are easier than the previous ones.
items.ipa: se.z‿ɛɡ.zɛʁ.sis sɔ̃ ply fa.sil kə le pʁe.se.dɑ̃
items.notes: “Faciles” takes an s in the plural to agree with “exercices”.

items.fr: Il fait plus chaud aujourd'hui qu'hier.
items.en: It is hotter today than yesterday.
items.ipa: il fɛ ply ʃo o.ʒuʁ.dɥi kjɛʁ
items.notes: “Que” becomes “qu'” before “hier” since its silent h does not block elision.

items.fr: Cette histoire est plus triste que la première.
items.en: This story is sadder than the first one.
items.ipa: sɛt is.twaʁ ɛ ply tʁist kə la pʁə.mjɛʁ
items.notes: “Histoire” is feminine, so it takes “cette” rather than the masculine elided form “cet”.

items.fr: C'est le plus grand bâtiment de la ville.
items.en: It's the tallest building in the city.
items.ipa: sɛ lə ply ɡʁɑ̃ bɑ.ti.mɑ̃ də la vil
items.notes: After a superlative, “de” introduces the group, not “dans”.

items.fr: C'est la plus belle maison du quartier.
items.en: It's the most beautiful house in the neighborhood.
