items.notes: “Rencontrées” agrees with “elles” because the reflexive pronoun here functions as a direct object.

items.fr: Nous avons construit une cabane dans les bois.
items.en: We built a cabin in the woods.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ kɔ̃s.tʁɥi yn ka.ban dɑ̃ le bwa
items.notes: “Construit” ends with a silent t, unlike what its pronunciation might suggest.

items.fr: Tu as ouvert la fenêtre parce qu'il faisait chaud.
items.en: You opened the window because it was hot.
items.ipa: ty a u.vɛʁ la fə.nɛtʁ paʁs.kil fə.zɛ ʃo
items.notes: “Ouvert” is the irregular past participle of “ouvrir”, which conjugates like an er-verb only in the present.

items.fr: Ils sont restés à la maison à cause de la pluie.
items.en: They stayed home because of the rain.
items.ipa: il sɔ̃ ʁɛs.te a la mɛ.zɔ̃ a koz də la plɥi
items.notes: “Restés” agrees with the masculine plural subject “ils” because “rester” is conjugated with être.

items.fr: Quand j'étais petite, j'adorais les dessins animés.
items.en: When I was little, I loved cartoons.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ ʒe.tɛ pə.tit ʒa.dɔ.ʁɛ le de.sɛ̃ a.ni.me
items.notes: “J'étais” comes from “être” and its imparfait stem “ét-” is completely irregular.

items.fr: Il faisait très froid quand nous sommes sortis.
items.en: It was very cold when we went out.
items.ipa: il fə.zɛ tʁɛ fʁwa kɑ̃ nu sɔm sɔʁ.ti
items.notes: “Faisait” is spelled with ai even though it is pronounced with a schwa, following the irregular stem of “faire”.

items.fr: Mes grands-parents habitaient à la campagne.
items.en: My grandparents used to live in the countryside.
items.ipa: me ɡʁɑ̃.pa.ʁɑ̃ a.bi.tɛ a la kɑ̃.paɲ
items.notes: “Habitaient” starts with a silent h, which must still be written even though it is never pronounced.

items.fr: Chaque été, nous allions chez nos cousins à la mer.
items.en: Every summer, we used to go to our cousins' house by the sea.
items.ipa: ʃak e.te nu.z‿a.ljɔ̃ ʃe no ku.zɛ̃ a la mɛʁ
items.notes: “Allions” needs the i before the ending to show the imparfait, distinguishing it from the present “allons”.

items.fr: Tu jouais du piano tous les soirs après l'école.
items.en: You used to play the piano every evening after school.
items.ipa: ty ʒu.wɛ dy pja.no tu le swaʁ a.pʁɛ le.kɔl
items.notes: “Jouais” sounds exactly like “jouait”, so only the subject pronoun shows which ending is correct.

items.fr: Il pleuvait quand elle est rentrée du travail.
items.en: It was raining when she got home from work.
items.ipa: il plœ.vɛ kɑ̃ ɛ.l‿ɛ ʁɑ̃.tʁe dy tʁa.vaj
items.notes: “Pleuvait” is only used in the third person singular because “pleuvoir” is an impersonal verb.

items.fr: Nous mangions souvent des crêpes le dimanche.
items.en: We used to eat crêpes often on Sundays.
items.ipa: nu mɑ̃.ʒjɔ̃ su.vɑ̃ de kʁɛp lə di.mɑ̃ʃ
items.notes: “Mangions” drops the e that appears in “je mangeais” because the i already softens the g before the ending.

items.fr: Quand vous étiez jeunes, vous voyagiez beaucoup.
items.en: When you were young, you used to travel a lot.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ vu.z‿e.tje ʒœn vu vwa.ja.ʒje bo.ku
items.notes: “Voyagiez” needs no extra e before -iez because the following i already keeps the g soft, unlike “je voyageais”.

items.fr: Ma grand-mère chantait pendant qu'elle cuisinait.
items.en: My grandmother used to sing while she cooked.
items.ipa: ma ɡʁɑ̃.mɛʁ ʃɑ̃.tɛ pɑ̃.dɑ̃ kɛl kɥi.zi.nɛ
items.notes: Both verbs stay in the imparfait because the sentence describes two simultaneous ongoing actions in the past.

items.fr: Il faisait nuit quand nous avons quitté le stade.
items.en: It was dark when we left the stadium.
items.ipa: il fə.zɛ nɥi kɑ̃ nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ki.te lə stad
items.notes: The background scene uses “faisait” in the imparfait, while “avons quitté” marks the completed action.

items.fr: Quand j'avais dix ans, je détestais les légumes.
items.en: When I was ten, I hated vegetables.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ ʒa.vɛ di.z‿ɑ̃ ʒə de.tɛs.tɛ le le.ɡym
items.notes: “Avais” comes from “avoir” and keeps the irregular stem “av-” throughout the imparfait.

items.fr: Elle portait toujours une écharpe rouge en hiver.
items.en: She always used to wear a red scarf in winter.
items.ipa: ɛl pɔʁ.tɛ tu.ʒuʁ yn e.ʃaʁp ʁuʒ ɑ̃.n‿i.vɛʁ
items.notes: “Portait” ends in -ait, never -er, since the imparfait never keeps the infinitive ending.

items.fr: Nous étions fatigués après la longue randonnée.
items.en: We were tired after the long hike.
items.ipa: nu.z‿e.tjɔ̃ fa.ti.ɡe a.pʁɛ la lɔ̃ɡ ʁɑ̃.dɔ.ne
items.notes: “Étions” is the irregular nous-form of “être” in the imparfait and must not be confused with “sommes”.

items.fr: Quand il était enfant, il avait peur du noir.
items.en: When he was a child, he was afraid of the dark.
items.ipa: kɑ̃.t‿il e.tɛ ɑ̃.fɑ̃ i.l‿a.vɛ pœʁ dy nwaʁ
items.notes: “Était” and “avait” both take the standard imparfait ending -ait for the third person singular.

items.fr: Autrefois, les enfants jouaient dans la rue après l'école.
items.en: In the old days, children used to play in the street after school.
items.ipa: o.tʁə.fwa le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ ʒwɛ dɑ̃ la ʁy a.pʁɛ le.kɔl
items.notes: “Jouaient” sounds identical to “jouait”, since the final -ent of the plural imparfait is always silent.

items.fr: Nous ne savions pas que la route était fermée.
items.en: We did not know that the road was closed.
items.ipa: nu nə sa.vjɔ̃ pa kə la ʁut e.tɛ fɛʁ.me
items.notes: “Savions” needs the i to show the imparfait ending, unlike the present tense “savons”.

items.fr: Tu avais toujours faim en rentrant de l'école.
items.en: You were always hungry coming home from school.
items.ipa: ty a.vɛ tu.ʒuʁ fɛ̃ ɑ̃ ʁɑ̃.tʁɑ̃ də le.kɔl
items.notes: “Avais” and “avait” sound identical in the imparfait, so only context tells the tu and il forms apart.

items.fr: Il faisait beau, alors nous sommes allés à la plage.
items.en: The weather was nice, so we went to the beach.
items.ipa: il fə.zɛ bo a.lɔʁ nu sɔm.z‿a.le a la plaʒ
items.notes: “Allés” agrees with the plural subject “nous” because “aller” always takes être as its auxiliary.

items.fr: Elle ne comprenait pas pourquoi le magasin était fermé.
items.en: She did not understand why the shop was closed.
items.ipa: ɛl nə kɔ̃.pʁə.nɛ pa puʁ.kwa lə ma.ɡa.zɛ̃ e.tɛ fɛʁ.me
items.notes: “Comprenait” follows the same imparfait pattern as “prendre”, keeping the stem “compren-”.

items.fr: Nous habitions près de l'école quand j'étais petit.
items.en: We used to live near the school when I was little.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.bi.tjɔ̃ pʁɛ də le.kɔl kɑ̃ ʒe.tɛ pə.ti
items.notes: “Habitions” keeps the silent h at the start, so no apostrophe is used before it.

items.fr: Vous aviez déjà mangé quand je suis arrivé.
items.en: You had already eaten when I arrived.
items.ipa: vu.z‿a.vje de.ʒa mɑ̃.ʒe kɑ̃ ʒə sɥi.z‿a.ʁi.ve
items.notes: “Aviez” carries the imparfait ending -iez for the vous form, never -ez alone.

items.fr: Le ciel était gris quand ils sont partis en vacances.
items.en: The sky was grey when they left on vacation.
items.ipa: lə sjɛl e.tɛ ɡʁi kɑ̃.t‿il sɔ̃ paʁ.ti ɑ̃ va.kɑ̃s
items.notes: “Partis” agrees with the masculine plural subject “ils” without needing any extra letter.

items.fr: Mon père travaillait dans une usine près de chez nous.
items.en: My father used to work in a factory near our house.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ pɛʁ tʁa.va.jɛ dɑ̃.z‿yn y.zin pʁɛ də ʃe nu
items.notes: “Travaillait” keeps the ill spelling pronounced as a y sound, not as a silent double l.

items.fr: Quand nous étions jeunes, nous ne regardions pas la télévision.
items.en: When we were young, we did not watch television.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ nu.z‿e.tjɔ̃ ʒœn nu nə ʁə.ɡaʁ.djɔ̃ pa la te.le.vi.zjɔ̃
items.notes: “Regardions” adds the i before -ons to mark the imparfait, unlike the present “regardons”.

items.fr: Elle avait l'habitude de courir tous les matins.
items.en: She used to have the habit of running every morning.
items.ipa: ɛ.l‿a.vɛ la.bi.tyd də ku.ʁiʁ tu le ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: “L'habitude” takes elision even though the h is silent, since “habitude” begins with a vowel sound.

items.fr: Nous parlions français à la maison quand j'étais jeune.
items.en: We used to speak French at home when I was young.
items.ipa: nu paʁ.ljɔ̃ fʁɑ̃.sɛ a la mɛ.zɔ̃ kɑ̃ ʒe.tɛ ʒœn
items.notes: “Parlions” carries the clear imparfait ending -ions, distinct from the present “parlons”.

items.fr: Il neigeait fort quand nous avons décidé de rentrer.
items.en: It was snowing hard when we decided to go home.
items.ipa: il nɛ.ʒɛ fɔʁ kɑ̃ nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ de.si.de də ʁɑ̃.tʁe
items.notes: “Neigeait” keeps the e after the g to preserve the soft sound before the a of the ending.

items.fr: Ma sœur et moi partagions toujours la même chambre.
items.en: My sister and I always used to share the same room.
items.ipa: ma sœʁ e mwa paʁ.ta.ʒjɔ̃ tu.ʒuʁ la mɛm ʃɑ̃bʁ
items.notes: “Partagions” needs no extra e before -ions because the following i already softens the g, unlike “je partageais”.

items.fr: La lettre qu'elle a écrite hier n'est jamais arrivée.
items.en: The letter she wrote yesterday never arrived.
items.ipa: la lɛtʁ kɛ.l‿a e.kʁit i.ɛʁ nɛ ʒa.mɛ.z‿a.ʁi.ve
items.notes: “Écrite” takes an extra e because the preceding direct object refers to the feminine noun “lettre”.

items.fr: Les valises que nous avons perdues n'ont jamais été retrouvées.
items.en: The suitcases we lost were never found.
items.ipa: le va.liz kə nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ pɛʁ.dy nɔ̃ ʒa.mɛ e.te ʁə.tʁu.ve
items.notes: “Perdues” agrees with the plural feminine “valises” because that direct object comes before the verb.

items.fr: Elle s'est cassé la jambe en skiant dans les Alpes.
items.en: She broke her leg while skiing in the Alps.
items.ipa: ɛl sɛ ka.se la ʒɑ̃b ɑ̃ ski.ɑ̃ dɑ̃ le.z‿alp
items.notes: “Cassé” stays invariable here because “la jambe” is a direct object placed after the verb, not before.

items.fr: Les photos qu'il a prises pendant le voyage étaient magnifiques.
items.en: The photos he took during the trip were magnificent.
items.ipa: le fɔ.to ki.l‿a pʁiz pɑ̃.dɑ̃ lə vwa.jaʒ e.tɛ ma.ɲi.fik
items.notes: “Prises” agrees with the preceding feminine plural object “photos”, so it ends in -ises.

items.fr: Nous nous sommes dépêchés pour ne pas rater le train.
items.en: We hurried so as not to miss the train.
items.ipa: nu nu sɔm de.pɛ.ʃe puʁ nə pa ʁa.te lə tʁɛ̃
items.notes: “Dépêchés” agrees with the masculine plural subject because the reflexive pronoun acts as a direct object.

items.fr: Après avoir fini ses études, elle est partie travailler à l'étranger.
items.en: After finishing her studies, she left to work abroad.
items.ipa: a.pʁɛ.z‿a.vwaʁ fi.ni se.z‿e.tyd ɛ.l‿ɛ paʁ.ti tʁa.va.je a le.tʁɑ̃.ʒe
items.notes: “Après avoir fini” uses the infinitive form because both clauses share the same subject “elle”.

items.fr: Ils se sont mariés dans une petite église de campagne.
items.en: They got married in a small country church.
items.ipa: il sə sɔ̃ ma.ʁje dɑ̃.z‿yn pə.tit e.ɡliz də kɑ̃.paɲ
items.notes: “Mariés” takes the plural agreement because the pronominal verb agrees with its subject “ils”.

items.fr: Le chien s'est enfui dès que la porte s'est ouverte.
items.en: The dog ran away as soon as the door opened.
items.ipa: lə ʃjɛ̃ sɛ.t‿ɑ̃.fɥi dɛ kə la pɔʁt sɛ.t‿u.vɛʁt
items.notes: “Ouverte” agrees with the feminine subject “porte” because “s'ouvrir” is conjugated with être.

items.fr: Nous avons dû changer nos plans à la dernière minute.
items.en: We had to change our plans at the last minute.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ dy ʃɑ̃.ʒe no plɑ̃ a la dɛʁ.njɛʁ mi.nyt
items.notes: “Dû” keeps its circumflex accent to distinguish it from the article “du”, even though both sound identical.

items.fr: Elle a finalement retrouvé le collier qu'elle croyait avoir perdu.
items.en: She finally found the necklace she thought she had lost.
items.ipa: ɛ.l‿a fi.nal.mɑ̃ ʁə.tʁu.ve lə kɔ.lje kɛl kʁwa.jɛ.t‿a.vwaʁ pɛʁ.dy
items.notes: “Perdu” stays masculine singular here because it is governed by the infinitive “avoir”, not agreeing with “collier”.

items.fr: Les enfants se sont couchés très tôt après leur longue journée.
items.en: The children went to bed very early after their long day.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ sə sɔ̃ ku.ʃe tʁɛ to a.pʁɛ lœʁ lɔ̃ɡ ʒuʁ.ne
items.notes: “Couchés” agrees with the plural subject “les enfants” because the reflexive pronoun acts as a direct object.

items.fr: Mon collègue a démissionné juste après avoir signé son nouveau contrat.
items.en: My colleague resigned right after signing his new contract.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ kɔ.lɛɡ a de.mi.sjɔ.ne ʒyst a.pʁɛ.z‿a.vwaʁ si.ɲe sɔ̃ nu.vo kɔ̃.tʁa
items.notes: “Démissionné” is spelled with two n's, unlike “démission”, to keep the nasal sound before the ending.

items.fr: Nous avons enfin réussi à réparer la voiture qui était tombée en panne.
items.en: We finally managed to repair the car that had broken down.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ɑ̃.fɛ̃ ʁe.y.si a ʁe.pa.ʁe la vwa.tyʁ ki e.tɛ tɔ̃.be ɑ̃ pan
items.notes: “Tombée” agrees with the feminine subject “voiture” because “tomber” is conjugated with être.

items.fr: Elle a menti à ses parents sur l'endroit où elle avait passé la soirée.
items.en: She lied to her parents about where she had spent the evening.
items.ipa: ɛ.l‿a mɑ̃.ti a se pa.ʁɑ̃ syʁ lɑ̃.dʁwa u ɛ.l‿a.vɛ pa.se la swa.ʁe
items.notes: “Menti” comes from “mentir” and forms the passé composé with avoir, unlike its cousin “partir”.

items.fr: Les touristes sont montés au sommet malgré la fatigue.
items.en: The tourists climbed to the summit despite their tiredness.
items.ipa: le tu.ʁist sɔ̃ mɔ̃.te o sɔ.mɛ mal.ɡʁe la fa.tiɡ
items.notes: “Montés” agrees with the plural subject because “monter” is conjugated with être when describing movement.

items.fr: Il a fallu attendre deux heures avant que le médecin nous reçoive.
items.en: We had to wait two hours before the doctor saw us.
items.ipa: i.l‿a fa.ly a.tɑ̃.dʁ dø.z‿œʁ a.vɑ̃ kə lə med.sɛ̃ nu ʁə.swav
items.notes: “Fallu” is the invariable past participle of the impersonal verb “falloir” and never changes form.

items.fr: Ma voisine a vendu sa maison sans prévenir personne.
items.en: My neighbor sold her house without telling anyone.
items.ipa: ma vwa.zin a vɑ̃.dy sa mɛ.zɔ̃ sɑ̃ pʁe.və.niʁ pɛʁ.sɔn
items.notes: “Vendu” follows the regular re-verb pattern for the past participle, ending simply in u.

items.fr: Nous sommes revenus plus tôt que prévu à cause de la tempête.
items.en: We came back earlier than planned because of the storm.
items.ipa: nu sɔm ʁə.və.ny ply to kə pʁe.vy a koz də la tɑ̃.pɛt
items.notes: “Revenus” agrees with the plural subject “nous” because “revenir” is built on “venir” and takes être.

items.fr: Le professeur a corrigé les copies qu'il avait ramassées la veille.
items.en: The teacher corrected the papers he had collected the day before.
items.ipa: lə pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ a kɔ.ʁi.ʒe le kɔ.pi ki.l‿a.vɛ ʁa.ma.se la vɛj
items.notes: “Ramassées” agrees with the preceding feminine plural object “copies” in this relative clause.

items.fr: Elle a couru jusqu'à la maison dès qu'elle a entendu la nouvelle.
items.en: She ran home as soon as she heard the news.
items.ipa: ɛ.l‿a ku.ʁy ʒys.ka la mɛ.zɔ̃ dɛ kɛ.l‿a ɑ̃.tɑ̃.dy la nu.vɛl
items.notes: “Couru” is the irregular past participle of “courir” and does not follow the -é pattern of er-verbs.

items.fr: Nous avons dû rentrer plus vite que d'habitude.
items.en: We had to go home faster than usual.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ dy ʁɑ̃.tʁe ply vit kə da.bi.tyd
items.notes: “Rentrer” stays as an infinitive after “dû” because modal constructions never conjugate the second verb.

items.fr: Le colis qu'elle attendait depuis des semaines est enfin arrivé.
items.en: The package she had been waiting for for weeks finally arrived.
items.ipa: lə kɔ.li kɛ.l‿a.tɑ̃.dɛ də.pɥi de smɛn ɛ.t‿ɑ̃.fɛ̃.n‿a.ʁi.ve
items.notes: “Arrivé” stays masculine singular here because it agrees with the masculine noun “colis”.

items.fr: Après avoir hésité longtemps, il a finalement accepté le poste.
items.en: After hesitating for a long time, he finally accepted the job offer.
items.ipa: a.pʁɛ.z‿a.vwaʁ e.zi.te lɔ̃.tɑ̃ i.l‿a fi.nal.mɑ̃ ak.sɛp.te lə pɔst
items.notes: “Hésité” begins with a silent h that still counts as a vowel sound, requiring liaison after “avoir”.

items.fr: Nous avons appris la nouvelle par un ami commun.
items.en: We learned the news through a mutual friend.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃.z‿a.pʁi la nu.vɛl paʁ œ̃.n‿a.mi kɔ.mœ̃
items.notes: “Appris” is spelled with a double p, unlike its cousin “pris”, to preserve the prefix of “apprendre”.

items.fr: Elle a dû partir avant la fin de la réunion à cause d'une urgence.
items.en: She had to leave before the end of the meeting because of an emergency.
items.ipa: ɛ.l‿a dy paʁ.tiʁ a.vɑ̃ la fɛ̃ də la ʁe.y.njɔ̃ a koz dyn yʁ.ʒɑ̃s
items.notes: “Partir” stays as an infinitive after “dû” because modal constructions never conjugate the second verb.

items.fr: Quand elle vivait à Marseille, elle prenait le bus tous les jours pour aller travailler.
items.en: When she lived in Marseille, she used to take the bus every day to go to work.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ ɛl vi.vɛ a maʁ.sɛj ɛl pʁə.nɛ lə bys tu le ʒuʁ puʁ a.le tʁa.va.je
items.notes: “Vivait” and “prenait” both stay in the imparfait because they describe repeated habits, not single events.

items.fr: La nuit tombait déjà lorsque nous sommes finalement arrivés au camping.
items.en: Night was already falling by the time we finally arrived at the campsite.
items.ipa: la nɥi tɔ̃.bɛ de.ʒa lɔʁs.kə nu sɔm fi.nal.mɑ̃ a.ʁi.ve o kɑ̃.piŋ
items.notes: “Tombait” describes the ongoing background scene, while “sommes arrivés” marks the single completed action.

items.fr: Mes parents se disputaient souvent quand j'étais adolescent.
items.en: My parents used to argue often when I was a teenager.
items.ipa: me pa.ʁɑ̃ sə dis.py.tɛ su.vɑ̃ kɑ̃ ʒe.tɛ.z‿a.dɔ.lɛ.sɑ̃
items.notes: “Se disputaient” agrees in number with the plural subject “mes parents” through the ending -aient.

items.fr: Nous ne savions pas encore que le vol avait été annulé.
items.en: We did not yet know that the flight had been cancelled.
items.ipa: nu nə sa.vjɔ̃ pa ɑ̃.kɔʁ kə lə vɔl a.vɛ e.te a.ny.le
items.notes: “Avait été annulé” forms a pluperfect, showing an event that happened before another past event.

items.fr: Elle attendait patiemment pendant que son mari cherchait une place de parking.
items.en: She waited patiently while her husband looked for a parking spot.
items.ipa: ɛ.l‿a.tɑ̃.dɛ pa.sjam.mɑ̃ pɑ̃.dɑ̃ kə sɔ̃ ma.ʁi ʃɛʁ.ʃɛ yn plas də paʁ.kiŋ
items.notes: “Patiemment” is spelled with emm, not amment, because it derives from the adjective “patient”.

items.fr: Quand nous étions étudiants, nous n'avions jamais assez d'argent.
items.en: When we were students, we never had enough money.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ nu.z‿e.tjɔ̃ e.ty.djɑ̃ nu.n‿a.vjɔ̃ ʒa.mɛ.z‿a.se daʁ.ʒɑ̃
items.notes: “N'avions” combines the elision of “ne” before a vowel with the irregular imparfait stem of “avoir”.

items.fr: Il pleuvait si fort que la route était complètement inondée.
items.en: It was raining so hard that the road was completely flooded.
items.ipa: il plœ.vɛ si fɔʁ kə la ʁut e.tɛ kɔ̃.plɛt.mɑ̃ i.nɔ̃.de
items.notes: “Pleuvait” and “était” both appear in the imparfait because they describe ongoing conditions, not a single action.

items.fr: Ma grand-mère racontait toujours la même histoire pendant les fêtes de famille.
items.en: My grandmother always used to tell the same story during family gatherings.
items.ipa: ma ɡʁɑ̃.mɛʁ ʁa.kɔ̃.tɛ tu.ʒuʁ la mɛm is.twaʁ pɑ̃.dɑ̃ le fɛt də fa.mij
items.notes: “Racontait” ends in -ait, describing a habitual past action repeated on many occasions.

items.fr: Comme il ne connaissait personne à la fête, il est reparti tout de suite.
items.en: Since he did not know anyone at the party, he left again right away.
items.ipa: kɔm il nə kɔ.nɛ.sɛ pɛʁ.sɔn a la fɛt i.l‿ɛ ʁə.paʁ.ti tu də sɥit
items.notes: “Connaissait” keeps the double s from “connaître” before the imparfait ending.

items.fr: Quand elles étaient jeunes, elles rêvaient de devenir actrices.
items.en: When they were young, they used to dream of becoming actresses.
items.ipa: kɑ̃.t‿ɛl.z‿e.tɛ ʒœn ɛl ʁɛ.vɛ də dəv.niʁ ak.tʁis
items.notes: “Étaient” carries the silent ending -ent that marks the third person plural in the imparfait.

items.fr: Il ne savait pas conduire quand il a acheté sa première voiture.
items.en: He did not know how to drive when he bought his first car.
items.ipa: il nə sa.vɛ pa kɔ̃.dɥiʁ kɑ̃.t‿i.l‿a a.ʃə.te sa pʁə.mjɛʁ vwa.tyʁ
items.notes: “Savait” in the imparfait describes an ongoing state of ignorance, contrasted with the single completed action “a acheté”.

items.fr: Nous habitions déjà ici quand cette rue s'appelait encore autrement.
items.en: We already lived here when this street was still called something else.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.bi.tjɔ̃ de.ʒa i.si kɑ̃ sɛt ʁy sa.plɛ ɑ̃.kɔʁ o.tʁə.mɑ̃
items.notes: “S'appelait” doubles the l because the imparfait keeps the same stem spelling as the infinitive “s'appeler”.

items.fr: Comme elle avait mal à la tête, elle est restée couchée toute la journée.
items.en: Since she had a headache, she stayed in bed all day.
items.ipa: kɔ.m‿ɛ.l‿a.vɛ mal a la tɛt ɛ.l‿ɛ ʁɛs.te ku.ʃe tut la ʒuʁ.ne
items.notes: “Restée” agrees with the feminine subject “elle” because “rester” always takes être as its auxiliary.

items.fr: Pendant que je faisais mes devoirs, mon frère regardait la télévision.
items.en: While I did my homework, my brother watched television.
items.ipa: pɑ̃.dɑ̃ kə ʒə fə.zɛ me dəv.wɑʁ mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ ʁə.ɡaʁ.dɛ la te.le.vi.zjɔ̃
items.notes: “Faisais” is spelled with ai even though it is pronounced with a schwa, following the irregular stem of “faire”.

items.fr: Ils ne pouvaient plus continuer parce que la nuit tombait déjà.
items.en: They could no longer continue because night was already falling.
items.ipa: il nə pu.vɛ ply kɔ̃.ti.nɥe paʁs.kə la nɥi tɔ̃.bɛ de.ʒa
items.notes: “Pouvaient” comes from the irregular stem “pouv-”, entirely different from the infinitive “pouvoir”.

items.fr: Elle portait encore son uniforme quand elle est rentrée du travail.
items.en: She was still wearing her uniform when she got home from work.
items.ipa: ɛl pɔʁ.tɛ ɑ̃.kɔʁ sɔ.n‿y.ni.fɔʁm kɑ̃.t‿ɛ.l‿ɛ ʁɑ̃.tʁe dy tʁa.vaj
items.notes: “Portait” describes the ongoing state of being dressed, while “est rentrée” marks the single completed action.

items.fr: Nous discutions tranquillement quand le téléphone a soudainement sonné.
items.en: We were chatting quietly when the phone suddenly rang.
items.ipa: nu dis.ky.tjɔ̃ tʁɑ̃.kil.mɑ̃ kɑ̃ lə te.le.fɔn a su.dɛn.mɑ̃ sɔ.ne
items.notes: “Discutions” takes the imparfait ending -ions for nous, unlike the passé composé form “avons discuté”.

items.fr: Comme il faisait beau ce jour-là, nous avons décidé de pique-niquer dehors.
items.en: Since the weather was nice that day, we decided to have a picnic outside.
items.ipa: kɔm il fə.zɛ bo sə ʒuʁ.la nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ de.si.de də pik.ni.ke də.ɔʁ
items.notes: “Pique-niquer” keeps the hyphen from the compound noun “pique-nique” even in its verb form.

items.fr: Quand j'étais enfant, je détestais me lever tôt pour aller à l'école.
items.en: When I was a child, I hated getting up early to go to school.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ ʒe.tɛ ɑ̃.fɑ̃ ʒə de.tɛs.tɛ mə lə.ve to puʁ a.le a le.kɔl
items.notes: “Détestais” ends in -ais for the je form of the imparfait, never in -é like a past participle.

items.fr: Elle ne comprenait toujours pas pourquoi il n'était pas venu à son anniversaire.
items.en: She still did not understand why he had not come to her birthday party.
items.ipa: ɛl nə kɔ̃.pʁə.nɛ tu.ʒuʁ pa puʁ.kwa i.l‿ne.tɛ pa və.ny a sɔ.n‿a.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ
items.notes: “N'était pas venu” forms the pluperfect, showing an action that had already happened before the moment of “comprenait”.

items.fr: Nous étions tellement fatigués que nous nous sommes endormis pendant le film.
items.en: We were so tired that we fell asleep during the movie.
items.ipa: nu.z‿e.tjɔ̃ tɛl.mɑ̃ fa.ti.ɡe kə nu nu sɔm.z‿ɑ̃.dɔʁ.mi pɑ̃.dɑ̃ lə film
items.notes: “Endormis” agrees with the plural subject “nous” because the reflexive pronoun functions as the direct object.

items.fr: Le marché battait déjà son plein quand nous sommes arrivés sur la place du village.
items.en: The market was already in full swing when we arrived at the village square.
items.ipa: lə maʁ.ʃe ba.tɛ de.ʒa sɔ̃ plɛ̃ kɑ̃ nu sɔm.z‿a.ʁi.ve syʁ la plas dy vi.laʒ
items.notes: “Battait” stays in the imparfait to describe the ongoing bustle, contrasted with the completed action “sommes arrivés”.

items.fr: Puisqu'elle ne connaissait personne en ville, elle a passé son premier week-end seule.
items.en: Since she did not know anyone in town, she spent her first weekend alone.
items.ipa: pɥis.kɛl nə kɔ.nɛ.sɛ pɛʁ.sɔn ɑ̃ vil ɛ.l‿a pa.se sɔ̃ pʁə.mje wi.kɛnd sœl
items.notes: “Puisque” elides its final e before “elle” because the next word begins with a vowel sound.

items.fr: Autrefois, on voyageait surtout en train parce que les billets d'avion coûtaient cher.
items.en: In the old days, people mostly traveled by train because plane tickets were expensive.
items.ipa: o.tʁə.fwa ɔ̃ vwa.ja.ʒɛ syʁ.tu ɑ̃ tʁɛ̃ paʁs.kə le bi.jɛ da.vjɔ̃ ku.tɛ ʃɛʁ
items.notes: “Voyageait” and “coûtaient” both remain in the imparfait since they describe a general habitual situation.

items.fr: Comme nous ne nous connaissions pas encore bien, la conversation était un peu gênée.
items.en: Since we did not yet know each other well, the conversation was a bit awkward.
items.ipa: kɔm nu nə nu kɔ.nɛ.sjɔ̃ pa ɑ̃.kɔʁ bjɛ̃ la kɔ̃.vɛʁ.sa.sjɔ̃ e.tɛ œ̃ pø ʒɛ.ne
items.notes: “Connaissions” adds the i before -ons to signal the imparfait, distinct from the present “connaissons”.

items.fr: Bien qu'elle ait prévu de partir tôt, elle s'est finalement attardée avec ses collègues jusqu'au soir.
items.en: Although she had planned to leave early, she ended up lingering with her colleagues until evening.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃.k‿ɛ.l‿ɛt pʁe.vy də paʁ.tiʁ to ɛl sɛ fi.nal.mɑ̃ a.taʁ.de a.vɛk se kɔ.lɛɡ ʒys.ko swaʁ
items.notes: “Attardée” takes an extra e to agree with the feminine subject “elle” because the pronominal verb is conjugated with être.

items.fr: Les documents que le directeur avait exigés la veille n'ont finalement jamais été envoyés.
items.en: The documents the director had demanded the day before were in fact never sent.
items.ipa: le dɔ.ky.mɑ̃ kə lə di.ʁɛk.tœʁ a.vɛ.t‿ɛɡ.zi.ʒe la vɛj nɔ̃ fi.nal.mɑ̃ ʒa.mɛ e.te ɑ̃.vwa.je
items.notes: “Exigés” agrees with the preceding masculine plural direct object “documents” in this pluperfect construction.

items.fr: Elle a fini par avouer qu'elle s'était trompée dès le début de la négociation.
items.en: She finally admitted that she had been mistaken from the very start of the negotiation.
items.ipa: ɛ.l‿a fi.ni pa.ʁ‿a.vwe kɛl se.tɛ tʁɔ̃.pe dɛ lə de.by də la ne.ɡɔ.sja.sjɔ̃
items.notes: “S'était trompée” is a pluperfect showing that the mistake occurred before the moment of admitting it.

items.fr: Malgré la fatigue accumulée, les ouvriers ont terminé le chantier avant la date prévue.
items.en: Despite their accumulated tiredness, the workers finished the construction site before the planned date.
items.ipa: mal.ɡʁe la fa.tiɡ a.ky.my.le le.z‿u.vʁje ɔ̃ tɛʁ.mi.ne lə ʃɑ̃.tje a.vɑ̃ la dat pʁe.vy
items.notes: “Terminé” stays invariable because it is used with avoir and no direct object precedes it.

items.fr: C'est à Lisbonne qu'ils se sont enfin retrouvés après des années de séparation.
items.en: It was in Lisbon that they finally found each other again after years apart.
items.ipa: sɛ.t‿a liz.bɔn kil sə sɔ̃.t‿ɑ̃.fɛ̃ ʁə.tʁu.ve a.pʁɛ de.z‿a.ne də se.pa.ʁa.sjɔ̃
items.notes: “Retrouvés” agrees with the masculine plural subject “ils” because the reflexive pronoun serves as their mutual direct object.

items.fr: Elle a longuement hésité avant d'accepter le poste qu'on lui avait proposé à l'étranger.
items.en: She hesitated for a long time before accepting the position she had been offered abroad.
items.ipa: ɛ.l‿a lɔ̃ɡ.mɑ̃ e.zi.te a.vɑ̃ dak.sɛp.te lə pɔst kɔ̃ lɥi a.vɛ pʁɔ.po.ze a le.tʁɑ̃.ʒe
items.notes: “Proposé” remains masculine singular here since it agrees with “poste”, the masculine antecedent of the relative pronoun.

items.fr: Nous avons dû reconnaître que notre stratégie initiale s'était révélée inefficace.
items.en: We had to admit that our initial strategy had proven ineffective.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ dy ʁə.kɔ.nɛtʁ kə nɔtʁ stʁa.te.ʒi i.ni.sjal se.tɛ ʁe.ve.le i.nɛ.fi.kas
items.notes: “S'était révélée” uses the pluperfect to place the strategy's failure before the moment of admission.

items.fr: Le témoin a affirmé avoir vu la scène se dérouler sous ses propres yeux.
items.en: The witness stated that he had seen the scene unfold with his own eyes.
items.ipa: lə te.mwɛ̃ a.t‿a.fiʁ.me a.vwaʁ vy la sɛn sə de.ʁu.le su se pʁɔpʁ jø
items.notes: “Affirmé” is spelled with a double f, echoing its Latin root, unlike other similar-sounding words.

items.fr: Après s'être longuement disputés, les deux frères ont fini par se réconcilier autour d'un café.
items.en: After a long argument, the two brothers eventually made up over a cup of coffee.
items.ipa: a.pʁɛ sɛtʁ lɔ̃ɡ.mɑ̃ dis.py.te le dø fʁɛʁ ɔ̃ fi.ni paʁ sə ʁe.kɔ̃.si.lje o.tuʁ dœ̃ ka.fe
items.notes: “Disputés” agrees with the plural subject “les deux frères” because it follows “s'être” in this compound infinitive.

items.fr: Le metteur en scène a expliqué que les acteurs avaient répété la pièce pendant des mois avant la première.
items.en: The director explained that the actors had rehearsed the play for months before opening night.
items.ipa: lə mɛ.tœʁ ɑ̃ sɛn a.t‿ɛks.pli.ke kə le.z‿ak.tœʁ a.vɛ ʁe.pe.te la pjɛs pɑ̃.dɑ̃ de mwa a.vɑ̃ la pʁə.mjɛʁ
items.notes: “Avaient répété” forms the pluperfect, showing the rehearsals took place before the director's explanation.

items.fr: À l'époque où nous vivions à l'étranger, nous ne rentrions en France que pour les fêtes de fin d'année.
items.en: Back when we lived abroad, we would only return to France for the end of year holidays.
items.ipa: a le.pɔk u nu vi.vjɔ̃ a le.tʁɑ̃.ʒe nu nə ʁɑ̃.tʁjɔ̃ ɑ̃ fʁɑ̃s kə puʁ le fɛt də fɛ̃ da.ne
items.notes: “Rentrions” keeps the imparfait ending -ions to describe a recurring habit rather than a single trip.

items.fr: Bien qu'il connaisse déjà la région, il s'est perdu à plusieurs reprises pendant son excursion.
items.en: Even though he already knew the area, he got lost several times during his outing.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃.k‿il kɔ.nɛs de.ʒa la ʁe.ʒjɔ̃ i.l‿sɛ pɛʁ.dy a plu.zjœʁ ʁə.pʁiz pɑ̃.dɑ̃ sɔ.n‿ɛks.kyʁ.sjɔ̃
items.notes: “Perdu” stays masculine singular here because it agrees with the masculine subject “il” in this être construction.

items.fr: Quand elle était plus jeune, elle rêvait de parcourir le monde avant de s'installer quelque part.
items.en: When she was younger, she used to dream of traveling the world before settling down somewhere.
items.ipa: kɑ̃.t‿ɛ.l‿e.tɛ ply ʒœn ɛl ʁɛ.vɛ də paʁ.ku.ʁiʁ lə mɔ̃d a.vɑ̃ də sɛ̃s.ta.le kɛl.kə paʁ
items.notes: “Rêvait” keeps the circumflex accent on the e inherited from the infinitive “rêver”.

items.fr: Les négociations traînaient depuis des semaines lorsque les deux parties sont enfin parvenues à un accord.
items.en: Negotiations had been dragging on for weeks when the two parties finally reached an agreement.
items.ipa: le ne.ɡɔ.sja.sjɔ̃ tʁɛ.nɛ də.pɥi de smɛn lɔʁs.kə le dø paʁ.ti sɔ̃.t‿ɑ̃.fɛ̃ paʁ.və.ny a œ̃.n‿a.kɔʁ
items.notes: “Parvenues” agrees with the feminine plural subject “parties” because “parvenir” is conjugated with être.

items.fr: Nous ignorions encore, à l'époque, que cette décision allait bouleverser toute notre existence.
items.en: We did not yet know, at the time, that this decision would upend our entire existence.
items.ipa: nu.z‿i.ɲɔ.ʁjɔ̃ ɑ̃.kɔʁ a le.pɔk kə sɛt de.si.zjɔ̃ a.lɛ bul.vɛʁ.se tut nɔ.tʁə.ɛɡ.zis.tɑ̃s
items.notes: “Ignorions” carries the imparfait ending -ions, describing an ongoing lack of awareness rather than a single moment.

items.fr: Comme elle n'avait jamais vraiment aimé son travail, elle a saisi l'occasion de démissionner sans regret.
items.en: Since she had never really liked her job, she seized the opportunity to resign without regret.
items.ipa: kɔm ɛl na.vɛ ʒa.mɛ vʁɛ.mɑ̃ ɛ.me sɔ̃ tʁa.vaj ɛ.l‿a sɛ.zi lɔ.ka.zjɔ̃ də de.mi.sjɔ.ne sɑ̃ ʁə.ɡʁɛ
items.notes: “N'avait jamais aimé” forms the pluperfect, situating her long dislike before the moment she resigned.

items.fr: Tandis que ses collègues discutaient encore du projet, il avait déjà pris sa décision depuis longtemps.
items.en: While his colleagues were still discussing the project, he had already made up his mind long before.
items.ipa: tɑ̃.di kə se kɔ.lɛɡ dis.ky.tɛ ɑ̃.kɔʁ dy pʁɔ.ʒɛ i.l‿a.vɛ de.ʒa pʁi sa de.si.zjɔ̃ də.pɥi lɔ̃.tɑ̃
items.notes: “Avait pris” is the pluperfect, marking an action completed before the ongoing discussion described by “discutaient”.

items.fr: Autrefois, les habitants du village se réunissaient chaque dimanche sur la place pour discuter des affaires locales.
items.en: In the old days, the villagers used to gather every Sunday in the square to discuss local matters.
items.ipa: o.tʁə.fwa le.z‿a.bi.tɑ̃ dy vi.laʒ sə ʁe.y.ni.sɛ ʃak di.mɑ̃ʃ syʁ la plas puʁ dis.ky.te de.z‿a.fɛʁ lɔ.kal
items.notes: “Se réunissaient” keeps the double s from “réunir” to preserve the unvoiced sound before the imparfait ending.

items.fr: Ce n'est qu'en relisant ses vieilles lettres qu'elle a compris à quel point sa jeunesse lui manquait.
items.en: It was only while rereading her old letters that she understood how much she missed her youth.
items.ipa: sə nɛ kɑ̃ ʁə.li.zɑ̃ se vjɛj lɛtʁ kɛ.l‿a kɔ̃.pʁi a kɛl pwɛ̃ sa ʒœ.nɛs lɥi mɑ̃.kɛ
items.notes: “Manquait” stays in the imparfait because it expresses the ongoing feeling discovered through the completed action “a compris”.

items.fr: Ce matin, j'ai raté le bus.
items.en: This morning, I missed the bus.

items.fr: Elle a acheté du pain à la boulangerie.
items.en: She bought bread at the bakery.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle a acheté","t":"she bought"},{"w":"du pain","t":"bread"},{"w":"à la boulangerie.","t":"at the bakery"}]}

items.fr: Nous avons visité le musée samedi dernier.
items.en: We visited the museum last Saturday.

items.fr: Il a oublié son parapluie au bureau.
items.en: He forgot his umbrella at the office.

items.fr: Tu as fini tes devoirs avant le dîner.
items.en: You finished your homework before dinner.

items.fr: J'ai rencontré un vieil ami au marché.
items.en: I met an old friend at the market.

items.fr: Mes parents sont arrivés à l'aéroport à midi.
items.en: My parents arrived at the airport at noon.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Mes parents","t":"my parents"},{"w":"sont arrivés","t":"arrived"},{"w":"à l'aéroport","t":"at the airport"},{"w":"à midi.","t":"at noon"}]}

items.fr: Elle est tombée dans l'escalier hier soir.
items.en: She fell down the stairs last night.

items.fr: Nous sommes rentrés très tard hier.
items.en: We got home very late yesterday.

items.fr: Il a réparé sa voiture ce week-end.
items.en: He fixed his car this weekend.

items.fr: J'ai téléphoné à ma sœur après le travail.
items.en: I called my sister after work.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"J'ai téléphoné","t":"I called"},{"w":"à ma sœur","t":"my sister"},{"w":"après le travail.","t":"after work"}]}

items.fr: Elle a fêté son anniversaire avec ses amis.
items.en: She celebrated her birthday with her friends.

items.fr: Nous avons mangé au restaurant vendredi soir.
items.en: We ate at the restaurant on Friday evening.

items.fr: Il est né dans un petit village.
items.en: He was born in a small village.

items.fr: J'ai perdu mon téléphone dans le taxi.
items.en: I lost my phone in the taxi.

items.fr: Elle a réussi son examen de français.
Nous avons regardé un film hier soir.
items.en: We watched a movie last night.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons regardé","t":"we watched"},{"w":"un film","t":"a movie"},{"w":"hier soir.","t":"last night"}]}

items.fr: Il a trouvé un travail la semaine dernière.
items.en: He found a job last week.

items.fr: J'ai lavé la voiture ce matin.
items.en: I washed the car this morning.

items.fr: Elle est partie en vacances en juillet.
items.en: She went on vacation in July.

items.fr: Nous avons acheté une nouvelle table.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons acheté","t":"we bought"},{"w":"une nouvelle table.","t":"a new table"}]}

items.fr: Il a cassé un verre dans la cuisine.
items.en: He broke a glass in the kitchen.

items.fr: J'ai écrit une lettre à mes grands-parents.
items.en: I wrote a letter to my grandparents.

items.fr: Elle a couru dix kilomètres dimanche.
items.en: She ran ten kilometers on Sunday.

items.fr: Nous avons planté des fleurs dans le jardin.
items.en: We planted flowers in the garden.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons planté","t":"we planted"},{"w":"des fleurs","t":"flowers"},{"w":"dans le jardin.","t":"in the garden"}]}

items.fr: Il s'est levé très tôt aujourd'hui.
items.en: He got up very early today.

items.fr: J'ai adopté un chat au refuge.
items.en: I adopted a cat at the shelter.

items.fr: Elle a gagné le match de tennis.
Quand elle a entendu la nouvelle, elle a immédiatement appelé sa mère.
items.en: When she heard the news, she immediately called her mother.

items.fr: Après avoir fini son travail, elle a rejoint ses collègues au café.
items.en: After finishing her work, she joined her colleagues at the café.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Après avoir fini son travail,","t":"after finishing her work,"},{"w":"elle a rejoint","t":"she joined"},{"w":"ses collègues au café.","t":"her colleagues at the café"}]}

items.fr: Nous avons dû changer nos plans parce qu'il a commencé à neiger.
items.en: We had to change our plans because it started to snow.

items.fr: Elle a appelé le médecin dès qu'elle a senti une forte douleur.
items.en: She called the doctor as soon as she felt a sharp pain.

items.fr: Ils ont raté leur vol parce qu'ils sont arrivés en retard à l'aéroport.
items.en: They missed their flight because they arrived late at the airport.

items.fr: Après avoir lu le message, il a couru jusqu'à la gare.
items.en: After reading the message, he ran to the station.

items.fr: Puisque le magasin a fermé plus tôt que prévu, nous avons dû revenir le lendemain.
items.en: Since the store closed earlier than expected, we had to come back the next day.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Puisque le magasin a fermé plus tôt que prévu,","t":"since the store closed earlier than expected,"},{"w":"nous avons dû revenir le lendemain.","t":"we had to come back the next day"}]}

items.fr: Quand nous sommes arrivés à l'hôtel, la réceptionniste nous a donné les clés de la chambre.
items.en: When we arrived at the hotel, the receptionist gave us the room keys.

items.fr: Il a tellement travaillé qu'il s'est endormi devant la télévision.
items.en: He worked so much that he fell asleep in front of the television.

items.fr: Elle s'est excusée après avoir cassé le vase de sa grand-mère.
items.en: She apologized after breaking her grandmother's vase.

items.fr: Nous avons attendu si longtemps que nous avons finalement décidé de partir.
items.en: We waited so long that we finally decided to leave.

items.fr: Dès que le professeur est entré, les élèves se sont tus.
items.en: As soon as the teacher came in, the students fell silent.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Dès que le professeur est entré,","t":"as soon as the teacher came in,"},{"w":"les élèves se sont tus.","t":"the students fell silent"}]}

items.fr: Il a fallu deux heures aux mécaniciens pour réparer la voiture.
items.en: It took the mechanics two hours to repair the car.

items.fr: Dès qu'il est arrivé chez lui, il a pris une douche chaude.
items.en: As soon as he got home, he took a hot shower.

items.fr: Comme elle a raté son train, elle a dû prendre le suivant.
items.en: Since she missed her train, she had to take the next one.

items.fr: Après avoir cherché partout, il a enfin retrouvé ses lunettes.
items.en: After searching everywhere, he finally found his glasses.

items.fr: Elle a tant couru qu'elle est arrivée essoufflée à la réunion.
items.en: She ran so much that she arrived out of breath at the meeting.

items.fr: Nous avons signé le contrat après avoir posé toutes nos questions.
items.en: We signed the contract after asking all our questions.

items.fr: Il a démissionné dès qu'il a trouvé un meilleur poste.
items.en: He resigned as soon as he found a better position.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il a démissionné","t":"he resigned"},{"w":"dès qu'il a trouvé","t":"as soon as he found"},{"w":"un meilleur poste.","t":"a better position"}]}

items.fr: Elle a rangé sa chambre avant que ses parents ne rentrent.
items.en: She tidied her room before her parents got home.

items.fr: Nous avons fêté sa réussite parce qu'elle a obtenu son diplôme.
items.en: We celebrated her success because she got her diploma.

items.fr: Il s'est cassé le bras en tombant de son vélo.
items.en: He broke his arm falling off his bike.

items.fr: Elle a pleuré de joie quand elle a revu ses parents.
items.en: She cried with joy when she saw her parents again.

items.fr: Nous avons dormi à l'hôtel parce que notre vol a été annulé.
items.en: We slept at the hotel because our flight was cancelled.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous avons dormi à l'hôtel","t":"we slept at the hotel"},{"w":"parce que notre vol a été annulé.","t":"because our flight was cancelled"}]}

items.fr: Il a appris la nouvelle par un ami qui l'a appelé le soir même.
items.en: He heard the news from a friend who called him that very evening.

items.fr: Bien qu'il ait plu toute la matinée, les organisateurs ont maintenu la fête au grand air.
items.en: Although it had rained all morning, the organizers kept the outdoor party going.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Bien qu'il ait plu toute la matinée,","t":"although it had rained all morning,"},{"w":"les organisateurs ont maintenu","t":"the organizers kept"},{"w":"la fête au grand air.","t":"the party outdoors"}]}

items.fr: Après s'être longuement excusé, il a fini par convaincre son ancien patron de le reprendre.
items.en: After apologizing at length, he finally managed to convince his former boss to take him back.

items.fr: Dès que la nouvelle s'est répandue dans le village, tout le monde s'est précipité vers la mairie.
items.en: As soon as the news spread through the village, everyone rushed to the town hall.

items.fr: Malgré la fatigue accumulée, elle a terminé le marathon sous les applaudissements de la foule.
items.en: Despite her accumulated fatigue, she finished the marathon to the applause of the crowd.

items.fr: Une fois le contrat signé, les deux entreprises ont officiellement scellé leur partenariat.
items.en: Once the contract was signed, the two companies officially sealed their partnership.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Une fois le contrat signé,","t":"once the contract was signed,"},{"w":"les deux entreprises","t":"the two companies"},{"w":"ont officiellement scellé leur partenariat.","t":"officially sealed their partnership"}]}

items.fr: Il a fallu attendre la tombée de la nuit pour que les secouristes retrouvent enfin les randonneurs égarés.
items.en: They had to wait until nightfall for the rescuers to finally find the lost hikers.

items.fr: Après avoir hésité pendant des semaines, elle s'est enfin décidée à changer de carrière.
items.en: After hesitating for weeks, she finally decided to change careers.

items.fr: Le conseil municipal a voté la construction du pont après de longs débats houleux.
items.en: The city council voted for the bridge's construction after long, heated debates.

items.fr: Il a posé le pied sur le quai et a aussitôt cherché son billet dans toutes ses poches.
items.en: He set foot on the platform and immediately searched all his pockets for his ticket.

items.fr: Grâce à l'aide de ses voisins, elle a pu déménager en un seul week-end.
items.en: Thanks to her neighbors' help, she managed to move in a single weekend.

items.fr: Quand j'étais petit, j'habitais à la campagne.
items.en: When I was little, I lived in the countryside.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Quand j'étais petit,","t":"when I was little,"},{"w":"j'habitais","t":"I lived"},{"w":"à la campagne.","t":"in the countryside"}]}

items.fr: Elle avait les cheveux longs et bouclés.
Nous allions à la piscine tous les samedis.
items.en: We used to go to the pool every Saturday.

items.fr: Il faisait toujours ses devoirs après l'école.
items.en: He always did his homework after school.

items.fr: Mes parents travaillaient dans une usine.
items.en: My parents worked in a factory.

items.fr: Tu jouais souvent au ballon dans la cour.
items.en: You often played ball in the yard.

items.fr: Il pleuvait beaucoup pendant l'été cette année-là.
items.en: It rained a lot during the summer that year.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il pleuvait beaucoup","t":"it rained a lot"},{"w":"pendant l'été","t":"during the summer"},{"w":"cette année-là.","t":"that year"}]}

items.fr: Elle chantait tous les matins sous la douche.
items.en: She sang every morning in the shower.

items.fr: Nous n'avions pas de voiture à cette époque.
items.en: We didn't have a car at that time.

items.fr: Le village était très calme le dimanche.
items.en: The village was very quiet on Sundays.

items.fr: J'aimais beaucoup lire des bandes dessinées.
Ma grand-mère faisait des gâteaux le dimanche.
items.en: My grandmother used to make cakes on Sundays.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Ma grand-mère faisait","t":"my grandmother used to make"},{"w":"des gâteaux","t":"cakes"},{"w":"le dimanche.","t":"on Sundays"}]}

items.fr: Il neigeait souvent en hiver dans cette région.
items.en: It often snowed in winter in that region.

items.fr: Nous habitions dans un petit appartement.
items.en: We lived in a small apartment.

items.fr: Elle portait toujours une robe bleue.
items.en: She always wore a blue dress.

items.fr: Les enfants jouaient dans la rue jusqu'au soir.
items.en: The children played in the street until evening.

items.fr: Il faisait très chaud ce jour-là.
items.en: It was very hot that day.

items.fr: Nous prenions le train tous les matins.
items.en: We used to take the train every morning.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Nous prenions le train","t":"we used to take the train"},{"w":"tous les matins.","t":"every morning"}]}

items.fr: Elle avait peur des chiens quand elle était jeune.
items.en: She was afraid of dogs when she was young.

items.fr: Mon grand-père racontait souvent des histoires drôles.
items.en: My grandfather often told funny stories.

items.fr: Le magasin fermait à midi pour le déjeuner.
items.en: The shop closed at noon for lunch.

items.fr: Nous étions très proches de nos voisins.
items.en: We were very close to our neighbors.

items.fr: Elle dessinait tout le temps dans son cahier.
items.en: She drew all the time in her notebook.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle dessinait tout le temps","t":"she drew all the time"},{"w":"dans son cahier.","t":"in her notebook"}]}

items.fr: Il conduisait très prudemment sur l'autoroute.
items.en: He drove very carefully on the highway.

items.fr: Les rues étaient désertes tôt le matin.
items.en: The streets were deserted early in the morning.

items.fr: Nous mangions souvent chez ma tante le dimanche.
items.en: We often ate at my aunt's on Sundays.

items.fr: Elle travaillait comme infirmière à l'hôpital.
items.en: She worked as a nurse at the hospital.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle travaillait","t":"she worked"},{"w":"comme infirmière","t":"as a nurse"},{"w":"à l'hôpital.","t":"at the hospital"}]}

items.fr: Il faisait toujours beau pendant nos vacances.
items.en: The weather was always nice during our vacations.

items.fr: Quand j'étais enfant, je passais tous les étés chez mes grands-parents à la montagne.
items.en: When I was a child, I spent every summer at my grandparents' in the mountains.

items.fr: Pendant qu'elle préparait le dîner, le téléphone a sonné.
items.en: While she was preparing dinner, the phone rang.

items.fr: Il faisait ses courses quand il a rencontré son ancien professeur.
items.en: He was doing his shopping when he ran into his former teacher.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Il faisait ses courses","t":"he was doing his shopping"},{"w":"quand il a rencontré","t":"when he ran into"},{"w":"son ancien professeur.","t":"his former teacher"}]}

items.fr: Comme il faisait très froid ce soir-là, nous sommes restés à la maison.
items.en: Since it was very cold that evening, we stayed home.

items.fr: Nous regardions la télévision quand la lumière s'est éteinte.
items.en: We were watching television when the light went out.

items.fr: Elle lisait un roman policier quand elle s'est endormie sur le canapé.
items.en: She was reading a detective novel when she fell asleep on the couch.

items.fr: Tandis que nous attendions le bus, il a commencé à pleuvoir très fort.
items.en: While we were waiting for the bus, it started to rain very hard.

items.fr: Il travaillait déjà dans cette entreprise quand il a rencontré sa femme.
items.en: He was already working at that company when he met his wife.

items.fr: Comme elle ne connaissait personne en ville, elle s'est inscrite à un club de sport.
items.en: Since she didn't know anyone in the city, she joined a sports club.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Comme elle ne connaissait personne en ville,","t":"since she didn't know anyone in the city,"},{"w":"elle s'est inscrite","t":"she joined"},{"w":"à un club de sport.","t":"a sports club"}]}

items.fr: Nous habitions encore chez nos parents quand nous avons trouvé notre premier travail.
items.en: We were still living with our parents when we found our first job.

items.fr: Pendant que les enfants dormaient, les parents ont rangé toute la maison.
items.en: While the children were sleeping, the parents tidied the whole house.

items.fr: Il pleuvait des cordes quand le mariage a enfin commencé.
items.en: It was pouring rain when the wedding finally began.

items.fr: Elle prenait son café tranquillement quand elle a reçu un appel urgent.
items.en: She was quietly drinking her coffee when she received an urgent call.

items.fr: Comme nous n'avions plus d'essence, nous avons dû marcher jusqu'à la station.
items.en: Since we had no more gas, we had to walk to the station.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Comme nous n'avions plus d'essence,","t":"since we had no more gas,"},{"w":"nous avons dû marcher","t":"we had to walk"},{"w":"jusqu'à la station.","t":"to the station"}]}

items.fr: Il faisait nuit noire quand ils sont finalement arrivés au camping.
items.en: It was pitch dark when they finally arrived at the campsite.

items.fr: Nous jouions aux cartes quand nous avons entendu un grand bruit dehors.
items.en: We were playing cards when we heard a loud noise outside.

items.fr: Elle habitait seule depuis peu quand elle a décidé d'adopter un chien.
items.en: She had been living alone for a short time when she decided to adopt a dog.

items.fr: Comme il n'y avait plus de place dans le train, nous avons voyagé debout.
items.en: Since there was no more room on the train, we traveled standing up.

items.fr: Tout le monde dormait encore quand le réveil a sonné.
items.en: Everyone was still asleep when the alarm rang.

items.fr: Elle traversait la rue quand elle a vu l'accident se produire.
items.en: She was crossing the street when she saw the accident happen.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Elle traversait la rue","t":"she was crossing the street"},{"w":"quand elle a vu","t":"when she saw"},{"w":"l'accident se produire.","t":"the accident happen"}]}

items.fr: Nous discutions tranquillement quand l'orage a soudain éclaté.
items.en: We were chatting quietly when the storm suddenly broke.

items.fr: Il se promenait dans le parc quand il a retrouvé un vieil ami d'école.
items.en: He was walking in the park when he ran into an old school friend.

items.fr: Comme la queue était trop longue au guichet, nous avons renoncé à acheter les billets.
items.en: Since the line at the counter was too long, we gave up buying the tickets.

items.fr: Elle faisait la vaisselle quand le vase de sa mère lui a glissé des mains.
items.en: She was doing the dishes when her mother's vase slipped from her hands.

items.fr: Nous étions en route vers l'aéroport quand nous avons appris l'annulation du vol.
items.en: We were on our way to the airport when we learned about the flight cancellation.

items.fr: Alors qu'elle contemplait le coucher du soleil depuis le balcon, elle a reçu la nouvelle qui allait bouleverser sa vie.
items.en: As she was watching the sunset from the balcony, she received the news that would upend her life.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Alors qu'elle contemplait le coucher du soleil depuis le balcon,","t":"as she was watching the sunset from the balcony,"},{"w":"elle a reçu la nouvelle","t":"she received the news"},{"w":"qui allait bouleverser sa vie.","t":"that would upend her life"}]}

items.fr: Pendant que la ville dormait encore, les pêcheurs quittaient déjà le port pour une longue journée en mer.
items.en: While the city was still asleep, the fishermen were already leaving the harbor for a long day at sea.

items.fr: Comme elle hésitait depuis des mois entre deux carrières, l'annonce de sa mutation a fini par trancher la question.
items.en: Since she had been hesitating for months between two careers, the announcement of her transfer finally settled the matter.

items.fr: Bien qu'il connaisse la région comme sa poche, il s'est égaré en pleine forêt ce soir-là.
items.en: Although he knew the region like the back of his hand, he got lost deep in the forest that evening.

items.fr: Le village vivait autrefois du commerce maritime, mais l'arrivée du chemin de fer a tout changé en quelques années.
items.en: The village once lived off maritime trade, but the arrival of the railway changed everything within a few years.

items.fr: Tandis que les invités discutaient encore au salon, la mariée s'est éclipsée un instant pour appeler sa mère.
items.en: While the guests were still chatting in the living room, the bride slipped away for a moment to call her mother.
items.notes: {"tiles":[{"w":"Tandis que les invités discutaient encore au salon,","t":"while the guests were still chatting in the living room,"},{"w":"la mariée s'est éclipsée un instant","t":"the bride slipped away for a moment"},{"w":"pour appeler sa mère.","t":"to call her mother"}]}

items.fr: Elle travaillait sans relâche depuis des semaines quand son entreprise a finalement décroché le contrat tant attendu.
items.en: She had been working tirelessly for weeks when her company finally landed the long-awaited contract.

items.fr: Comme la grève des trains paralysait tout le pays, des milliers de voyageurs ont dû improviser un autre moyen de transport.
items.en: Since the train strike was paralyzing the whole country, thousands of travelers had to improvise another means of transport.

items.fr: Il régnait un silence pesant dans la salle quand le juge a enfin annoncé le verdict.
items.en: A heavy silence hung over the room when the judge finally announced the verdict.

items.fr: Je vais chercher un nouvel emploi cette année.
items.en: I'm going to look for a new job this year.
items.ipa: ʒə vɛ ʃɛʁ.ʃe œ̃ nu.vɛl ɑ̃.plwa sɛt a.ne
items.notes: “nouvel” takes the special masculine form before a vowel sound in “nouvel emploi”.

items.fr: Tu vas apprendre à conduire l'année prochaine.
items.en: You're going to learn to drive next year.
items.ipa: ty va a.pʁɑ̃dʁ a kɔ̃.dɥiʁ la.ne pʁɔ.ʃɛn
items.notes: the second person singular of “aller” is “vas”, not “vais”.

items.fr: Nous allons visiter le Portugal en été.
items.en: We're going to visit Portugal in the summer.
items.notes: “allons” ends in a silent “s” that only surfaces as liaison before a vowel.

items.fr: Elle va garder son petit frère samedi.
items.en: She's going to look after her little brother on Saturday.
items.ipa: ɛl va gaʁ.de sɔ̃ pə.ti fʁɛʁ sam.di
items.notes: “son” must agree with the masculine noun “frère”, not with the feminine subject “elle”.

items.fr: Ils vont acheter une nouvelle voiture bientôt.
items.en: They're going to buy a new car soon.
items.ipa: il vɔ̃ aʃ.te yn nu.vɛl vwa.tyʁ bjɛ̃.to
items.notes: “vont” ends in a silent “t” that is never pronounced except in liaison.

items.fr: Vous allez fêter votre anniversaire au restaurant.
items.en: You're going to celebrate your birthday at the restaurant.
items.ipa: vu.z‿a.le fɛ.te vɔtʁ a.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ o ʁɛs.to.ʁɑ̃
items.notes: “fêter” keeps its circumflex accent, unlike the English “fete”.

items.fr: Je vais me lever plus tôt demain.
items.en: I'm going to get up earlier tomorrow.
items.ipa: ʒə vɛ mə lə.ve ply to də.mɛ̃
items.notes: the reflexive pronoun “me” stays right before the infinitive “lever”, not before “vais”.

items.fr: On va manger au marché ce week-end.
items.en: We're going to eat at the market this weekend.
items.ipa: ɔ̃ va mɑ̃.ʒe o maʁ.ʃe sə wik.ɛnd
items.notes: “on” always takes the same verb form as “il” or “elle”, so “va”, not “vont”.

items.fr: Tu vas t'inscrire au club de sport, non ?
items.en: You're going to sign up for the sports club, right?
items.ipa: ty va tɛ̃s.kʁiʁ o klœb də spɔʁ nɔ̃
items.notes: the reflexive pronoun “te” elides to “t'” before the vowel of “inscrire”.

items.fr: Nous allons peindre la cuisine en jaune.
items.en: We're going to paint the kitchen yellow.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ pɛ̃dʁ la kɥi.zin ɑ̃ ʒon
items.notes: after “allons”, the verb stays in the infinitive “peindre”, never conjugated.

items.fr: Elles vont partir en voyage scolaire.
items.en: They're going to go on a school trip.
items.ipa: ɛl vɔ̃ paʁ.tiʁ ɑ̃ vwa.jaʒ skɔ.lɛʁ
items.notes: “elles” needs “vont” here, agreeing in the plural like “ils”.

items.fr: Je vais essayer ce nouveau restaurant italien.
items.en: I'm going to try this new Italian restaurant.
items.ipa: ʒə vɛ e.se.je sə nu.vo ʁɛs.to.ʁɑ̃ i.ta.ljɛ̃
items.notes: “essayer” is spelled with two “s”, unlike the English “essay”.

items.fr: Vous allez recevoir votre diplôme en juin.
items.en: You're going to receive your diploma in June.
items.ipa: vu.z‿a.le ʁə.sə.vwaʁ vɔtʁ di.plom ɑ̃ ʒɥɛ̃
items.notes: “diplôme” carries a circumflex accent that the English “diploma” does not.

items.fr: Ils vont s'installer près de la gare.
items.en: They're going to settle down near the station.
items.ipa: il vɔ̃ sɛ̃s.ta.le pʁɛ də la gaʁ
items.notes: the reflexive “se” elides to “s'” before the vowel of “installer”.

items.fr: Je vais aider ma sœur à ranger sa chambre.
items.en: I'm going to help my sister tidy her room.
items.ipa: ʒə vɛ e.de ma sœʁ a ʁɑ̃.ʒe sa ʃɑ̃bʁ
items.notes: “sœur” keeps its unusual “œu” spelling rather than a phonetic one.

items.fr: Nous allons organiser une fête surprise.
items.en: We're going to organize a surprise party.
items.notes: “organiser” takes a single “s”, pronounced [z] between two vowels.

items.fr: Tu vas devenir grand-père cette année, félicitations !
items.en: You're going to become a grandfather this year, congratulations!
items.ipa: ty va dəv.niʁ gʁɑ̃.pɛʁ sɛt a.ne fe.li.si.ta.sjɔ̃
items.notes: “grand-père” keeps its hyphen and never agrees in the feminine.

items.fr: Elle va rendre visite à ses grands-parents.
items.en: She's going to visit her grandparents.
items.ipa: ɛl va ʁɑ̃dʁ vi.zit a se gʁɑ̃.pa.ʁɑ̃
items.notes: “ses” must be plural to match “grands-parents”, not the singular “sa”.

items.fr: On va prendre le train de huit heures.
items.en: We're going to take the eight o'clock train.
items.ipa: ɔ̃ va pʁɑ̃dʁ lə tʁɛ̃ də ɥi.t‿œʁ
items.notes: “huit” triggers a liaison with the following “heures”, pronounced [ɥitœʁ].

items.fr: Je vais poser ma candidature dans cette entreprise.
items.en: I'm going to apply for a job at this company.
items.ipa: ʒə vɛ po.ze ma kɑ̃.di.da.tyʁ dɑ̃ sɛt ɑ̃.tʁə.pʁiz
items.notes: “entreprise” is feminine, so the demonstrative must be “cette”, not “ce”.

items.fr: Vous allez signer le contrat vendredi.
items.en: You're going to sign the contract on Friday.
items.notes: the final “t” of “contrat” is silent.

items.fr: Ils vont fêter leur mariage au printemps.
items.en: They're going to celebrate their wedding in the spring.
items.ipa: il vɔ̃ fɛ.te lœʁ ma.ʁjaʒ o pʁɛ̃.tɑ̃
items.notes: “leur” stays invariable here since only one wedding is shared, unlike the plural “leurs”.

items.fr: Nous allons planter des fleurs dans le jardin.
items.en: We're going to plant flowers in the garden.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ plɑ̃.te de flœʁ dɑ̃ lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃
items.notes: “fleurs” takes a plural “s” that stays silent in speech.

items.fr: Je vais réserver une table pour ce soir.
items.en: I'm going to book a table for tonight.
items.ipa: ʒə vɛ ʁe.zɛʁ.ve yn tabl puʁ sə swaʁ
items.notes: “réserver” needs an acute accent on its first “e”.

items.fr: Tu vas t'entraîner tous les jours avant la course.
items.en: You're going to train every day before the race.
items.ipa: ty va tɑ̃.tʁɛ.ne tu le ʒuʁ a.vɑ̃ la kuʁs
items.notes: “entraîner” keeps its circumflex accent on the “i”.

items.fr: On va célébrer son anniversaire dimanche.
items.en: We're going to celebrate her birthday on Sunday.
items.notes: “célébrer” carries two acute accents, not grave ones.

items.fr: Elles vont apprendre le japonais l'an prochain.
items.en: They're going to learn Japanese next year.
items.ipa: ɛl vɔ̃ a.pʁɑ̃dʁ lə ʒa.pɔ.nɛ lɑ̃ pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃
items.notes: “japonais” stays lowercase in French, unlike the English “Japanese”.

items.fr: Je vais m'inscrire à la bibliothèque du quartier.
items.en: I'm going to register at the neighbourhood library.
items.ipa: ʒə vɛ mɛ̃s.kʁiʁ a la bi.bli.jɔ.tɛk dy kaʁ.tje
items.notes: “bibliothèque” takes a grave accent on its final “e”, not an acute one.

items.fr: Quand elle aura son diplôme, elle va partir travailler à l'étranger.
items.en: When she gets her diploma, she's going to go work abroad.
items.ipa: kɑ̃.t‿ɛl.o.ʁa sɔ̃ di.plom ɛl va paʁ.tiʁ tʁa.va.je a le.tʁɑ̃.ʒe
items.notes: after “quand” referring to the future, French requires the future tense “aura”, not the present.

items.fr: Comme il fait beau, nous allons pique-niquer au parc cet après-midi.
items.en: Since the weather's nice, we're going to have a picnic in the park this afternoon.
items.ipa: kɔm il fɛ bo nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ pik.ni.ke o paʁk sɛ.t‿a.pʁɛ.mi.di
items.notes: “pique-niquer” keeps its hyphen even once turned into a verb.

items.fr: Puisque le loyer augmente, ils vont déménager dans une ville moins chère.
items.en: Since the rent is going up, they're going to move to a cheaper city.
items.ipa: pɥisk lə lwa.je o.gmɑ̃t il vɔ̃ de.me.na.ʒe dɑ̃.z‿yn vil mwɛ̃ ʃɛʁ
items.notes: “chère” must agree in the feminine with “ville”, so it cannot stay “cher”.

items.fr: Bien qu'elle soit fatiguée, elle va terminer son rapport ce soir.
items.en: Even though she's tired, she's going to finish her report tonight.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃.kɛl swa fa.ti.ge ɛl va tɛʁ.mi.ne sɔ̃ ʁa.pɔʁ sə swaʁ
items.notes: “bien que” always triggers the subjunctive “soit”, never the indicative “est”.

items.fr: Avant de partir en retraite, il va former son remplaçant.
items.en: Before retiring, he's going to train his replacement.
items.ipa: a.vɑ̃ də paʁ.tiʁ ɑ̃ ʁə.tʁɛt il va fɔʁ.me sɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.pla.sɑ̃
items.notes: “avant de” is always followed by an infinitive, never a conjugated verb.

items.fr: Pour que le projet réussisse, l'équipe va se réunir chaque semaine.
items.en: For the project to succeed, the team is going to meet every week.
items.ipa: puʁ kə lə pʁɔ.ʒɛ ʁe.y.sis le.kip va sə ʁe.y.niʁ ʃak sə.mɛn
items.notes: “pour que” requires the subjunctive “réussisse”, not the indicative “réussit”.

items.fr: Comme elle n'a pas encore de logement, elle va habiter chez ses parents.
items.en: Since she doesn't have a place to live yet, she's going to live with her parents.
items.ipa: kɔm ɛl na pa.z‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ də lɔʒ.mɑ̃ ɛl va a.bi.te ʃe se pa.ʁɑ̃
items.notes: “habiter” starts with a mute “h”, so liaison still glides into it from “va”.

items.fr: Puisqu'ils ont trouvé un acheteur, ils vont vendre la maison en octobre.
items.en: Since they've found a buyer, they're going to sell the house in October.
items.ipa: pɥis.kil.z‿ɔ̃ tʁu.ve œ̃.n‿aʃ.tœʁ il vɔ̃ vɑ̃dʁ la mɛ.zɔ̃ ɑ̃.n‿ɔk.tɔbʁ
items.notes: “puisque” elides its final “e” before the vowel of “ils”.

items.fr: Dès que les résultats seront publiés, nous allons fêter la réussite.
items.en: As soon as the results are published, we're going to celebrate the success.
items.ipa: dɛ kə le ʁe.zyl.ta sə.ʁɔ̃ py.blje nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ fɛ.te la ʁe.y.sit
items.notes: “dès que” with a future meaning always calls for the future tense “seront”, not the present.

items.fr: Comme la circulation est mauvaise, on va partir une heure plus tôt.
items.en: Since traffic is bad, we're going to leave an hour earlier.
items.ipa: kɔm la siʁ.ky.la.sjɔ̃ ɛ mo.vɛz ɔ̃ va paʁ.tiʁ y.n‿œʁ ply to
items.notes: “mauvaise” must agree with the feminine noun “circulation”.

items.fr: Après avoir fini ses études, elle va s'installer à Lyon.
items.en: After finishing her studies, she's going to settle in Lyon.
items.ipa: a.pʁɛ.z‿a.vwaʁ fi.ni se.z‿e.tyd ɛl va sɛ̃s.ta.le a ljɔ̃
items.notes: “après avoir fini” uses the past infinitive, not “après finir”.

items.fr: Tant qu'il n'aura pas son visa, il ne va pas pouvoir voyager.
items.en: As long as he doesn't have his visa, he won't be able to travel.
items.ipa: tɑ̃.kil no.ʁa pa sɔ̃ vi.za il nə va pa pu.vwaʁ vwa.ja.ʒe
items.notes: “tant que” referring to a future condition needs “n'aura pas”, the future, not the present.

items.fr: Puisque son contrat se termine, elle va chercher un autre emploi.
items.en: Since her contract is ending, she's going to look for another job.
items.ipa: pɥi.skə sɔ̃ kɔ̃.tʁa sə tɛʁ.min ɛl va ʃɛʁ.ʃe œ̃.n‿otʁ ɑ̃.plwa
items.notes: “un autre” is used, not “une autre”, because “emploi” is masculine.

items.fr: Même s'il pleut, les enfants vont jouer dehors samedi.
items.en: Even if it rains, the children are going to play outside on Saturday.
items.ipa: mɛm sil plø le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ vɔ̃ ʒwe də.ʁɔʁ sam.di
items.notes: “même si” is followed by the indicative “pleut”, never the subjunctive.

items.fr: Puisque nous avons économisé assez, nous allons acheter un appartement.
items.en: Since we've saved enough, we're going to buy an apartment.
items.ipa: pɥi.skə nu.z‿a.vɔ̃.z‿e.kɔ.no.mi.ze a.se nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ aʃ.te œ̃.n‿a.paʁ.tə.mɑ̃
items.notes: “appartement” doubles its “p”, unlike the single-letter English “apartment”.

items.fr: Comme il vient d'obtenir sa licence, il va commencer à travailler tout de suite.
items.en: Since he's just gotten his degree, he's going to start working right away.
items.ipa: kɔm il vjɛ̃ dɔp.tə.niʁ sa li.sɑ̃s il va kɔ.mɑ̃.se a tʁa.va.je tu.d‿sɥit
items.notes: “vient d'obtenir” expresses a recent past action with “venir de”, not a future one.

items.fr: Avant que le bébé n'arrive, ils vont repeindre la chambre.
items.en: Before the baby arrives, they're going to repaint the room.
items.ipa: a.vɑ̃ kə lə be.be na.ʁiv il vɔ̃ ʁə.pɛ̃dʁ la ʃɑ̃bʁ
items.notes: “avant que” needs the subjunctive “n'arrive”, where “ne” here is purely expletive.

items.fr: Puisqu'elle parle déjà bien anglais, elle va postuler dans une entreprise internationale.
items.en: Since she already speaks English well, she's going to apply to an international company.
items.ipa: pɥis.kɛl paʁl de.ʒa bjɛ̃.n‿ɑ̃.glɛ ɛl va pɔs.ty.le dɑ̃.z‿yn ɑ̃.tʁə.pʁiz ɛ̃.tɛʁ.na.sjɔ.nal
items.notes: “anglais” stays lowercase as an adjective, unlike the capitalized English “English”.

items.fr: Comme les billets sont moins chers en semaine, nous allons partir un mardi.
items.en: Since tickets are cheaper on weekdays, we're going to leave on a Tuesday.
items.ipa: kɔm le bi.jɛ sɔ̃ mwɛ̃ ʃɛʁ ɑ̃ sə.mɛn nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ paʁ.tiʁ œ̃ maʁ.di
items.notes: “chers” agrees in the masculine plural with “billets”.

items.fr: Dès qu'ils auront signé le bail, ils vont emménager dans le nouvel appartement.
items.en: As soon as they've signed the lease, they're going to move into the new apartment.
items.ipa: dɛ.kil.z‿o.ʁɔ̃ si.ɲe lə baj il vɔ̃ ɑ̃.me.na.ʒe dɑ̃ lə nu.vɛl a.paʁ.tə.mɑ̃
items.notes: “emménager” (to move in) should not be confused with the near-homophone “aménager” (to fit out).

items.fr: Puisque tu as déjà ton billet, tu vas pouvoir partir plus tôt.
items.en: Since you already have your ticket, you're going to be able to leave earlier.
items.ipa: pɥi.skə ty a de.ʒa tɔ̃ bi.jɛ ty va pu.vwaʁ paʁ.tiʁ ply to
items.notes: “tôt” carries a circumflex accent that distinguishes it from other short adverbs.

items.fr: Comme elle a raté son examen, elle va le repasser en septembre.
items.en: Since she failed her exam, she's going to retake it in September.
items.ipa: kɔm ɛl a ʁa.te sɔ̃.n‿ɛg.za.mɛ̃ ɛl va lə ʁə.pa.se ɑ̃ sɛp.tɑ̃bʁ
items.notes: “rater” (to fail) should not be confused with the near-homophone “raser” (to shave).

items.fr: Vu que le loyer est trop élevé, on va chercher une colocation.
items.en: Given that the rent is too high, we're going to look for a shared flat.
items.ipa: vy kə lə lwa.je ɛ tʁo.p‿e.lə.ve ɔ̃ va ʃɛʁ.ʃe yn kɔ.lɔ.ka.sjɔ̃
items.notes: “élevé” needs its acute accents even though the sound resembles the English “elevated”.

items.fr: Puisque la réunion est annulée, nous allons rentrer plus tôt aujourd'hui.
items.en: Since the meeting is cancelled, we're going to head home earlier today.
items.ipa: pɥi.skə la ʁe.y.njɔ̃ ɛ.t‿a.ny.le nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.tʁe ply to o.ʒuʁ.dɥi
items.notes: “annulée” agrees in the feminine with “réunion”, so it keeps a final “e”.

items.fr: Comme il n'a pas encore de permis, il va prendre des leçons de conduite.
items.en: Since he doesn't have a licence yet, he's going to take driving lessons.
items.ipa: kɔm il na pa.z‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ də pɛʁ.mi il va pʁɑ̃dʁ de lə.sɔ̃ də kɔ̃.dɥit
items.notes: “permis” ends in a silent “s” whether singular or plural.

items.fr: Étant donné que les négociations progressent favorablement, la direction va annoncer un accord dès la semaine prochaine.
items.en: Given that negotiations are progressing favourably, management is going to announce an agreement as early as next week.
items.ipa: e.tɑ̃ dɔ.ne kə le ne.gɔ.sja.sjɔ̃ pʁɔ.gʁɛs fa.vɔ.ʁa.blə.mɑ̃ la di.ʁɛk.sjɔ̃ va a.nɔ̃.se œ̃.n‿a.kɔʁ dɛ la sə.mɛn pʁɔ.ʃɛn
items.notes: “favorablement” keeps a single “l”, inherited whole from the adjective “favorable”.

items.fr: Conscients des enjeux climatiques, les habitants vont adopter des gestes plus responsables dès cet automne.
items.en: Aware of the climate stakes, the residents are going to adopt more responsible habits starting this autumn.
items.ipa: kɔ̃.sjɑ̃ de.z‿ɑ̃.ʒø kli.ma.tik le.z‿a.bi.tɑ̃ vɔ̃ a.dɔp.te de ʒɛst ply ʁɛs.pɔ̃.sabl dɛ sɛ.t‿o.tɔn
items.notes: “conscients” agrees in the masculine plural with “habitants”, even though it precedes it.

items.fr: Malgré les incertitudes économiques, l'entreprise va investir massivement dans la recherche l'an prochain.
items.en: Despite the economic uncertainties, the company is going to invest heavily in research next year.
items.ipa: mal.gʁe le.z‿ɛ̃.sɛʁ.ti.tyd e.kɔ.nɔ.mik lɑ̃.tʁə.pʁiz va ɛ̃.vɛs.tiʁ ma.si.və.mɑ̃ dɑ̃ la ʁə.ʃɛʁʃ lɑ̃ pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃
items.notes: “malgré” governs a noun phrase directly and never takes “que” before it.

items.fr: Convaincue que ce poste correspond à ses ambitions, elle va accepter l'offre dès demain.
items.en: Convinced that this position matches her ambitions, she's going to accept the offer as early as tomorrow.
items.ipa: kɔ̃.vɛ̃.ky kə sə pɔst kɔ.ʁɛs.pɔ̃.d‿a se.z‿ɑ̃.bi.sjɔ̃ ɛl va ak.sɛp.te lɔfʁ dɛ də.mɛ̃
items.notes: “convaincue” must end in “e” to agree with the feminine subject “elle”.

items.fr: Face à la pénurie de logements, la municipalité va lancer un vaste programme de construction.
items.en: Faced with the housing shortage, the city council is going to launch a large-scale construction programme.
items.ipa: fas a la pe.ny.ʁi də lɔʒ.mɑ̃ la my.ni.si.pa.li.te va lɑ̃.se œ̃ vast pʁɔ.gʁam də kɔ̃s.tʁyk.sjɔ̃
items.notes: “municipalité” is feminine, which is why “la” is required rather than “le”.

items.fr: Puisque les jeunes diplômés peinent à trouver un emploi stable, le gouvernement va créer de nouvelles aides.
items.en: Since young graduates are struggling to find stable employment, the government is going to create new forms of support.
items.ipa: pɥi.skə le ʒœn di.plo.me pɛn a tʁu.ve œ̃.n‿ɑ̃.plwa stabl lə gu.vɛʁ.nə.mɑ̃ va kʁe.e də nu.vɛl ɛd
items.notes: “diplômés” keeps its circumflex accent on the “o” even in the plural.

items.fr: Bien qu'elle soit encore hésitante, tout porte à croire qu'elle va accepter cette mutation à l'étranger.
items.en: Although she's still hesitant, everything suggests that she's going to accept this transfer abroad.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃.kɛl swa.t‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ e.zi.tɑ̃t tu pɔʁt a kʁwaʁ kɛl va ak.sɛp.te sɛt my.ta.sjɔ̃ a le.tʁɑ̃.ʒe
items.notes: “bien que” triggers the subjunctive “soit”, never the indicative “est”.

items.fr: Étant donné la hausse constante des loyers, de nombreux jeunes actifs vont quitter la capitale.
items.en: Given the constant rise in rents, many young working people are going to leave the capital.
items.ipa: e.tɑ̃ dɔ.ne la os kɔ̃s.tɑ̃t de lwa.je də nɔ̃.bʁø ʒœn ak.tif vɔ̃ ki.te la ka.pi.tal
items.notes: “hausse” starts with an aspirate “h”, which blocks elision, so it stays “la hausse”.

items.fr: Consciente des risques, elle va tout de même se lancer dans cette aventure entrepreneuriale.
items.en: Aware of the risks, she's still going to embark on this entrepreneurial venture.
items.ipa: kɔ̃.sjɑ̃t de ʁisk ɛl va tu.d‿mɛm sə lɑ̃.se dɑ̃ sɛt a.vɑ̃.tyʁ ɑ̃.tʁə.pʁə.nœ.ʁjal
items.notes: “consciente” ends in “e” to agree with the feminine “elle”, unlike the masculine “conscient”.

items.fr: Résolus à changer de vie, ils vont tout vendre pour s'installer à la campagne.
items.en: Determined to change their lives, they're going to sell everything to settle in the countryside.
items.ipa: ʁe.zɔ.ly a ʃɑ̃.ʒe də vi il vɔ̃ tu vɑ̃dʁ puʁ sɛ̃s.ta.le a la kɑ̃.paɲ
items.notes: “résolus” agrees in the masculine plural with “ils”, so it takes a final “s”.

items.fr: L'an prochain, nous habiterons dans une maison plus grande.
items.en: Next year, we will live in a bigger house.
items.ipa: lɑ̃ pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃ nu.z‿a.bi.tə.ʁɔ̃ dɑ̃.z‿yn mɛ.zɔ̃ ply gʁɑ̃d
items.notes: the future of “habiter” adds “-ons” directly onto the infinitive, without dropping the final “r”.

items.fr: Plus tard, il sera médecin dans un hôpital pour enfants.
items.en: Later on, he'll be a doctor at a children's hospital.
items.ipa: ply taʁ il sə.ʁa med.sɛ̃ dɑ̃.z‿œ̃.n‿o.pi.tal puʁ ɑ̃.fɑ̃
items.notes: “être” has the irregular future stem “ser-”, not “êtr-”.

items.fr: Bientôt, tu auras ton propre appartement.
items.en: Soon, you'll have your own apartment.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃.to ty o.ʁa tɔ̃ pʁɔpʁ a.paʁ.tə.mɑ̃
items.notes: “avoir” takes the irregular future stem “aur-”, not “avr-”.

items.fr: L'été prochain, nous irons camper dans les Alpes.
items.en: Next summer, we'll go camping in the Alps.
items.ipa: le.te pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃ nu.z‿i.ʁɔ̃ kɑ̃.pe dɑ̃ le.z‿alp
items.notes: “aller” becomes “ir-” in the future, an irregular stem unrelated to the infinitive.

items.fr: Un jour, elle fera le tour du monde en bateau.
items.en: One day, she'll travel around the world by boat.
items.ipa: œ̃ ʒuʁ ɛl fə.ʁa lə tuʁ dy mɔ̃d ɑ̃ ba.to
items.notes: “faire” changes its stem to “fer-” in the future, not “fair-”.

items.fr: Mes parents fêteront leurs trente ans de mariage l'an prochain.
items.en: My parents will celebrate their thirtieth wedding anniversary next year.
items.ipa: me pa.ʁɑ̃ fɛt.ʁɔ̃ lœʁ tʁɑ̃t ɑ̃ də ma.ʁjaʒ lɑ̃ pʁɔ.ʃɛ̃
items.notes: the future stem of “fêter” keeps its circumflex accent throughout the conjugation.

items.fr: Quand je serai grand, je serai pompier.
items.en: When I grow up, I'll be a firefighter.
items.ipa: kɑ̃ ʒə sə.ʁɛ gʁɑ̃ ʒə sə.ʁɛ pɔ̃.pje
items.notes: “serai” and “serais” sound identical but are spelled differently for the future and the conditional.

items.fr: Nous finirons nos devoirs avant le dîner.
items.en: We'll finish our homework before dinner.
items.ipa: nu fi.ni.ʁɔ̃ no dəv.wɑʁ a.vɑ̃ lə di.ne
items.notes: “finirons” adds the future ending directly onto the “-ir” infinitive, keeping the final “r”.

items.fr: Elle choisira un cadeau pour sa meilleure amie.
items.en: She'll choose a gift for her best friend.
items.ipa: ɛl ʃwa.zi.ʁa œ̃ ka.do puʁ sa mɛ.jœʁ a.mi
items.notes: “meilleure” must end in “e” because “amie” is feminine.

items.fr: Tu réussiras cet examen si tu travailles sérieusement.
items.en: You'll pass this exam if you study seriously.
items.ipa: ty ʁe.y.si.ʁa sɛ.t‿ɛg.za.mɛ̃ si ty tʁa.vaj se.ʁjøz.mɑ̃
items.notes: after “si” in this pattern, the present tense is used, while the result clause takes the future.

items.fr: Ils vendront leur ancienne voiture avant d'en acheter une neuve.
items.en: They will sell their old car before buying a new one.
items.ipa: il vɑ̃.dʁɔ̃ lœʁ ɑ̃.sjɛn vwa.tyʁ a.vɑ̃ dɑ̃.n‿aʃ.te yn nœv
items.notes: “ancienne” agrees in the feminine with “voiture”, doubling the “n”.

items.fr: Nous partirons en vacances dès que possible.
items.en: We'll go on vacation as soon as possible.
items.ipa: nu paʁ.ti.ʁɔ̃ ɑ̃ va.kɑ̃s dɛ kə pɔ.sibl
items.notes: “partirons” is built on the infinitive “partir” plus the regular future endings.

items.fr: Vous recevrez la réponse par courriel demain.
items.en: You'll receive the answer by email tomorrow.
items.ipa: vu ʁə.sə.vʁe la ʁe.pɔ̃s paʁ ku.ʁjɛl də.mɛ̃
items.notes: “recevoir” drops its “-oir” ending and adds “-evr-” before the future endings.

items.fr: Elle achètera du pain frais chaque matin.
items.en: She'll buy fresh bread every morning.
items.ipa: ɛl a.ʃɛ.tə.ʁa dy pɛ̃ fʁɛ ʃak ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: “acheter” takes a grave accent throughout the future, becoming “achète-”.

items.fr: Nous appellerons le médecin s'il y a un problème.
items.en: We'll call the doctor if there's a problem.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.pɛl.ʁɔ̃ lə med.sɛ̃ sil.j.a œ̃ pʁɔ.blɛm
items.notes: “appeler” doubles its “l” in the future stem, giving “appell-”.

items.fr: Un jour, mon fils deviendra pilote de ligne.
items.en: One day, my son will become an airline pilot.
items.ipa: œ̃ ʒuʁ mɔ̃ fis də.vjɛ̃.dʁa pi.lɔt də liɲ
items.notes: “devenir” keeps the irregular stem “viendr-” borrowed from “venir”.

items.fr: Je te promets que je t'appellerai tous les soirs.
items.en: I promise you I'll call you every night.
items.ipa: ʒə tə pʁɔ.mɛ kə ʒə ta.pɛl.ʁe tu le swaʁ
items.notes: “appellerai” doubles the “l” before the future ending “-erai”.

items.fr: Bientôt, il saura nager sans brassière.
items.en: Soon, he'll know how to swim without a life jacket.
items.ipa: bjɛ̃.to il so.ʁa na.ʒe sɑ̃ bʁa.sjɛʁ
items.notes: “savoir” uses the irregular future stem “saur-”, not “sav-”.

items.fr: Nous serons prêts pour huit heures.
items.en: We'll be ready by eight o'clock.
items.notes: “prêts” agrees in the masculine plural with “nous” here and keeps its circumflex accent.

items.fr: Elle sera contente de te revoir.
items.en: She'll be happy to see you again.
items.ipa: ɛl sə.ʁa kɔ̃.tɑ̃t də tə ʁə.vwaʁ
items.notes: “contente” agrees in the feminine with the subject “elle”.

items.fr: Mes cousins viendront nous rendre visite en août.
items.en: My cousins will come visit us in August.
items.ipa: me ku.zɛ̃ vjɛ̃.dʁɔ̃ nu ʁɑ̃dʁ vi.zit ɑ̃.n‿ut
items.notes: “viendront” keeps the irregular stem “viendr-”, never “venir-”.

items.fr: Tu verras, tout se passera bien.
items.en: You'll see, everything will go well.
items.ipa: ty vɛ.ʁa tu sə pa.sə.ʁa bjɛ̃
items.notes: “voir” doubles its “r” in the future stem, giving “verr-”.

items.fr: Je finirai ce livre avant la fin de la semaine.
items.en: I'll finish this book before the end of the week.
items.ipa: ʒə fi.ni.ʁe sə livʁ a.vɑ̃ la fɛ̃ də la sə.mɛn
items.notes: “finirai” ends in “-ai”, pronounced like “é”, not like the “ait” of the conditional.

items.fr: Elle enverra son dossier avant vendredi.
items.en: She'll send her file before Friday.
items.ipa: ɛl ɑ̃.vɛ.ʁa sɔ̃ dɔ.sje a.vɑ̃ vɑ̃.dʁə.di
items.notes: “envoyer” has the irregular future stem “enverr-”, with a double “r”.

items.fr: Nous devrons partir tôt pour éviter les embouteillages.
